## [PART III]{.HLabel1}[Incorporation, Continuance and Discontinuance]{.HTitleText1} {#h-258045 .Part}

### [Formalities of Incorporation]{.HTitleText2} {#h-258046 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Incorporation of company or society

**[[22]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-22 .sectionLabel}** On the application of one
or more persons made in accordance with this Act, the Minister may,
subject to this Part, issue letters patent incorporating a company or
society.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restrictions on incorporation

- **[[23]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-23
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Letters patent incorporating a
  company or society may not be issued if the application therefor is
  made by or on behalf of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Her Majesty in right of Canada or in right of a
    province, an agency of Her Majesty in either of those rights, or an
    entity controlled by Her Majesty in either of those rights;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the government of a foreign country or any
    political subdivision thereof;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} an agency of the government of a foreign country or
    any political subdivision thereof; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} an entity, other than a foreign institution or any
    subsidiary of a foreign institution, that is controlled by the
    government of a foreign country or any political subdivision
    thereof.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Societies

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Letters patent incorporating a society may not be
  issued if the society is to operate for profit or as a commercial
  enterprise or its property is not to be under the control of persons
  periodically elected by members of the society.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 23
- 1997, c. 15, s. 169
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}National treatment

- **[[24]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-24 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a
  proposed company would be a subsidiary of a foreign institution that
  is engaged in the insurance business, letters patent to incorporate
  the company may not be issued unless the Minister is satisfied that,
  if the application is made by a non-WTO Member foreign institution,
  treatment as favourable for companies to which this Act applies exists
  or will be provided in the jurisdiction in which the foreign
  institution principally carries on business, either directly or
  through a subsidiary.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Part XII of the [Bank
  Act](/eng/acts/B-1.01)

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Nothing in subsection (1) affects the operation of
  Part XII of the [Bank Act](/eng/acts/B-1.01).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 24
- 1999, c. 28, s. 120
- 2001, c. 9, s. 354
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application for incorporation

- **[[25]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-25 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  application for letters patent to incorporate a company or society
  setting out the names of the first directors of the company or society
  shall be filed with the Superintendent, together with such other
  information, material and evidence as the Superintendent may require.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publishing notice of intent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Before filing an application referred to in
  subsection (1), the applicant or one of the applicants, as the case
  may be, shall, at least once a week for a period of four consecutive
  weeks, publish, in a form satisfactory to the Superintendent, a notice
  of intention to make the application in the [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) and in a newspaper in general
  circulation at or near the place where the head office of the company
  or society is to be situated.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Objections to incorporation

- **[[26]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-26 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Any
  person who objects to the proposed incorporation of a company or
  society may, within thirty days after the date of the last publication
  under subsection 25(2) in respect of the proposed company or society,
  submit the objection in writing to the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Minister to be informed

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} On receipt of an objection under subsection (1), the
  Superintendent shall inform the Minister of the objection.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Inquiry into objection and report

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} On receipt of an objection under subsection (1), and
  if the application for the issuance of the letters patent to which the
  objection relates has been received, the Superintendent shall, if
  satisfied that it is necessary and in the public interest to do so,
  hold or cause to be held a public inquiry into the objection as it
  relates to the application and, on completion of the inquiry, the
  Superintendent shall report the findings of the inquiry to the
  Minister.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report to be made available

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Within thirty days after receiving a report under
  subsection (3), the Minister shall make the report available to the
  public.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Rules governing proceedings

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the approval of the Governor in Council,
  the Superintendent may make rules governing the proceedings at public
  inquiries held under this section.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Matters for consideration

**[[27]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-27 .sectionLabel}** Before issuing letters
patent to incorporate a company or society, the Minister shall take into
account all matters that the Minister considers relevant to the
application, including

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the nature and sufficiency of the financial resources
  of the applicant or applicants as a source of continuing financial
  support for the company or society;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the soundness and feasibility of the plans of the
  applicant or applicants for the future conduct and development of the
  business of the company or society;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the business record and experience of the applicant
  or applicants;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the character and integrity of the applicant or
  applicants or, if the applicant or any of the applicants is a body
  corporate, its reputation for being operated in a manner that is
  consistent with the standards of good character and integrity;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} whether the company or society will be operated
  responsibly by persons with the competence and experience suitable for
  involvement in the operation of a financial institution;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the impact of any integration of the operations and
  businesses of the applicant or applicants with those of the company or
  society on the conduct of those operations and businesses; and

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the best interests of the financial system in Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 27
- 2001, c. 9, s. 355
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents of letters patent

- **[[28]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-28 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} There
  shall be set out in the letters patent incorporating a company or
  society

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name of the company or society;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the province in which the head office of the
    company or society is to be situated;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the date that the company or society came, or is to
    come, into existence; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of letters patent incorporating a
    company, whether the company is to be a mutual company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Fraternal benefit societies

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In addition to the information required to be
  included under subsection (1), there shall be set out in the letters
  patent of a society

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the criteria for membership in the society;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the manner in which the capital of the society is
    to be acquired; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the disposition to be made of the property of the
    society on liquidation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Provisions in letters patent

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may set out in the letters patent
  incorporating a company or society any provision not contrary to this
  Act that the Minister considers advisable in order to take into
  account the particular circumstances of the proposed company or
  society.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Terms and conditions

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may impose such terms and conditions in
  respect of the issuance of letters patent incorporating a company or
  society as the Minister considers necessary or appropriate.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 28
- 2005, c. 54, s. 219
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-28-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 28"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Letters patent of incorporation on
application of converted companies

- **[[28.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-28.1 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  the Minister, under section 22, issues letters patent incorporating a
  company on the application of a converted company in respect of which
  subsection 407(4) or (11) applies or applied at any time, the Minister
  may include in the letters patent of incorporation of the company a
  provision deeming shares of the company to be issued, on a share for
  share basis, to all shareholders of the converted company in exchange
  for all the issued and outstanding shares of the converted company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of provision

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Shares of a company deemed to be issued under
  subsection (1) are subject to the same designation, rights, privileges
  and restrictions or conditions and, subject to any agreement to the
  contrary, to the same charges, encumbrances and other restrictions as
  the shares of the converted company for which they are exchanged and
  the shares of the converted company, on the issuance of the letters
  patent, become the property of the company free and clear of any
  charge, encumbrance or other restriction.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of provision

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An exchange of shares of a converted company referred
  to in subsection (1) under a provision included in the letters patent
  incorporating a company does not deprive a person who was a holder of
  shares of the converted company immediately before the exchange of any
  right or privilege with respect to the shares or relieve the person of
  any liability in respect of the shares, but that right or privilege
  must be exercised in accordance with this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transfer and voting of company shares

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (3), no share of a company that is
  deemed to be issued under a provision included in the letters patent
  incorporating a company may subsequently be transferred or voted
  contrary to this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholder and policyholder approval

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} No provision described in subsection (1) may be
  included in letters patent issued under section 22 unless the
  application for the letters patent is accompanied by evidence that the
  request for the provision was approved by a special resolution of the
  shareholders and policyholders of the converted company who are
  entitled to vote at a meeting of shareholders and policyholders called
  to consider the application.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exchange of share certificates

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} If, under a provision included in the letters patent
  incorporating a company, a share exchange is deemed to have taken
  place, the company shall, within ninety days after the issuance of the
  letters patent, make provision for the issue of share certificates
  representing shares of the company and for the exchange of those
  certificates for share certificates representing the shares of the
  converted company that were outstanding on the day the letters patent
  were issued.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 356
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proposal involving fundamental change

- **[[28.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-28.2 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  application, made in accordance with the regulations, by a converted
  company in respect of which subsection 407(4) or (11) applies or
  applied at any time to give effect to a proposal to incorporate a
  company as the holding body corporate of the converted company, to
  continue a body corporate as a company that is the holding body
  corporate of the converted company or to amalgamate two or more bodies
  corporate and continue those bodies corporate as a company that is the
  holding body corporate of the converted company --- and to make any
  other fundamental change to the converted company, including an
  exchange of any or all of the shares of the converted company for
  shares of the company ---, the Minister may, to give effect to the
  proposal,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} include in the letters patent of the company issued
    under section 22, 34 or 251 any provision the Minister considers
    necessary; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} despite any provision of the Act specified in
    regulations made under paragraph (2)(e), give any approval that the
    Minister considers necessary.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council may make regulations

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} respecting applications referred to in subsection
    (1), including their form and the information to be contained in
    them, and authorizing the Superintendent to require additional
    information in respect of such applications;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} respecting proposals to which subsection (1)
    applies, including the information to be contained in the proposals
    and the times within which the transactions involved in them must
    occur;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} respecting the procedures to be followed by a
    converted company that makes an application under subsection (1);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} respecting the approval, confirmation or
    authorization, if any, of all or any portion of proposals to which
    subsection (1) applies, including the approval of shareholders and
    policyholders and including the terms and conditions of those
    approvals, confirmations or authorizations and their effect; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} specifying provisions of the Act for the purpose of
    paragraph (1)(b).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 356
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of issue of letters patent

**[[29]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-29 .sectionLabel}** The Superintendent shall
cause to be published in the [Canada Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/)
a notice of the issuance of letters patent incorporating a company or
society.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}First directors

**[[30]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-30 .sectionLabel}** The first directors of a
company or society are the directors named in the application for
letters patent to incorporate the company or society.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of letters patent

**[[31]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-31 .sectionLabel}** A company or society
comes into existence on the date provided therefor in its letters
patent.

### [Continuance]{.HTitleText2} {#h-258147 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Federal corporations

- **[[32]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-32 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A body
  corporate incorporated under the [Canada Business Corporations
  Act](/eng/acts/C-44) or any other Act of Parliament, including an
  insurance holding company but not including a federal credit union,
  may apply to the Minister for letters patent continuing the body
  corporate as a company under this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Other corporations

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A body corporate incorporated otherwise than by or
  under an Act of Parliament may, if so authorized by the laws of the
  jurisdiction where it is incorporated, apply to the Minister for
  letters patent continuing the body corporate as a company under this
  Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Fraternal benefit societies

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A fraternal benefit society incorporated otherwise
  than by or under an Act of Parliament may, if so authorized by the
  laws of the jurisdiction where it is incorporated, apply to the
  Minister for letters patent continuing the fraternal benefit society
  as a society.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 32
- 1994, c. 24, s. 34(F)
- 1997, c. 15, s. 170
- 2001, c. 9, s. 357
- 2010, c. 12, s. 2118
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-32-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 32"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application for continuance

- **[[33]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-33 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where
  a body corporate applies for letters patent under subsection
  32(1), (2) or (3), sections 23 to 27 apply in respect of the
  application, with such modifications as the circumstances require.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Special resolution approval

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a body corporate applies for letters patent
  under subsection 32(1), (2) or (3), the application must be duly
  authorized by a special resolution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Copy of special resolution

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A copy of the special resolution referred to in
  subsection (2) shall be filed with the application.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 33
- 1997, c. 15, s. 171
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Power to issue letters patent

- **[[34]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-34 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On the
  application of a body corporate under subsection 32(1) or (2), the
  Minister may, subject to this Part, issue letters patent continuing
  the body corporate as a company under this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Power to issue letters patent to
  fraternal benefit society

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} On the application of a fraternal benefit society
  under subsection 32(3), the Minister may, subject to this Part, issue
  letters patent continuing the fraternal benefit society as a society.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Issue of letters patent

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Section 28 applies in respect of the issue of letters
  patent under subsection (1) or (2), with such modifications as the
  circumstances require.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 34
- 1997, c. 15, s. 172
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of letters patent

- **[[35]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-35 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On the
  day set out in the letters patent continuing a body corporate as a
  company under subsection 34(1),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the body corporate becomes a company as if it had
    been incorporated under this Act; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the letters patent are deemed to be the
    incorporating instrument of the continued company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of letters patent --- society

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} On the day set out in the letters patent continuing a
  fraternal benefit society as a society under subsection 34(2),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the fraternal benefit society becomes a society as
    if it had been incorporated under this Act; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the letters patent are deemed to be the
    incorporating instrument of the continued society.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 35
- 1997, c. 15, s. 173
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Copy of letters patent

- **[[36]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-36 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where
  a body corporate is continued as a company or society under this Part,
  the Superintendent shall without delay send a copy of the letters
  patent to the appropriate official or public body in the jurisdiction
  in which the body corporate was authorized to apply to be continued
  under this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of issuance of letters patent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent shall publish in the [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) a notice of the issuance of
  letters patent continuing a body corporate as a company or society
  under this Act.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 36
- 1997, c. 15, s. 174(E)
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effects of continuance

**[[37]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-37 .sectionLabel}** Where a body corporate is
continued as a company or society under this Part,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the property of the body corporate continues to be
  the property of the company or society;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the company or society continues to be liable for the
  obligations of the body corporate;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} an existing cause of action or claim by or against
  the body corporate or any liability of the body corporate to
  prosecution is unaffected;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a civil, criminal or administrative action or
  proceeding pending by or against the body corporate may continue to be
  prosecuted by or against the company or society;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} a conviction against, or any ruling, order or
  judgment in favour of or against the body corporate may be enforced by
  or against the company or society;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} a person who, on the day the body corporate becomes a
  company or society, is the holder of a security issued by the body
  corporate is not deprived of any right or privilege available to the
  person at that time in respect of the security or relieved of any
  liability in respect of it, but any such right or privilege may be
  exercised only in accordance with this Act; and

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the by-laws of the body corporate, except those that
  are in conflict with this Act, continue as the by-laws of the company
  or society.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 37
- 1997, c. 15, s. 175
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transitional

- **[[38]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-38
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Notwithstanding any other provision
  of this Act or the regulations, the Minister may, on the
  recommendation of the Superintendent, by order, grant to a company or
  society in respect of which letters patent were issued under
  subsection 34(1) or (2) permission to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} engage in a business activity specified in the
    order that the company or society would not otherwise be permitted
    by this Act to engage in and that the body corporate continued as
    the company or society was engaging in at the time the application
    for the letters patent was made;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} continue to have issued and outstanding debt
    obligations the issue of which is not authorized by this Act if the
    debt obligations were outstanding at the time the application for
    the letters patent was made;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 1994, c. 47, s. 119\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} hold assets that the company or society would not
    otherwise be permitted by this Act to hold, if the assets were held
    by the body corporate continued as the company or society at the
    time the application for the letters patent was made;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} acquire and hold assets that the company or society
    would not otherwise be permitted by this Act to acquire or hold, if
    the body corporate continued as the company or society was obliged,
    at the time the application for the letters patent was made, to
    acquire those assets; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} maintain outside Canada any records or registers
    required by this Act to be maintained in Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duration

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The permission granted under subsection (1) shall be
  expressed to be granted for a period specified in the order not
  exceeding

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} with respect to any activity described in paragraph
    (1)(a), thirty days after the date of issue of the letters patent
    or, where the activity is conducted pursuant to an agreement
    existing on the date of issue of the letters patent, the expiration
    of the agreement;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} with respect to any matter described in paragraph
    (1)(b), ten years; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} with respect to any matter described in any of
    paragraphs (1)(d) to (f), two years.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Renewal

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), the Minister may, on the
  recommendation of the Superintendent, by order, renew a permission
  granted by order under subsection (1) with respect to any matter
  described in paragraphs (1)(b) to (e) for such further period or
  periods as the Minister considers necessary.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitation

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall not grant to a company or society
  any permission

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} with respect to matters described in paragraph
    (1)(b), that purports to be effective more than ten years after the
    date of the approval for the company or society to commence and
    carry on business, unless the Minister is satisfied on the basis of
    evidence on oath provided by an officer of the company or society
    that the company or society will not be able at law to redeem at the
    end of the ten years the outstanding debt obligations to which the
    permission relates; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} with respect to matters described in paragraphs
    (1)(d) and (e), that purports to be effective more than ten years
    after the date of the approval for the company or society to
    commence and carry on business.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 38
- 1994, c. 47, s. 119
- 1997, c. 15, s. 176
- 2007, c. 6, s. 190
:::

Version](section-38-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 38"){.PITLink}
