  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), a person referred to in that
  subsection is entitled to be indemnified by the company in respect of
  all costs, charges and expenses reasonably incurred by them in
  connection with the defence of any civil, criminal, administrative,
  investigative or other proceeding to which the person is subject
  because of the association referred to in subsection (1) with the
  company or other entity described in that subsection if the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} was not judged by the court or other competent
    authority to have committed any fault or omitted to do anything that
    they ought to have done; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} fulfils the conditions set out in subsection (3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Heirs and personal representatives

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} A company may, to the extent referred to in
  subsections (1) to (5) in respect of the person, indemnify the heirs
  or personal representatives of any person whom the company may
  indemnify under those subsections.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 221
- 2001, c. 9, s. 385(F)
- 2005, c. 54, s. 258
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-221-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 221"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors' and officers' insurance

**[[222]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-222 .sectionLabel}** A company may purchase
and maintain insurance for the benefit of any person referred to in
section 221 against any liability incurred by the person

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the capacity of a director or an officer of the
  company, except where the liability relates to a failure to act
  honestly and in good faith with a view to the best interests of the
  company; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the capacity of a director or officer of another
  entity or while acting in a similar capacity for another entity, if
  they act or acted in that capacity at the company's request, except if
  the liability relates to a failure to act honestly and in good faith
  with a view to the best interests of the entity.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 222
- 2005, c. 54, s. 259
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-222-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 222"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application to court for indemnification

- **[[223]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-223 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  company or a person referred to in section 221 may apply to a court
  for an order approving an indemnity under that section and the court
  may so order and make any further order it thinks fit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice to Superintendent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An applicant under subsection (1) shall give the
  Superintendent written notice of the application and the
  Superintendent is entitled to appear and to be heard at the hearing of
  the application in person or by counsel.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Other notice

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} On an application under subsection (1), the court may
  order notice to be given to any interested person and that person is
  entitled to appear and to be heard in person or by counsel at the
  hearing of the application.

### [DIVISION III]{.HLabel2}[Fundamental Changes]{.HTitleText2} {#h-260378 .Subheading}

#### [Amendments --- Letters Patent]{.HTitleText3} {#h-260379 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Incorporating instrument

**[[224]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-224 .sectionLabel}** On the application of a
company or society duly authorized by special resolution, the Minister
may approve a proposal to add, change or remove any provision that is
permitted by this Act to be set out in the incorporating instrument of
the company or society.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 224
- 1997, c. 15, s. 214
- 2001, c. 9, s. 386
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Letters patent to amend

- **[[225]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-225 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  receipt of an application referred to in section 224, the Minister may
  issue letters patent to effect the proposal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of letters patent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Letters patent issued pursuant to subsection (1)
  become effective on the day stated in the letters patent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 225
- 2001, c. 9, s. 387
:::

#### [Mutualization]{.HTitleText3} {#h-260391 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Mutualization

- **[[226]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-226 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  the application of a company that has common shares but does not have
  securities that are not convertible into common shares until after, or
  options or rights to acquire those shares that are not exercisable
  until after, the time of the application, the Minister may approve a
  proposal to convert the company into a mutual company by the purchase,
  or other acquisition, for the purpose of cancellation of those shares,
  securities, options and rights.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In sections 227 to 236,

  [[common share]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[common share]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a security currently convertible into a common
        share, and

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a currently exercisable option or a right to
        acquire a common share or a security referred to in paragraph
        (a); ([action ordinaire]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[mutualization proposal]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[mutualization proposal]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a proposal
      referred to in subsection (1). ([proposition de
      mutualisation]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Saving

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Nothing in this section or sections 227 to 236 limits
  the powers of companies under subsection 75(1).

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents of mutualization proposal

- **[[227]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-227
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every mutualization proposal shall
  set out the terms and means of effecting the conversion, and, in
  particular,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the manner in which all issued and outstanding
    shares of the company, other than shares that may be issued by a
    mutual company, are to be purchased or otherwise acquired for the
    purpose of cancellation;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the price to be paid for those shares;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the nature of the consideration to be paid for
    those shares;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the amount of any dividends to be paid to the
    holders of those shares after their purchase or other acquisition;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the period within which the company intends to
    purchase or otherwise acquire those shares;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the anticipated date when the company will become a
    mutual company; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the proposed by-laws of the converted company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Idem

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The mutualization proposal shall also contain such
  other information and evidence as the Minister may require.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholder and policyholder approval

- **[[228]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-228 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  directors of a company that makes a mutualization proposal shall,
  before applying to the Minister for approval of the proposal, submit
  it for approval to a meeting of the shareholders and policyholders
  entitled to vote and, subject to subsection (3), to the holders of
  each class or series of shares.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Right to vote

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Each share of a company that makes a mutualization
  proposal carries the right to vote in respect of the proposal whether
  or not it otherwise carries the right to vote.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Class vote

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The holders of shares of a class or series of shares
  of a company that makes a mutualization proposal are entitled to vote
  separately as a class or series in respect of the proposal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Policyholder vote

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Policyholders who are entitled to vote are entitled
  to vote separately from shareholders in respect of a mutualization
  proposal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Special resolution

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (3) and (4), a mutualization
  proposal is approved when the shareholders and the policyholders who
  are entitled to vote have approved the proposal by special resolution.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application to Minister

- **[[229]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-229 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  company shall, within three months after the approval of a
  mutualization proposal in accordance with section 228, apply to the
  Minister for approval of the proposal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Criteria for approval

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In determining whether to approve a mutualization
  proposal, the Minister shall consider all matters that the Minister
  considers relevant and may not approve the proposal unless satisfied
  that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the proposal was approved by the shareholders and
    policyholders pursuant to section 228;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the conversion of the company into a mutual company
    may reasonably be expected to be achieved under the terms of the
    proposal and in accordance with this section and sections 230 to
    236;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} there are no reasonable grounds for believing that
    the conversion would cause the company to be in contravention of
    subsection 515(1), any regulation made under subsection 515(2) or
    any order made under subsection 515(3);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the stated capital of the company has ceased to be
    an important factor in safeguarding the interests of the
    policyholders of the company, having regard to the quality and
    amount of the assets of the company, the surplus of the company
    relative to its liabilities, the nature of the business carried on
    by the company and any other considerations deemed by the Minister
    to be relevant;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the price fixed by the directors for the purchase
    or other acquisition of the common shares of the company under the
    proposal is fair and reasonable in the circumstances; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the proposal is in the best interests of the
    financial system in Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 229
- 2007, c. 6, s. 202
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-229-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 229"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of Minister's approval

- **[[230]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-230
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where the Minister approves a
  mutualization proposal made by a company,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the company may not issue any shares other than a
    share that may be issued by a mutual company;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the company may solicit offers from the holders of
    the shares of the company that are to be purchased or otherwise
    acquired to effect the conversion of the company but shall not
    purchase or otherwise acquire those shares until the approval of the
    Superintendent under section 234 is obtained; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any change in the proposal must be approved by the
    shareholders and policyholders and by the Minister.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application of ss. 228 to 230

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Sections 228 to 230 apply with such modifications as
  the circumstances require in respect of changes in mutualization
  proposals.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Register to be kept

**[[231]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-231 .sectionLabel}** A company shall prepare
and maintain a register recording the offers for sale of shares under
the terms of a mutualization proposal in the order in which those offers
are received by the company, showing, in respect of each offer,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the date of receipt by the company of the offer;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the shareholder making the
  offer;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the number of shares so offered by the shareholder
  making the offer;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the price at which each of the shares so offered may
  be purchased or otherwise acquired;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the date of purchase, if any, of each of the shares
  so offered and the number of shares purchased; and

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the date of withdrawal, if any, of the offer and the
  number of shares affected by the withdrawal.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application to Superintendent

**[[232]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-232 .sectionLabel}** A company that holds
binding offers from the holders of at least ninety per cent of each
class of shares for the purchase or other acquisition of those shares
pursuant to a mutualization proposal shall apply to the Superintendent
for approval of the purchase or other acquisition of the shares.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Criteria for approval

**[[233]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-233 .sectionLabel}** The Superintendent
shall approve the purchase or other acquisition of shares pursuant to a
mutualization proposal if the Superintendent is satisfied that

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the purchase or other acquisition of shares would not
  cause the company to be in contravention of subsection 515(1), any
  regulation made under subsection 515(2) or any order made under
  subsection 515(3); and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the stated capital of the shares has, in the opinion
  of the Superintendent, ceased to be an important factor in
  safeguarding the interests of the policyholders of the company, having
  regard to the quality and amount of the assets of the company, the
  surplus of the company relative to its liabilities, the nature of the
  business carried on by the company and any other considerations deemed
  by the Superintendent to be relevant.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 233
- 2007, c. 6, s. 203
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-233-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 233"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of Superintendent's approval

**[[234]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-234 .sectionLabel}** Where the
Superintendent approves the purchase or other acquisition of shares of a
company pursuant to a mutualization proposal, the company

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} shall, within the period set out in the mutualization
  proposal, purchase or otherwise acquire the shares for the purchase or
  other acquisition of which pursuant to the proposal the company holds
  binding offers; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} may acquire the remaining shares in accordance with
  Division X, which applies in respect of that acquisition with such
  modifications as the circumstances require, as if each reference in
  that Division to

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the "offeree company" or the "offeror" were a
    reference to the "company",

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a "dissenting offeree" were a reference to a
    holder of a share of the company who has not offered to sell his or
    her share under the terms of the mutualization proposal,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} an "offeree who accepted the take-over bid" were
    a reference to a holder of a share of the company who has offered to
    sell his or her share under the terms of the mutualization proposal,
    and

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the "date of the take-over bid" or the "date of
    termination of the take-over bid" were a reference to the date on
    which the Superintendent approves the purchase or other acquisition
    of the shares of the company pursuant to a mutualization proposal.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Payment

**[[235]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-235 .sectionLabel}** Notwithstanding
anything in this Act, a company may, with the approval of the
Superintendent, pay for shares purchased or otherwise acquired pursuant
to a mutualization proposal by

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} making a promissory note that is, or issuing debt
  securities that are, payable at a fixed or determinable future time
  not later than ten years after the date of its making or their issue;
  or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} issuing shares that a mutual company may issue.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conversion into mutual company

- **[[236]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-236
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where a company purchases or
  otherwise acquires all of its common shares pursuant to a
  mutualization proposal,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the company shall cancel those shares; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the directors of the company shall apply to the
    Minister for the issue of letters patent to effect the conversion of
    the company into a mutual company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Issue of letters patent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} On receipt of an application referred to in
  subsection (1), the Minister shall issue letters patent to effect the
  conversion of the company into a mutual company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of letters patent

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Letters patent issued pursuant to subsection (2)
  become effective on the day stated in the letters patent.

#### [Conversion into Company with Common Shares]{.HTitleText3} {#h-260484 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

**[[236.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-236.1 .sectionLabel}** The following
definitions apply in sections 237 to 237.2.

[[conversion proposal]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[conversion proposal]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a proposal to
    convert a mutual company into a company with common
    shares. ([proposition de transformation]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[converting company]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[converting company]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} has the meaning given to
    that expression by the regulations. ([société en
    transformation]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[eligible policyholder]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[eligible policyholder]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} has the meaning given
    to that expression by the regulations. ([souscripteur
    admissible]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[letters patent of conversion]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[letters patent of conversion]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means letters
    patent issued under paragraph 237(1)(b). ([lettres patentes de
    transformation]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 1, s. 4
- 2011, c. 15, s. 30
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-236.1-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 236.1"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conversion into company with common
shares

- **[[237]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-237 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  the application of a mutual company made in accordance with the
  regulations, the Minister may, on the recommendation of the
  Superintendent,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} approve a conversion proposal; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} issue letters patent of conversion to effect the
    conversion proposal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Special meeting of eligible
  policyholders

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} Before an application is made under subsection (1),
  the directors of the company must call a special meeting of eligible
  policyholders to obtain

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} approval of the conversion proposal;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} confirmation of any by-law or of any amendment to
    or repeal of a by-law that is necessary to implement the conversion
    proposal; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} authorization to make the application.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of meeting and policyholder list

  [(1.2)]{.lawlabel} A company shall, in respect of a special meeting,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} send, not less than 45 days and not more than 75
    days before the meeting, to each eligible policyholder a notice of
    the time and place of the meeting, describing the conversion
    proposal in sufficient detail to permit a policyholder to form a
    reasoned judgment about the terms of the proposal and its impact on
    both policyholders and the company, together with the prescribed
    information in respect of the conversion proposal; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} prepare, not less than 45 days before the meeting,
    a list, which may be in electronic form, of all eligible
    policyholders.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application of subsection 149(5)

  [(1.3)]{.lawlabel} Subsection 149(5) applies, with any modifications
  that the circumstances require, in respect of the list of eligible
  policyholders.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Entitlement to notice and right to vote

  [(1.4)]{.lawlabel} Only eligible policyholders are entitled to notice
  of and to vote at a special meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Special resolution

  [(1.5)]{.lawlabel} Any approval, confirmation or authorization
  referred to in subsection (1.1) must be given by special resolution of
  the eligible policyholders.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council may make regulations

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} respecting the application referred to in
    subsection (1), including the form of the application and the
    information to be contained in the application, and authorizing the
    Superintendent to require additional information in order to make a
    recommendation;

  - [(a.01)]{.lawlabel} respecting the process that precedes the calling
    of a special meeting under subsection (1.1), including the
    development of a conversion proposal, and respecting the calling of
    that meeting;

  - [(a.1)]{.lawlabel} respecting the conversion proposal, including the
    information to be contained in the conversion proposal, and
    authorizing the Superintendent to approve the measures to be taken
    by the converting company in respect of any proposed amendment to
    the conversion proposal;

  - [(a.2)]{.lawlabel} respecting the value of a converting company for
    the purposes of the regulations and authorizing the Superintendent
    to specify a day at which the value shall be estimated by the
    converting company;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} concerning the fair and equitable treatment of
    policyholders under a conversion proposal;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} governing the ownership of shares issued by a
    mutual company that has been converted into a company with common
    shares, including limiting the circumstances in which the Minister
    may give approval under subsection 407(1);

  - [(c.1)]{.lawlabel} respecting the authorization by the
    Superintendent of the sending of a notice of a special meeting
    referred to in subsection (1.1), including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} prescribing the information to be submitted by
      the converting company in support of an authorization,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} authorizing the Superintendent to consider
      information in addition to that referred to in subparagraph (i),
      and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} authorizing the Superintendent to require that
      information, in addition to the prescribed information referred to
      in paragraph (1.2)(a), be sent with a notice;

  - [(c.2)]{.lawlabel} authorizing the Superintendent to

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} require the converting company to hold one or
      more information sessions for eligible policyholders and to take
      other measures to assist eligible policyholders in forming a
      reasoned judgment on the conversion proposal, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} set the rules under which the information
      sessions must be held;

  - [(c.3)]{.lawlabel} respecting restrictions on any fee, compensation
    or other consideration that may be paid, in respect of the
    conversion of a mutual company into a company with common shares, to
    any director, officer or employee of the company or to any entity
    with which a director, officer or employee of the company is
    associated;

  - [(c.4)]{.lawlabel} prohibiting, during the period set out in the
    regulations, the issuance or provision of shares, share options or
    rights to acquire shares, of a company that has been converted from
    a mutual company into a company with common shares to

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} any director, officer or employee of the company,
      or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} any person who was a director, officer or
      employee of the company during the year preceding the effective
      date of conversion of the company; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} generally, respecting the conversion of a mutual
    company into a company with common shares.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations made under paragraph
  (2)(a.01)

  [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} Regulations made under paragraph (2)(a.01) may
  provide for court intervention in the process referred to in that
  paragraph, including the circumstances in which the court is to be
  seized of any matter in relation to that process, and may govern the
  court's powers and procedures in that regard. They may also govern
  authorizations by the Superintendent in respect of notices to be sent
  in the context of that process.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exemption by Superintendent

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A regulation made under subsection (2) may provide
  that the Superintendent may, on such terms and conditions as the
  Superintendent considers appropriate, exempt a company from prescribed
  requirements of that regulation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exemption by Minister

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may, on such terms and conditions as the
  Minister considers appropriate, exempt a company from any requirement
  of this Act or the regulations if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the company is a mutual company applying for the
    approval of a proposal to convert the company into a company with
    common shares; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the Minister is of the opinion that the company is,
    or is about to be, in financial difficulty and that the exemption
    would help to facilitate an improvement in the financial condition
    of the company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 237
- 1994, c. 26, s. 38(E)
- 1997, c. 15, s. 215
- 1999, c. 1, s. 5
- 2014, c. 20, s. 211
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-237-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 237"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of letters patent of conversion

- **[[237.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-237.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Letters patent of conversion become
  effective on the day stated in the letters patent of conversion, and
  on that day

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the company ceases to be a mutual company; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the policyholders of the company cease to have any
    rights with respect to or any interest in the company as a mutual
    company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Consideration for shares

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection 69(1) and section 70,
  shares issued by a company under a conversion proposal are deemed to
  be fully paid for in money and the amount of consideration received by
  the company for those shares is deemed to be equal to the book value
  of the company immediately after the effective date of its conversion,
  determined in accordance with the accounting principles referred to in
  subsection 331(4) and calculated without taking into account any
  amounts remaining at that time in the participating accounts that the
  company maintains under section 456.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 216
- 1999, c. 1, s. 6
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Distribution prohibited

- **[[237.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-237.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A mutual company shall not take any
  action or series of actions directed toward the distribution of all or
  part of its property to its policyholders or shareholders or the
  provision of any other benefit to its policyholders or shareholders,
  other than as provided in subsections 237(1) to (1.2), until a
  conversion proposal has been approved by the Minister under subsection
  237(1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Nothing in subsection (1) prevents

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the directors of the company from declaring a
    dividend on shares or a policy dividend, bonus or other benefit
    payable to policyholders in the ordinary course of business; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the company from paying or otherwise satisfying a
    dividend, bonus or other benefit referred to in paragraph (a).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Non-application

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} This section does not apply to a company that is
  insolvent within the meaning of the [Winding-up and Restructuring
  Act](/eng/acts/W-11).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2011, c. 15, s. 31
:::

#### [Amendments --- By-laws]{.HTitleText3} {#h-260563 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-laws

- **[[238]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-238 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  directors of a company may make, amend or repeal any by-laws, in the
  manner set out in subsections (2) and (3) and sections 239 to 244, to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} change the maximum number, if any, of shares of any
    class that the company is authorized to issue;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} create new classes of shares;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} change the designation of any or all of the
    company's shares, and add, change or remove any rights, privileges,
    restrictions and conditions, including rights to accrued dividends,
    in respect of any or all of the company's shares, whether issued or
    unissued;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} change the shares of any class or series, whether
    issued or unissued, into a different number of shares of the same
    class or series or into the same or a different number of shares of
    other classes or series;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} divide a class of shares, whether issued or
    unissued, into series and fix the maximum number of shares, if any,
    in each series and the rights, privileges, restrictions and
    conditions attached thereto;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} authorize the directors to divide any class of
    unissued shares into series and fix the maximum number of shares, if
    any, in each series and the rights, privileges, restrictions and
    conditions attached thereto;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} authorize the directors to change the rights,
    privileges, restrictions and conditions attached to unissued shares
    of any series;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} revoke, diminish or enlarge any authority conferred
    under paragraphs (f) and (g);

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} change the rights of policyholders to vote at
    meetings of shareholders or policyholders, subject to subsection
    153(1);

  - [(i.1)]{.lawlabel} change the name of the company;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} increase or decrease the number of directors, the
    minimum or maximum number of directors, the number of directors who
    are to be elected by the shareholders or the number of directors who
    are to be elected by the policyholders, subject to subsections
    167(1) and 173(4) and (4.1) and section 176; or

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} change the province in which the head office of the
    company is situated.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholder or policyholder approval

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The directors shall submit a by-law, or an amendment
  to or a repeal of a by-law, that is made under subsection (1) to the
  shareholders and policyholders entitled to vote, and the shareholders
  and policyholders may, by special resolution, confirm, amend or reject
  the by-law, amendment or repeal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Right to vote

  [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} The by-laws of a company may provide that each
  participating share, as defined in section 83.01, of a mutual company
  carries the right to vote on a proposed addition or amendment to the
  by-laws to do anything referred to in any of paragraphs (1)(a) to
  (h), (j) and (k). Where that right is provided for in the by-laws,
  each of those shares carries that right even if they do not otherwise
  carry the right to vote.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Separate vote

  [(2.2)]{.lawlabel} The holders of shares who are entitled under
  subsection (2.1) to vote on a proposed addition or amendment referred
  to in that subsection are entitled to vote on it separately from
  policyholders.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effective date of by-law

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A by-law, or an amendment to or a repeal of a by-law,
  made under subsection (1) is not effective until it is confirmed or
  confirmed as amended by the shareholders and policyholders under
  subsection (2) and, in the case of a by-law respecting a change to the
  name of the company, approved by the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Letters patent

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the name of a company or the province in Canada in
  which the head office of the company is situated is changed under this
  section, the Superintendent may issue letters patent to amend the
  company's incorporating instrument accordingly.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of letters patent

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Letters patent issued under subsection (4) become
  effective on the day stated in the letters patent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 238
- 1997, c. 15, s. 217
- 2001, c. 9, s. 388
- 2005, c. 54, s. 260
- 2007, c. 6, s. 204
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-238-20060427.html "Link to previous version of section 238"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Class vote

- **[[239]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-239 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  holders of shares of a class or, subject to subsection (2), of a
  series are, unless the by-laws otherwise provide in the case of an
  amendment to the by-laws referred to in paragraph (a), (b) or (e),
  entitled to vote separately as a class or series on a proposal to
  amend the by-laws to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} increase or decrease any maximum number of
    authorized shares of that class, or increase any maximum number of
    authorized shares of a class having rights or privileges equal or
    superior to the shares of that class;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} effect an exchange, reclassification or
    cancellation of all or part of the shares of that class;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} add, change or remove the rights, privileges,
    restrictions or conditions attached to the shares of that class and,
    without limiting the generality of the foregoing,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} remove or change prejudicially rights to accrued
      dividends or rights to cumulative dividends,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} add, remove or change prejudicially redemption
      rights,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} reduce or remove a dividend preference or a
      liquidation preference, or

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} add, remove or change prejudicially conversion
      privileges, options, voting, transfer or pre-emptive rights, or
      rights to acquire securities of the company, or sinking fund
      provisions;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} increase the rights or privileges of any class of
    shares having rights or privileges equal or superior to the shares
    of that class;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} create a new class of shares equal or superior to
    the shares of that class;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} make any class of shares having rights or
    privileges inferior to the shares of that class equal or superior to
    the shares of that class; or

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} effect an exchange or create a right of exchange of
    all or part of the shares of another class into the shares of that
    class.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Right limited

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The holders of a series of shares of a class are
  entitled to vote separately as a series under subsection (1) if that
  series is affected by an addition or amendment to the by-laws in a
  manner different from other shares of the same class.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Right to vote

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subsections (1) and (2) apply whether or not the
  shares of a class otherwise carry the right to vote.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Participating policyholder vote

- **[[240]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-240
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Participating policyholders are
  entitled to vote separately on a proposal to amend the by-laws to add
  to, change or remove the rights of policyholders, other than
  participating policyholders, to vote at meetings of shareholders or
  policyholders.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Policyholder vote

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Policyholders who are entitled to vote, other than
  participating policyholders, are entitled to vote separately on a
  proposal to amend the by-laws to add to, change or remove the rights
  of policyholders, other than participating policyholders, to vote at
  meetings of shareholders or policyholders.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Right limited

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The holders of a class of non-participating policies
  who are entitled to vote are entitled to vote separately as a class if
  the right to vote attached to policies of that class is added to,
  changed or removed by an addition or amendment to the by-laws in a
  manner different from the right to vote attached to other
  non-participating policies.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Separate resolutions

- **[[241]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-241 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  proposed addition or amendment to the by-laws referred to in
  subsection 239(1) is adopted when the holders of the shares of each
  class or series entitled to vote separately thereon as a class or
  series and the policyholders have approved the addition or amendment
  by a special resolution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Idem

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A proposed addition or amendment to the by-laws
  referred to in section 240 is adopted when the participating
  policyholders, the non-participating policyholders who are entitled to
  vote and the holders of each class of non-participating policies
  entitled to vote separately thereon as a class and the shareholders
  have approved the addition or amendment by a special resolution.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Revoking resolution

**[[242]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-242 .sectionLabel}** Where a special
resolution referred to in subsection 238(2) so states, the directors
may, without further approval of the shareholders or policyholders,
revoke the special resolution.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proposal to amend

- **[[243]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-243
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), a
  director or a shareholder or policyholder who is entitled to vote at
  an annual meeting of shareholders and policyholders of a company may,
  in accordance with sections 147 and 148, make a proposal to make an
  application referred to in section 224 or to make, amend or repeal the
  by-laws referred to in subsection 238(1) of the company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of amendment

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Notice of a meeting of shareholders or policyholders
  at which a proposal to amend the incorporating instrument or to make,
  amend or repeal the by-laws of a company to effect any of the changes
  referred to in subsection 238(1) is to be considered must set out the
  proposal.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 243
- 2001, c. 9, s. 389
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Rights preserved

**[[244]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-244 .sectionLabel}** No amendment to the
incorporating instrument or by-laws of a company affects an existing
cause of action or claim or liability to prosecution in favour of or
against the company or its directors or officers, or any civil, criminal
or administrative action or proceeding to which the company or any of
its directors or officers are a party.

#### [Amalgamation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-260634 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application to amalgamate

- **[[245]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-245 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  the joint application of two or more bodies corporate, incorporated by
  or under an Act of Parliament, including companies and insurance
  holding companies but not including federal credit unions, the
  Minister may issue letters patent amalgamating and continuing the
  applicants as one mutual company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application to amalgamate

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} On the joint application of two or more bodies
  corporate incorporated by or under an Act of Parliament, including
  companies --- other than mutual companies --- and insurance holding
  companies but not including federal credit unions, the Minister may
  issue letters patent amalgamating and continuing the applicants as one
  company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application to amalgamate societies

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} On the joint application of two or more societies,
  the Minister may issue letters patent amalgamating and continuing the
  applicants as one society.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 245
- 1997, c. 15, s. 218
- 2001, c. 9, s. 390
- 2010, c. 12, s. 2119
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-245-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 245"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Amalgamation agreement

- **[[246]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-246 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Each
  applicant proposing to amalgamate shall enter into an amalgamation
  agreement.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents of agreement --- company

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Every amalgamation agreement for an amalgamation to
  which subsection 245(1) or (2) applies shall set out the terms and
  means of effecting the amalgamation and, in particular,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name of the amalgamated company and the
    province in which its head office is to be situated;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} whether the amalgamated company is to be a mutual
    company or a company with common shares;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the name and place of ordinary residence of each
    proposed director of the amalgamated company;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the manner in which any shares of each applicant
    are to be converted into shares or other securities of the
    amalgamated company;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} if any shares of an applicant are not to be
    converted into shares or other securities of the amalgamated
    company, the amount of money or securities that the holders of those
    shares are to receive in addition to or in lieu of shares or other
    securities of the amalgamated company;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the manner of payment of money in lieu of the issue
    of fractional shares of the amalgamated company or of any other body
    corporate that are to be issued in the amalgamation;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the proposed by-laws of the amalgamated company;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} details of any other matter necessary to perfect
    the amalgamation and to provide for the subsequent management and
    operation of the amalgamated company; and

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the proposed effective date of the amalgamation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents of agreement --- society

  [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} Every amalgamation agreement for an amalgamation to
  which subsection 245(3) applies shall set out the terms and means of
  effecting the amalgamation and, in particular,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name of the amalgamated society and the
    province in which its head office is to be situated;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name and place of ordinary residence of each
    proposed director of the amalgamated society;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the proposed by-laws of the amalgamated society;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} details of any other matter necessary to perfect
    the amalgamation and to provide for the subsequent management and
    operation of the amalgamated society; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the proposed effective date of the amalgamation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Cross ownership of shares

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If shares of one of the applicants are held by or on
  behalf of another of the applicants, other than shares held in the
  capacity of a personal representative or by way of security, the
  amalgamation agreement must provide for the cancellation of those
  shares when the amalgamation becomes effective without any repayment
  of capital in respect thereof, and no provision shall be made in the
  agreement for the conversion of those shares into shares of the
  amalgamated company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 246
- 1997, c. 15, s. 219
- 2005, c. 54, s. 261
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-246-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 246"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Approval of agreement by Superintendent

- **[[247]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-247 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  amalgamation agreement must be submitted to the Superintendent for
  approval and any approval of the agreement under subsection 248(5) by
  the shareholders, policyholders or members of an applicant is invalid
  unless, before the date of the approval, the Superintendent has
  approved the agreement in writing.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report of independent actuary

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An amalgamation agreement submitted to the
  Superintendent for approval must be accompanied by the report of an
  independent actuary on the agreement.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 247
- 1997, c. 15, s. 220(E)
- 2007, c. 6, s. 205
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-247-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 247"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Approval by shareholders, policyholders
and members

- **[[248]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-248 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  directors of each applicant shall submit an amalgamation agreement for
  approval

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} to a meeting of the shareholders and policyholders
    entitled to vote of the applicant company of which they are
    directors and to the holders of each class or series of shares;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} to a meeting of the shareholders of the body
    corporate of which they are directors and to the holders of each
    class or series of shares; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} to a meeting of the members of the applicant
    society of which they are directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Right to vote

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Each share of an applicant carries the right to vote
  in respect of an amalgamation agreement whether or not it otherwise
  carries the right to vote.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Separate vote for class or series

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The holders of shares of a class or series of shares
  of each applicant are entitled to vote separately as a class or series
  in respect of an amalgamation agreement if the agreement contains a
  provision that, if it were contained in a proposed amendment to the
  by-laws or incorporating instrument of the applicant, would entitle
  those holders to vote separately as a class or series.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Policyholder vote

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Policyholders who are entitled to vote are entitled
  to vote separately from shareholders in respect of an amalgamation
  agreement.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Special resolution

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (3) and (4), an amalgamation
  agreement is approved when it has been approved by special resolution
  by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the shareholders and the policyholders who are
    entitled to vote of each applicant company;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the shareholders of each applicant body corporate;
    and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the members of each applicant society.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Termination

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} An amalgamation agreement may provide that, at any
  time before the issue of letters patent of amalgamation, the agreement
  may be terminated by the directors of an applicant even though the
  agreement has been approved by the shareholders, policyholders or
  members of all or any of the applicant companies, bodies corporate or
  societies.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 248
- 1997, c. 15, s. 221
- 2005, c. 54, s. 262
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-248-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 248"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Vertical short-form amalgamation

- **[[249]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-249 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  company that does not have any participating policyholders may,
  without complying with sections 246 to 248, amalgamate with one or
  more bodies corporate that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} are incorporated by or under an Act of Parliament,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} are wholly-owned subsidiaries of the company, and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} do not have any participating policyholders

  if

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the amalgamation is approved by a resolution of the
    directors of the company and of each amalgamating subsidiary, and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the resolutions provide that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the shares of each amalgamating subsidiary will
      be cancelled without any repayment of capital in respect thereof,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the letters patent of amalgamation and the
      by-laws of the amalgamated company will be the same as the
      incorporating instrument and the by-laws of the amalgamating
      company that is the holding body corporate, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} no securities will be issued by the amalgamated
      company in connection with the amalgamation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Horizontal short-form amalgamation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Two or more bodies corporate that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} are incorporated by or under an Act of Parliament,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} are wholly-owned subsidiaries of the same holding
    body corporate, and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} do not have any participating policyholders

  may amalgamate and continue as one company without complying with
  sections 246 to 248 if

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} at least one of the applicants is a company,

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the amalgamation is approved by a resolution of the
    directors of each of the applicants, and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the resolutions provide that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the shares of all applicants, except those of one
      of the applicants that is a company, will be cancelled without any
      repayment of capital in respect thereof,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the letters patent of amalgamation and the
      by-laws of the amalgamated company will be the same as the
      incorporating instrument and the by-laws of the amalgamating
      company whose shares are not cancelled, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the stated capital of the amalgamating
      companies and bodies corporate whose shares are cancelled will be
      added to the stated capital of the amalgamating company whose
      shares are not cancelled.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 249
- 2005, c. 54, s. 263
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-249-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 249"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Joint application to Minister

- **[[250]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-250
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), unless an
  amalgamation agreement is terminated in accordance with subsection
  248(6), the applicants shall, within three months after the approval
  of the agreement in accordance with subsection 248(5) or the approval
  of the directors in accordance with subsection 249(1) or (2), jointly
  apply to the Minister for letters patent of amalgamation continuing
  the applicants as one company or society.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conditions precedent to application

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No application for the issue of letters patent under
  subsection (1) may be made unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} notice of intention to make such an application has
    been published at least once a week for a period of four consecutive
    weeks in the [Canada Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) and in a
    newspaper in general circulation at or near the place where the head
    office of each applicant is situated; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the application is supported by satisfactory
    evidence that the applicants have complied with the requirements of
    this Part relating to amalgamations.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application of sections 23 to 26

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If two or more bodies corporate, none of which is a
  company or society, apply for letters patent under subsection (1),
  sections 23 to 26 apply in respect of the application with any
  modifications that the circumstances require.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Matters for consideration

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Before issuing letters patent of amalgamation
  continuing the applicants as one company or society, the Minister
  shall take into account all matters that the Minister considers
  relevant to the application, including

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the sources of continuing financial support for the
    amalgamated company or society;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the soundness and feasibility of the plans of the
    applicants for the future conduct and development of the business of
    the amalgamated company or society;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the business record and experience of the
    applicants;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the reputation of the applicants for being operated
    in a manner that is consistent with the standards of good character
    and integrity;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} whether the amalgamated company or society will be
    operated responsibly by persons with the competence and experience
    suitable for involvement in the operation of a financial
    institution;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the impact of any integration of the operations and
    businesses of the applicants on the conduct of those operations and
    businesses;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} if one of the applicants is a converted company in
    respect of which the Minister has issued an order under subsection
    407(8) or a converted company in respect of which subsection 407(11)
    applied at any time, or a body corporate that controls, within the
    meaning of paragraph 3(1)(d), such a company, the opinion of the
    Superintendent regarding the extent to which the proposed corporate
    structure of the amalgamated company and its affiliates may affect
    the supervision and regulation of the amalgamated company, having
    regard to

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the nature and extent of the proposed financial
      services activities to be carried out by the amalgamated company
      and its affiliates, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the nature and degree of supervision and
      regulation applying to the proposed financial services activities
      to be carried out by the affiliates of the amalgamated company;
      and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the best interests of the financial system in
    Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may not, before January 1, 2002, issue
  letters patent under section 251 amalgamating a converted company in
  respect of which subsection 407(4) or (11) applies, a company to which
  subsection 407(5) or (12) applies or an insurance holding company to
  which subsection 407(6) or (13) applies with any other body corporate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} If one of the applicants for letters patent of
  amalgamation is a converted company in respect of which subsection
  407(4) applies, or a company to which subsection 407(5) applies or an
  insurance holding company to which subsection 407(6) applies, the
  Minister may not issue the letters patent of amalgamation unless the
  amalgamated company is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} widely held; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} controlled, within the meaning of paragraph
    3(1)(d), by a company to which subsection 407(5) applies, or by an
    insurance holding company to which subsection 407(6) applies, that
    controlled one of the applicants at the time the application was
    made.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deeming

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} If one of the applicants for letters patent of
  amalgamation is a converted company in respect of which subsection
  407(4) applies, a company to which subsection 407(5) applies or an
  insurance holding company to which subsection 407(6) applies and the
  letters patent of amalgamation are issued, the amalgamated company is
  deemed to be a converted company in respect of which subsection 407(4)
  applies or a company to which subsection 407(5) applies, as the case
  may be.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 250
- 1997, c. 15, s. 222
- 2001, c. 9, s. 391
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Issue of letters patent

- **[[251]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-251
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where an application has been made
  to the Minister in accordance with section 250, the Minister may issue
  letters patent of amalgamation continuing the applicants as one
  company or society.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Letters patent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where letters patent are issued pursuant to this
  section, section 28 applies with such modifications as the
  circumstances require in respect of the issue of the letters patent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication of notice

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent shall cause to be published in the
  [Canada Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) notice of the issuance of
  letters patent pursuant to subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 251
- 1997, c. 15, s. 223
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Court enforcement

- **[[251.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-251.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a company or society, or any
  director, officer, employee or agent of a company or society, is
  contravening or has failed to comply with any term or condition made
  in respect of the issuance of letters patent of amalgamation, the
  Minister may, in addition to any other action that may be taken under
  this Act, apply to a court for an order directing the company or
  society, or the director, officer, employee or agent, to comply with
  the term or condition, cease the contravention or do any thing that is
  required to be done, and on the application the court may so order and
  make any other order it thinks fit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appeal

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An appeal from an order of a court under this section
  lies in the same manner as, and to the same court to which, an appeal
  may be taken from any other order of the court.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 392
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of letters patent

- **[[252]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-252 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  the day provided for in the letters patent issued under section 251

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the amalgamation of the applicants and their
    continuance as one company or society becomes effective;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the property of each applicant continues to be the
    property of the amalgamated company or society;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the amalgamated company or society continues to be
    liable for the obligations of each applicant;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} any existing cause of action, claim or liability to
    prosecution is unaffected;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} any civil, criminal or administrative action or
    proceeding pending by or against an applicant may be continued to be
    prosecuted by or against the amalgamated company or society;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} any conviction against, or ruling, order or
    judgment in favour of or against, an applicant may be enforced by or
    against the amalgamated company or society;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} if any director or officer of an applicant
    continues as a director or officer of the amalgamated company, any
    disclosure by that director or officer of a material interest in any
    contract made to the applicant shall be deemed to be disclosure to
    the amalgamated company; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the letters patent of amalgamation are the
    incorporating instrument of the amalgamated company or society.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Minutes

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Any deemed disclosure under paragraph (1)(g) shall be
  recorded in the minutes of the first meeting of directors of the
  amalgamated company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 252
- 1997, c. 15, s. 224
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transitional

- **[[253]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-253
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Notwithstanding any other provision
  of this Act or the regulations, the Minister may, by order, on the
  recommendation of the Superintendent, grant to a company or society in
  respect of which letters patent were issued under subsection 251(1)
  permission to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} engage in a business activity specified in the
    order that the company or society would not otherwise be permitted
    by this Act to engage in and that one or more of the amalgamating
    bodies corporate was engaging in at the time application for the
    letters patent was made;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} continue to have issued and outstanding debt
    obligations the issue of which is not authorized by this Act if the
    debt obligations were outstanding at the time the application for
    the letters patent was made;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 1994, c. 47, s. 121\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} hold assets that the company or society would not
    otherwise be permitted by this Act to hold, if the assets were held
    by one or more of the amalgamating bodies corporate at the time the
    application for the letters patent was made;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} acquire and hold assets that the company or society
    would not otherwise be permitted by this Act to acquire or hold, if
    one or more of the amalgamating bodies corporate were obliged, at
    the time the application for the letters patent was made, to acquire
    those assets; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} maintain outside Canada any records or registers
    required by this Act to be maintained in Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duration of exceptions

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The permission granted under subsection (1) shall be
  expressed to be granted for a period specified in the order not
  exceeding

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} with respect to any matter described in paragraph
    (1)(a), thirty days after the date of issue of the letters patent
    or, where the activity is conducted pursuant to an agreement
    existing on the date of issue of the letters patent, the expiration
    of the agreement;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} with respect to any matter described in paragraph
    (1)(b), ten years; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} with respect to any matter described in any of
    paragraphs (1)(d) to (f), two years.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Renewal

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), the Minister, on the
  recommendation of the Superintendent, may by order renew a permission
  granted by order under subsection (1) with respect to any matter
  described in any of paragraphs (1)(b) to (e) for any further period or
  periods that the Minister considers necessary.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitation

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall not grant to a company or society
  any permission

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} with respect to matters described in paragraph
    (1)(b), that purports to be effective more than ten years after the
    date of the approval for the company or society to commence and
    carry on business, unless the Minister is satisfied on the basis of
    evidence on oath provided by an officer of the company or society
    that the company or society will not be able at law to redeem at the
    end of the ten years the outstanding debt obligations to which the
    permission relates; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} with respect to matters described in paragraphs
    (1)(d) and (e), that purports to be effective more than ten years
    after the date of issue of the letters patent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 253

- 1997, c. 15, s. 225
- 2007, c. 6, s. 206
:::

#### [Transfer of Business and Reinsurance]{.HTitleText3} {#h-260807 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restricted transactions

- **[[254]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-254
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except in accordance with this
  section or an order made under subsection 678.5(1), a company or
  society shall not

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} cause itself to be reinsured, on an assumption
    basis, against all or any portion of the risks undertaken under its
    policies; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} sell all or substantially all of its assets.

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2007, c. 6, s. 207\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Approval of the Minister

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A company or society may, with the approval of the
  Minister,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} cause itself to be reinsured, on an assumption
    basis, against all or substantially all of the risks undertaken
    under its policies, by one or more of the following entities:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a company or society,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a foreign company that, in Canada, reinsures
      those risks,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a body corporate incorporated or formed by or
      under the laws of a province, if the Superintendent has entered
      into satisfactory arrangements concerning the reinsurance with
      either or both of the body corporate and the appropriate official
      or public body responsible for the supervision of the body
      corporate, or

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} an entity that is authorized to reinsure those
      risks, if the risks were undertaken outside Canada by the company
      or society; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} sell all or substantially all of its assets.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Approval of the Superintendent

  [(2.01)]{.lawlabel} A company or society may, with the approval of the
  Superintendent, cause itself to be reinsured, on an assumption basis,
  against less than substantially all of the risks undertaken under its
  policies, by one or more of the following entities:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a company or society;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a foreign company that, in Canada, reinsures those
    risks;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a body corporate incorporated or formed by or under
    the laws of a province, if the Superintendent has entered into
    satisfactory arrangements concerning the reinsurance with either or
    both of the body corporate and the appropriate official or public
    body responsible for the supervision of the body corporate; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} an entity that is authorized to reinsure those
    risks, if the risks were undertaken outside Canada by the company or
    society.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prescribed transactions

  [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} The approval of the Minister or Superintendent is
  not required for a prescribed transaction or a transaction in a
  prescribed class of transactions.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Procedure

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The company or society must, at least 30 days before
  it applies for the Minister's or Superintendent's approval, publish a
  notice in the [Canada Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) and in a
  newspaper in general circulation at or near the place where the head
  office of the company or society is situated stating the day on or
  after which it will apply.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where a company or society publishes a notice
  referred to in subsection (3), the Superintendent may direct the
  company or society to provide its shareholders, policyholders and
  members with such information as the Superintendent may require.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report of independent actuary

  [(4.1)]{.lawlabel} An application for approval under paragraph (2)(a)
  must, if the Superintendent so requires, be accompanied by the report
  of an independent actuary on the proposed reinsurance agreement.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Inspection

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If a company or society publishes a notice referred
  to in subsection (3), it must make the agreement for the transaction
  that the Minister or Superintendent is asked to approve available at
  its head office for the inspection of its shareholders, policyholders
  and members for at least 30 days after the publication of the notice
  and must provide a copy of the agreement to any shareholder,
  policyholder or member who requests one by writing to the head office
  of the company or society.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Superintendent may shorten periods

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent is of the opinion that it is in
  the best interests of a group of policyholders affected by the
  transaction that the Minister or the Superintendent is asked to
  approve, the Superintendent may shorten the periods of 30 days
  referred to in subsections (3) and (5).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 254
- 1997, c. 15, s. 226
- 2001, c. 9, s. 393
- 2007, c. 6, s. 207
:::

Version](section-254-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 254"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Taking of effect of approval

**[[255]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-255 .sectionLabel}** A transaction referred
to in subsection 254(2) or (2.01) has no effect until it has been
approved by the Minister or the Superintendent, as the case may be.

6, s. 208\]]{.Repealed}

[Previous
Version](section-256-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 256"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholder and policyholder approval

- **[[257]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-257 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  company or society proposing to transfer all or substantially all of
  its policies, to cause itself to be reinsured, on an assumption basis,
  against all or substantially all of the risks undertaken under its
  policies, or to sell all or substantially all of its assets shall
  submit the proposal for approval to a meeting of the shareholders and
  policyholders who are entitled to vote, or to a meeting of members,
  and, subject to subsection (3), to the holders of each class or series
  of shares.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice to Superintendent

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} A company or society proposing to transfer all or
  substantially all of its policies must give notice of the proposal to
  the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information

  [(1.2)]{.lawlabel} After receiving the notice, the Superintendent may
  direct the company or society to provide its shareholders,
  policyholders and members with any information that the Superintendent
  may require.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Right to vote

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Each share of the company carries the right to vote
  in respect of the proposal whether or not the share otherwise carries
  the right to vote.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Class vote

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The holders of shares of a class or series of shares
  of the company are entitled to vote separately as a class or series in
  respect of the proposal if the shares of the class or series are
  affected by the proposed transaction in a manner different from the
  shares of another class or series.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Policyholder vote

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Policyholders who are entitled to vote are entitled
  to vote separately from shareholders in respect of the proposal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Special resolution

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of subsection (1), and subject to
  subsections (3) and (4), the proposal is not approved by the
  shareholders and the policyholders who are entitled to vote or the
  members unless they approve it by special resolution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Abandoning transfer or reinsurance

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Where a special resolution under subsection (5)
  approving a proposed transaction so states, the directors of a company
  or society may, subject to the rights of third parties, abandon the
  transaction without further approval of the shareholders,
  policyholders or members.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application to Minister

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} Except in the case of a transaction to transfer all
  or substantially all of a company's or society's policies, the company
  or society shall, within three months after the approval of the
  transaction in accordance with subsection (5), apply to the Minister
  for approval of the transaction, unless the transaction is abandoned
  in accordance with subsection (6).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}When section does not apply

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} This section does not apply if the transfer or
  reinsurance is made under an order made under subsection 678.5(1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 257
- 1997, c. 15, s. 227
- 2001, c. 9, s. 394
- 2007, c. 6, s. 209
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-257-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 257"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

**[[258]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-258 .sectionLabel}** The Governor in Council
may, for the purposes of section 254 or 257, make regulations respecting
the circumstances in which companies or societies are deemed to be
causing themselves to be reinsured, on an assumption basis, against
risks undertaken under their policies.

### [DIVISION IV]{.HLabel2}[Head Office and Corporate Records]{.HTitleText2} {#h-260875 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Head office

- **[[260]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-260 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  company shall at all times have a head office in the province
  specified in its incorporating instrument or by-laws.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Change of head office

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The directors of a company may change the address of
  the head office within the province specified in the incorporating
  instrument or by-laws.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of change of address

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A company shall send to the Superintendent, within
  fifteen days after any change of address of its head office, a notice
  of the change of address.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 260
- 2005, c. 54, s. 264
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-260-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 260"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Company records

- **[[261]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-261 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  company shall prepare and maintain records containing

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} its incorporating instrument and the by-laws of the
    company and all amendments thereto;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} minutes of meetings and resolutions of shareholders
    or policyholders;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the information referred to in paragraphs
    668(1)(a), (c) and (e) to (h) contained in all returns provided to
    the Superintendent pursuant to section 668;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} particulars of any authorizations, conditions and
    limitations established by the Superintendent under subsection 58(1)
    or (2) or 59(1) that are from time to time applicable to the
    company; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} particulars of exceptions granted under section 38
    or 253 that are from time to time applicable to the company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Additional records

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In addition to the records described in subsection
  (1), a company shall prepare and maintain adequate

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} corporate accounting records;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} records containing minutes of meetings and
    resolutions of the directors and any committee thereof; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} records showing, for each customer of, or claimant
    under a policy issued by, the company, the amount owing to the
    company and the nature of the liabilities of the company to the
    customer or claimant.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Former-Act and continued companies

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of paragraph (1)(b) and subsection
  (2),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a body corporate continued as a
    company under this Act, [[records]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes
    similar records required by law to be maintained by the body
    corporate before it was so continued;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a body corporate amalgamated and
    continued as a company under this Act,
    [[records]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes similar records required by
    law to be maintained by the body corporate before it was so
    amalgamated; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a former-Act company,
    [[records]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes similar records required by
    law to be maintained by the company before the coming into force of
    this section.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 261
- 1997, c. 15, s. 228(E)
- 2007, c. 6, s. 211(E)
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-261-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 261"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Place of records

- **[[262]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-262 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  records described in section 261 shall be kept at the head office of
  the company or at such other place in Canada as the directors think
  fit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of place of records

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where any of the records described in section 261 are
  not kept at the head office of a company, the company shall notify the
  Superintendent of the place where the records are kept.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of records
  of an office of the company outside Canada or in respect of customers
  of such an office.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3.1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection 268(1.1), subsection (1) does
  not apply to a company that is a subsidiary of a regulated foreign
  entity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Inspection

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The records described in section 261, other than
  those described in paragraph 261(2)(c), shall at all reasonable times
  be open to inspection by the directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Access to company records

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A company's shareholders, policyholders entitled to
  vote and creditors and their personal representatives may examine the
  records referred to in subsection 261(1) during the usual business
  hours of the company and may take extracts from them free of charge or
  have copies of them made on payment of a reasonable fee. If the
  company is a distributing company, any other person may on payment of
  a reasonable fee examine those records during the usual business hours
  of the company and take extracts from them or have copies of them
  made.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Electronic access

  [(5.1)]{.lawlabel} A company may make the information contained in
  records referred to in subsection 261(1) available to persons by any
  system of mechanical or electronic data processing or any other
  information storage device that is capable of reproducing the records
  in intelligible written form within a reasonable time.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Copies of by-laws for shareholders

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Every shareholder of a company is entitled, on
  request made not more often than once in each calendar year, to
  receive free of charge one copy of the by-laws of the company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Copies of by-laws for policyholders

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} Every policyholder of a company who is entitled to
  vote at a meeting of policyholders or shareholders and policyholders
  of the company is entitled, on request made not more often than once
  in each calendar year, to receive free of charge one copy of the
  by-laws of the company.

::: HistoricalNote

- 1997, c. 15, s. 229
- 2001, c. 9, s. 395
- 2005, c. 54, s. 265

  role="button"}
:::
