[Previous
Version](section-262-20061128.html "Link to previous version of section 262"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholder lists

- **[[263]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-263 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person who is entitled to a basic list of shareholders of a company
  (in this section referred to as the "applicant") may request the
  company to furnish the applicant with a basic list within ten days
  after receipt by the company of the affidavit referred to in
  subsection (2) and, on payment of a reasonable fee by the applicant,
  the company shall comply with the request.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Affidavit and contents

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A request under subsection (1) must be accompanied by
  an affidavit containing

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the applicant,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name and address for service of the entity, if
    the applicant is an entity, and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} an undertaking that the basic list and any
    supplemental lists obtained pursuant to subsections (5) and (6) will
    not be used except as permitted under section 265,

  and, if the applicant is an entity, the affidavit shall be made by a
  director or an officer of the entity, or any person acting in a
  similar capacity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Entitlement to list

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A company's shareholders, policyholders entitled to
  vote and creditors and their personal representatives are --- or if
  the company is a distributing company, any person is --- entitled to a
  basic list of shareholders of the company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Basic list of shareholders

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A basic list of shareholders of a company consists of
  a list of shareholders that is made up to a date not more than ten
  days before the receipt of the affidavit referred to in subsection (2)
  and that sets out

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the names of the shareholders of the company;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number of shares owned by each shareholder; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the address of each shareholder as shown in the
    records of the company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Supplemental lists

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A person requiring a company to supply a basic list
  of shareholders may, if the person states in the accompanying
  affidavit that supplemental lists are required, request the company or
  its agent, on payment of a reasonable fee, to provide supplemental
  lists of shareholders setting out any changes from the basic list in
  the names and addresses of the shareholders and the number of shares
  owned by each shareholder for each business day following the date to
  which the basic list is made up.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}When supplemental lists to be furnished

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} A company or its agent shall provide a supplemental
  list of shareholders required under subsection (5)

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} within ten days following the date the basic list
    is provided, where the information relates to changes that took
    place prior to that date; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} within ten days following the day to which the
    supplemental list relates, where the information relates to changes
    that took place on or after the date the basic list was provided.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 263
- 2005, c. 54, s. 266
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-263-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 263"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Option holders

**[[264]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-264 .sectionLabel}** A person requiring a
company to supply a basic list or a supplemental list of shareholders
may also require the company to include in that list the name and
address of any known holder of an option or right to acquire shares of
the company.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Use of shareholder list

**[[265]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-265 .sectionLabel}** A list of shareholders
obtained under section 263 shall not be used by any person except in
connection with

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} an effort to influence the voting of shareholders of
  the company;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} an offer to acquire shares of the company; or

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} any other matter relating to the affairs of the
  company.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Form of records

- **[[266]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-266 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  register or other record required or authorized by this Act to be
  prepared and maintained by a company

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} may be in a bound or loose-leaf form or in a
    photographic film form; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} may be entered or recorded by any system of
    mechanical or electronic data processing or any other information
    storage device that is capable of reproducing any required
    information in intelligible written form within a reasonable time.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conversion of records

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Registers and records maintained in one form may be
  converted to any other form.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Destruction of converted records

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Notwithstanding section 269, a company may destroy
  any register or other record referred to in subsection (1) at any time
  after the register or other record has been converted to another form.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Protection of records

**[[267]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-267 .sectionLabel}** A company and its
agents shall take reasonable precautions to

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} prevent loss or destruction of,

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} prevent falsification of entries in,

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} facilitate detection and correction of inaccuracies
  in, and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} ensure that unauthorized persons do not have access
  to or use of information in,

the registers and records required or authorized by this Act to be
prepared and maintained.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Requirement to maintain copies and
process information in Canada

- **[[268]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-268 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  the Superintendent is of the opinion that it is incompatible with the
  fulfilment of the Superintendent's responsibilities under this Act for
  a company to maintain, in another country, copies of records referred
  to in section 261 or of its central securities register or for a
  company to process, in another country, information or data relating
  to the preparation and maintenance of those records or of its central
  securities register --- or if the Superintendent is advised by the
  Minister that, in the opinion of the Minister, it is not in the
  national interest for a company to do any of those activities in
  another country --- the Superintendent shall direct the company to not
  maintain those copies, or to not process the information or data, as
  the case may be, in that other country or to maintain those copies or
  to process the information or data only in Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Direction --- immediate, direct,
  complete and ongoing access

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} Where a company referred to in subsection 262(3.1)
  or 274(3) maintains records referred to in section 261 or the central
  securities register at a place outside Canada, the Superintendent may,
  in the case referred to in paragraph (a), and shall, in the case
  referred to in paragraph (b), by order, direct the company to maintain
  a copy of those records or register at any place in Canada as the
  directors think fit

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the Superintendent is of the opinion that he or
    she does not have immediate, direct, complete and ongoing access to
    those records or register; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the Superintendent is advised by the Minister
    that the Minister is of the opinion that it is not in the national
    interest for the company not to maintain a copy of those records or
    register in Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Company to comply

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A company shall without delay comply with any order
  issued under subsection (1) or (1.1).

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Retention of records

**[[269]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-269 .sectionLabel}** A company shall retain

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the records of the company referred to in subsection
  261(1);

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} any record of the company referred to in paragraph
  261(2)(a) or (b); and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the central securities register referred to in
  subsection 271(1).

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

**[[270]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-270 .sectionLabel}** The Governor in Council
may make regulations respecting the records, papers and documents to be
retained by a company, including the length of time those records,
papers and documents are to be retained, and what constitutes immediate,
direct, complete and ongoing access, for the purpose of paragraph
268(1.1)(a).

### [DIVISION V]{.HLabel2}[Securities Registers]{.HTitleText2} {#h-260985 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Central securities register

- **[[271]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-271 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  company shall maintain a central securities register in which it shall
  record the securities, within the meaning of section 85, issued by it
  in registered form, showing in respect of each class or series of
  securities

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the names, alphabetically arranged, and latest
    known addresses of the persons who are security holders, and the
    names and latest known addresses of the persons who have been
    security holders;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number of securities held by each security
    holder; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the date and particulars of the issue and transfer
    of each security.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Former-Act and continued companies

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), [[central
  securities register]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes similar registers
  required by law to be maintained by a former-Act company or by a body
  corporate continued, or amalgamated and continued, as a company under
  this Act before the continuance, amalgamation or coming into force of
  this section, as the case may be.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Access to central securities register

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A company's shareholders, policyholders entitled to
  vote and creditors and their personal representatives may examine the
  central securities register during the usual business hours of the
  company and may take extracts from it free of charge or have copies of
  it made on payment of a reasonable fee. If the company is a
  distributing company, any other person may on payment of a reasonable
  fee examine the central securities register during the usual business
  hours of the company and take extracts from it or have copies of it
  made.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Electronic access

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The company may make the information contained in the
  central securities register available by any mechanical or electronic
  data processing system or other information storage device that is
  capable of reproducing it in intelligible written form within a
  reasonable time.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Affidavit and undertaking

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A person who wishes to examine the central securities
  register, take extracts from it or have copies of it made shall
  provide the company with an affidavit containing their name and
  address --- or if they are an entity, the name and address for service
  of the entity --- and with an undertaking that the information
  contained in the register will not be used except in the same way as a
  list of shareholders may be used under section 265. In the case of an
  entity, the affidavit is to be sworn by a director or officer of the
  entity or a person acting in a similar capacity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Supplementary information

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} A person who wishes to examine a central securities
  register, take extracts from it or have copies of it made may on
  payment of a reasonable fee, if they state in the accompanying
  affidavit that supplementary information is required, request the
  company or its agent to provide supplementary information setting out
  any changes made to the register.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}When supplementary information to be
  provided

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} A company or its agent shall provide the
  supplementary information within

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 10 days after the day on which the central
    securities register is examined if the changes take place before
    that day; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 10 days after the day to which the supplementary
    information relates if the changes take place on or after the day on
    which the central securities register is examined.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 271
- 2001, c. 9, s. 397
- 2005, c. 54, s. 268
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-271-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 271"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Branch registers

**[[272]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-272 .sectionLabel}** A company may establish
as many branch securities registers as it considers necessary.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Agents

**[[273]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-273 .sectionLabel}** A company may appoint
an agent to maintain its central securities register and each of its
branch securities registers.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Location of central securities register

- **[[274]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-274 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  central securities register of a company shall be maintained by the
  company at its head office or at any other place in Canada designated
  by the directors of the company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Location of branch securities register

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A branch securities register of a company may be kept
  at any place in or outside Canada designated by the directors of the
  company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection 268(1.1), subsection (1) does
  not apply to a company that is a subsidiary of a regulated foreign
  entity.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 274
- [2020, c. 1, s. 175](#1238255-1311957){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1238255-1311957.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-274-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 274"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of registration

**[[275]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-275 .sectionLabel}** Registration of the
issue or transfer of a security in the central securities register or in
a branch securities register is complete and valid registration for all
purposes.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Particulars in branch register

- **[[276]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-276 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  branch securities register shall only contain particulars of the
  securities issued or transferred at the branch for which that register
  is established.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Particulars in central securities
  register

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Particulars of each issue or transfer of a security
  registered in a branch securities register of a company shall also be
  kept in the central securities register of the company.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Destruction of certificates

**[[277]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-277 .sectionLabel}** A company, its agent or
a trustee within the meaning of section 317 is not required to produce

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a cancelled security certificate in registered form
  or an instrument referred to in subsection 73(1) that is cancelled or
  a like cancelled instrument in registered form after six years from
  the date of its cancellation;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a cancelled security certificate in bearer form or an
  instrument referred to in subsection 73(1) that is cancelled or a like
  cancelled instrument in bearer form after the date of its
  cancellation; or

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} an instrument referred to in subsection 73(1) or a
  like instrument, irrespective of its form, after the date of its
  expiration.

### [DIVISION VI]{.HLabel2}[Corporate Name and Seal]{.HTitleText2} {#h-261029 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication of name

**[[278]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-278 .sectionLabel}** A company shall set out
its name in legible characters in all contracts, premium notices,
applications for policies, policies, negotiable instruments and other
documents evidencing rights or obligations with respect to other parties
that are issued or made by or on behalf of the company.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Corporate seal

- **[[279]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-279 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  company may adopt a corporate seal and change one that it adopted.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Validity of unsealed documents

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A document executed on behalf of a company is not
  invalid merely because a corporate seal is not affixed to it.

- 2005, c. 54, s. 269
:::

### [DIVISION VII]{.HLabel2}[\[Repealed, 1997, c. 15, s. 230\]]{.HTitleText2} {#h-261039 .Subheading}

### [DIVISION VIII]{.HLabel2}[Insiders]{.HTitleText2} {#h-261040 .Subheading}

#### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-261041 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

- **[[288]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-288 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In
  this Division,

  [[affiliate]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[affiliate]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a body corporate that is
      affiliated with another body corporate within the meaning of
      subsection 6(2); ([groupe]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[business combination]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[business combination]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an acquisition
      of all or substantially all of the assets of one body corporate by
      another, an amalgamation of two or more bodies corporate or any
      similar reorganization between two or more bodies
      corporate; ([regroupement d'entreprises]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[call]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[call]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an option, transferable by
      delivery, to demand delivery of a specified number or amount of
      shares at a fixed price within a specified time but does not
      include an option or right to acquire shares of the body corporate
      that granted the option or right to acquire; ([option
      d'achat]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[distributing company]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[distributing company]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed, 2005, c.
      54, s. 270\]]{.Repealed}

  [[insider]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[insider]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed, 2005, c. 54, s.
      270\]]{.Repealed}

  [[officer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[officer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, in relation to a company, means

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an officer as defined in paragraph (a) of the
        definition [[officer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} in section 2, or

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any natural person who performs functions for
        the company similar to those performed by a person referred to
        in paragraph (a) of the definition
        [[officer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} in section 2; ([dirigeant d'une
        société]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[put]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[put]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an option, transferable by
      delivery, to deliver a specified number or amount of shares at a
      fixed price within a specified time; ([option de
      vente]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[share]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[share]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a voting share and includes

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a security currently convertible into a voting
        share, and

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a currently exercisable option or a right to
        acquire a voting share or a security referred to in paragraph
        (a). ([action]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Control

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Division, a person controls
  a body corporate where the person controls the body corporate within
  the meaning of section 3, determined without regard to paragraph
  3(1)(d).

- [(3) and (4)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2005, c. 54, s.
  270\]]{.Repealed}

#### [Insider Reporting]{.HTitleText3} {#h-261062 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Insider report

**[[289]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-289 .sectionLabel}** An insider shall submit
an insider report in accordance with the regulations.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exemption by Superintendent

**[[290]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-290 .sectionLabel}** On application by an
insider, the Superintendent may in writing and on any terms that the
Superintendent thinks fit exempt the insider from any of the
requirements of section 289. The exemption may be given retroactive

exemption and the reasons for it in a periodical available to the
public.

**[[291]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-291 .sectionLabel}** The Governor in Council
may make regulations for carrying out the purposes of sections 289 and
290, including

  and 290;

#### [Insider Trading]{.HTitleText3} {#h-261080 .Subheading}

Meaning of [[insider]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

- **[[293]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-293 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In
  this section, [[insider]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means with respect to a
  distributing company

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a director or officer of the company;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a director or officer of a subsidiary of the
    company;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a director or officer of a body corporate that
    enters into a business combination with the company; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a person employed or retained by the company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- short sale

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No insider may knowingly sell, directly or
  indirectly, a security of a distributing company or of any of the
  distributing company's affiliates if the insider does not own or has
  not fully paid for the security.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (2), an insider may sell a
  security that they do not own if they own another security that is
  convertible into the security that was sold or they own an option or
  right to acquire the security that was sold, and if within 10 days
  after the sale they

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} exercise the conversion privilege, option or right
    and deliver the security so acquired to the purchaser; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} transfer the convertible security, option or right
    to the purchaser.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition --- calls and puts

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} No insider may knowingly, directly or indirectly, buy
  or sell a call or put in respect of a security of a company or of any
  of the company's affiliates.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 293
- 2005, c. 54, s. 272
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-293-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 293"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Civil remedies]{.HTitleText3} {#h-261098 .Subheading}

Extended meaning of [[insider]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

- **[[294]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-294 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In
  this section and sections 294.1 and 295,
  [[insider]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} with respect to a company means

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the company;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an affiliate of the company;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a director or officer of the company or of any
    person described in paragraph (b), (d) or (f);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a person who beneficially owns directly or
    indirectly, or who exercises control or direction over or has a
    combination of ownership, control and direction in respect of,
    shares of the company carrying more than the prescribed percentage
    of the voting rights attached to all of the company's outstanding
    shares not including shares held by the person as underwriter while
    those shares are in the course of a distribution to the public;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a person, other than a person described in
    paragraph (f), who is employed or retained by the company or by a
    person described in paragraph (f);

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a person who engages in or proposes to engage in
    any business or professional activity with or on behalf of the
    company;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a person who received material confidential
    information concerning the company while they were a person
    described in any of paragraphs (a) to (f);

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} a person who receives material confidential
    information from a person who is and who they know or ought
    reasonably to have known is a person described in this subsection,
    including in this paragraph, or subsection (3) or (4); or

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a prescribed person.

- Extended meaning of [[security]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section, each of the
  following is deemed to be a security of a company:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a put, call, option or other right or obligation to
    purchase or sell a security of the company; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a security of another entity, the market price of
    which varies materially with the market price of the securities of
    the company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed insider --- take-over bid or
  business combination

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section and subsection
  294.1(1), a person who proposes to make a take-over bid as defined in
  the regulations for securities of a company or to enter into a
  business combination with a company is an insider of the company with
  respect to material confidential information obtained from the
  company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed insider --- affiliate or
  associate

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} An insider of a person referred to in subsection (3),
  or the person's affiliate or associate, is an insider of the company
  referred to in that subsection. Paragraphs (1)(b) to (i) apply in
  making this determination except that references to "company" are to
  be read as references to "person described in subsection (3)".

- Meaning of [[associate]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} In subsection (4), [[associate]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
  means with respect to a person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a body corporate that the person directly or
    indirectly controls, determined without regard to paragraph 3(1)(d),
    or of which they beneficially own shares or securities currently
    convertible into shares carrying more than 10% of the voting rights
    under all circumstances or by reason of the occurrence of an event
    that has occurred and is continuing or a currently exercisable
    option or right to purchase the shares or convertible securities;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a partner of the person acting on behalf of the
    partnership of which they are partners;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a trust or estate in which the person has a
    substantial beneficial interest or in respect of which they serve as
    a trustee or a liquidator of the succession or in a similar
    capacity;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a spouse or common-law partner of the person;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a child of the person or of their spouse or
    common-law partner; or

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} if that relative has the same residence as the
    person, a relative of the person or of their spouse or common-law
    partner.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Insider trading --- compensation to
  sellers and purchasers

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} An insider of a company who purchases or sells a
  security of the company with knowledge of confidential information
  that if it were generally known might reasonably be expected to
  materially affect the value of any of the securities of the company is
  liable to compensate the seller or purchaser of the security, as the
  case may be, for any loss suffered by them as a result of the purchase
  or sale unless the insider establishes that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the insider reasonably believed that the
    information had been generally disclosed;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the information was known or ought reasonably to
    have been known by the seller or purchaser; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the purchase or sale of the security took place in
    the prescribed circumstances.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Insider trading --- compensation to
  company

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} The insider is accountable to the company for any
  benefit or advantage received or receivable by the insider as a result
  of a purchase or sale described in subsection (5), unless they
  establish the circumstances described in paragraph (6)(a).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 294
- 2005, c. 54, s. 272
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-294-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 294"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Tipping --- compensation to sellers and
purchasers

- **[[294.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-294.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An insider of a company who
  discloses confidential information with respect to the company that
  has not been generally disclosed and that if it were generally known
  might reasonably be expected to materially affect the value of any of
  the securities of the company is liable to compensate any person who
  subsequently sells securities of the company to or purchases them from
  any person who received the information unless the insider establishes
  that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the insider reasonably believed that the
    information had been generally disclosed;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the information was known or ought reasonably to
    have been known by the person who alleges that they suffered the
    loss;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the insider is not a person described in
    subsection 294(3) or (4), the disclosure of the information was
    necessary in the course of their business; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} if the insider is a person described in subsection
    294(3) or (4), the disclosure of the information was necessary to
    effect the take-over bid or business combination.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Tipping --- compensation to company

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The insider is accountable to the company for any
  benefit or advantage received or receivable by them as a result of a
  disclosure of information as described in subsection (1) unless they
  establish the circumstances described in paragraph (1)(a), (c) or (d).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 272
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Measure of damages

- **[[295]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-295 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  court may assess damages under subsection 294(6) or 294.1(1) in
  accord­ance with any measure of damages that it considers relevant in
  the circumstances. However, in assessing damages in respect of a
  security of a distributing company, the court shall consider the
  following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the plaintiff is a purchaser, the price that
    they paid for the security less the average market price of the
    security over the 20 trading days immediately following general
    disclosure of the information; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the plaintiff is a seller, the average market
    price of the security over the 20 trading days immediately following
    general disclosure of the information, less the price that they
    received for the security.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Liability --- more than one insider

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If more than one insider is liable under subsection
  294(6) or 294.1(1) with respect to the same transaction or series of
  transactions, their liability is joint and several, or solidary.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitation

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An action to enforce a right created by subsection
  294(6) or (7) or section 294.1 may be commenced only within two years
  after discovery of the facts that gave rise to the cause of action.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 295
- 2005, c. 54, s. 272
:::

Version](section-295-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 295"){.PITLink}
:::

### [DIVISION IX]{.HLabel2}[Prospectus]{.HTitleText2} {#h-261158 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Distribution

- **[[296]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-296 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  person including a company shall distribute securities of a company
  except in accordance with the regulations made under subsection (2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council may make regulations
  respecting the distribution of securities of a company, including

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} respecting the information that is to be disclosed
    by a company before the distribution of any of its securities,
    including the information that is to be included in a prospectus;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} respecting the manner of disclosure and the form of
    the information that is to be disclosed; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} exempting any class of distribution of securities
    from the application of subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 296
- 2005, c. 54, s. 272
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-296-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 296"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Order of exemption

- **[[297]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-297 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  application by a company or any person proposing to make a
  distribution, the Superintendent may, by order, exempt that
  distribution from the application of any regulations made under
  subsection 296(2) if the Superintendent is satisfied that the company
  has disclosed or is about to disclose, in compliance with the laws of
  the relevant jurisdiction, information relating to the distribution
  that in form and content substantially complies with the requirements
  of those regulations.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conditions

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An order under subsection (1) may contain any
  conditions or limitations that the Superintendent deems appropriate.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 297
- 2005, c. 54, s. 272
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-297-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 297"){.PITLink}
:::

### [DIVISION IX.1]{.HLabel2}[Going-private Transactions and Squeeze-out Transactions]{.HTitleText2} {#h-261176 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Going-private transactions

**[[298]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-298 .sectionLabel}** A company may carry out
a going-private transaction if it complies with any applicable
provincial securities laws.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 298
- 2005, c. 54, s. 272
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-298-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 298"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Squeeze-out transactions

**[[299]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-299 .sectionLabel}** No company may carry
out a squeeze-out transaction unless, in addition to any approval by
holders of shares required by or under this Act or the company's
by-laws, the transaction is approved by ordinary resolution of the
holders of each class of shares affected by the transaction, voting
separately, whether or not the shares otherwise carry the right to vote.
However, the following do not have the right to vote on the resolution:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} affiliates of the company; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} holders of shares that following the squeeze-out
  transaction would be entitled to consideration of greater value or to
  superior rights or privileges than those available to other holders of
  shares of the same class.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 299
- 1994, c. 26, s. 39(F)
- 1999, c. 31, s. 140
- 2005, c. 54, s. 272
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-299-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 299"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Right to dissent

- **[[300]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-300 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  holder of shares of a company may dissent if the company resolves to
  carry out a going-private transaction or squeeze-out transaction that
  affects those shares.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Payment for shares

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In addition to any other right that the shareholder
  may have, but subject to subsection (25), a shareholder who complies
  with this section is, when the action approved by the resolution from
  which the shareholder dissents becomes effective, entitled to be paid
  by the company the fair value of the shares in respect of which the
  shareholder dissents, determined as of the close of business on the
  day before the resolution was adopted by the policyholders entitled to
  vote and the shareholders.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No partial dissent

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A dissenting shareholder may claim under this section
  only with respect to all of the shares of a class held on behalf of
  any one beneficial owner and registered in the name of the dissenting
  shareholder.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Objection

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A dissenting shareholder shall send to the company,
  at or before any meeting of shareholders and policyholders at which a
  resolution referred to in subsection (2) is to be voted on by the
  policyholders entitled to vote and the shareholders, a written
  objection to the resolution unless the company did not give notice to
  the shareholder of the purpose of the meeting and their right to
  dissent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice that resolution was adopted

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The company shall within 10 days after the day on
  which the policyholders entitled to vote and the shareholders adopt
  the resolution send to each shareholder who sent an objection under
  subsection (4) notice that the resolution was adopted. If it is
  necessary for the Minister or Superintendent to approve the
  transaction within the meaning of subsection 1016(1) before it becomes
  effective, the company shall send notice within 10 days after the
  approval. Notice is not required to be sent to a shareholder who voted
  for the resolution or one who has withdrawn their objection.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Demand for payment

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} A dissenting shareholder shall within 20 days after
  receiving the notice referred to in subsection (5) --- or, if they do
  not receive it, within 20 days after learning that the resolution was
  adopted by the policyholders entitled to vote and the shareholders ---
  send to the company a written notice containing

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} their name and address;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number and class of shares in respect of which
    they dissent; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a demand for payment of the fair value of those
    shares.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Share certificates

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} A dissenting shareholder shall within 30 days after
  sending a notice under subsection (6) send the certificates
  representing the shares in respect of which they dissent to the
  company or its transfer agent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Forfeiture

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} A dissenting shareholder who fails to comply with
  subsection (7) has no right to make a claim under this section.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Endorsing certificate

  [(9)]{.lawlabel} A company or its transfer agent shall endorse on any
  share certificate received in accordance with subsection (7) a notice
  that the holder is a dissenting shareholder under this section and
  shall without delay return the share certificates to the dissenting
  shareholder.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Suspension of rights

  [(10)]{.lawlabel} On sending a notice under subsection (6), a
  dissenting shareholder ceases to have any rights as a shareholder
  other than to be paid the fair value of their shares as determined
  under this section. However, the shareholder's rights are reinstated
  as of the date the notice was sent if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the shareholder withdraws the notice before the
    company makes an offer under subsection (11);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the company fails to make an offer in accordance
    with subsection (11) and the shareholder withdraws the notice; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the directors revoke under section 242 the special
    resolution that was made in respect of the going-private transaction
    or squeeze-out transaction.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Offer to pay

  [(11)]{.lawlabel} A company shall, no later than seven days after the
  later of the day on which the action approved by the resolution from
  which the shareholder dissents becomes effective and the day on which
  the company received the notice referred to in subsection (6), send to
  each dissenting shareholder who sent a notice

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a written offer to pay for their shares in an
    amount considered by the directors of the company to be the fair
    value, accompanied by a statement showing how the fair value was
    determined; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if subsection (25) applies, a notice that it is
    unable to lawfully pay dissenting shareholders for their shares.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Same terms

  [(12)]{.lawlabel} Every offer made under subsection (11) for shares of
  the same class or series is to be on the same terms.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Payment

  [(13)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (25), a company shall pay for
  the shares of a dissenting shareholder within 10 days after the day on
  which an offer made under subsection (11) is accepted, but the offer
  lapses if the company does not receive an acceptance within 30 days
  after the day on which the offer is made.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Court may fix fair value

  [(14)]{.lawlabel} If a company fails to make an offer under
  subsection (11) or if a dissenting shareholder fails to accept an
  offer, the company may, within 50 days after the day on which the
  action approved by the resolution from which the shareholder dissents
  becomes effective or within any further period that a court may allow,
  apply to the court to fix a fair value for the shares of any
  dissenting shareholder.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholder application

  [(15)]{.lawlabel} If a company fails to apply to a court under
  subsection (14), a dissenting shareholder may apply to a court for the
  same purpose within a further period of 20 days or within any further
  period that the court may allow.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Venue

  [(16)]{.lawlabel} An application under subsection (14) or (15) is to
  be made to a court having jurisdiction where the company's head office
  is situated or, if the company carries on business in the province in
  which the dissenting shareholder resides, in that province.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No security for costs

  [(17)]{.lawlabel} A dissenting shareholder is not required to give
  security for costs in an application made under subsection (14) or
  (15).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Parties

  [(18)]{.lawlabel} On an application to a court under subsection (14)
  or (15),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} all dissenting shareholders whose shares have not
    been purchased by the company are to be joined as parties and are
    bound by the decision of the court;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the company shall notify each of them of the date,
    place and consequences of the application and their right to appear
    and be heard in person or by counsel; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the company shall notify the Superintendent of the
    date and place of the application and the Superintend­ent may appear
    and be heard in person or by counsel.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers of court

  [(19)]{.lawlabel} On an application to a court under subsection (14)
  or (15), the court may determine whether any other person is a
  dissenting shareholder and is to be joined as a party and the court
  shall then fix a fair value for the shares of all dissenting
  shareholders.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appraisers

  [(20)]{.lawlabel} The court may appoint one or more appraisers to
  assist the court to fix a fair value for the shares of the dissenting
  shareholders.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Final order

  [(21)]{.lawlabel} The final order of the court is to be rendered
  against the company in favour of each dissenting shareholder for the
  value of the shares as fixed by the court.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Interest

  [(22)]{.lawlabel} The court may allow a reasonable rate of interest on
  the amount payable to each dissenting shareholder from the date the
  action approved by the resolution from which the shareholder dissents
  becomes effective until the date of payment.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice that s. (25) applies

  [(23)]{.lawlabel} If subsection (25) applies, the company shall within
  10 days after an order is made under subsection (21) notify each
  dissenting shareholder that it is unable to lawfully pay dissenting
  shareholders for their shares.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of s. (25)

  [(24)]{.lawlabel} If subsection (25) applies, a dissenting shareholder
  may by written notice delivered to the company within 30 days after
  receiving notice under subsection (23)

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} withdraw their notice of dissent, in which case the
    company is deemed to consent to the withdrawal and the shareholder
    is reinstated to their full rights as a shareholder; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} retain their status as a claimant against the
    company, to be paid as soon as the company is able to lawfully pay
    them or, in a liquidation, to be ranked subordinate to the rights of
    the company's creditors but in priority to its shareholders.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitation

  [(25)]{.lawlabel} A company may not make a payment to a dissenting
  shareholder under this section if there are reasonable grounds for
  believing that the company is or the payment would cause the company
  to be in contravention of a regulation referred to in subsection
  515(1) or (2) or 516(1) or (2) or of an order made under subsection
  515(3) or 516(4).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 300
- 1999, c. 31, s. 141
- 2005, c. 54, s. 272
:::
