[Previous
Version](section-569-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 569"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Saving]{.HTitleText3} {#h-264485 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Saving

**[[570]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570 .sectionLabel}** Nothing in this Part
requires

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the termination of a loan or a commitment to make a
  loan or investment or to increase a loan or investment, or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the disposal of an investment

made before the coming into force of this Part but, if the loan or
investment would be precluded or limited by this Part, the amount of the
loan or investment shall not, except as provided in sections 557, 558
and 559, or pursuant to a commitment referred to in paragraph (a), be
increased after the coming into force of this Part.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Saving

**[[570.001]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.001 .sectionLabel}** A loan or
investment referred to in section 570 is deemed not to be prohibited by
the provisions of this Part.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 441
:::

### [Liquidation and Dissolution of a Society]{.HTitleText2} {#h-264495 .Subheading}

#### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-264496 .Subheading}

Definition of [[court]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

**[[570.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.01 .sectionLabel}** In sections
570.02 to 570.3, [[court]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a court having
jurisdiction in the place where the society has its head office.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

#### [Application]{.HTitleText3} {#h-264501 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application of sections 570.03 to 570.3

- **[[570.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.02
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Sections 570.03 to 570.3 do not
  apply to a society that is insolvent within the meaning of the
  [Winding-up and Restructuring Act](/eng/acts/W-11).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Staying proceedings on insolvency

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Any proceedings taken under sections 570.04 to 570.3
  to dissolve or to liquidate and dissolve a society shall be stayed if
  the society is at any time found to be insolvent within the meaning of
  the [Winding-up and Restructuring Act](/eng/acts/W-11).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

#### [Duty to Provide Information]{.HTitleText3} {#h-264509 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Returns to Superintendent

**[[570.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.03 .sectionLabel}** A liquidator
appointed under this Part to wind up the business of a society shall
provide the Superintendent with such information relating to the
business and affairs of the society as the Superintendent requires, in
such form as the Superintendent requires.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

#### [Simple Liquidation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-264514 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No property and no liabilities

- **[[570.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.04
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A society that has no property and
  no liabilities may, if authorized by a special resolution or, if there
  are no members, by a resolution of the society's supreme governing
  body, apply to the Minister for letters patent dissolving the society.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Dissolution by letters patent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where the Minister has received an application under
  subsection (1) and is satisfied that all the circumstances so warrant,
  the Minister may issue letters patent dissolving the society.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of letters patent

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A society in respect of which letters patent are
  issued under subsection (2) is dissolved and ceases to exist on the
  day stated in the letters patent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proposing liquidation

- **[[570.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.05
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The voluntary liquidation and
  dissolution of a society, other than a society referred to in
  subsection 570.04(1),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} may be proposed by its supreme governing body; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} may be initiated by way of a proposal made in
    accordance with the society's by-laws by a member who is entitled to
    vote at a meeting of the society's members at which the proposal may
    be voted on.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Terms must be set out

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A notice of any meeting of members at which the
  voluntary liquidation and dissolution of a society is to be proposed
  shall set out the terms of the proposal.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Members' resolution

**[[570.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.06 .sectionLabel}** Where the
voluntary liquidation and dissolution of a society is proposed, the
society may apply to the Minister for letters patent dissolving the
society if authorized by a special resolution.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Approval of Minister required

- **[[570.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.07
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No action directed toward the
  voluntary liquidation and dissolution of a society shall be taken by a
  society, other than as provided in sections 570.05 and 570.06, until
  an application made by the society under section 570.06 has been
  approved by the Minister.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conditional approval

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister is satisfied, on the basis of an
  application made under section 570.06, that the circumstances warrant
  the voluntary liquidation and dissolution of a society, the Minister
  may, by order, approve the application.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of approval

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister approves an application made under
  section 570.06 with respect to a society, the society shall not carry
  on business except to the extent necessary to complete its voluntary
  liquidation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Liquidation process

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister approves an application made under
  section 570.06 with respect to a society, the society shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} cause notice of the approval to be sent to each
    known claimant, except members, against the society and to each
    known creditor of the society;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} publish notice of the approval once a week for four
    consecutive weeks in the [Canada Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/)
    and once a week for two consecutive weeks in one or more newspapers
    in general circulation in each province in which the company
    transacted any business within the preceding twelve months;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} proceed to collect its property, dispose of
    property that is not to be distributed in kind to its members,
    discharge or provide for all its obligations and do all other acts
    required to liquidate its business; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} after giving the notice required under
    paragraphs (a) and (b) and adequately providing for the payment or
    discharge of all its obligations, distribute its remaining property,
    either in money or in kind, among its members according to their
    respective rights.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
- 2012, c. 5, s. 143
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-570.07-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 570.07"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Dissolution instrument

- **[[570.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.08
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Unless a court has made an order in
  accordance with subsection 570.09(1), the Minister may, if satisfied
  that the society has complied with subsection 570.07(4) and that all
  the circumstances so warrant, issue letters patent dissolving the
  society.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Society dissolved

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A society in respect of which letters patent are
  issued under subsection (1) is dissolved and ceases to exist on the
  day stated in the letters patent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

#### [Court-supervised Liquidation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-264559 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application for court supervision

- **[[570.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.09
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent or any interested
  person may, at any time during the liquidation of a society, apply to
  a court for an order for the continuance of the voluntary liquidation
  under the supervision of the court in accordance with this section and
  sections 570.1 to 570.21. On that application, the court may so order
  and make any further order it thinks fit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application to state reasons

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An application under subsection (1) to a court to
  supervise a voluntary liquidation shall state the reasons, verified by
  an affidavit of the applicant, why the court should supervise the
  liquidation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice to Superintendent

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where a person, other than the Superintendent, makes
  an application under subsection (1), the person shall give the
  Superintendent notice of the application and the Superintendent may
  appear and be heard in person or by counsel at the hearing of the
  application.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Court supervision

- **[[570.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a court makes an order under
  subsection 570.09(1), the liquidation of the society shall continue
  under the supervision of the court.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Beginning of liquidation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The supervision of the liquidation of a society by
  the court under an order made under subsection 570.09(1) begins on the
  day the order is made.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers of court

**[[570.11]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.11 .sectionLabel}** In connection
with the liquidation and dissolution of a society, if the court is
satisfied that the society is able to pay or adequately provide for the
discharge of all its obligations and to make satisfactory arrangements
for the protection of its policyholders, the court may make any order it
thinks fit, including

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} an order to liquidate;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} an order appointing a liquidator, with or without
  security, fixing a liquidator's remuneration and replacing a
  liquidator;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} an order appointing inspectors or referees,
  specifying their powers, fixing their remuneration and replacing
  inspectors or referees;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} an order determining the notice to be given to any
  interested person, or dispensing with notice to any person;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} an order determining the validity of any claims made
  against the society;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} an order, at any stage of the proceedings,
  restraining the directors and officers of the society from

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} exercising any of their powers, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} collecting or receiving any debt or other property
    of the society, and from paying out or transferring any property of
    the society, except as permitted by the court;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} an order determining and enforcing the duty or
  liability of any present or former director, officer or member

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} to the society, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} for an obligation of the society;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} an order approving the payment, satisfaction or
  compromise of claims against the society and the retention of assets
  for that purpose, and determining the adequacy of provisions for the
  payment, discharge or transfer of any obligation of the society,
  whether liquidated, unliquidated, future or contingent;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} with the concurrence of the Superintendent, an order
  providing for the disposal or destruction of the documents, records or
  registers of the society;

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} on the application of a creditor, an inspector or the
  liquidator, an order giving directions on any matter arising in the
  liquidation;

- [(k)]{.lawlabel} after notice has been given to all interested
  parties, an order relieving the liquidator from any omission or
  default on such terms as the court thinks fit and confirming any act
  of the liquidator;

- [(l)]{.lawlabel} subject to sections 570.18 to 570.2, an order
  approving any proposed, interim or final distribution to members, if
  any, or to incorporators, in money or in kind;

- [(m)]{.lawlabel} an order disposing of any property belonging to
  creditors, members and incorporators who cannot be found;

- [(n)]{.lawlabel} on the application of any director, officer, member,
  incorporator or creditor or the liquidator,

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} an order staying the liquidation proceedings on
    such terms and conditions as the court thinks fit,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} an order continuing or discontinuing the
    liquidation proceedings, or

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} an order to the liquidator to restore to the
    society all of its remaining property; and

- [(o)]{.lawlabel} after the liquidator has rendered the liquidator's
  final account to the court, an order directing the society to apply to
  the Minister for letters patent dissolving the society.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Cessation of business and powers

- **[[570.12]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.12
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where a court makes an order for the
  liquidation of a society,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the society continues in existence but shall cease
    to carry on business, except the business that is, in the opinion of
    the liquidator, required for an orderly liquidation; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the powers of the directors and members, if any,
    are vested in the liquidator and cease to be vested in the directors
    or members, except as specifically authorized by the court.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Delegation by liquidator

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A liquidator may delegate any of the powers vested by
  paragraph (1)(b) to the directors or members, if any.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointment of liquidator

**[[570.13]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.13 .sectionLabel}** When making an
order for the liquidation of a society or at any later time, the court
may appoint any person, including a director, an officer or a member of
the society or any other society, as liquidator of the society.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Vacancy in liquidator's office

**[[570.14]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.14 .sectionLabel}** Where an order
for the liquidation of a society has been made and the office of
liquidator is or becomes vacant, the property of the society is under
the control of the court until the office of liquidator is filled.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duties of liquidator

- **[[570.15]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.15
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A liquidator shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} without delay after appointment, give notice of the
    appointment to the Superintendent and to each claimant and creditor
    of the society known to the liquidator;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} without delay after appointment, publish notice of
    the appointment once a week for four consecutive weeks in the
    [Canada Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) and once a week for two
    consecutive weeks in one or more newspapers in general circulation
    in each province in which the society has transacted any business
    within the preceding twelve months, requiring

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} any person indebted to the society to render an
      account and pay to the liquidator at the time and place specified
      in the notice any amount owing,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} any person possessing property of the society to
      deliver it to the liquidator at the time and place specified in
      the notice, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} any person having a claim against the society,
      whether liquidated, unliquidated, future or contingent, other than
      a policyholder having an unliquidated claim, to present
      particulars of the claim in writing to the liquidator not later
      than sixty days after the first publication of the notice;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} take into custody and control the property of the
    society;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} open and maintain a trust account for the money
    received by the liquidator in the course of the liquidation of the
    society;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} keep accounts of the money received and paid out by
    the liquidator in the course of the liquidation of the society;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} maintain separate lists of each class of creditors,
    members and other persons having claims against the society;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} if at any time the liquidator determines that the
    society is unable to pay or adequately provide for the discharge of
    its obligations, apply to the court for directions;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} deliver to the court and to the Superintendent, at
    least once in every twelve-month period after the liquidator's
    appointment or more often as the court requires, the society's
    financial statements prepared in such manner as the liquidator
    thinks proper or as the court requires; and

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} after the final accounts are approved by the court,
    distribute any remaining property of the society among the members,
    if any, or incorporators, according to their respective rights.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers of liquidator

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A liquidator may

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} retain actuaries, lawyers, notaries, accountants,
    appraisers and other professional advisers;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} bring, defend or take part in any civil, criminal
    or administrative action or proceeding in the name of, and on behalf
    of, the society;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} carry on the business of the society as required
    for an orderly liquidation;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} sell by public auction or private sale any property
    of the society;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} do all acts and execute documents in the name of,
    and on behalf of, the society;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} borrow money on the security of the property of the
    society;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} settle or compromise any claims by or against the
    society; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} do all other things necessary for the liquidation
    of the society and distribution of its property.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reliance on statements

**[[570.16]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.16 .sectionLabel}** A liquidator is
not liable if the liquidator relies in good faith on

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} financial statements of the society represented to
  the liquidator by an officer of the society, or on a written report of
  the auditor of the society, to reflect fairly the financial condition
  of the society; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} an opinion, report or statement of an actuary,
  lawyer, notary, accountant, appraiser or other professional adviser
  retained by the liquidator.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Examination of others

- **[[570.17]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.17
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a liquidator has reason to
  believe that any property of the society is in the possession or under
  the control of a person or that a person has concealed, withheld or
  misappropriated the property, the liquidator may apply to the court
  for an order requiring that person to appear before the court at the
  time and place designated in the order and to be examined.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restoration and compensation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If an examination conducted under subsection (1)
  discloses that a person has concealed, withheld or misappropriated any
  property of the society, the court may order that person to restore
  the property or pay compensation to the liquidator.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Costs of liquidation

**[[570.18]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.18 .sectionLabel}** A liquidator
shall pay the costs of liquidation out of the property of the society
and shall pay or make adequate provision for all claims against the
society.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Final accounts

- **[[570.19]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.19
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Within one year after the
  appointment of a liquidator and after paying or making adequate
  provision for all claims against the society, the liquidator shall
  apply to the court

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} for approval of the final accounts of the
    liquidator and for an order permitting the distribution, in money or
    in kind, of the remaining property of the society to its members, if
    any, or to the incorporators, according to their respective rights;
    or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} for an extension of time, setting out the reasons
    for the extension.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Member application

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a liquidator fails to make the application
  required by subsection (1), a member of the society or, if there are
  no members of the society, an incorporator may apply to the court for
  an order for the liquidator to show cause why a final accounting and
  distribution should not be made.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notification of final accounts

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A liquidator who intends to make an application under
  subsection (1) shall give notice of that intention to the
  Superintendent, to each inspector appointed under section 570.11, to
  each member of the society or, if there are no members, to each
  incorporator and to any person who provided a security or fidelity
  bond for the liquidation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The liquidator shall publish the notice required
  under subsection (3) in the [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/), and once a week for two
  consecutive weeks in one or more newspapers in general circulation in
  each province in which the society has transacted any business within
  the preceding twelve months, or as otherwise directed by the court.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Final order

- **[[570.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If the court approves the final
  accounts rendered by a liquidator, the court shall make an order

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} directing the society to apply to the Minister for
    letters patent dissolving the society;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} directing the custody or disposal of the documents,
    records and registers of the society; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} discharging the liquidator except in respect of the
    duty of a liquidator under subsection (2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Delivery of order

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The liquidator shall without delay send a certified
  copy of the order referred to in subsection (1) to the Superintendent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Right to distribution of money

- **[[570.21]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.21
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A member or incorporator may apply
  to the court for an order requiring the distribution of the remaining
  property of a society to be in money if, in the course of the
  liquidation of the society, the members resolve to, or the liquidator
  proposes to,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} exchange all or substantially all of the remaining
    property of the society for securities of another entity that are to
    be distributed to the members or to the incorporators; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} distribute all or part of the remaining property of
    the society to the members or to the incorporators in kind.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers of court

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} On an application under subsection (1), the court may
  order

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} all of the remaining property of the society to be
    converted into and distributed in money; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the claim of any member or incorporator applying
    under this section to be satisfied by a distribution in money.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Order by court

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where an order is made by a court under paragraph
  (2)(b), the court

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} shall fix a fair value on the share of the property
    of the society attributable to the member or incorporator;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} may in its discretion appoint one or more
    appraisers to assist the court in fixing a fair value in accordance
    with paragraph (a); and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} shall render a final order against the society in
    favour of the member or incorporator for the amount of the share of
    the property of the society attributable to the member or
    incorporator.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Dissolution by letters patent

- **[[570.22]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.22
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On an application made under an
  order under paragraph 570.2(1)(a), the Minister may issue letters
  patent dissolving the society.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Society dissolved

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A society in respect of which letters patent are
  issued under subsection (1) is dissolved and ceases to exist on the
  date of the issuance of the letters patent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

#### [General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-264709 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

**[[570.23]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.23 .sectionLabel}** In sections
570.25 and 570.26, [[member]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} and
[[incorporator]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} include the heirs and personal
representatives of a member or incorporator.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Continuation of actions

- **[[570.24]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.24
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Even if a society has been dissolved
  under this Part,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a civil, criminal or administrative action or
    proceeding brought by or against the society before its dissolution
    may be continued as if the society had not been dissolved;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a civil, criminal or administrative action or
    proceeding may be brought against the society within two years after
    its dissolution as if the society had not been dissolved; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any property that would have been available to
    satisfy any judgment or order if the society had not been dissolved
    remains available for that purpose.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Service on society

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Service of a document on a society after its
  dissolution may be effected by serving the document on a person shown
  as a director in the incorporating instrument of the society or, if
  applicable, in the latest return sent to the Superintendent under
  subsection 549(1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitations on liability

- **[[570.25]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.25
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Even if a society has been
  dissolved, a member or incorporator to whom any of its property has
  been distributed is liable to any person claiming under subsection
  570.24(1), to the extent of the amount received by that member or
  incorporator on the distribution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An action to enforce liability under subsection (1)
  may not be commenced more than two years after the date of the
  dissolution of the society.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Action against class

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A court may order an action referred to in
  subsections (1) and (2) to be brought against the persons who were
  members or incorporators as a class, subject to such conditions as the
  court thinks fit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reference

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the plaintiff establishes a claim in an action
  under subsection (3), the court may refer the proceedings to a referee
  or other officer of the court who may

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} add as a party to the proceedings each person found
    by the plaintiff to have been a member or incorporator;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} determine, subject to subsection (1), the amount
    that each person who was a member or incorporator must contribute
    towards satisfaction of the plaintiff's claim; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} direct payment of the amounts so determined.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Where creditor cannot be found

**[[570.26]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.26 .sectionLabel}** If a creditor,
member or incorporator to whom property is to be distributed on the
dissolution of a society cannot be found, the portion of the property to
be distributed to that creditor, member or incorporator shall be
converted into money and paid in accordance with section 570.28.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Vesting in Crown

**[[570.27]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.27 .sectionLabel}** Subject to
subsection 570.24(1) and sections 570.28 and 570.29, property of a
society that has not been disposed of at the date of the dissolution of
the society vests in Her Majesty in right of Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Unclaimed money on winding-up

- **[[570.28]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.28
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where the business of a society is
  being wound up under this Part, the liquidator or the society shall
  pay to the Minister on demand, and in any event before the final
  winding-up of that business, any amount that is payable by the
  liquidator or the society to a creditor, member or incorporator of the
  society and that has not, for any reason, been paid.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Records

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a liquidator or a society makes a payment to the
  Minister under subsection (1) with respect to a creditor, member or
  incorporator, the liquidator or society shall at the same time forward
  to the Minister all documents, records and registers in the possession
  of the liquidator or society that relate to the entitlement of the
  creditor, member or incorporator.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Payment to Receiver General

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall pay to the Receiver General all
  amounts paid to the Minister under subsection (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Liquidator and company discharged

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Payment by a liquidator or a society to the Minister
  under subsection (1) discharges the liquidator and the society in
  respect of which the payment is made from all liability for the amount
  so paid, and payment by the Minister to the Receiver General under
  subsection (3) discharges the Minister from all liability for the
  amount so paid.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Recovery

**[[570.29]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.29 .sectionLabel}** If at any time a
person establishes an entitlement to any money paid to the Receiver
General under this Part, the Receiver General shall pay an equivalent
amount to that person out of the Consolidated Revenue Fund.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Custody of records after dissolution

**[[570.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-570.3 .sectionLabel}** A person who has
been granted custody of the documents, records and registers of a
dissolved society shall keep them available for production for six years
after the date of the dissolution of the society or until the end of
such shorter period as may be ordered by the court when it orders the
dissolution.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 298
:::

## [PART XIII]{.HLabel1}[Foreign Companies]{.HTitleText1} {#h-264765 .Part}

### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText2} {#h-264766 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

**[[571]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-571 .sectionLabel}** In this Part,

[[association]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[association]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an association of persons
    formed in a foreign country on the plan known as Lloyd's, whereby
    each member of the association participating in a policy becomes
    liable for a stated, limited or proportionate part of the whole
    amount payable under the policy; ([association]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[chief agency]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[chief agency]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the principal office of a
    foreign company in Canada; ([agence principale]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[chief agent]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[chief agent]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, in respect of a foreign
    company, means the natural person appointed pursuant to subsection
    579(3) and named as such in the power of attorney referred to in
    paragraph 579(1)(b); ([agent principal]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[exchange]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[exchange]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a group of persons formed in
    a foreign country for the purpose of exchanging reciprocal contracts
    of indemnity or inter-insurance with each other through the same
    attorney, where the principal office of the exchange is in a foreign
    country; ([groupe d'échange]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[foreign entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[foreign entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an entity incorporated
    or formed by or under the laws of a country other than Canada, and
    includes an association and an exchange; ([entité
    étrangère]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[foreign fraternal benefit society]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[foreign fraternal benefit society]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a
    fraternal benefit society incorporated outside Canada; ([société de
    secours étrangère]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[foreign life company]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[foreign life company]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a foreign company
    that is authorized to insure risks that fall within the class of
    life insurance; ([société d'assurance-vie
    étrangère]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[foreign marine company]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[foreign marine company]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a foreign
    company that is authorized to solely insure risks within the class
    of marine insurance; ([société d'assurance maritime
    étrangère]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[foreign property and casualty company]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[foreign property and casualty company]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means
    a foreign company other than a foreign life company or a foreign
    marine company. ([société d'assurances multirisques
    étrangère]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[fraternal benefit society]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[fraternal benefit society]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed,
    1997, c. 15, s. 299\]]{.Repealed}

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 571
- 1996, c. 6, s. 83.1
- 1997, c. 15, s. 299
- 2007, c. 6, s. 256
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-571-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 571"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Application]{.HTitleText2} {#h-264781 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application --- insurance business in
Canada

**[[572]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-572 .sectionLabel}** This Part applies only
in respect of the insurance business in Canada of a foreign entity.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 572
- 2007, c. 6, s. 257
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-572-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 572"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

**[[572.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-572.1 .sectionLabel}** Despite section
572, this Part does not apply in respect of the insurance against injury
to persons or loss of or damage to property, or liability for such
injury, loss or damage, caused by nuclear energy, including ionizing
radiation and contamination by radioactive substances, to the extent
that, in the opinion of the Superintendent, that insurance is not
available within Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 6, s. 257
:::

### [Insurance of Risks]{.HTitleText2} {#h-264790 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction on insuring of risks unless
authorized

- **[[573]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-573 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  foreign entity shall not insure in Canada a risk unless it is
  authorized by order made under subsection 574(1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction to specified classes of
  insurance

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A foreign company shall not insure in Canada a risk
  unless the risk falls within a class of insurance that is specified in
  the order made under subsection 574(1) in respect of the foreign
  company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction on issuance of annuities or
  endowment insurance

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Unless authorized to insure in Canada risks falling
  within the class of life insurance, a foreign company shall not issue
  annuities or policies of endowment insurance in Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transitional

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A certificate of registry issued to a foreign entity
  under the Foreign Insurance Companies Act or Part VIII of the Canadian
  and British Insurance Companies Act, or any other authorization, that
  had not expired or been withdrawn before June 1, 1992 is deemed to be
  an order made under subsection 574(1) and the foreign entity remains
  subject to any and all other conditions and limitations contained in
  the certificate or other authorization.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Continuance of certificate limitations

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A class of insurance specified in a certificate of
  registry or other authorization referred to in subsection (4) is
  deemed to be specified in an order of the Superintendent approving the
  insuring in Canada of risks by the foreign company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 573
- 1997, c. 15, s. 300(F)
- 2007, c. 6, s. 259
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-573-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 573"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application for order

- **[[574]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-574 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  application by a foreign entity, the Superintendent may, with the
  approval of the Minister but subject to the other provisions of this
  Part, make an order approving the insuring in Canada of risks by the
  foreign entity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reciprocal treatment

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the application is made by a foreign entity that
  is not controlled by a WTO Member resident, the Minister shall not
  approve the making of an order under subsection (1) unless the
  Minister is satisfied that treatment as favourable for companies to
  which this Act applies exists or will be provided in the jurisdiction
  in which the foreign entity principally carries on business, either
  directly or through a subsidiary.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 574
- 1999, c. 28, s. 125
- 2007, c. 6, s. 260
:::

:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Policies and procedures --- integrity or
security

**[[574.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-574.1 .sectionLabel}** A foreign company
shall establish and adhere to policies and procedures to protect itself
against threats to its integrity or security in relation to its business
in Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2023, c. 26, s. 582](#1411071-1437428){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1411071-1437428.html"
  role="button"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibited names

- **[[575]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-575 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  order made under subsection 574(1) may not provide for the use of a
  name that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is prohibited by an Act of Parliament;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is, in the opinion of the Superintendent,
    deceptively misdescriptive;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} is the same as or, in the opinion of the
    Superintendent, substantially the same as or confusingly similar to,
    any existing trademark, trade name or corporate name of a body
    corporate, except where

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the trademark or trade name is being changed or
      the body corporate is being dissolved or is changing its corporate
      name, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} consent to the use of the trademark, trade name
      or corporate name is signified to the Superintendent in any manner
      that the Superintendent may require;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} is the same as or, in the opinion of the
    Superintendent, substantially the same as or confusingly similar to,
    the known name under or by which any entity carries on business or
    is identified; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} is reserved under section 45 for a company or
    society or proposed company or society.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Affiliated entity

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), an order made under
  subsection 574(1) may provide for the use of a name that is the same
  or substantially the same as that of an entity with which the foreign
  entity is affiliated, within the meaning of subsection 6(2), if that
  other entity consents to the use of the name.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Representations to Superintendent

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent does not make an order for one
  of the reasons specified in subsection (1), he or she must, by a
  notice in writing to that effect, give the foreign entity and any
  other interested party an opportunity to make representations.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 575
- 1996, c. 6, s. 84
- 1997, c. 15, s. 301
- 2007, c. 6, s. 260
- [2014, c. 20, s. 366(E)](#1034903-1145572){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1034903-1145572.html"
  role="button"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-575-20070420.html "Link to previous version of section 575"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Change of name

- **[[576]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-576 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  the application of a foreign company, the Superintendent may, subject
  to subsection 575(1), by further order, change the name under which a
  foreign company insures risks.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2007, c. 6, s. 261\]]{.Repealed}

- 2007, c. 6, s. 261

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Direction to change of name

- **[[577]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-577 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  through inadvertence or otherwise a foreign company is permitted by an
  order made under subsection 574(1) to insure risks under a name that
  is prohibited by section 575, the Superintendent may direct the
  foreign company to change the name without delay.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Revoking name

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a foreign company has been directed under
  subsection (1) to change the name under which it insures risks and has
  not, within sixty days after the service of the direction, changed
  that name to a name that is not prohibited by this Part, the
  Superintendent may revoke the name under which the foreign company
  insures risks and assign to it a name and, until changed in accordance
  with subsection 576(1), the name under which the foreign company is to
  insure risks is thereafter the name so assigned.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 577
- 1996, c. 6, s. 84
- 2007, c. 6, s. 262
:::

Version](section-577-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 577"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}French, English or foreign form of name

- **[[578]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-578 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  name under which a foreign company is authorized to insure risks, as
  set out in the order made under subsection 574(1), may be in an
  English form, a French form, an English form and a French form, a
  combined English and French form or a form combining words in a
  language other than English or French with one of the forms specified
  in this subsection.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Other name

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (3) and (4), a foreign company
  may carry on its insurance business in Canada under a name other than
  the name set out in the order made under subsection 574(1) in respect
  of the foreign company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Direction to change name

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a foreign company carries on its insurance
  business in Canada under a name other than a name set out in the order
  made under subsection 574(1) in respect of the foreign company, the
  Superintendent may direct the foreign company not to use that other
  name if the Superintendent is of the opinion that the other name is a
  name referred to in any of paragraphs 575(1)(a) to (e).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication of name

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A foreign company shall set out, or cause to be set
  out, its name and, if different, the name under which it is authorized
  to insure risks, in legible characters in all contracts, premium
  notices, applications for policies, policies, negotiable instruments
  and other documents evidencing rights and obligations with respect to
  other parties that are issued or made by or on behalf of the foreign
  company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication of statement

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A foreign company shall set out or cause to be set
  out in legible characters in all premium notices, applications for
  policies and policies that are issued or made by or on behalf of the
  foreign company a statement that the document was issued or made in
  the course of its insurance business in Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Continuation of registered names

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} The name of a foreign company, as set out in a
  certificate of registry referred to in subsection 573(4), or in any
  other authorization, is deemed to be set out in an order of the
  Superintendent made under subsection 574(1) in respect of the foreign
  company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 578
- 2007, c. 6, s. 263
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-578-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 578"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application

- **[[579]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-579 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  application for an order under subsection 574(1) must be filed with
  the Superintendent, together with the information, material and
  evidence that the Superintendent may require, including

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} documents relating to the constitution of the
    foreign entity;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a power of attorney to the chief agent appointed
    under subsection (3), in the form that the Superintendent may
    require;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a statement, in the form that the Superintendent
    may require, of the financial condition of the foreign entity and of
    the business of insurance undertaken by the foreign entity, and any
    additional statements or information that the Superintendent may
    require as to its solvency and its ability to meet all of its
    obligations;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} evidence satisfactory to the Superintendent that
    the foreign entity is authorized under the laws of the country where
    it is incorporated or formed to insure risks within each class of
    insurance in Canada that that foreign entity has applied to insure;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a foreign fraternal benefit society,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a report of an actuary appointed by the foreign
      fraternal benefit society, in the form that the Superintendent may
      require, on the results of an actuarial valuation made by the
      actuary, as of the preceding December 31 or as of any later date
      specified by the Superintendent, of each of the benefit funds
      maintained by the foreign fraternal benefit society, having regard
      to the prospective liabilities of and contributions to each fund,
      and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the opinion of the actuary that the assets of
      the foreign fraternal benefit society applicable to each fund,
      taken at the value accepted by the Superintendent, together with
      the premiums, dues and other contributions to be received after
      the date of the valuation from the members according to the scale
      in force at the date of the valuation, are sufficient to provide
      for the payment at maturity of all of the obligations of the fund
      without deduction or abatement; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a copy of the resolution respecting the investment
    and lending policies, standards and procedures that the foreign
    entity is to establish and adhere to in accordance with subsection
    615(1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents of power of attorney

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A power of attorney referred to in paragraph (1)(b)
  must expressly authorize the chief agent to receive all notices under
  the laws of Canada from the Minister or the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointment of chief agent

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A foreign company shall appoint a natural person who
  is ordinarily resident in Canada to be its chief agent for the
  purposes of this Part.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 579
- 1997, c. 15, s. 302
- 2007, c. 6, s. 264
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-579-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 579"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publishing notice of intention

**[[580]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-580 .sectionLabel}** Before filing an
application referred to in subsection 579(1), a foreign entity must, at
least once a week for four consecutive weeks, publish, in a form
satisfactory to the Superintendent, a notice of intention to make the
application in the [Canada Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) and in a
newspaper in general circulation at or near the place where its chief
agency is to be situated if it is granted an order under subsection
574(1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 580
- 2007, c. 6, s. 265
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-580-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 580"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conditions for order

- **[[581]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-581 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Superintendent shall not make an order under subsection 574(1) in
  respect of a foreign entity until it has been shown to the
  satisfaction of the Superintendent that all relevant requirements of
  this Act have been complied with and that the foreign entity has

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} vested in trust assets of at least five million
    dollars or any greater amount that the Superintendent specifies;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} appointed an actuary under section 623 and an
    auditor under section 633; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} established its chief agency.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conditions of order

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The order may contain any conditions or limitations
  that are consistent with this Act and that the Superintendent
  considers appropriate.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 581
- 2005, c. 54, s. 299
- 2007, c. 6, s. 265
- 2012, c. 5, s. 144
:::

Version](section-581-20070420.html "Link to previous version of section 581"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Permissible securities

- **[[582]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-582 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  assets of a foreign entity to be vested in trust under paragraph
  581(1)(a) are to consist of unencumbered securities of or guaranteed
  by Canada or a province.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Other permissible securities

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Those assets may also consist of other securities at
  the accepted value and on the conditions established by the
  Superintendent.

::: HistoricalNote

- 2007, c. 6, s. 266(E)
- 2012, c. 5, s. 145(E)

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents of order

**[[583]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-583 .sectionLabel}** An order made under
subsection 574(1) in respect of a foreign company must set out

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name of the foreign company and, if different,
  the name under which it is authorized to insure risks;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the day on which the order becomes effective;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the classes of insurance risks that the foreign
  company is authorized to insure; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the conditions or limitations that are consistent
  with this Act that are considered appropriate by the Superintendent.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Public notice

- **[[584]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-584 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  the making of an order under subsection 574(1) in respect of a foreign
  company, the foreign company must publish a notice of the making of
  the order in a newspaper in general circulation at or near the place
  where its chief agency is located.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice in [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/)

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent shall cause to be published in the
  [Canada Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) a notice of the making of
  the order referred to in subsection (1).

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication of list

**[[585]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-585 .sectionLabel}** Unless the regulations
provide otherwise, the Superintendent shall cause to be published
quarterly in the [Canada Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) a list of

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} foreign companies;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the classes of insurance specified in the orders of
  the Superintendent approving the insurance of risks by them;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} their chief agents; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the province in which their chief agencies are

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Variations

- **[[586]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-586 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In
  respect of an order made under subsection 574(1) in respect of a
  foreign company, the Superintendent may at any time, by further order,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} specify additional classes of insurance risks that
    the foreign company is authorized to insure;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} make the order subject to conditions or limitations
    that are consistent with this Act and that are considered
    appropriate by the Superintendent; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} amend or revoke any authorization contained in the
    order or any condition or limitation to which the order is subject.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Representations

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Before making any such further order, the
  Superintendent must give the foreign company an opportunity to make
  representations regarding that further order.

- [(3) to (6)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 1996, c. 6, s. 85\]]{.Repealed}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Change of chief agent

- **[[587]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-587 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  foreign company that changes its chief agent shall, without delay
  after doing so, file with the Superintendent a further power of
  attorney appointing the new chief agent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Change of address

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A foreign company that changes the address of its
  chief agency shall, within 15 days after doing so, send a notice of
  the change of address to the Superintendent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 587
- 2007, c. 6, s. 271
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restricted transactions

- **[[587.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-587.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except in accordance with this
  section or an order made under subsection 678.6(1), a foreign company
  shall not cause itself to be reinsured, on an assumption basis,
  against all or any portion of the risks undertaken under its policies.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Approval of the Superintendent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A foreign company may, with the approval of the
  Superintendent, cause itself to be reinsured, on an assumption basis,
  against all or any portion of the risks undertaken under its policies,
  by one or more of the following entities:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a company or society;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} another foreign company that, in Canada, reinsures
    those risks; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a body corporate incorporated or formed by or under
    the laws of a province, if the Superintendent has entered into
    satisfactory arrangements concerning the reinsurance with either or
    both of the body corporate and the appropriate official or public
    body responsible for the supervision of the body corporate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prescribed transactions

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The approval of the Superintendent is not required
  for a prescribed transaction or a transaction in a prescribed class of
  transactions.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Procedure

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The foreign company must, at least 30 days before it
  applies for the Superintendent's approval, publish a notice in the
  [Canada Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) and in a newspaper in
  general circulation at or near the place where its chief agency is
  situated stating the day on or after which it will apply.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If a foreign company publishes a notice referred to
  in subsection (4), the Superintendent may direct the foreign company
  to provide its policyholders with any information that the
  Superintendent may require.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report of independent actuary

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} An application for approval must, if the
  Superintendent so requires, be accompanied by the report of an
  independent actuary on the proposed reinsurance agreement.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Inspection

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} If a foreign company publishes a notice referred to
  in subsection (4), it must make the agreement for the transaction that
  the Superintendent is asked to approve available at its chief agency
  for the inspection of its policyholders for at least 30 days after the
  publication of the notice and must provide a copy of the agreement to
  any policyholder who requests one by writing to the chief agency.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Superintendent may shorten periods

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent is of the opinion that it is in
  the best interests of a group of policyholders affected by the
  transaction that the Superintendent is asked to approve, the
  Superintendent may shorten the periods of 30 days referred to in
  subsections (4) and (7).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

  [(9)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council may make regulations
  respecting the circumstances in which foreign companies are deemed to
  be causing themselves to be reinsured, on an assumption basis, against
  risks undertaken under their policies.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 303
- 1999, c. 1, s. 9
- 2001, c. 9, s. 442
- 2005, c. 54, s. 301
- 2007, c. 6, s. 271
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-587.1-20060427.html "Link to previous version of section 587.1"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Approval by Superintendent

**[[587.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-587.2 .sectionLabel}** A transaction
referred to in subsection 587.1(2) has no effect until it has been
approved by the Superintendent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 6, s. 271
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice to Superintendent

- **[[587.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-587.3
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A foreign company proposing to
  transfer all or substantially all of its policies must give notice of
  the proposal to the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} After receiving the notice, the Superintendent may
  direct the foreign company to provide its policyholders with any
  information that the Superintendent may require.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 6, s. 271
:::

### [Classes of Insurance]{.HTitleText2} {#h-264969 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction to reinsurance

- **[[588]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-588 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  foreign company may reinsure, but shall not otherwise insure, a risk
  falling within a class of insurance specified in the order made under
  subsection 574(1) in respect of the foreign company if the order
  limits the foreign company to the reinsurance of those risks.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Continuation of certificate conditions

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A condition that limits a foreign company to the
  reinsurance of risks falling within a class of insurance and that is
  contained in a certificate of registry issued under the Foreign
  Insurance Companies Act or under Part VIII of the Canadian and British
  Insurance Companies Act, or in any other authorization, that had not
  expired or been withdrawn before June 1, 1992 is deemed to be a
  condition in an order made under subsection 574(1) in respect of the
  foreign company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 588
- 2007, c. 6, s. 272
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-588-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 588"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No new foreign composite companies

**[[589]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-589 .sectionLabel}** The Superintendent may
not make or vary an order made under subsection 574(1) in respect of a
foreign company if the foreign company would as a result be permitted to
insure both risks falling within the class of life insurance and risks
falling within any other class of insurance other than accident and
sickness insurance, credit protection insurance and other approved
products insurance.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 589
- 1997, c. 15, s. 304
- 2007, c. 6, s. 272
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-589-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 589"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Saving for existing foreign composite
companies

- **[[590]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-590
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite section 589, subsections
  573(4) and 588(2) permit a foreign company to which was issued under
  the Foreign Insurance Companies Act or Part VIII of the Canadian and
  British Insurance Companies Act a certificate of registry or other
  authorization specifying both risks falling within the class of life
  insurance and risks falling within some other class of insurance,
  other than accident and sickness insurance, accident insurance,
  personal accident insurance and sickness insurance, to insure those
  risks.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Separate accounts for life insurance

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A foreign company referred to in subsection (1) shall
  maintain an account and funds in respect of the insurance of risks
  falling within the classes of life insurance and accident and sickness
  insurance, accident insurance, personal accident insurance and
  sickness insurance separately from those maintained in respect of the
  insurance of risks falling within any other class of insurance.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 590
- 2007, c. 6, s. 273
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-590-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 590"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Compensation association

- **[[591]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-591
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every foreign company that is
  insuring risks that fall within a class of insurance shall become and
  remain a member of any compensation association designated by order of
  the Minister for that class of insurance.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Designation limitation

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} A compensation association shall not be designated
  under subsection (1) unless, in the opinion of the Minister, it has
  the authority to levy an assessment on each of its members of not less
  than eighty-five one hundredths of one per cent of the member's
  average annual premium income from policies that are eligible for
  compensation from the association.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exceptions

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} to a foreign company that may reinsure but may not
    otherwise insure risks;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in respect of a class of insurance that, in the
    opinion of the Minister, is adequately covered by some other
    compensation plan for that class of insurance;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in respect of the insuring in Canada of risks
    against the loss of, or damage to, property caused by fire, by
    lightning, by an explosion due to ignition, by smoke or by breakage
    of or leakage from a sprinkler, from other fire protection equipment
    or from another fire protection system by a foreign company that is
    a member of the Fire Mutuals Guarantee Fund; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} to a foreign company that is a foreign fraternal
    benefit society or an exchange.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 591
- 1996, c. 6, s. 86
- 1997, c. 15, s. 305
- 2007, c. 6, s. 274
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-591-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 591"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Segregated Funds]{.HTitleText2} {#h-265001 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Segregated funds restricted to foreign
life companies

**[[592]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-592 .sectionLabel}** Unless authorized to
insure risks that fall within the class of life insurance, a foreign
company shall not

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} insure risks under policies, or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} accept or retain on the direction of a policyholder
  or beneficiary policy dividends or bonuses, or policy proceeds that
  are payable on the surrender or maturity of the policy or on the death
  of the person whose life is insured,

where the liabilities of the foreign company in respect of the policies
or the amounts accepted or retained vary in amount depending on the
market value of a fund consisting of a specified group of assets.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 592
- 2007, c. 6, s. 275
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-592-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 592"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Where segregated funds required

**[[593]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-593 .sectionLabel}** A foreign company that
issues policies described in section 592 or accepts or retains amounts
so described shall, in respect of those policies or amounts,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} maintain separate accounts; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} establish and maintain one or more funds consisting
  of assets in Canada that are segregated from the other assets in
  Canada of the foreign company and that are specified as the assets on
  the market value of which the liabilities of the foreign company in
  respect of those policies or amounts depend.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Claims against segregated funds

**[[594]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-594 .sectionLabel}** A claim against a
segregated fund maintained as required by section 593 under a policy or
for an amount in respect of which the fund is maintained has priority
over any other claim against the assets of that fund, including the
claims referred to in section 161 of the [Winding-up and Restructuring
Act](/eng/acts/W-11), except to the extent that the payment of that
other claim is secured by a security interest in or on a specific,
identifiable asset of the segregated fund.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 594
- 1996, c. 6, s. 167
- 1997, c. 15, s. 306
- 2007, c. 6, s. 276
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-594-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 594"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction of claims

**[[595]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-595 .sectionLabel}** The liability of a
foreign company under a policy or for an amount in respect of which a
segregated fund is maintained pursuant to section 593

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} does not, except to the extent that the assets of the
  fund are insufficient to satisfy a claim for any minimum amount that
  the foreign company agrees to pay under the policy or in respect of
  the amount, give rise to a claim against any assets in Canada of the
  foreign company, other than the assets of that fund,

but

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} to the extent that the assets of the fund are
  insufficient to satisfy such a claim, gives rise to a claim against
  the assets in Canada of the foreign company, other than the assets of
  that fund, that has the priority referred to in subsection 161(2) of
  the [Winding-up and Restructuring Act](/eng/acts/W-11).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 595
- 1996, c. 6, s. 167
- 2007, c. 6, s. 276
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-595-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 595"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Reinsurance]{.HTitleText2} {#h-265024 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

- **[[596]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-596 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Governor in Council may make regulations limiting the extent to which
  foreign companies may cause themselves to be reinsured against risks
  undertaken under their policies.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulation may provide for discretion

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A regulation made pursuant to subsection (1) may
  provide that the Superintendent may, by order, determine the matters
  or exercise the discretion that the regulation may specify.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 596
- 2007, c. 6, s. 277
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-596-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 596"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction re related parties

- **[[597]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-597
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except with the approval of the
  Superintendent, a foreign company may cause itself to be reinsured, in
  respect of risks undertaken under its policies, by a related party of
  the foreign company only if the related party is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a company; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a foreign company that, in Canada, reinsures those
    risks.

- Meaning of [[related party]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section, [[related
  party]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, in relation to a foreign company, means a
  [[related party]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} within the meaning of Part XI,
  with such modifications as the circumstances require.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 597
- 2007, c. 6, s. 278
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-597-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 597"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Borrowing Costs]{.HTitleText2} {#h-265041 .Subheading}

Definition of [[cost of borrowing]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

**[[598]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-598 .sectionLabel}** For the purposes of
this section and sections 598.1 to 605, [[cost of
borrowing]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means, in respect of a loan or an
advance on the security or against the cash surrender value of a policy
made by a foreign company,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the interest or discount applicable to the loan or
  advance;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} any amount charged in connection with the loan or
  advance that is payable by the borrower to the foreign company; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} any charge prescribed to be included in the cost of
  borrowing.

For those purposes, however, [[cost of borrowing]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
does not include any charge prescribed to be excluded from the cost of
borrowing.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 598
- 1997, c. 15, s. 307
- 2001, c. 9, s. 443
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Rebate of borrowing costs

- **[[598.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-598.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where a foreign company makes a loan
  in respect of which the disclosure requirements of section 599 apply,
  and the loan is not secured by a mortgage on real property and is
  required to be repaid either on a fixed future date or by instalments,
  the foreign company shall, if there is a prepayment of the loan,
  rebate to the borrower a portion of the charges included in the cost
  of borrowing in respect of the loan.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The charges to be rebated do not include the interest
  or discount applicable to the loan.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council may make regulations
  governing the rebate of charges under subsection (1). The rebate shall
  be made in accordance with those regulations.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 307
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disclosing borrowing costs

- **[[599]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-599 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  foreign company shall not include in its assets in Canada any loan to
  a natural person that is repayable in Canada unless the cost of
  borrowing, as calculated and expressed in accordance with section 600,
  and other prescribed information have been disclosed by the foreign
  company to the borrower at the prescribed time and place and in the
  prescribed form and manner.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Non-application

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of a loan
  that is of a prescribed class of loans.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 599
- 1997, c. 15, s. 307
- 2012, c. 5, s. 146
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-599-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 599"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Calculating borrowing costs

**[[600]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-600 .sectionLabel}** The cost of borrowing
shall be calculated, in the prescribed manner, on the basis that all
obligations of the borrower are duly fulfilled and shall be expressed as
a rate per annum and, in prescribed circumstances, as an amount in
dollars and cents.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Additional disclosure

- **[[601]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where a foreign company makes a loan
  in respect of which the disclosure requirements of section 599 are
  applicable and the loan is required to be repaid either on a fixed
  future date or by instalments, the foreign company shall disclose to
  the borrower, in accordance with the regulations,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} whether the borrower has the right to repay the
    amount borrowed before the maturity of the loan and, if applicable,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} any terms and conditions relating to that right,
      including the particulars of the circumstances in which the
      borrower may exercise that right, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} whether, in the event that the borrower
      exercises the right, any portion of the cost of borrowing is to be
      rebated, the manner in which any such rebate is to be calculated
      or, if a charge or penalty will be imposed on the borrower, the
      manner in which the charge or penalty is to be calculated;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the event that an amount borrowed is not repaid
    at maturity or, if applicable, an instalment is not paid on the day
    the instalment is due to be paid, particulars of the charges or
    penalties to be paid by the borrower because of the failure to repay
    or pay in accordance with the contract governing the loan;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} at the prescribed time and place and in the
    prescribed form and manner, any changes respecting the cost of
    borrowing or the loan agreement;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} particulars of any other rights and obligations of
    the borrower; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} any other prescribed information, at the prescribed
    time and place and in the prescribed form and manner.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disclosure in credit card applications

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A foreign company shall, in accordance with the
  regulations, at the prescribed time and place and in the prescribed
  form and manner, provide prescribed information in any application
  forms or related documents that it prepares for the issuance of
  credit, payment or charge cards in Canada and provide prescribed
  information to any person applying to it in Canada for a credit,
  payment or charge card.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disclosure re credit cards

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where a foreign company issues in Canada or has
  issued in Canada a credit, payment or charge card to a natural person,
  the foreign company shall, in addition to disclosing the costs of
  borrowing in respect of any loan that is obtained through the use of
  the card and that is repayable in Canada, disclose to the person, in
  accordance with the regulations,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any charges or penalties described in paragraph
    (1)(b);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} particulars of the person's rights and obligations;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any charges for which the person becomes
    responsible by accepting or using the card;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} at the prescribed time and place and in the
    prescribed form and manner, any prescribed changes respecting the
    cost of borrowing or the loan agreement; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} any other prescribed information, at the prescribed
    time and place and in the prescribed form and manner.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Additional disclosure re other loans

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where a foreign company enters into or has entered
  into an arrangement, including a line of credit, for the making of a
  loan in respect of which the disclosure requirements of section 599
  apply and the loan is not one in respect of which subsection (1)
  or (3) applies, the foreign company shall, in addition to disclosing
  the costs of borrowing, disclose to the person, in accordance with the
  regulations,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any charges or penalties described in paragraph
    (1)(b);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} particulars of the person's rights and obligations;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any charges for which the person is responsible
    under the arrangement;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} at the prescribed time and place and in the
    prescribed form and manner, any prescribed changes respecting the
    cost of borrowing or the loan agreement; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} any other prescribed information, at the prescribed
    time and place and in the prescribed form and manner.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 601
- 1997, c. 15, s. 308
- 2012, c. 5, s. 147
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-601-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 601"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Renewal statement

**[[601.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.1 .sectionLabel}** If a foreign
company makes a loan in respect of which the disclosure requirements of
section 599 apply and the loan is secured by a mortgage on real
property, the foreign company shall disclose to the borrower, at the
prescribed time and place and in the prescribed form and manner, any
information that is prescribed respecting the renewal of the loan.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 309
- 2012, c. 5, s. 148
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-601.1-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 601.1"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disclosure in advertising

**[[601.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.2 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
authorize the publication, issue or appearance of any advertisement in
Canada relating to arrangements referred to in subsection 601(4), loans,
credit cards, payment cards or charge cards, offered to natural persons
by a foreign company, and purporting to disclose prescribed information
about the cost of borrowing or about any other matter unless the
advertisement discloses prescribed information at the prescribed time
and place and in the prescribed form and manner.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1997, c. 15, s. 309
- 2012, c. 5, s. 148
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-601.2-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 601.2"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disclosing borrowing costs --- advances

**[[602]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602 .sectionLabel}** If regulations have
