been made respecting the manner in which the cost of borrowing is to be
disclosed in respect of an advance on the security or against the cash
surrender value of a policy, a foreign company shall not make such an
advance unless the cost of borrowing, as calculated and expressed in
accordance with the regulations, has, at the prescribed time and place
and in the prescribed form and manner, been disclosed by the foreign
company or otherwise as prescribed to the policyholder at or before the
time when the advance is made.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 602
- 2007, c. 6, s. 279
- 2012, c. 5, s. 148
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-602-20070420.html "Link to previous version of section 602"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations re borrowing costs

**[[603]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603 .sectionLabel}** The Governor in Council
may make regulations

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} respecting the time and place at which, and the form
  and manner in which, a foreign company is to disclose to a borrower

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the cost of borrowing,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} any rebate of the cost of borrowing, and

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} any other information relating to a loan,
    arrangement, credit card, payment card or charge card referred to in
    section 601;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} respecting the contents of any statement disclosing
  the cost of borrowing and other information required to be disclosed
  by a foreign company to a borrower;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} respecting the manner of calculating the cost of
  borrowing;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} respecting the circumstances under which the cost of
  borrowing is to be expressed as an amount in dollars and cents;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} specifying any class of loans that are not to be
  subject to section 598.1, subsection 599(1) or 601(1) or (4) or
  section 601.1 or 601.2 or the regulations or any specified provisions
  of the regulations;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} specifying any class of advances that are not to be
  subject to section 602 or the regulations or any specified provisions
  of the regulations;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} respecting the time and place at which, and the form
  and manner in which, any rights, obligations, charges or penalties
  referred to in sections 598.1 to 602 are to be disclosed;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} prohibiting the imposition of any charge or penalty
  referred to in section 601 or providing that the charge or penalty, if
  imposed, will not exceed a prescribed amount;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} respecting the nature or amount of any charge or
  penalty referred to in paragraph 601(1)(b), (3)(a) or (4)(a) and the
  costs of the foreign company that may be included or excluded in the
  determination of the charge or penalty;

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} respecting the method of calculating the amount of
  rebate of the cost of borrowing, or the portion of the cost of
  borrowing referred to in subparagraph 601(1)(a)(ii);

- [(k)]{.lawlabel} respecting advertisements made by a foreign company
  regarding arrangements referred to in subsection 601(4), loans, credit
  cards, payment cards or charge cards;

- [(l)]{.lawlabel} respecting the renewal of loans; and

- [(m)]{.lawlabel} respecting such other matters or things as are
  necessary to carry out the purposes of sections 598.1 to 602.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 603
- 1997, c. 15, s. 310
- 2012, c. 5, s. 149
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-603-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 603"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Complaints]{.HTitleText2} {#h-265128 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Procedures for dealing with complaints

- **[[604]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  foreign company shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} establish procedures for dealing with complaints
    made by persons having requested or received products or services in
    Canada from the foreign company;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} designate one of its officers or employees in
    Canada, or an agent in Canada, to be responsible for implementing
    those procedures; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} designate one or more of its officers or employees
    in Canada, or agents in Canada, to receive and deal with those
    complaints.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Procedures to be filed with
  Commissioner

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A foreign company shall file with the Commissioner a
  copy of its procedures established under paragraph (1)(a).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}How procedures to be made available

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A foreign company shall make its procedures
  established under paragraph (1)(a) available

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} on its websites through which products or services
    are offered in Canada; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in written format to be sent to any person who
    requests them.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information on contacting Agency

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A foreign company shall also make prescribed
  information on how to contact the Agency available whenever it makes
  its procedures established under paragraph (1)(a) available under
  subsection (3).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 604
- 1997, c. 15, s. 311
- 2001, c. 9, s. 444
- 2007, c. 6, s. 280
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-604-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 604"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation to be member of complaints
body

**[[604.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.1 .sectionLabel}** In any province, if
there is no law of the province that makes a foreign company subject to
the jurisdiction of an organization that deals with complaints made by
persons having requested or received products or services in the
province from a foreign company, the foreign company shall be a member
of an organization in Canada that is not controlled by it and that deals
with those complaints that have not been resolved to the satisfaction of
the persons under procedures established under paragraph 604(1)(a).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 444
- 2007, c. 6, s. 281
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-604.1-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 604.1"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information on contacting Agency

- **[[605]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  foreign company shall, in accordance with the regulations, at the
  prescribed time and place and in the prescribed form and manner,
  provide a person in Canada requesting or receiving a product or
  service in Canada from it with prescribed information on how to
  contact the Agency if the person has a complaint about an arrangement
  referred to in subsection 601(3), a payment, credit or charge card
  referred to in subsection 601(2), the disclosure of or manner of
  calculating the cost of borrowing in respect of a loan repayable in
  Canada or an advance on the security or against the cash surrender
  value of a policy, or about any other obligation of the foreign
  company under a consumer provision.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Commissioner shall prepare a report, to be
  included in the report referred to in section 34 of the [Financial
  Consumer Agency of Canada Act](/eng/acts/F-11.1), respecting

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} procedures for dealing with complaints established
    by foreign companies pursuant to paragraph 604(1)(a); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number and nature of complaints that have been
    brought to the attention of the Agency by persons who have requested
    or received a product or service from a foreign company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 605
- 1997, c. 15, s. 312
- 2001, c. 9, s. 444
- 2007, c. 6, s. 282
- 2012, c. 5, s. 150
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-605-20070420.html "Link to previous version of section 605"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Miscellaneous]{.HTitleText2} {#h-265158 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prepayment protected

- **[[606]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-606 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  foreign company shall not include in its assets in Canada any loan to
  a natural person that is repayable in Canada, the terms of which
  prohibit prepayment of the money advanced or any instalment thereon
  before its due date.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Non-application of subsection (1)

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of a loan

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} that is secured by a mortgage on real property; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} that is made for business purposes and the
    principal amount of which is more than \$100,000 or such other
    amount as may be prescribed.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 606
- 1997, c. 15, s. 313
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations --- activities

**[[606.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-606.1 .sectionLabel}** The Governor in
Council may make regulations respecting any matters involving a foreign
company's dealings, or its employees' or representatives' dealings, with
customers or the public, including

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} what a foreign company may or may not do in carrying
  out any of the activities in which it is permitted to engage, or in
  providing any of the services that it may provide, under this Act and
  any ancillary, related or incidental activities or services; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the time and place at which and the form and manner
  in which any of those activities are to be carried out or any of those
  services are to be provided.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2009, c. 2, s. 286
- 2012, c. 5, s. 151
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-606.1-20090312.html "Link to previous version of section 606.1"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations re customer information

**[[607]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-607 .sectionLabel}** The Governor in Council
may make regulations

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} requiring a foreign company to establish procedures
  regarding the collection, retention, use and disclosure of any
  information about its customers in Canada or any class of customers in
  Canada;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} requiring a foreign company to establish procedures
  for dealing with complaints made by a customer in Canada about the
  collection, retention, use or disclosure of information about the
  customer;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} respecting the disclosure by a foreign company of
  information relating to the procedures referred to in paragraphs (a)
  and (b);

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} requiring a foreign company to designate the officers
  and employees of the company who are responsible for

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} implementing the procedures referred to in
    paragraph (b), and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} receiving and dealing with complaints made by a
    customer, in Canada, of the foreign company about the collection,
    retention, use or disclosure of information about the customer;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} requiring a foreign company to report information
  relating to

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} complaints made by its customers in Canada about
    the collection, retention, use or disclosure of information, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} its actions taken to deal with the complaints; and

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} defining [[information]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm},
  [[collection]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} and
  [[retention]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} for the purposes of paragraphs (a)
  to (e) and the regulations made under those paragraphs.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 607
- 1997, c. 15, s. 314
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations re disclosure

**[[607.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-607.1 .sectionLabel}** The Governor in
Council may, subject to any other provisions of this Act relating to the
disclosure of information, make regulations respecting the disclosure of
information by foreign companies or any prescribed class of foreign
companies, including regulations respecting

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the information that must be disclosed, including
  information relating to

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} any product or service or prescribed class of
    products or services offered by them,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} any of their policies, procedures or practices
    relating to the offer by them of any product or service or
    prescribed class of products or services,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} anything they are required to do or to refrain
    from doing under a consumer provision, and

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} any other matter that may affect their dealings,
    or their employees' or representatives' dealings, with customers or
    the public;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the time and place at which, the form and manner in
  which and the persons to whom information is to be disclosed; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the content and form of any advertisement by foreign
  companies or any prescribed class of foreign companies relating to any
  matter referred to in paragraph (a).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 445
- 2007, c. 6, s. 283
- 2012, c. 5, s. 152
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-607.1-20070420.html "Link to previous version of section 607.1"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Provisions that do not apply

- **[[607.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-607.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Sections 598 to 607.1 do not apply
  in respect of a foreign company if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the order made under subsection 574(1) in respect
    of the foreign company restricts it to the reinsurance of risks
    within a class of insurance specified in the order;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the foreign company has provided the Commissioner
    with a declaration stating that it is not dealing with a prescribed
    group of consumers; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} after providing the declaration, the foreign
    company continues to not deal with that prescribed group.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice if action taken that causes
  provisions to apply

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The foreign company must give notice to the
  Commissioner if it subsequently deals with the prescribed group
  referred to in the declaration.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 6, s. 284
:::

### [Adequacy of Assets]{.HTitleText2} {#h-265209 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Adequacy of assets and appropriate forms
of liquidity

- **[[608]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-608 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  foreign company shall maintain in Canada an adequate margin of assets
  over liabilities in respect of its insurance business in Canada as
  shown in the records it is required to maintain under section 647, and
  adequate and appropriate forms of liquidity, and shall comply with any
  regulations in relation to an adequate margin of assets over
  liabilities and adequate and appropriate forms of liquidity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Liabilities

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), the liabilities
  in Canada of a foreign company include the reserve included in the
  annual return required under subsection 665(2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Guidelines

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent may make guidelines in respect of
  any matter referred to in paragraph 610(1)(a).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directives

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Even though a foreign company is complying with
  regulations made under paragraph 610(1)(a) or guidelines made under
  subsection (3), the Superintendent may, by order, direct the foreign
  company to increase the margin of its assets over its liabilities that
  it is required to maintain in Canada or to provide additional
  liquidity in the forms and the amounts that the Superintendent
  requires.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Compliance

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A foreign company shall comply with an order made
  under subsection (4) within the time that the Superintendent specifies
  in the order.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 608
- 1996, c. 6, s. 87
- 2001, c. 9, s. 446
- 2007, c. 6, s. 286
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-608-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 608"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Adequacy of assets

- **[[609]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-609 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  foreign company shall, in relation to each class of insurance risks
  that it is permitted to insure, maintain in Canada, in accordance with
  the regulations, assets the total value of which shall be determined
  in accordance with the regulations.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Guidelines

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent may make guidelines in respect
  of any matter referred to in paragraph 610(1)(b).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directives

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Even though a foreign company is complying with
  regulations made under paragraph 610(1)(b) or guidelines made under
  subsection (1.1), the Superintendent may, by order, direct the foreign
  company to increase the assets that it is required to maintain in
  Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Compliance

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A foreign company shall comply with an order made
  under subsection (2) within such time as the Superintendent specifies
  therein.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 609
- 1996, c. 6, s. 88
- 2007, c. 6, s. 287
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-609-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 609"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

- **[[610]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-610 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Governor in Council may make regulations

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} respecting the maintenance by foreign companies of
    an adequate margin of assets in Canada over liabilities in Canada
    and adequate and appropriate forms of liquidity;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} respecting the maintenance by foreign companies of
    assets in Canada of a particular value, which regulations may make
    special provision for associations and exchanges;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} prescribing rules for determining the value,
    location and protection of the assets of foreign companies;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} governing the determination of the reserves to be
    included in the liabilities of foreign companies;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} determining the method of calculating the value of
    interests of foreign companies in real property for the purposes of
    section 618; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} prescribing anything that is required or authorized
    by this Part to be prescribed.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulation may provide for discretion

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A regulation made pursuant to paragraph (1)(b) may
  provide that the Superintendent may, by order, determine the matters
  or exercise the discretion that the regulations may specify.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 610
- 2001, c. 9, s. 447(E)
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Vesting in trust

- **[[611]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-611 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  assets that a foreign company is required to maintain in Canada under
  sections 608 and 609 and the regulations made under section 610 must
  be vested in trust in a Canadian financial institution chosen by the
  foreign company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conflict of interest

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No Canadian financial institution may be appointed as
  trustee if at the time of the appointment there is a material conflict
  of interest between the Canadian financial institution's role as
  trustee and any other of its roles.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Trust deed

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A trust deed must be approved by the Superintendent
  before it is entered into.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Determination of value of assets in
  Canada

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent shall determine the value at which
  assets shall be accepted for the purposes of this Part.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Maintenance of value of assets in
  Canada

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The trustee of a foreign company may deal with the
  assets in Canada in any manner provided for in the trust deed, but in
  such a way that the value for the purposes of this Part of the assets
  in Canada does not fall below that required by this Part.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 611
- 2001, c. 9, s. 448
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Inadmissible assets

- **[[612]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-612 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  foreign company may not vest in trust

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} securities issued by or debt obligations of the
    foreign company or one of its affiliates;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} real property, or ground rents or mortgages on real
    property, situated outside Canada;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} shares or ownership interests, however designated,
    in any entity in such number as would constitute a substantial
    investment in that entity without regard to any shares or ownership
    interests held by any other entity; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a loan made in Canada on the security of
    residential property in Canada for the purpose of purchasing,
    renovating or improving that property, if the amount of the loan,
    together with the amount then outstanding of any mortgage having an
    equal or prior claim against the property, would exceed 80 per cent
    of the value of the property at the time of the loan.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite paragraphs (1)(a) and (c), a foreign company
  may vest in trust a substantial investment in an entity that is
  primarily engaged in

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} holding, managing or otherwise dealing with real
    property; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} holding shares or ownership interests in entities
    that are primarily engaged in any of the activities referred to in
    paragraph (a).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Idem

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Notwithstanding paragraph (1)(d), a foreign company
  may vest in trust

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a loan made or guaranteed under the [National
    Housing Act](/eng/acts/N-11) or any other Act of Parliament by or
    pursuant to which a different limit on the value of property on the
    security of which the foreign company may make a loan is
    established;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a loan if repayment of the amount of the loan that
    exceeds the maximum amount set out in subsection (1) is guaranteed
    or insured by a government agency or a private insurer approved by
    the Superintendent; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} securities issued or guaranteed by an entity that
    are secured on any residential property, whether in favour of a
    trustee or otherwise, or a loan made by the foreign company to the
    entity against the issue of such securities.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 612
- 1993, c. 34, s. 85(E)
- 1997, c. 15, s. 315
- 2007, c. 6, s. 290
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-612-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 612"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Investments]{.HTitleText2} {#h-265278 .Subheading}

#### [Definitions and Application]{.HTitleText3} {#h-265279 .Subheading}

Definition of [[commercial loan]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

**[[613]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-613 .sectionLabel}** In sections 615 to 620,
[[commercial loan]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} has the same meaning as in Part
IX.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Non-application

- **[[614]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-614
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Sections 612 and 615 to 620 do not
  apply in respect of assets of a foreign company held in relation to a
  segregated fund maintained pursuant to section 593.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exclusion of liabilities of segregated
  funds

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A reference in sections 615 to 619 and in regulations
  made under section 620 to the assets in Canada or the liabilities in
  Canada of a foreign company does not include liabilities of the
  foreign company for the policies and amounts in respect of which a
  segregated fund is maintained pursuant to section 593.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 614
- 2007, c. 6, s. 291
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-614-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 614"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [General Constraints on Investments]{.HTitleText3} {#h-265289 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Investment standards

- **[[615]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-615 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  foreign company shall, in respect of its assets in Canada, establish
  and adhere to investment and lending policies, standards and
  procedures that a reasonable and prudent person would apply in respect
  of a portfolio of investments and loans to avoid undue risk of loss
  and obtain a reasonable return.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Resolution of board of directors

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A foreign company to which subsection 573(4) applies
  shall, during the period of ninety days following the coming into
  force of this Part, file with the Superintendent a certified copy of a
  resolution of its board of directors establishing the investment and
  lending policies, standards and procedures referred to in subsection
  (1).

#### [Commercial Lending by Foreign Life Companies]{.HTitleText3} {#h-265295 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Lending limit --- foreign life companies

- **[[616]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-616 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  total accepted value of commercial loans vested in trust by a foreign
  life company for the classes of life insurance, accident and sickness
  insurance, credit protection insurance and other approved products
  insurance shall not at any time exceed the prescribed percentage of
  the value of its assets in Canada for those classes.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Lending limit --- foreign composite
  companies

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The total accepted value of the commercial loans and
  loans to natural persons vested in trust by a foreign life company for
  the classes of insurance other than life insurance, accident and
  sickness insurance, credit protection insurance and other approved
  products insurance, shall not at any time exceed the prescribed
  percentage of the value of its assets in Canada for those classes.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 616
- 2007, c. 6, s. 292
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-616-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 616"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Consumer and Commercial Lending by Foreign Property and Casualty Companies and Foreign Marine Companies]{.HTitleText3} {#h-265303 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Lending limit --- foreign property and
casualty companies and foreign marine companies

**[[617]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-617 .sectionLabel}** The total accepted
value of the commercial loans and loans to natural persons vested in
trust by a foreign property and casualty company, or a foreign marine
company, shall not at any time exceed the prescribed percentage of the
value of its assets in Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 617
- 2007, c. 6, s. 292
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-617-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 617"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Real Property]{.HTitleText3} {#h-265308 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limit on total property interest ---
foreign life companies

- **[[618]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-618 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  total accepted value of interests in real property vested in trust by
  a foreign life company for the classes of life insurance, accident and
  sickness insurance, credit protection insurance and other approved
  products insurance shall not at any time exceed the prescribed
  percentage of the value of its assets in Canada for those classes.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limit on total property interest ---
  foreign composite companies

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The total accepted value of interests in real
  property vested in trust by a foreign life company for the classes of
  insurance other than life insurance, accident and sickness insurance,
  credit protection insurance and other approved products insurance,
  shall not at any time exceed the prescribed percentage of the value of
  its assets in Canada for those classes.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limit on total property interest ---
  foreign property and casualty companies and foreign marine companies

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The total accepted value of interests in real
  property vested in trust by a foreign property and casualty company,
  or a foreign marine company, shall not at any time exceed the
  prescribed percentage of the value of its assets in Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 618
- 2007, c. 6, s. 292
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-618-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 618"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Equities]{.HTitleText3} {#h-265318 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limit on equity acquisitions --- foreign
life companies

- **[[619]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-619 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  total accepted value of the participating shares, within the meaning
  of Part IX, of any body corporate and any ownership interests,
  howsoever designated, in any unincorporated entities vested in trust
  by a foreign life company for the classes of life insurance, accident
  and sickness insurance, credit protection insurance and other approved
  products insurance shall not at any time exceed the prescribed
  percentage of the value of its assets in Canada for those classes.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limit on equity acquisitions ---
  foreign composite companies

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The total accepted value of the participating shares,
  within the meaning of Part IX, of any body corporate and any ownership
  interests, howsoever designated, in any unincorporated entities vested
  in trust by a foreign life company for the classes of insurance, other
  than life insurance, accident and sickness insurance, credit
  protection insurance and other approved products insurance, shall not
  at any time exceed the prescribed percentage of the value of its
  assets in Canada for those classes.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limit on equity acquisitions ---
  foreign property and casualty companies and foreign marine companies

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The total accepted value of the participating shares,
  within the meaning of Part IX, of any body corporate and any ownership
  interests, howsoever designated, in any unincorporated entities vested
  in trust by a foreign property and casualty company, or a foreign
  marine company, shall not at any time exceed the prescribed percentage
  of the value of its assets in Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 619
- 2007, c. 6, s. 292
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-619-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 619"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Aggregate Limit]{.HTitleText3} {#h-265328 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limit on aggregate value

**[[620]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-620 .sectionLabel}** The aggregate value of
each of the following total accepted values, namely,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the total accepted values referred to in subsections
  618(1) and 619(1),

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the total accepted values referred to in subsections
  618(2) and 619(2), and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the total accepted values referred to in subsections
  618(3) and 619(3),

shall not at any time exceed the respective prescribed percentage of the
value of the assets in Canada.

### [Self-dealing]{.HTitleText2} {#h-265335 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibited transactions

**[[621]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-621 .sectionLabel}** A foreign company shall
not vest in trust any asset in accordance with this Part if the asset
was acquired through a transaction that at the time of acquisition would
be prohibited for a company pursuant to section 521.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

**[[622]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-622 .sectionLabel}** A foreign company may
vest in trust an asset if the asset was acquired through a transaction
described in any of sections 524 to 533 and

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the transaction was entered into on terms and
  conditions that are at least as favourable to the foreign company as
  market terms and conditions, as defined in subsection 534(2); and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the foreign company files a notice of the vesting
  with the Superintendent on vesting the asset in trust.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 622
- 1997, c. 15, s. 316
- 2007, c. 6, s. 293
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-622-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 622"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Actuaries]{.HTitleText2} {#h-265344 .Subheading}

#### [Appointment]{.HTitleText3} {#h-265345 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointment of actuary

- **[[623]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-623 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  foreign company that is required by this Act to provide the
  Superintendent with the report of an actuary shall without delay
  appoint a person to be the actuary of the foreign company for its
  insurance business in Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of appointment

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A foreign company shall, forthwith after the
  appointment of an actuary of the foreign company, notify the
  Superintendent in writing of the appointment.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 623
- 1997, c. 15, s. 317
:::

**[[624]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-624 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed, 1997, c.
15, s. 318\]]{.Repealed}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Chief agent

- **[[624.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-624.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The chief agent of a foreign company
  may not be appointed as or hold the position of actuary of the foreign
  company unless authorized in writing by the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duration of authorization

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An authorization under subsection (1) ceases to be in
  effect on the day specified therein but not later than the day that is
  six months after it is issued, and a person appointed or holding the
  position of actuary pursuant to the authorization shall not hold that
  position after that day.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1996, c. 6, s. 88.1
:::

#### [Vacancies]{.HTitleText3} {#h-265361 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Revocation of appointment

- **[[625]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-625 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  foreign company may revoke the appointment of the actuary of the
  foreign company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of revocation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A foreign company shall, forthwith after the
  revocation of the appointment of the actuary of the foreign company,
  notify the Superintendent in writing of the revocation.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ceasing to hold office

- **[[626]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-626 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person ceases to hold office as the actuary of a foreign company when

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person resigns as actuary of the foreign
    company;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person ceases to be an actuary;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the person dies; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the appointment of the person as actuary of the
    foreign company is revoked by the foreign company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effective date of resignation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The resignation of an actuary of a foreign company
  becomes effective at the time a written resignation is sent to the
  foreign company or at the time specified in the resignation, whichever
  is later.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Filling vacancy

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where a vacancy occurs in the office of actuary of a
  foreign company, the foreign company shall forthwith notify the
  Superintendent in writing of the vacancy and fill the vacancy.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 626
- 1997, c. 15, s. 319
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Statement of actuary

- **[[627]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-627 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  actuary of a foreign company who resigns or whose appointment is
  revoked shall submit to the chief agent of the foreign company and the
  Superintendent a written statement of the circumstances and reasons
  why the actuary resigned or why, in the actuary's opinion, the
  actuary's appointment was revoked.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duty of replacement actuary

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where an actuary of a foreign company resigns or the
  appointment of an actuary of a foreign company is revoked, no person
  shall accept an appointment or consent to be appointed as actuary of
  the foreign company before requesting and receiving from the other
  actuary the written statement referred to in subsection (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A person may accept an appointment or consent to be
  appointed as actuary of a company if no reply is received from the
  other actuary within fifteen days after a request under subsection (2)
  is made.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of non-compliance

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Unless subsection (3) applies, an appointment as
  actuary of a company is void if subsection (2) is not complied with.

#### [Valuations and Reports]{.HTitleText3} {#h-265389 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Right to information

- **[[628]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-628 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  the request of the actuary of a foreign company, the present or former
  directors, chief agents, officers, employees or representatives of the
  foreign company shall, to the extent that they are reasonably able to
  do so,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} permit access to such records held by the foreign
    company, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} provide such information and explanations

  as are, in the opinion of the actuary, necessary to enable the actuary
  to perform the duties of actuary of the foreign company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No civil liability

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who in good faith makes an oral or written
  communication under subsection (1) shall not be liable in any civil
  action arising from having made the communication.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Actuary's valuation

- **[[629]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-629 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  actuary of a foreign company shall value

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the actuarial and other policy liabilities of the
    foreign company with respect to its insurance business in Canada as
    at the end of a financial year; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any other matters specified in any direction that
    may be made by the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Actuarial practices

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An actuary's valuation shall be in accordance with
  generally accepted actuarial practice with such changes as may be
  determined by the Superintendent and any additional directions that
  may be made by the Superintendent.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Superintendent may appoint actuary

- **[[629.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-629.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent may appoint an
  actuary to value the matters referred to in paragraph 629(1)(a) or (b)
  in relation to a foreign company if the Superintendent is of the
  opinion that the appointment is necessary. That actuary may not be an
  actuary of the foreign company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Expenses payable by foreign company

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The expenses incurred in carrying out a valuation
  under subsection (1) are payable by the foreign company on being
  approved in writing by the Superintendent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1996, c. 6, s. 89
- 1997, c. 15, s. 320
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report to chief agent

**[[630]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-630 .sectionLabel}** The actuary of a
foreign company shall meet with the chief agent of the foreign company
at least once during each financial year in order to report, in
accordance with generally accepted actuarial practice, on the financial
position of the insurance business in Canada of the foreign company,
and, where a direction that may be made by the Superintendent so
specifies, the expected future financial condition of the foreign
company as it affects its insurance business in Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 630
- 1997, c. 15, s. 321
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report to chief agent

- **[[631]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-631 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  actuary of a foreign company shall report in writing to the chief
  agent of the foreign company any matters that have come to the
  actuary's attention in the course of carrying out the duties of the
  actuary and that in the actuary's opinion have material adverse
  effects on the financial condition of the foreign company with respect
  to its insurance business in Canada and require rectification.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transmission of report

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An actuary of a foreign company who makes a report
  under subsection (1) shall forthwith provide a copy of it to the
  directors of the foreign company and to any person designated by them
  as responsible for the insurance business in Canada of the foreign
  company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Failure to take action

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where, in the opinion of the actuary of the foreign
  company, suitable action is not taken to rectify the matters referred
  to in subsection (1), the actuary shall forthwith provide a copy of
  the report to the Superintendent and advise the chief agent of the
  foreign company that the actuary has done so.

#### [Qualified Privilege]{.HTitleText3} {#h-265423 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Qualified privilege for statements

- **[[632]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-632 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Any
  oral or written statement or report made under this Act by the actuary
  or former actuary of a foreign company has qualified privilege.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No civil liability

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The actuary or a former actuary of a foreign company
  who in good faith makes an oral or written statement under subsection
  627(1) or section 631 shall not be liable in any civil action seeking
  indemnification for damages attributable to the actuary or former
  actuary having made the statement or report.

### [Auditors]{.HTitleText2} {#h-265429 .Subheading}

#### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-265430 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

**[[632.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-632.1 .sectionLabel}** In sections 634 to
643, the expressions [[firm of accountants]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} and
[[member]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} have the meanings assigned to those
expressions by section 336.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 6, s. 294
:::

#### [Appointment]{.HTitleText3} {#h-265435 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointment of auditor

- **[[633]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-633 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  foreign company shall appoint an auditor for its insurance business in
  Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of appointment

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A foreign company shall, forthwith after the
  appointment of the auditor of the foreign company, notify the
  Superintendent in writing of the appointment.

#### [Qualifications]{.HTitleText3} {#h-265441 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Qualification of auditor

- **[[634]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-634 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  natural person or firm of accountants is qualified to be an auditor of
  a foreign company if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a natural person, the person is an
    accountant who

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} is a member in good standing of an institute or
      association of accountants incorporated by or under an Act of the
      legislature of a province,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} has at least five years experience at a senior
      level in performing audits of a financial institution,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} is ordinarily resident in Canada, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} is independent of the foreign company and its
      chief agent; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a firm of accountants, the member of
    the firm jointly designated by the firm and the foreign company to
    conduct the audit of the foreign company on behalf of the firm is
    qualified in accordance with paragraph (a).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Independence

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} independence is a question of fact; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a person is deemed not to be independent of a
    foreign company if that person, a business partner of that person or
    a firm of accountants of which that person is a member

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} is a business partner, director, officer or
      employee of the foreign company or of any affiliate of the foreign
      company or is a business partner of any director, officer or
      employee of the foreign company or of any affiliate of the foreign
      company,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} beneficially owns or controls, directly or
      indirectly, a material interest in the shares of the foreign
      company or of any affiliate of the foreign company, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} has been a liquidator, trustee in bankruptcy,
      receiver or receiver and manager of any affiliate of the foreign
      company within the two years immediately preceding the person's
      proposed appointment as auditor of the foreign company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Business partners

  [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (2),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of the appointment of a natural person
    as the auditor of a foreign company, a business partner of the
    person includes a shareholder of the business partner; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of the appointment of a firm of
    accountants as the auditor of a foreign company, a business partner
    of a member of the firm includes another member of the firm and a
    shareholder of the firm or of a business partner of the member.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of designation

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Within 15 days after the appointment of a firm of
  accountants as auditor of a foreign company, the foreign company and
  the firm of accountants shall jointly designate a member of the firm
  who meets the qualifications described in subsection (1) to conduct
  the audit of the foreign company on behalf of the firm and the foreign
  company shall without delay notify the Superintendent in writing of
  the designation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}New designation

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where for any reason a member of a firm of
  accountants designated pursuant to subsection (3) ceases to conduct
  the audit of the foreign company, the foreign company and the firm of
  accountants may jointly designate another member of the same firm of
  accountants who meets the qualifications described in subsection (1)
  to conduct the audit of the foreign company and the foreign company
  shall forthwith notify the Superintendent in writing of the
  designation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed vacancy

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} In any case where subsection (4) applies and a
  designation is not made pursuant to that subsection within thirty days
  after the designated member ceases to conduct the audit of the foreign
  company, there shall be deemed to be a vacancy in the office of
  auditor of the foreign company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 634
- 2005, c. 54, s. 302
- 2007, c. 6, s. 295(E)
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-634-20061128.html "Link to previous version of section 634"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duty to resign

- **[[635]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-635 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  auditor who ceases to be qualified under section 634 shall resign
  forthwith after the auditor, where the auditor is a natural person, or
  any member of the firm of accountants, where the auditor is a firm of
  accountants, becomes aware that the auditor or the firm has ceased to
  be so qualified.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disqualification order

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Any interested person may apply to a court for an
  order declaring that an auditor of a foreign company has ceased to be
  qualified under section 634 and declaring the office of auditor to be
  vacant.

#### [Vacancies]{.HTitleText3} {#h-265475 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Revocation of appointment

- **[[636]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-636 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  foreign company may revoke the appointment of an auditor of the
  foreign company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Idem

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent may at any time revoke the
  appointment of an auditor made under subsection (3) or section 633 or
  638 by notice in writing signed by the Superintendent and sent by
  registered mail to the auditor and to the chief agent of the foreign
  company addressed to the usual place of business of the auditor and
  the chief agent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Filling vacancy

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A vacancy created by the revocation of the
  appointment of an auditor under subsection (1) shall be filled by the
  foreign company under section 638.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ceasing to hold office

- **[[637]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-637 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  auditor of a foreign company ceases to hold office when

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the auditor resigns;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the auditor, where the auditor is a natural person,
    dies; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the appointment of the auditor is revoked by the
    foreign company or the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effective date of resignation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The resignation of an auditor becomes effective at
  the time a written resignation is sent to the foreign company or at
  the time specified in the resignation, whichever is later.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Filling vacancy

- **[[638]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-638
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where a vacancy occurs in the office
  of auditor of a foreign company, the foreign company shall forthwith
  fill the vacancy.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Where Superintendent may fill vacancy

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where the foreign company fails to fill a vacancy in
  accordance with subsection (1), the Superintendent may fill the
  vacancy.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Designation of member of firm

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where the Superintendent has, pursuant to subsection
  (2), appointed a firm of accountants to fill a vacancy, the
  Superintendent shall designate the member of the firm who is to
  conduct the audit on behalf of the firm.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Statement of auditor

**[[639]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-639 .sectionLabel}** An auditor of a foreign
company who

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} resigns, or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} receives a notice or otherwise learns that another
  person is to be appointed in the auditor's stead, whether because of
  the auditor's resignation or revocation of appointment,

shall submit to the chief agent of the foreign company and the
Superintendent a written statement giving the reasons for the
resignation or the reasons why the auditor opposes any proposed action.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duty of replacement auditor

- **[[640]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-640
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where an auditor of a foreign
  company has resigned or the appointment of an auditor has been
  revoked, no person or firm shall accept an appointment or consent to
  be appointed as auditor of the foreign company until the person or
  firm has requested and received from the other auditor a written
  statement of the circumstances and reasons why the other auditor
  resigned or why, in the other auditor's opinion, the other auditor's
  appointment was revoked.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Notwithstanding subsection (1), a person or firm may
  accept an appointment or consent to be appointed as auditor of a
  foreign company if, within fifteen days after a request under that
  subsection is made, no reply from the other auditor is received.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of non-compliance

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Unless subsection (2) applies, an appointment as
  auditor of a foreign company is void if subsection (1) has not been
  complied with.

#### [Examinations and Reports]{.HTitleText3} {#h-265510 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Auditor's examination

- **[[641]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-641 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  auditor of a foreign company shall make such examination as the
  auditor considers necessary to enable the auditor to report on the
  annual return required by subsection 665(2) and on other financial
  statements required by this Act to be filed with the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Auditing standards

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The auditor's examination referred to in
  subsection (1) shall, except as otherwise specified by the
  Superintendent, be conducted in accordance with generally accepted
  auditing standards, the primary source of which is the Handbook of the
  Chartered Professional Accountants of Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reliance on actuary

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An auditor of a foreign company may, in conducting
  the examination referred to in subsection (1), use the valuation by
  the actuary of the foreign company of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the actuarial and other policy liabilities of the
    foreign company as at the end of a financial year; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the increase in the actuarial liabilities of the
    foreign company for a financial year.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 641
- 2017, c. 26, s. 62
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-641-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 641"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Right to information

- **[[642]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-642 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  the request of the auditor of a foreign company, the present or former
  chief agents, directors, officers, employees or representatives of the
  foreign company shall, to the extent that they are reasonably able to
  do so,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} permit access to such records, assets and security
    held by the foreign company, or any entity in which the foreign
    company has a substantial investment, in respect of the insurance
    business in Canada of the foreign company, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} provide such information and explanations

  as are, in the opinion of the auditor, necessary to enable the auditor
  to perform the duties of auditor of the foreign company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No civil liability

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who in good faith makes an oral or written
  communication under subsection (1) shall not be liable in any civil
  action arising from having made the communication.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Auditor's report and extended examination

- **[[643]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-643 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Superintendent may, in writing, require that the auditor of a foreign
  company report to the Superintendent on the extent of the auditor's
  procedures in the examination of the annual return and may, in
  writing, require that the auditor enlarge or extend the scope of that
  examination or direct that any other particular procedure be performed
  in any particular case, and the auditor shall comply with any such
  requirement of the Superintendent and report to the Superintendent
  thereon.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Special examination

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In respect of the insurance business in Canada of a
  foreign company, the Superintendent may, in writing, require that the
  auditor of the foreign company make a particular examination relating
  to the adequacy of the procedures adopted by the foreign company for
  the safety of its creditors and policyholders, or any other
  examination that, in the Superintendent's opinion, the public interest
  may require, and report to the Superintendent on the examination.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Idem

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} In respect of the insurance business in Canada of a
  foreign company, the Superintendent may direct that a special audit of
  the foreign company be made if, in the opinion of the Superintendent,
  it is so required and may appoint for that purpose an accountant or a
  firm of accountants qualified pursuant to subsection 634(1) to be an
  auditor of the foreign company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Expenses payable by foreign company

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The expenses entailed by any examination or audit
  referred to in any of subsections (1) to (3) are payable by the
  foreign company on being approved in writing by the Superintendent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 643
- 2007, c. 6, s. 296
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-643-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 643"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Auditor's report

- **[[644]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-644 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  auditor of a foreign company shall, not later than the earlier of May
  31 in each year and the day in each year on which the auditor is
  required to make a report under the laws under which the foreign
  company is incorporated, make a report to the chief agent in writing
  on the annual return required by subsection 665(2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Auditor's opinion

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In each report required under subsection (1), the
  auditor shall state whether, in the auditor's opinion, the annual
  return presents fairly, in accordance with the accounting principles
  referred to in subsection 331(4), the financial position of the
  insurance business in Canada of the foreign company as at the end of
  the financial year to which it relates and the results of the
  operations and changes in the financial position of the insurance
  business in Canada of the foreign company for that financial year.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Auditor's remarks

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} In each report referred to in subsection (2), the
  auditor shall include such remarks as the auditor considers necessary
  when

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the examination has not been made in accordance
    with the auditing standards referred to in subsection 641(2);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the annual return has not been prepared on a basis
    consistent with that of the preceding financial year; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the annual return does not present fairly, in
    accordance with the accounting principles referred to in subsection
    331(4), the financial position of the insurance business in Canada
    of the foreign company as at the end of the financial year to which
    it relates or the results of the operations or changes in the
    financial position of the foreign company for that financial year.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 644
- 1994, c. 26, s. 44(F)
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report to chief agent

- **[[645]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-645 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} It
  is the duty of the auditor of a foreign company to report in writing
  to the chief agent of the foreign company any transactions or
  conditions in respect of the insurance business in Canada of the
  foreign company that have come to the auditor's attention affecting
  the well-being of the foreign company that in the auditor's opinion
  are not satisfactory and require rectification and, without
  restricting the generality of the foregoing, the auditor shall, as
  occasion requires, make a report to the chief agent in respect of
  transactions in respect of the insurance business in Canada of the
  foreign company that have come to the auditor's attention and that in
  the auditor's opinion have not been within the powers of the foreign
  company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transmission of report

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where the auditor of a foreign company makes a report
  under subsection (1), the auditor shall, at the time of transmitting
  the report to the chief agent provide the Superintendent with a copy
  of the report.

#### [Qualified Privilege]{.HTitleText3} {#h-265558 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Qualified privilege for statements

**[[646]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-646 .sectionLabel}** Any oral or written
statement or report made under this Act by the auditor or a former
auditor of a foreign company has qualified privilege.

### [Records]{.HTitleText2} {#h-265561 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Records

- **[[647]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-647 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  foreign company shall prepare and maintain

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} copies of all orders of the Superintendent in
    relation to the foreign company;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} accounting records respecting its insurance
    business in Canada; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} with respect to its insurance business in Canada,
    records showing, for each customer of, or claimant under a policy
    issued by, the foreign company, the amount owing to the foreign
    company and the nature of the liabilities of the foreign company to
    the customer or claimant.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Standards for record keeping

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The records described in paragraphs (1)(b) and (c)
  shall be kept in a manner that enables the chief agent of the foreign
  company to provide the Superintendent with the information required by
  section 664 and with the annual return required by subsection 665(2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Place of records

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The records described in subsection (1) shall be kept
  at the chief agency of the foreign company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection 268(1.1), subsection (3) does
  not apply to a foreign company incorporated or formed otherwise in a
  country or territory other than Canada in which a trade agreement
  listed in Schedule IV of the [Bank Act](/eng/acts/B-1.01) is
  applicable or that is a subsidiary of a regulated foreign entity.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 647
- 2001, c. 9, s. 449
- 2007, c. 6, s. 297
- [2020, c. 1, s. 177](#1238259-1311966){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1238259-1311966.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-647-20100101.html "Link to previous version of section 647"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Examination of books

**[[648]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-648 .sectionLabel}** The Superintendent may
examine the books, vouchers, receipts and other documents of a foreign
company relating to its insurance business in Canada for the purpose of
verifying information provided to the Superintendent pursuant to section
664 or 665.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Sections 266 to 270 apply

**[[649]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-649 .sectionLabel}** Section 266 to 270
apply, with such modifications as the circumstances require, to foreign
companies.

### [Release of Assets]{.HTitleText2} {#h-265578 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application for release of assets in
Canada

**[[650]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-650 .sectionLabel}** A foreign company that
proposes to cease to insure in Canada risks may apply to the
Superintendent for the release of its assets in Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 650
- 2007, c. 6, s. 298
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-650-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 650"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conditions of release

**[[651]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-651 .sectionLabel}** Except as otherwise
provided in this Act, the Superintendent may, by order, authorize the
release of the assets in Canada of a foreign company if the foreign
company

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} has, in respect of its policies,

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} obtained their surrender,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} transferred them,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} caused itself to be reinsured, on an assumption
    basis, against the risks undertaken under them, or

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} otherwise discharged its liabilities under them,
    or provided for their discharge in a manner satisfactory to the
    Superintendent;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} has discharged all of its obligations, other than
  liabilities under its policies, or provided for them in a manner
  satisfactory to the Superintendent; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} has provided the Superintendent with proof of the
  publication, for four consecutive weeks, in the [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) and in at least one newspaper of
  general circulation at or near the place where the chief agency of the
  foreign company is situated, of a notice that it will apply to the
  Superintendent for the release of its assets in Canada on a day
  specified in the notice, which must be at least six weeks after the
  date of the notice, and calling on its creditors and policyholders
  opposing that release to file their opposition with the Superintendent
  on or before the day.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 651
- 1996, c. 6, s. 90
- 2007, c. 6, s. 298
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-651-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 651"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Release of assets to liquidator

**[[652]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-652 .sectionLabel}** Despite sections 650
and 651, the assets in Canada of a foreign company that is in
liquidation may, on the order of any court having jurisdiction under the
[Winding-up and Restructuring Act](/eng/acts/W-11), be released to the
liquidator.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 652
- 2007, c. 6, s. 298
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-652-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 652"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Revocation of order

**[[653]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-653 .sectionLabel}** The Superintendent may
revoke the order made under subsection 574(1) in respect of a foreign
company if in the opinion of the Superintendent the foreign company is
not insuring in Canada risks, or if the foreign company does not

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} provide information to the Superintendent as required
  by section 664;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} provide the annual return to the Superintendent as
  required by section 665;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} permit the examination authorized by section 648 or
  674; or

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} provide any information in its possession or control
  that is requested for the purpose of any such examination.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 653
- 2007, c. 6, s. 298
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-653-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 653"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed revocation

**[[654]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-654 .sectionLabel}** An order made under
subsection 574(1) in respect of a foreign company is deemed to be
revoked when an order is made under section 651 or 652 authorizing the
release of its assets in Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 654
- 1996, c. 6, s. 167
- 2007, c. 6, s. 298
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-654-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 654"){.PITLink}
:::

**[[655]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-655 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed, 2007, c.
6, s. 298\]]{.Repealed}

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-655-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 655"){.PITLink}
:::

## [PART XIV]{.HLabel1}[Provincial Companies]{.HTitleText1} {#h-265611 .Part}

### [Application]{.HTitleText2} {#h-265612 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application of other provisions

- **[[656]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-656
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Divisions XII to XIV of Part VI,
  other than subsection 330(2), Parts VIII to XI and Part XX apply to
  provincial companies.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Idem

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsections 15(1) and (2), sections 254 to 256 and
  subsections 268(1) and (2) apply, with such modifications as the
  circumstances require, to every provincial company for which an order
  for the commencement and carrying on of business under this Part has
  been made to the same extent that they are applicable to, or in
  respect of, a company, but to the extent to which any provision
  referred to in this section would effect an enlargement, in any
  respect, of the corporate powers or rights of any provincial company
  under its incorporating instrument, that provision does not apply to
  the provincial company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 656
- 2005, c. 54, s. 303
- [2020, c. 1, s. 178](#1238261-1311969){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1238261-1311969.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-656-20110601.html "Link to previous version of section 656"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Order to Commence and Carry on Business]{.HTitleText2} {#h-265620 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Making of order

- **[[657]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-657
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Forthwith on the coming into force
  of this Part, the Superintendent shall make an order approving the
  commencement and carrying on of business by every provincial company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Order to specify classes of insurance

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An order approving the commencement and carrying on
  of business by a provincial company under subsection (1) shall specify
  the classes of insurance risks that the provincial company is
  permitted to insure pursuant to section 443, as applied by subsection
  656(1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conditions of order

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An order approving the commencement and carrying on
  of business by a provincial company may contain such conditions or
  limitations that are consistent with this Act and relate to the
  business of the provincial company as the Superintendent deems
  expedient and necessary.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Variations

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} In respect of the order approving the commencement
  and carrying on of business by a provincial company, the
  Superintendent may at any time, by further order,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} specify additional classes of insurance risks that
    the provincial company is permitted to insure pursuant to section
    443, as applied by subsection 656(1),

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} make the order subject to such conditions or
    limitations that are consistent with this Act and that relate to the
    business of the provincial company as the Superintendent deems
    expedient and necessary, or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} amend or revoke any authorization contained in the
    order or any condition or limitation to which the order is subject,

  but before making any such further order the Superintendent shall
  provide the provincial company with an opportunity to make
  representations regarding that further order.

- [(5) and (6)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 1996, c. 6, s. 91\]]{.Repealed}

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 657
- 1996, c. 6, s. 91
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Policies and procedures --- integrity or
security

**[[657.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-657.1 .sectionLabel}** A provincial
company shall establish and adhere to policies and procedures to protect
itself against threats to its integrity or security, including foreign
interference.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2023, c. 26, s. 583](#1411073-1437432){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1411073-1437432.html"
  role="button"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Undertaking

**[[658]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-658 .sectionLabel}** Every provincial
company for which an order has been made under section 657 shall provide
the Superintendent with an undertaking in such form as may be required
by the Superintendent that it will, so long as the order is not
rescinded, submit to and comply with all of the provisions of this Act
applicable to it in respect of the classes of insurance specified in the
order and any conditions or limitations set out in the order.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transitional

**[[659]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-659 .sectionLabel}** A provincial company
that deposited securities with the Receiver General pursuant to section
76 or 82 of the Canadian and British Insurance Companies Act shall apply
for the return of those securities within such period following the
coming into force of this section as may be fixed by order of the
Governor in Council.

### [Duties of Directors]{.HTitleText2} {#h-265641 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointment of actuary, auditor and
conduct review committee

- **[[660]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-660 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  directors of a provincial company shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} appoint the actuary of the provincial company
    forthwith after the Superintendent makes an order for the provincial
    company under section 657;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} appoint the auditor of the provincial company for
    the purposes of this Act forthwith after the Superintendent makes an
    order for the provincial company under section 657; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} establish a conduct review committee consisting of
    at least three directors who are not affiliated with the company,
    determined in accordance with regulations made under section 170.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duties of conduct review committee

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The conduct review committee of a provincial company
  shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} require the management of the provincial company to
    establish procedures for complying with Part XI;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} review those procedures and their effectiveness in
    ensuring that the provincial company is complying with Part XI;

  - [(b.1)]{.lawlabel} if an insurance holding company or a bank holding
    company that is widely held has a significant interest in any class
    of shares of the provincial company, establish policies for entering
    into transactions referred to in section 528.1; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} review the practices of the provincial company to
    ensure that any transactions with related parties of the provincial
    company that may have a material effect on the stability or solvency
    of the provincial company are identified.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Provincial company report to
  Superintendent

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A provincial company shall report to the
  Superintendent on the mandate and responsibilities of the conduct
  review committee and the procedures established by the committee under
  paragraph (2)(a).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Committee report to directors

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} After each meeting of the conduct review committee of
  a provincial company, the committee shall report to the directors of
  the provincial company on all transactions and other matters reviewed
  by the committee.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors' report to Superintendent

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Within ninety days after the end of each financial
  year, the directors of a provincial company shall report to the
  Superintendent on the proceedings of the conduct review committee and
  on all transactions and other matters reviewed by the committee during
  the year.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 660
- 2001, c. 9, s. 450
:::

### [Corporate Records]{.HTitleText2} {#h-265662 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Provincial company to provide information

- **[[661]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-661 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  provincial company shall provide the Superintendent with such
  information, material and evidence, at such times and in such form, as
  the Superintendent may require, and, without limiting the generality
  of the foregoing, the information, material and evidence shall include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} copies of its incorporating instrument and the
    by-laws of the provincial company; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} copies of any of the records referred to in section
    662.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Names of directors and auditors

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A provincial company shall, within thirty days after
  each annual meeting of the provincial company, provide the
  Superintendent with a return showing

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name, residence and citizenship of each
    director holding office immediately following the meeting;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the mailing address of each director holding office
    immediately following the meeting;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the bodies corporate of which each director
    referred to in paragraph (a) is an officer or director and the firms
    of which each director is a member;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the affiliation, within the meaning of section 170,
    with the provincial company of each director referred to in
    paragraph (a);

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the names of the directors referred to in
    paragraph (a) who are officers or employees of the provincial
    company or any affiliate of the provincial company, and the
    positions they occupy;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the name of each committee of the provincial
    company on which each director referred to in paragraph (a) serves;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the date of expiration of the term of each director
    referred to in paragraph (a); and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the name, address and date of appointment of the
    auditor of the provincial company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Changes

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any information relating to a director or auditor
    of a provincial company shown in the latest return made to the
    Superintendent under subsection (2), other than information referred
    to in paragraph (2)(c) or (d), becomes inaccurate or incomplete,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a vacancy in the position of auditor of the
    provincial company occurs or is filled by another person, or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a vacancy on the board of directors of the
    provincial company occurs or is filled,

  the provincial company shall forthwith provide the Superintendent with
  such information as is required to maintain the return in a complete
  and accurate form.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Records

- **[[662]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-662 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  provincial company shall prepare and maintain adequate

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} corporate accounting records; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} records showing, for each customer of, or claimant
    under a policy issued by, the provincial company, the amount owing
    to the provincial company and the nature of the liabilities of the
    provincial company to the customer or claimant.

- Definition of [[records]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1),
  [[records]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes similar records required by
  law to be maintained by the provincial company before the coming into
  force of this section.

## [PART XV]{.HLabel1}[Regulation of Companies, Societies, Foreign Companies and Provincial Companies --- Superintendent]{.HTitleText1} {#h-265691 .Part}

### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText2} {#h-265692 .Subheading}

Definition of [société]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"}

**[[663]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-663 .sectionLabel}** In the French version
of this Part, [société]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"} means a
[société]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"}, [société de
secours]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"}, [société
étrangère]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"} or [société
provinciale]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"} within the meaning of section
2.

### [Supervision]{.HTitleText2} {#h-265695 .Subheading}

#### [Returns]{.HTitleText3} {#h-265696 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Required information

**[[664]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-664 .sectionLabel}** A company, society,
foreign company or provincial company shall provide the Superintendent
with such information, at such times and in such form as the
Superintendent may require.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Annual return --- companies, societies
and provincial companies

- **[[665]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-665 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
