  company, society or provincial company shall prepare annually a return
  of the condition and affairs of the company, society or provincial
  company as at the end of each financial year, showing its assets and
  liabilities and its income and expenditures during that financial year
  together with such other information as the Superintendent may deem
  necessary.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Annual return: foreign companies

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A foreign company, in respect of its insurance
  business in Canada, shall prepare annually a return of the condition
  and affairs of the foreign company as at the end of each financial
  year, showing its assets and liabilities and its income and
  expenditures during that financial year together with such other
  information as the Superintendent may deem necessary.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2007, c. 6, s. 299\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Accounting principles

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The annual return shall be prepared in accordance
  with the accounting principles referred to in subsection 331(4).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 665
- 1997, c. 15, s. 322
- 2007, c. 6, s. 299
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-665-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 665"){.PITLink}
:::

**[[666]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-666 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed, 1997, c.
15, s. 323\]]{.Repealed}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Valuation of actuarial and other policy
liabilities

- **[[667]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-667 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  liabilities of a company, society, foreign company or provincial
  company shown in its annual return must include as a reserve the value
  of the actuarial and other policy liabilities and other matters
  determined under section 365 or section 629.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report of actuary

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The actuary of a company, society, foreign company or
  provincial company shall make, and the company, society, foreign
  company or provincial company shall file with its annual return, a
  report in a form determined by the Superintendent on the reserve
  referred to in subsection (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Auditor's remarks

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The auditor of a company, society or provincial
  company shall attach to the annual return a report stating whether, in
  the auditor's opinion, the annual return presents fairly, in
  accordance with accounting principles referred to in subsection
  331(4), the financial position of the company, society or provincial
  company as at the end of the financial year to which it relates and
  the results of the operations and changes in the financial position of
  the company, society or provincial company for that financial year.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Idem

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} In each report referred to in subsection (3), the
  auditor shall include such remarks as the auditor considers necessary
  when

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the examination has not been made in accordance
    with the auditing standards referred to in subsection 346(2);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the annual return has not been prepared on a basis
    consistent with that of the preceding financial year; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the annual return does not present fairly, in
    accordance with the accounting principles referred to in subsection
    331(4), the financial position of the company, society or provincial
    company as at the end of the financial year to which it relates or
    the results of the operations or changes in the financial position
    of the company, society or provincial company for that financial
    year.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Names of directors and auditors

- **[[668]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-668 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  company shall, within thirty days after each annual meeting of the
  company, provide the Superintendent with a return showing

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name, residence and citizenship of each
    director holding office immediately following the meeting;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the mailing address of each director holding office
    immediately following the meeting;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the bodies corporate of which each director
    referred to in paragraph (a) is an officer or director and the firms
    of which each director is a member;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the affiliation, within the meaning of section 170,
    with the company of each director referred to in paragraph (a);

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the names of the directors referred to in
    paragraph (a) who are officers or employees of the company or any
    affiliate of the company, and the positions they occupy;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the name of each committee of the company on which
    each director referred to in paragraph (a) serves;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the date of expiration of the term of each director
    referred to in paragraph (a); and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the name, address and date of appointment of the
    auditor of the company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Changes

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any information relating to a director or auditor
    of a company shown in the latest return made to the Superintendent
    under subsection (1), other than information referred to in
    paragraph (1)(c) or (d), becomes inaccurate or incomplete,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a vacancy in the position of auditor of the company
    occurs or is filled by another person, or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a vacancy on the board of directors of the company
    occurs or is filled,

  the company shall forthwith provide the Superintendent with such
  information as is required to maintain the return in a complete and
  accurate form.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Copy of by-laws

**[[669]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-669 .sectionLabel}** A company shall send to
the Superintendent, within thirty days after the coming into effect of a
by-law or an amendment to a by-law, a copy of the by-law or amendment.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 669
- 2001, c. 9, s. 452
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registers

- **[[670]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-670 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Superintendent shall cause a register to be maintained in respect of
  each company or society for which an order has been made approving the
  commencement and carrying on of business.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Register for company

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The register in respect of a company shall contain a
  copy of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the incorporating instrument of the company; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the information referred to in paragraphs
    668(1)(a), (c) and (e) to (h) contained in the latest return
    provided to the Superintendent by the company as required by section
    668.

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2001, c. 9, s. 453\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Register for society

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The register in respect of a society shall contain a
  copy of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the incorporating instrument of the society; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the information referred to in paragraphs 549(1)(a)
    and (c) to (f) contained in the latest return provided to the
    Superintendent by the society as required by subsection 549(1).

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2001, c. 9, s. 453\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Form

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The register may be maintained in

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a bound or loose-leaf form or a photographic film
    form; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a system of mechanical or electronic data
    processing or any other information storage device that is capable
    of reproducing any required information in intelligible written form
    within a reasonable time.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Access

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Persons are entitled to reasonable access to the
  register and may make copies of or take extracts from the information
  in it.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Evidence

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} A statement containing information in the register
  and purporting to be certified by the Superintendent is admissible in
  evidence in all courts as proof, in the absence of evidence to the
  contrary, of the facts stated in the statement without proof of the
  appointment or signature of the Superintendent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 670
- 1997, c. 15, s. 324
- 2001, c. 9, s. 453
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Certificate

**[[670.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-670.1 .sectionLabel}** On the application
of a company or society that has been incorporated by a special Act of
Parliament, the Superintendent may issue a certificate stating that it
was incorporated by a special Act of Parliament, and may include with
the certificate any information in the Superintendent's possession that
relates to the company's or society's incorporation.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2012, c. 5, s. 153
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Production of information and documents

- **[[671]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-671 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Superintendent may, by order, direct a person who controls a company
  or any entity that is affiliated with a company to provide the
  Superintendent with any information or documents that may be specified
  in the order if the Superintendent believes that the production of the
  information or documents is necessary in order to be satisfied that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the provisions of this Act are being duly observed
    and that the company is in a sound financial condition; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the company has adequate policies and procedures to
    protect itself against threats to its integrity or security.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Time

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Any person to whom a direction has been issued under
  subsection (1) shall provide the information or documents specified in
  the order within the time specified in the order and, where the order
  does not specify a time, the person shall provide the information or
  documents within a reasonable time.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exemption

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of an entity
  that controls a company or is affiliated with a company where that
  entity is a financial institution regulated

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} by or under an Act of Parliament; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} by or under an Act of the legislature of a province
    where the Superintendent has entered into an agreement with the
    appropriate official or public body responsible for the supervision
    of financial institutions in that province concerning the sharing of
    information on such financial institutions.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 671
- [2023, c. 26, s. 584](#1411075-1415729){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1411075-1415729.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-671-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 671"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Confidential information

- **[[672]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-672
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 673, all
  information regarding the business or affairs of a company, society,
  foreign company or provincial company, or regarding a person dealing
  with any of them, that is obtained by the Superintendent, or by any
  person acting under the direction of the Superintendent, as a result
  of the administration or enforcement of any Act of Parliament, and all
  information prepared from that information, is confidential and shall
  be treated accordingly.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disclosure permitted

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Nothing in subsection (1) prevents the Superintendent
  from disclosing any information

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} to any government agency or body that regulates or
    supervises financial institutions, for purposes related to that
    regulation or supervision,

  - [(a.01)]{.lawlabel} to any other agency or body that regulates or
    supervises financial institutions, for purposes related to that
    regulation or supervision,

  - [(a.1)]{.lawlabel} to any compensation association designated by
    order of the Minister pursuant to subsection 449(1) or 591(1), for
    purposes related to its operation, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} to the Deputy Minister of Finance or any officer of
    the Department of Finance authorized in writing by the Deputy
    Minister of Finance or to the Governor of the Bank of Canada or any
    officer of the Bank of Canada authorized in writing by the Governor
    of the Bank of Canada, for the purposes of policy analysis related
    to the regulation of financial institutions,

  if the Superintendent is satisfied that the information will be
  treated as confidential by the agency, body or person to whom it is
  disclosed.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 672
- 1996, c. 6, s. 92
- 1997, c. 15, s. 325
- 2001, c. 9, s. 454
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

**[[672.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-672.1 .sectionLabel}** The Governor in
Council may make regulations prohibiting, limiting or restricting the
disclosure by companies, societies, foreign companies or provincial
companies of prescribed supervisory information.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1999, c. 28, s. 126
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Evidentiary privilege

- **[[672.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-672.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Prescribed supervisory information
  shall not be used as evidence in any civil proceedings and is
  privileged for that purpose.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No testimony or production

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall by an order of any court, tribunal or
  other body be required in any civil proceedings to give oral testimony
  or to produce any document relating to any prescribed supervisory
  information.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exceptions to subsection (1)

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the Minister, the Superintendent or the Attorney
    General of Canada may, in accordance with the regulations, if any,
    use prescribed supervisory information as evidence in any
    proceedings; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a company, a society, a foreign company or a
    provincial company may, in accordance with the regulations, if any,
    use prescribed supervisory information as evidence in any
    proceedings in relation to the administration or enforcement of this
    Act or the [Winding-up and Restructuring Act](/eng/acts/W-11) that
    are commenced by the company, the society, the foreign company, the
    provincial company, the Minister, the Superintendent or the Attorney
    General of Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exceptions to subsections (1) and (2)

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsections (1) and (2) and section 39.1 of
  the [Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
  Act](/eng/acts/O-2.7), a court, tribunal or other body may, by order,
  require the Minister, the Superintendent, a company, a society, a
  foreign company or a provincial company to give oral testimony or to
  produce any document relating to any prescribed supervisory
  information in any civil proceedings in relation to the administration
  or enforcement of this Act that are commenced by the Minister, the
  Superintendent, the Attorney General of Canada, the company, the
  society, the foreign company or the provincial company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No waiver

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The disclosure of any prescribed supervisory
  information, other than under subsection (3) or (4), does not
  constitute a waiver of the privilege referred to in subsection (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council may, for the purposes of
  subsection (3), make regulations respecting the circumstances in which
  prescribed supervisory information may be used as evidence.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2015, c. 36, s. 236
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No waiver

- **[[672.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-672.3
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For greater certainty, the
  disclosure by a company, society, foreign company or provincial
  company --- or by a person who controls one or by an entity that is
  affiliated with one --- to the Superintendent of any information that
  is subject to a privilege under the law of evidence, solicitor-client
  privilege or the professional secrecy of advocates and notaries or to
  litigation privilege does not constitute a waiver of any of those
  privileges or that secrecy.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No disclosure

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent shall not disclose any information
  referred to in subsection (1) to any person whose powers, duties or
  functions include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the investigation or prosecution of an offence
    under any Act of Parliament or of the legislature of a province; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the investigation of, or conduct of proceedings in
    respect of, a violation under an Act referred to in paragraph (a).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2018, c. 27, s. 172
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disclosure by Superintendent

- **[[673]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-673 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Superintendent shall disclose, at such times and in such manner as the
  Minister may determine, such information obtained by the
  Superintendent under this Act as the Minister considers ought to be
  disclosed for the purposes of the analysis of the financial condition
  of a company, society, foreign company or provincial company and that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is contained in returns filed pursuant to the
    Superintendent's financial regulatory reporting requirements in
    respect of companies, societies, foreign companies or provincial
    companies; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} has been obtained as a result of an industry-wide
    or sectoral survey conducted by the Superintendent in relation to an
    issue or circumstances that could have an impact on the financial
    condition of companies, societies, foreign companies or provincial
    companies.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prior consultation required

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall consult with the Superintendent
  before making any determination under subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 673
- 1994, c. 26, s. 45
- 1996, c. 6, s. 93
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disclosure by a company, etc.

- **[[673.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-673.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A company, society, foreign company
  or provincial company shall make available to the public such
  information concerning

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the compensation of its executives, as that
    expression is defined by the regulations, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} its business and affairs for the purposes of the
    analysis of its financial condition,

  in such form and manner and at such times as may be required by or
  pursuant to such regulations as the Governor in Council may make for
  the purpose.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exemption by regulation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Paragraph (1)(a) does not apply to a company,
  society, foreign company or provincial company that is within such
  class or classes of companies, societies, foreign companies or
  provincial companies as may be prescribed.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1996, c. 6, s. 93
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exceptions to disclosure

**[[673.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-673.2 .sectionLabel}** Subject to any
regulations made under section 489 or 607, no information obtained by a
company, society, foreign company or provincial company regarding any of
its customers shall be disclosed or made available under subsection
673(1) or section 673.1.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1996, c. 6, s. 93
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report respecting disclosure

**[[673.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-673.3 .sectionLabel}** The Superintendent
shall prepare a report, to be included in the report referred to in
section 40 of the [Office of the Superintendent of Financial
Institutions Act](/eng/acts/O-2.7), respecting the disclosure of
information by companies, societies, foreign companies or provincial
companies and describing the state of progress made in enhancing the
disclosure of information in the financial services industry.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1996, c. 6, s. 93
- 2001, c. 9, s. 455
:::

#### [Inspection of Companies, Societies, Foreign Companies and Provincial Companies]{.HTitleText3} {#h-265848 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Examination of companies, etc.

- **[[674]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-674 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Superintendent, from time to time, but at least once in each calendar
  year, shall make or cause to be made any examination and inquiry into
  the business and affairs of each company, society, foreign company and
  provincial company that the Superintendent considers to be necessary
  or expedient to determine whether the company, society, foreign
  company or provincial company is complying with the provisions of this
  Act, whether the company, society or provincial company or the
  insurance business in Canada of the foreign company is in a sound
  financial condition and whether the company, society or provincial
  company has adequate policies and procedures to protect itself against
  threats to its integrity or security or the foreign company has
  adequate policies and procedures to protect itself against threats to
  its integrity or security in relation to its business in Canada. After
  the conclusion of each examination and inquiry, the Superintendent
  shall report on it to the Minister.

- [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2023, c. 26, s. 585\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Examination need not be made annually

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If, in the opinion of the Superintendent, the
  circumstances so warrant in the case of a company, a provincial
  company or a foreign company that is not a fraternal benefit society,
  the examination and inquiry may be made less frequently than annually
  but not less frequently than triennially.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Examination need not be made annually

  [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} If, in the opinion of the Superintendent, the
  circumstances so warrant in the case of a society or a foreign company
  that is a fraternal benefit society, the examination and inquiry may
  be made less frequently than annually.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Access to records of company

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent or a person acting under the
  Superintendent's direction

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} has a right of access to any records, cash, assets
    and security held by or on behalf of a company, society or
    provincial company or held by or on behalf of a foreign company in
    respect of its insurance business in Canada; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} may require the directors, officers, auditor and
    actuary of a company, society or provincial company or the chief
    agent, actuary and auditor of a foreign company to provide
    information and explanations, to the extent that they are reasonably
    able to do so, in respect of the condition and affairs of the
    company, society, foreign company or provincial company or any
    entity in which it has a substantial investment.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 674
- 2001, c. 9, s. 456
- [2023, c. 26, s. 585](#1411077-1415732){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1411077-1415732.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-674-20230622.html "Link to previous version of section 674"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Power of Superintendent on inquiry

**[[675]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-675 .sectionLabel}** The Superintendent has
all the powers of a person appointed as a commissioner under Part II of
the [Inquiries Act](/eng/acts/I-11) for the purpose of obtaining
evidence under oath, and may delegate those powers to any person acting
under the Superintendent's direction.

### [Remedial Powers]{.HTitleText2} {#h-265864 .Subheading}

#### [Prudential Agreements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-265865 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prudential agreement

**[[675.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-675.1 .sectionLabel}** The Superintendent
may enter into an agreement, called a "prudential agreement", with

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a company, society or provincial company for the
  purposes of implementing any measure designed to maintain or improve
  its safety and soundness or establishing adequate policies and
  procedures to protect it against threats to its integrity or security;
  or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a foreign company for the purposes of implementing
  any measure designed to protect the interests of its policyholders and
  creditors in relation to its insurance business in Canada or
  establishing adequate policies and procedures to protect it against
  threats to its integrity or security in relation to its business in
  Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 457
- [2023, c. 26, s. 586](#1411083-1415737){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1411083-1415737.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-675.1-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 675.1"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Directions of Compliance]{.HTitleText3} {#h-265870 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Superintendent's directions to companies,
etc.

- **[[676]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-676
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where, in the opinion of the
  Superintendent, a company, society, foreign company or provincial
  company, or a person with respect to a company, society, foreign
  company or provincial company,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is committing, or is about to commit, an act that
    is an unsafe or unsound practice in conducting the business of the
    company, society, foreign company or provincial company, or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is pursuing or is about to pursue any course of
    conduct that is an unsafe or unsound practice in conducting the
    business of the company, society, foreign company or provincial
    company,

  the Superintendent may direct the company, society, foreign company,
  provincial company or person to

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} cease or refrain from committing the act or
    pursuing the course of conduct, and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} perform such acts as in the opinion of the
    Superintendent are necessary to remedy the situation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directions --- policies and procedures

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} If, in the opinion of the Superintendent, a
  company, society, or provincial company does not have adequate
  policies and procedures to protect itself against threats to its
  integrity or security, or a foreign company does not have adequate
  policies and procedures to protect itself against threats to its
  integrity or security in relation to its business in Canada, the
  Superintendent may direct the company, society, foreign company or
  provincial company to take any measures that in the opinion of the
  Superintendent are necessary to remedy the situation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Opportunity for representations

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), no direction shall be
  issued to a company, society, foreign company, provincial company or
  person under subsection (1) or (1.1) unless the company, society,
  foreign company, provincial company or person is provided with a
  reasonable opportunity to make representations in respect of the
  matter.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Temporary direction

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If, in the opinion of the Superintendent, the length
  of time required for representations to be made under subsection (2)
  might be prejudicial to the public interest, the Superintendent may
  make a temporary direction with respect to the matters referred to in
  paragraphs (1)(a) and (b) or subsection (1.1) having effect for a
  period of not more than 15 days.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Idem

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 677, a temporary direction under
  subsection (3) continues to have effect after the expiration of the
  fifteen day period referred to in that subsection if no
  representations are made to the Superintendent within that period or,
  if representations have been made, the Superintendent notifies the
  company, society, foreign company, provincial company or person that
  the Superintendent is not satisfied that there are sufficient grounds
  for revoking the direction.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 676
- [2023, c. 26, s. 587](#1411085-1415746){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1411085-1415746.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-676-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 676"){.PITLink}
:::

**[[677]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-677 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed, 1996, c.
6, s. 94\]]{.Repealed}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Court enforcement

- **[[678]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-678
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where a company, society, foreign
  company, provincial company or person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is contravening or has failed to comply with a
    prudential agreement entered into under section 675.1 or a direction
    of the Superintendent issued to the company, society, foreign
    company, provincial company or person under subsection 676(1),
    (1.1.) or (3),

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is contravening this Act, or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} has omitted to do any thing under this Act that is
    required to be done by or on the part of the company, society,
    foreign company, provincial company or person,

  the Superintendent may, in addition to any other action that may be
  taken under this Act, apply to a court for an order requiring the
  company, society, foreign company, provincial company or person to
  comply with the prudential agreement or direction, cease the
  contravention or do any thing that is required to be done, and on such
  application the court may so order and make any other order it thinks
  fit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appeal

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An appeal from a decision of a court under
  subsection (1) lies in the same manner, and to the same court, as an
  appeal from any other order of the court.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 678
- 2001, c. 9, s. 458
- [2023, c. 26, s. 588](#1411087-1415748){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1411087-1415748.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-678-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 678"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Disqualification and Removal]{.HTitleText3} {#h-265897 .Subheading}

Meaning of [[senior officer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

**[[678.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-678.01 .sectionLabel}** In sections 678.1
and 678.2, [[senior officer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the chief
executive officer, secretary, treasurer, controller or actuary of a
company, society or provincial company, or any other officer reporting
directly to its board of directors or chief executive officer.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 459
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application

- **[[678.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-678.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This section applies only in respect
  of a company, society or provincial company

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} that has been notified by the Superintendent that
    this section applies to it where the company, society or provincial
    company is subject to measures designed to maintain or improve its
    safety and soundness, which measures

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} have been specified by the Superintendent by way
      of conditions or limitations in respect of the order approving the
      commencement and carrying on of its business, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} are contained in a prudential agreement entered
      into under section 675.1 or an undertaking given by the company,
      society or provincial company to the Superintendent; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} that is the subject of a direction made under
    section 676 or an order made under subsection 515(3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information to be provided

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A company, society or provincial company shall
  provide the Superintendent with the name of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} each person who has been nominated for election or
    appointment as a member of its board of directors,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} each person who has been selected by the company,
    society or provincial company for appointment as a senior officer,
    and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} each person who is newly elected as a director of
    the company, society or provincial company at a meeting of
    shareholders and policyholders and who was not proposed for election
    by anyone involved in the management of the company, society or
    provincial company,

  together with such other information about the background, business
  record and experience of the person as the Superintendent may require.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}When information to be provided

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The information required by subsection (2) shall be
  provided to the Superintendent

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at least thirty days prior to the date or proposed
    date of the election or appointment or within such shorter period as
    the Superintendent may allow; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a person referred to in paragraph
    (2)(c), within fifteen days after the date of the election of the
    person.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disqualification or removal

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent is of the opinion that, on the
  basis of the competence, business record, experience, conduct or
  character of a person, he or she is not suitable to hold that
  position, the Superintendent may, by order

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a person referred to in paragraph
    (2)(a) or (b), disqualify the person from being elected or appointed
    as a director of the company, society or provincial company or from
    being appointed as a senior officer; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a person referred to in paragraph
    (2)(c), remove the person from office as a director of the company,
    society or provincial company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Risk of prejudice

  [(4.1)]{.lawlabel} In forming an opinion under subsection (4), the
  Superintendent must consider whether the interests of the
  policyholders and creditors of the company, society or provincial
  company would likely be prejudiced if the person were to take office
  or continue to hold office, as the case may be.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Representations may be made

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent must in writing notify the person
  concerned and the company, society or provincial company of any action
  that the Superintendent proposes to take under subsection (4) and must
  afford them an opportunity within 15 days after the date of the
  notice, or within any longer period that the Superintendent allows, to
  make representations to the Superintendent in relation to the matter.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Where an order has been made under subsection (4)

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} disqualifying a person from being elected or
    appointed to a position, the person shall not be, and the company,
    society or provincial company shall not permit the person to be,
    elected or appointed to the position; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} removing a director from office, the person shall
    not continue to hold, and the company, society or provincial company
    shall not permit the person to continue to hold, office as a
    director.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1996, c. 6, s. 95
- 2001, c. 9, s. 460
- 2007, c. 6, s. 300
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-678.1-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 678.1"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Removal of directors or senior officers

- **[[678.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-678.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent may, by order,
  remove a person from office as a director or senior officer of a
  company, society or provincial company if the Superintendent is of the
  opinion that the person is not suitable to hold that office

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} on the basis of the competence, business record,
    experience, conduct or character of the person; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} because the person has contravened or, by action or
    negligence, has contributed to the contravention of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} this Act or the regulations made under it,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a direction made under section 676,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} an order made under subsection 515(3),

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a condition or limitation in respect of the
      order approving the commencement and carrying on of business by
      the company, society or provincial company, or

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} a prudential agreement entered into under section
      675.1 or an undertaking given by the company, society or
      provincial company to the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Risk of prejudice

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In forming an opinion under subsection (1), the
  Superintendent must consider whether the interests of the
  policyholders and creditors of the company, society or provincial
  company have been or are likely to be prejudiced by the person's
  holding office as a director or senior officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Representations may be made

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent must in writing notify the person
  concerned and the company, society or provincial company of any
  removal order that the Superintendent proposes to make under
  subsection (1) and must afford them an opportunity within 15 days
  after the date of the notice, or within any longer period that the
  Superintendent allows, to make representations to the Superintendent
  in relation to the matter.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Suspension

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent is of the opinion that the
  public interest may be prejudiced by the director or senior officer
  continuing to exercise the powers or carry out the duties and
  functions of that office during the period for making representations,
  the Superintendent may make an order suspending the director or senior
  officer. The suspension may not extend beyond 10 days after the
  expiration of that period.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of order

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent shall, without delay, notify the
  director or senior officer, as the case may be, and the company,
  society or provincial company of a removal order or suspension order.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Consequences of removal order

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} The director or senior officer, as the case may be,
  ceases to hold that office as of the date the removal order is made or
  any later date specified in the order.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appeal

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} The director or senior officer, as the case may be,
  or the company, society or provincial company, as the case may be,
  may, within 30 days after the date of receipt of notice of the removal
  order under subsection (5), or within any longer period that the Court
  allows, appeal the matter to the Federal Court.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers of Federal Court

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} The Federal Court, in the case of an appeal, may
  dismiss the appeal or set aside the removal order.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Order not stayed by appeal

  [(9)]{.lawlabel} A removal order is not stayed by an appeal.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 461
- 2007, c. 6, s. 301
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-678.2-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 678.2"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application

- **[[678.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-678.3
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This section applies only in respect
  of a foreign company

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} that has been notified by the Superintendent that
    this section applies to it where the foreign company is subject to
    measures designed to protect the interests of its policyholders and
    creditors in respect of its insurance business in Canada, which
    measures

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} have been specified by the Superintendent by way
      of conditions or limitations in respect of the order made under
      subsection 574(1) in respect of the foreign company, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} are contained in a prudential agreement entered
      into under section 675.1 or an undertaking given by the foreign
      company to the Superintendent; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} that is the subject of a direction made under
    section 676 or an order made under subsection 608(4) or 609(2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information to be provided

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A foreign company shall provide the Superintendent
  with the name of any person who has been selected by the foreign
  company for appointment as chief agent together with such other
  information about the background, business record and experience of
  the person as the Superintendent may require.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}When information to be provided

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The information required by subsection (2) shall be
  provided to the Superintendent at least 30 days prior to the date of
  the appointment or within any shorter period that the Superintendent
  may allow.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disqualification

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent is of the opinion that, on the
  basis of the competence, business record, experience, conduct or
  character of a person, he or she is not suitable to hold the position
  of chief agent, the Superintendent may, by order, disqualify the
  person from being appointed to that office.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Risk of prejudice

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} In forming an opinion under subsection (4), the
  Superintendent must consider whether the interests of the
  policyholders and creditors of the foreign company in respect of its
  insurance business in Canada would likely be prejudiced if the person
  were to take office.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Representations may be made

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent must in writing notify the person
  concerned and the foreign company of an order that the Superintendent
  proposes to make under subsection (4) and must afford them an
  opportunity within 15 days after the date of the notice, or within any
  longer period that the Superintendent allows, to make representations
  to the Superintendent in relation to the matter.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} If an order is made under subsection (4)
  disqualifying a person from being appointed as chief agent, the person
  shall not be, and the foreign company shall not permit the person to
  be, appointed to that position.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 461
- 2007, c. 6, s. 302
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Removal

- **[[678.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-678.4
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent may, by order,

#### [Supervisory Intervention]{.HTitleText3} {#h-266010 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Direction to transfer policies or to
reinsure risks --- society

- **[[678.5]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-678.5
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If the circumstances described in
  any of paragraphs 679(1.1)(a) to (e) or (f.1) to (i) exist in respect
  of a society, the Superintendent may, by order, subject to any terms
  and conditions the Superintendent may specify, direct it to transfer
  all or any portion of its policies to, or cause itself to be
  reinsured, against all or any portion of the risks undertaken under
  its policies, by any company, society, foreign company or body
  corporate incorporated or formed by or under the laws of a province
  that is authorized to transact the classes of insurance to be so
  transferred or reinsured.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Compliance

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The society shall comply with the order within the
  time that the Superintendent specifies in the order or within any
  further period specified by the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Opportunity for representations

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} No order shall be issued to a society under
  subsection (1) unless the society is provided with a reasonable
  opportunity to make representations in respect of the matter.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 462
- 2007, c. 6, s. 304
- [2023, c. 26, s. 589](#1411089-1415750){.wb-lbx

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Direction to transfer policies or to
reinsure risks --- foreign fraternal benefit society

- **[[678.6]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-678.6
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If the circumstances described in
  any of paragraphs 679(1.2)(a) to (d) or (f) to (h) exist in respect of
  a foreign fraternal benefit society, the Superintendent may, by order,
  subject to any terms and conditions the Superintendent may specify,
  direct it to transfer all or any portion of its policies in respect of
  its insurance business in Canada to, or cause itself to be reinsured,
  against all or any portion of the risks undertaken under those
  policies, by any company, society, foreign company or body corporate
  incorporated or formed by or under the laws of a province that is
  authorized to transact the classes of insurance to be so transferred
  or reinsured.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Compliance

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The foreign company shall comply with the order
  within the time that the Superintendent specifies in the order or
  within any further period specified by the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Opportunity for representations

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} No order shall be issued to a foreign company under
  subsection (1) unless the foreign company is provided with a
  reasonable opportunity to make representations in respect of the
  matter.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Superintendent may take control

- **[[679]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-679
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to this Act, where any of
  the circumstances described in subsection (1.1) exist in respect of a
  company, society or provincial company or any of the circumstances
  described in subsection (1.2) exist in respect of a foreign company,
  the Superintendent may

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} take control, for a period not exceeding sixteen
    days, of the assets of the company, society or provincial company
    and the assets under its administration or, in the case of a foreign
    company, of its assets in Canada together with its other assets held
    in Canada under control of its chief agent, including all amounts
    received or receivable in respect of its insurance business in
    Canada; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} unless the Minister advises the Superintendent that
    the Minister is of the opinion that it is not in the public interest
    to do so,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} take control, for a period exceeding sixteen
      days, of the assets of the company, society or provincial company
      and the assets under its administration or, in the case of a
      foreign company, of its assets in Canada together with its other
      assets held in Canada under the control of its chief agent,
      including all amounts received or receivable in respect of its
      insurance business in Canada,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where control of assets has been taken under
      paragraph (a), continue the control beyond the sixteen days
      referred to in that paragraph, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} take control of the company, society or
      provincial company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Circumstances re other than foreign
  company

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} Control by the Superintendent under subsection (1)
  may be taken in respect of a company, society or provincial company,
  other than a foreign company, where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the company, society or provincial company has
    failed to pay its liabilities or, in the opinion of the
    Superintendent, will not be able to pay its liabilities as they
    become due and payable;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2001, c. 9, s. 463\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the assets of the company, society or provincial
    company are not, in the opinion of the Superintendent, sufficient to
    give adequate protection to its policyholders and creditors;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} any asset appearing on the books or records of the
    company, society or provincial company or held under its
    administration is not, in the opinion of the Superintendent,
    satisfactorily accounted for;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the regulatory capital of the company, society or
    provincial company has, in the opinion of the Superintendent,
    reached a level or is eroding in a manner that may detrimentally
    affect its policyholders or creditors;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the company, society or provincial company has
    failed to comply with an order of the Superintendent made under
    subsection 515(3) to increase its capital or with an order of the
    Superintendent made under subsection 678.5(1);

  - [(f.1)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a company, in the opinion of the
    Superintendent, the company's policyholders or creditors may be
    detrimentally affected because all of the common shares of the
    company must be disposed of under a direction made by the Minister
    or because there is a prohibition under this Act in respect of the
    exercise of the right to vote attached to all of the common shares
    of the company;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} in the opinion of the Superintendent, any other
    state of affairs exists in respect of the company, society or
    provincial company that may be materially prejudicial to the
    interests of the company's, society's or provincial company's
    policyholders or creditors or the owners of any assets under the
    company's, society's or provincial company's administration,
    including where proceedings under a law relating to bankruptcy or
    insolvency have been commenced in Canada or elsewhere in respect of
    the holding body corporate of the company or provincial company;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} in the opinion of the Superintendent, the continued
    operation of the company, society or provincial company by its
    directors or by the officers responsible for its management would be
    materially prejudicial to its integrity or security; or

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in the opinion of the Superintendent, the continued
    operation of the company, society or provincial company by its
    directors or by the officers responsible for its management would
    pose a risk to national security.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Circumstances re foreign company

  [(1.2)]{.lawlabel} Control by the Superintendent under subsection (1)
  may be taken in respect of a foreign company where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in respect of its insurance business in Canada, it
    has failed to pay its liabilities or, in the opinion of the
    Superintendent, will not be able to pay its liabilities as they
    become due and payable;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2001, c. 9, s. 463\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} its assets in Canada are not, in the opinion of the
    Superintendent, sufficient to give adequate protection to its
    policyholders and creditors in respect of its insurance business in
    Canada;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} any asset relating to its insurance business in
    Canada appearing on the books or records of the foreign company is
    not, in the opinion of the Superintendent, satisfactorily accounted
    for;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} it has failed to comply with an order of the
    Superintendent made under subsection 608(4) to increase the margin
    of its assets in Canada over its liabilities in Canada or with an
    order of the Superintendent made under subsection 609(2) or
    678.6(1);

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} in the opinion of the Superintendent, any other
    state of affairs exists in respect of the foreign company that may
    be materially prejudicial to the interests of the foreign company's
    policyholders or creditors in respect of its insurance business in
    Canada, or to the interests of the owners of any assets under the
    foreign company's administration in Canada, including where
    proceedings under a law relating to bankruptcy or insolvency have
    been commenced in Canada or elsewhere in respect of the foreign
    company or its holding body corporate;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} in the opinion of the Superintendent, the continued
    operation of the foreign company in Canada would be materially
    prejudicial to the integrity or security of its business in Canada;
    or

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} in the opinion of the Superintendent, the continued
    operation of the foreign company in Canada would pose a risk to
    national security.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Minister's powers

  [(1.21)]{.lawlabel} Subject to this Act, the Minister may, for reasons
  related to national security, direct the Superintendent to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} take control, for a period not exceeding 16 days,
    of the assets of the company, society or provincial company and the
    assets under its administration or, in the case of a foreign
    company, of its assets in Canada together with its other assets held
    in Canada under the control of its chief agent, including all
    amounts received or receivable in respect of its insurance business
    in Canada;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} take control, for a period exceeding 16 days, of
    the assets of the company, society or provincial company and the
    assets under its administration or, in the case of a foreign
    company, of its assets in Canada together with its other assets held
    in Canada under the control of its chief agent, including all
    amounts received or receivable in respect of its insurance business
    in Canada;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if control of assets has been taken under paragraph
    (a), continue the control beyond the 16 days referred to in that
    paragraph; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} take control of the company, society or provincial
    company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of proposed action

  [(1.3)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent must notify a company, society,
  provincial company or foreign company of any action proposed to be
  taken in respect of it under paragraph (1)(b) and of its right to make
  written representations to the Superintendent within the time
  specified in the notice, not exceeding ten days after it receives the
  notice.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice --- up to 16 days

  [(1.4)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent takes control of the assets
  of a company, society, provincial company or foreign company under
  paragraph (1.21)(a), the Superintendant shall notify the company,
  society, provincial company or foreign company that control has been
  taken at the direction of the Minister.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice --- more than 16 days

  [(1.5)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister is considering whether to exercise
  the powers under any of paragraphs (1.21)(b) to (d), the
  Superintendent shall notify the company, society, provincial company
  or foreign company of the action that is being considered and of its
  right to make written representations to the Minister within the time
  specified in the notice, not exceeding 10 days after it receives the
  notice.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice --- Committee and Review Agency

  [(1.6)]{.lawlabel} Within 30 days after exercising any of the powers
  under subsection (1.21), the Minister shall notify

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the [[Committee]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}, as defined
    in section 2 of the [National Security and Intelligence Committee of
    Parliamentarians Act](/eng/acts/N-16.6); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the [[Review Agency]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}, as
    defined in section 2 of the [National Security and Intelligence
    Review Agency Act](/eng/acts/N-16.62).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Objectives of Superintendent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent has control under
  subsection (1) or (1.21) of the assets of a company, society,
  provincial company or foreign company referred to in that subsection,
  the Superintendent may do all things necessary or expedient to protect
  the rights and interests of the policyholders and creditors of the
  company, society or provincial company or the policyholders and
  creditors in respect of the foreign company's insurance business in
  Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers of Superintendent

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent has control under
  subsection (1) or (1.21) of the assets of a company, society,
  provincial company or foreign company referred to in that subsection,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the company, society, provincial company or foreign
    company shall not make, acquire or transfer any loan or make any
    purchase, sale or exchange of securities or any disbursement or
    transfer of cash of any kind without the prior approval of the
    Superintendent or a representative designated by the Superintendent;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} no director, officer or employee of the company,
    society, provincial company or foreign company nor the chief agent
    of the foreign company shall have access to any cash or securities
    held by the company, society, provincial company or foreign company
    unless

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a representative of the Superintendent
      accompanies the director, officer or employee or the chief agent,
      or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the access is previously authorized by the
      Superintendent or the Superintendent's representative.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers of directors and officers
suspended

- **[[683]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-683 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  the Superintendent takes control of a company, society or provincial
  company under subparagraph 679(1)(b)(iii) or paragraph 679(1.21)(d),
  the powers, duties, functions, rights and privileges of the directors
  of the company, society or provincial company and of the officers of
  the company, society or provincial company responsible for its
  management are suspended.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Superintendent to manage company

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent takes control of a company,
  society or provincial company under subparagraph 679(1)(b)(iii) or
  paragraph 679(1.21)(d), the Superintendent shall manage the business
  and affairs of the company, society or provincial company and in so
  doing the Superintendent

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} may perform any of the duties and functions that
    the persons referred to in subsection (1) were performing prior to
    the taking of control; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} has and may exercise any power, right or privilege
    that any such person had or could have exercised prior to the taking
    of control.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Persons to assist

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent takes control of a company,
  society or provincial company under subparagraph 679(1)(b)(iii) or
  paragraph (1.21)(d), or of the assets of a foreign company under
  subparagraph 679(1)(b)(i) or (ii) or paragraph 679(1.21)(b) or (c),
  the Superintendent may appoint one or more persons to assist in the
  management of the company, society or provincial company or of the
  insurance business in Canada of the foreign company.

- 1991, c. 47, s. 683
- 1996, c. 6, s. 97

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Expiration of control

- **[[684]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-684
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Control by the Superintendent under
  subsection 679(1) of a company, society or provincial company or of
  the assets of a company, society or provincial company or of the
  assets in Canada of a foreign company together with its other assets
  held in Canada under the control of its chief agent including all
  amounts received or receivable in respect of its insurance business in
  Canada expires on the day on which a notice by the Superintendent is
  sent to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the directors and officers who conducted the
    business and affairs of the company, society or provincial company,
    or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the chief agent in Canada of the foreign company,

  stating that the Superintendent is of the opinion that the
  circumstances leading to the taking of control by the Superintendent
  have been substantially rectified and that the company, society or
  provincial company or the foreign company, as the case may be, can
  resume control of its business and affairs, assets or its insurance
  business in Canada, as the case may be.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Expiration of control --- Minister's
  direction

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Control by the Superintendent under subsection
  679(1.21) of a company, society or provincial company or of the assets
  of a company, society or provincial company or of the assets in Canada
  of a foreign company together with its other assets held in Canada
  under the control of its chief agent including all amounts received or
  receivable in respect of its insurance business in Canada expires on
  the day on which a notice by the Superintendent is sent to the
  directors and officers who conducted the business and affairs of the
  company, society or provincial company, or the chief agent in Canada
  of the foreign company, stating that the Minister is of the opinion,
  on the recommendation of the Superintendant, that corrective measures
  have been taken in response to the reasons related to national
  security and that the company, society or provincial company or the
  foreign company, as the case may be, can resume control of its
  business and affairs, assets or its insurance business in Canada, as
  the case may be.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Superintendent may request winding-up

**[[684.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-684.1 .sectionLabel}** The Superintendent
may, at any time before the receipt of a request under section 685 to
relinquish control of a company, society or provincial company or of the
assets of a company, society or provincial company or of the assets in
Canada of a foreign company together with its other assets held in
Canada under the control of its chief agent including all amounts
received or receivable in respect of its insurance business in Canada,
request the Attorney General of Canada to apply for a winding-up order
under section 10.1 of the [Winding-up and Restructuring
Act](/eng/acts/W-11) in respect of

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the company, society or provincial company, if the
  assets of the company, society or provincial company are under the
  control of the Superintendent under subparagraph 679(1)(b)(i) or (ii)
  or paragraph 679(1.21)(b) or (c);

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the insurance business in Canada of the foreign
  company, if the assets in Canada of the foreign company together with
  its other assets referred to in subparagraph 679(1)(b)(i) or (ii) or
  paragraph 679(1.21)(b) or (c) are under the control of the
  Superintendent under those subparagraphs or paragraphs; or

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the company, society or provincial company, if it is
  under the control of the Superintendent under subparagraph
  679(1)(b)(iii) or paragraph 679(1.21)(d).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1996, c. 6, s. 97
- [2023, c. 26, s. 594](#1411117-1415800){.wb-lbx

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Requirement to relinquish control

**[[685]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-685 .sectionLabel}** If no action has been
taken by the Superintendent under section 684.1 and, after 30 days
following the taking of control by the Superintendent under subsection
679(1) or (1.21) of a company, society or provincial company or of the
assets of a company, society or provincial company or of the assets in
Canada of a foreign company together with its other assets held in
Canada under the control of its chief agent including all amounts
received or receivable in respect of its insurance business in Canada,
the Superintendent receives from the board of directors of the company,
society or provincial company or, in case of a foreign company, its
chief agent, a notice in writing requesting the Superintendent to
relinquish control, the Superintendent shall, not later than 12 days
after receipt of the notice,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} comply with the request; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} request the Attorney General of Canada to apply for a
  winding-up order under section 10.1 of the [Winding-up and
  Restructuring Act](/eng/acts/W-11) in respect of the company, society
  or provincial company or the insurance business in Canada of the
  foreign company.

#### [Special Assessments of Companies, Societies, Foreign Companies and Provincial Companies]{.HTitleText3} {#h-266098 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Superintendent to ascertain amounts

- **[[686]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-686 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Superintendent shall, before December 31 in each year,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} ascertain the total amount of expenses incurred
    during the immediately preceding fiscal year in

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} exercising control of a company, society or
      provincial company,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} exercising control of the assets of a foreign
      company under subparagraph 679(1)(b)(i) or (ii) or paragraph
      679(1.21)(b) or (c),

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} carrying out as liquidator the winding-up of a
      company, society or provincial company or of the insurance
      business in Canada of a foreign company,

    including amounts paid as interest charges on money borrowed by or
    on behalf of the company, society or provincial company to meet its
    requirements for liquid funds or as the cost of terminating leases
    or employment contracts or other similar expenses; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} ascertain the portion of the expenses described in
    paragraph (a) that were incurred by the company, society, foreign
    company or provincial company in respect of its policies of accident
    and sickness insurance, its policies of life insurance and annuity
    and its other policies by multiplying those expenses by

    ::: {#266108 .Paragraph}
    A/D, B/D and C/D, respectively,

    where

    [A, B and C]{.dfn}

    :   represent the total of the gross premium income of the company,
        society, foreign company or provincial company, as determined by
        the Superintendent, in respect of

        - [(i)]{.lawlabel} its policies of accident and sickness
          insurance,

        - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} its policies of life insurance and
          annuities, and

        - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} its other policies,

        respectively, during the period referred to in the description
        of D, and

    [D]{.dfn}
    :   represents the total of the gross premium income of the company,
        society, foreign company or provincial company, as determined by
        the Superintendent, during the period of five calendar years
        preceding the first to occur of the calendar year in which the
        Superintendent took control of the company, society or
        provincial company, or in the case of a foreign company, the
        assets, and that in which a winding-up order was issued in
        respect of the company, society, foreign company or provincial
        company.
    :::

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Amounts conclusive

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The amounts ascertained by the Superintendent
  pursuant to subsection (1) are final and conclusive for the purposes
  of this section and sections 687 and 688.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 686
- 1996, c. 6, s. 98

  role="button"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Assessment

**[[687]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-687 .sectionLabel}** As soon as possible
after ascertaining the portions described in paragraph 686(1)(b), the
Superintendent shall, subject to this section and to the extent and in
the manner that the Governor in Council may prescribe, assess those
portions against each company, society, foreign company and provincial
company, other than the company, society, foreign company or provincial
company in respect of which the expenses were incurred, in the following
proportion:

::: {#266121 .Section}
A/B

where

[A]{.dfn}
:   represents the net premiums during the immediately preceding
    calendar year of the company, society, foreign company or provincial
    company from
    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} policies of accident and sickness insurance,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} policies of life insurance and annuities, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} other policies; and

[B]{.dfn}
:   represents the total net premiums during the immediately preceding
    calendar year of all companies, societies, foreign companies and
    provincial companies, other than the company, society, foreign
    company or provincial company in respect of which the expenses were
    incurred, from
    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} policies of accident and sickness insurance,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} policies of life insurance and annuities, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} other policies.
:::

- 2007, c. 6, s. 308

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application of certain provisions of the
[Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
Act](/eng/acts/O-2.7)

- **[[688]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-688
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subsection 23(4) and section 23.2 of
  the [Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
  Act](/eng/acts/O-2.7) apply, with such modifications as the
  circumstances require, in respect of an assessment under section 687.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In this section and sections 686 and 687,

  [[gross premium income]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[gross premium income]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} of a company,
      society, foreign company or provincial company means its premium
      income from its insurance business in Canada calculated without
      reduction in respect of reinsurance premiums paid or
      payable; ([produit brut]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[net premiums]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[net premiums]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} of a company, society,
      foreign company or provincial company means its gross premium
      income less

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} premiums paid or payable in respect of the
        reinsurance of risks undertaken under its policies in respect of
        its insurance business in Canada, and

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} dividends paid or allowed by it to its
        policyholders in respect of its insurance business in
        Canada. ([primes nettes]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[special insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[special insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed, 2007, c.
      6, s. 309\]]{.Repealed}

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 688
- 1997, c. 15, s. 327
- 2007, c. 6, s. 309
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-688-20070420.html "Link to previous version of section 688"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Advisory committee

- **[[689]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-689 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Superintendent may, from among the companies, societies, foreign
  companies and provincial companies that are subject to an assessment
  under section 687 on account of the control of a company, society or
  provincial company or control of the assets of a foreign company,
  appoint a committee of not more than six members to advise the
  Superintendent in respect of assets, management and all other matters
  pertinent to the duties and responsibilities of the Superintendent in
  exercising that control.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 1996, c. 6, s. 99\]]{.Repealed}

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 689
- 1996, c. 6, s. 99
:::

**[[690]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-690 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed, 1996, c.
6, s. 100\]]{.Repealed}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Expenses payable by company, etc.

- **[[691]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-691 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  the Superintendent has taken control of a company, society or
  provincial company under subparagraph 679(1)(b)(iii) or paragraph
  679(1.21)(d) and the control expires or is relinquished under section
  684 or paragraph 685(a), the Superintendent may direct that the
  company, society or provincial company be liable for repayment of all
  or part of the expenses resulting from the taking of control of the
  company, society or provincial company and assessed against and paid
  by other companies, societies, provincial companies and foreign
  companies under section 687, together with any interest in respect of
  the expenses at any rate that is specified by the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Expenses payable by foreign company

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent has taken control of the assets
  of a foreign company under subparagraph 679(1)(b)(i) or (ii) or
  paragraph 679(1.21)(b) or (c) and the control expires or is
  relinquished under section 684 or paragraph 685(a), the Superintendent
  may direct that the foreign company be liable for repayment of all or
  part of the expenses resulting from the taking of control of the
  assets of the foreign company and assessed against and paid by other
  companies, societies, foreign companies and provincial companies under
  section 687, together with any interest in respect of the expenses at
  any rate that is specified by the Superintendent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 691
- 1996, c. 6, s. 101
- [2023, c. 26, s. 597(E)](#1411123-1415808){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1411123-1415808.html"
  role="button"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-691-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 691"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reduction of assessments

**[[692]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-692 .sectionLabel}** Any amount paid to or
recovered by Her Majesty under section 691 of this Act or paragraph
161(1)(d) or (6)(c) or subparagraph 161(8)(b)(iv) of the [Winding-up and
Restructuring Act](/eng/acts/W-11) in respect of a company, society,
foreign company or provincial company shall be applied to the extent and
the manner that may be prescribed.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 692
- 1996, c. 6, s. 167
- 1997, c. 15, s. 328
- 2001, c. 9, s. 464(F)
:::

## [PART XVI]{.HLabel1}[Regulation of Companies and Foreign Companies --- Commissioner]{.HTitleText1} {#h-266163 .Part}

Definition of [société]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"}

**[[693]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-693 .sectionLabel}** In the French version
of this Part, [société]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"} means a
[société]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"} or [société
étrangère]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"} within the meaning of section 2.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 693
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Required information

**[[694]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-694 .sectionLabel}** A company or foreign
company shall provide the Commissioner with the information at the times
and in the form that the Commissioner may require for the purposes of
the administration of the [Financial Consumer Agency of Canada
Act](/eng/acts/F-11.1) and the consumer provisions.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 694
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Confidential information

- **[[695]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-695
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2),
  information regarding the business or affairs of a company or foreign
  company or regarding persons dealing with any of them that is obtained
  by the Commissioner or by any person acting under the direction of the
  Commissioner, in the course of the exercise or performance of powers,
  duties and functions referred to in subsection 5(1) of the [Financial
  Consumer Agency of Canada Act](/eng/acts/F-11.1), and any information
  prepared from that information, is confidential and shall be treated
  accordingly.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disclosure permitted

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the Commissioner is satisfied that the information
  will be treated as confidential by the agency, body or person to whom
  it is disclosed, subsection (1) does not prevent the Commissioner from
  disclosing it

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} to any government agency or body that regulates or
    supervises financial institutions, for purposes related to that
    regulation or supervision;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} to any other agency or body that regulates or
    supervises financial institutions, for purposes related to that
    regulation or supervision;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} to any compensation association designated by order
    of the Minister under subsection 449(1) or 591(1), for purposes
    related to its operation; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} to the Deputy Minister of Finance or any officer of
    the Department of Finance authorized in writing by the Deputy
    Minister of Finance or to the Governor of the Bank of Canada or any
    officer of the Bank of Canada authorized in writing by the Governor
    of the Bank of Canada, for the purposes of policy analysis related
    to the regulation of financial institutions.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 695
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Examination

- **[[696]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-696 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Commissioner, from time to time, but at least once in each calendar
  year, shall make or cause to be made any examination and inquiry that
  the Commissioner considers necessary for the purposes of satisfying
  the Commissioner that the applicable consumer provisions are being
  complied with and, after the conclusion of each examination and
  inquiry, shall report on it to the Minister.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Access to records

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Commissioner or a person acting under the
  Commissioner's direction in carrying out his or her duties under
  subsection (1)

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} has a right of access to any records, including
    electronic records, of a company or foreign company; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} may require the directors or officers of a company
    or foreign company to provide information and explanations, to the
    extent that they are reasonably able to do so, in respect of any
    matter subject to examination or inquiry under subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 696
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Power of Commissioner on inquiry

**[[697]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-697 .sectionLabel}** The Commissioner, in
carrying out his or her duties in relation to consumer provisions, has
all the powers of a person appointed as a commissioner under Part II of
the [Inquiries Act](/eng/acts/I-11) for the purpose of obtaining
evidence under oath, and may delegate those powers to any person acting
under the Commissioner's direction.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 697
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Compliance agreement

**[[698]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-698 .sectionLabel}** The Commissioner may
enter into an agreement, called a "compliance agreement", with a company
or foreign company for the purposes of implementing any measure designed
to further compliance by it with the consumer provisions.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 698
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

## [PART XVII]{.HLabel1}[Insurance Holding Companies]{.HTitleText1} {#h-266200 .Part}

### [Purpose]{.HTitleText2} {#h-266201 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Purpose

**[[699]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-699 .sectionLabel}** The purpose of this
Part is to provide for the incorporation, formation and regulation of
