insurance holding companies that are holding bodies corporate of life
companies.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 699
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

**[[699.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-699.1 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed, 2001,
c. 9, s. 465\]]{.Repealed}

### [DIVISION 1]{.HLabel2}[Interpretation]{.HTitleText2} {#h-266207 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

- **[[700]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  following definitions apply in this Part.

  [[affairs]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[affairs]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, with respect to an insurance
      holding company, means the relationships among the insurance
      holding company and its affiliates and the shareholders, directors
      and officers of the insurance holding company and its affiliates,
      but does not include the business of the insurance holding company
      or any of its affiliates. ([affaires internes]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[complainant]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[complainant]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, in relation to an insurance
      holding company or any matter concerning an insurance holding
      company, means

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a registered holder or beneficial owner, and a
        former registered holder or beneficial owner, of a security of
        the insurance holding company or any of its affiliates;

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a director or an officer, or a former director
        or officer, of the insurance holding company or any of its
        affiliates; or

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any other person who, in the discretion of a
        court, is a proper person to make an application under section
        912, 916 or 1031. ([plaignant]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[subordinated indebtedness]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[subordinated indebtedness]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an
      instrument evidencing an indebtedness of an insurance holding
      company that by its terms provides that the indebtedness will, in
      the event of the insolvency or winding-up of the insurance holding
      company, be subordinate in right of payment to all liabilities of
      the insurance holding company except those liabilities that, by
      their terms, rank equally with or are subordinate to such
      indebtedness. ([titre secondaire]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Provisions in other Parts

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A reference in a provision in this Part to a
  provision in any other Part is deemed to be a reference to that
  provision as it has been made applicable by this Part in respect of
  insurance holding companies.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}References in other Parts

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A reference in a provision of another Part to a
  provision that has been made applicable in respect of insurance
  holding companies by this Part is to be read as including a reference
  to that provision as it has been made applicable in respect of
  insurance holding companies.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 700
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

### [DIVISION 2]{.HLabel2}[Status and Powers]{.HTitleText2} {#h-266223 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Corporate powers

- **[[701]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  insurance holding company has the capacity of a natural person and,
  subject to this Act, the rights, powers and privileges of a natural
  person.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers restricted

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An insurance holding company shall not carry on any
  business or exercise any power that it is restricted by this Act from
  carrying on or exercising, or exercise any of its powers in a manner
  contrary to this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Business in Canada

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An insurance holding company may carry on business
  throughout Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers outside Canada

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subject to this Act, an insurance holding company has
  the capacity to carry on its business, conduct its affairs and
  exercise its powers in any jurisdiction outside Canada to the extent
  and in the manner that the laws of that jurisdiction permit.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 701
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Policies and procedures --- integrity or
security

**[[701.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.1 .sectionLabel}** An insurance
holding company shall establish and adhere to policies and procedures to
protect itself against threats to its integrity or security, including
foreign interference.

::: HistoricalNote
- [2023, c. 26, s. 598](#1411125-1437438){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1411125-1437438.html"
  role="button"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No invalidity

**[[702]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702 .sectionLabel}** No act of an insurance
holding company, including any transfer of property to or by an
insurance holding company, is invalid by reason only that the act or
transfer is contrary to the insurance holding company's incorporating
instrument or this Act.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 702
- 1996, c. 6, s. 102
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-law not necessary

**[[703]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703 .sectionLabel}** It is not necessary for
an insurance holding company to pass a by-law in order to confer any
particular power on the insurance holding company or its directors.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 703
- 1996, c. 6, s. 103
- 1997, c. 15, s. 330
- 1999, c. 31, s. 145(F)
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No personal liability

**[[704]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704 .sectionLabel}** The shareholders of an
insurance holding company are not, as shareholders, liable for any
liability, act or default of the insurance holding company except as
otherwise provided by this Act.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 704
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No constructive notice

**[[705]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705 .sectionLabel}** No person is affected
by or is deemed to have notice or knowledge of the contents of a
document concerning an insurance holding company by reason only that the
document has been filed with the Superintendent or the Minister or is
available for inspection at an office of the insurance holding company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 705
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Authority of directors, officers and
representatives

- **[[706]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-706 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  insurance holding company and no guarantor of an obligation of an
  insurance holding company may assert against a person dealing with the
  insurance holding company or against a person who has acquired rights
  from the insurance holding company that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the insurance holding company's incorporating
    instrument or any by-laws of the insurance holding company have not
    been complied with;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the persons named as directors of the insurance
    holding company in the most recent return sent to the Superintendent
    under section 994 are not the directors of the insurance holding
    company;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the place named in the incorporating instrument or
    by-laws of the insurance holding company is not the place where the
    head office of the insurance holding company is situated;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a person held out by the insurance holding company
    as a director, officer or representative of the insurance holding
    company has not been duly appointed or has no authority to exercise
    the powers and perform the duties that are customary in the business
    of the insurance holding company or usual for a director, officer or
    representative; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a document issued by any director, officer or
    representative of the insurance holding company with actual or usual
    authority to issue the document is not valid or not genuine.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- knowledge

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of a person
  who has or ought to have knowledge of a situation described in that
  subsection by virtue of their relationship to the insurance holding
  company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 706
- 1997, c. 15, s. 331
- 2000, c. 12, s. 157
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 304
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-706-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 706"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Sunset provision

- **[[707]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-707
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) and (4),
  insurance holding companies shall not carry on business after June 30,
  2026.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Extension

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council may, by order, extend by up
  to six months the time during which insurance holding companies may
  continue to carry on business. No more than one order may be made
  under this subsection.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Order not a regulation

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The order is not a regulation for the purposes of the
  [Statutory Instruments Act](/eng/acts/S-22). However, it shall be
  published in Part II of the [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- dissolution

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If Parliament dissolves on the day set out in
  subsection (1) or on any day within the six-month period before that
  day or on any day within an extension ordered under subsection (2),
  insurance holding companies may continue to carry on business until
  the end of the 180th day after the first day of the first session of
  the next Parliament.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 707
- 1997, c. 15, s. 332
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2006, c. 4, s. 201.1
- 2007, c. 6, s. 310
- 2012, c. 5, s. 154
- 2016, c. 7, s. 121
- 2018, c. 12, s. 358
- [2021, c. 23, s. 157](#1307153-1311374){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1307153-1311374.html"
  role="button"}
- [2024, c. 17, s. 407](#1468542-1479968){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1468542-1479968.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-707-20210629.html "Link to previous version of section 707"){.PITLink}
:::

### [DIVISION 3]{.HLabel2}[Incorporation, Continuance and Discontinuance]{.HTitleText2} {#h-266274 .Subheading}

#### [Formalities of Incorporation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-266275 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Incorporation of insurance holding
company

**[[708]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-708 .sectionLabel}** On the application of
one or more persons made in accordance with this Part, the Minister may,
subject to this Division, issue letters patent incorporating an
insurance holding company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 708
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restrictions on incorporation

**[[709]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-709 .sectionLabel}** Letters patent
incorporating an insurance holding company may not be issued if the
application therefor is made by or on behalf of

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} Her Majesty in right of Canada or in right of a
  province, an agency of Her Majesty in either of those rights, or an
  entity controlled by Her Majesty in either of those rights;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the government of a foreign country or any political
  subdivision thereof;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} an agency of the government of a foreign country or
  any political subdivision thereof; or

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} an entity, other than a foreign institution or any
  subsidiary of a foreign institution, that is controlled by the
  government of a foreign country or any political subdivision thereof.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 709
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}National treatment

- **[[710]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-710 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a
  proposed insurance holding company would be a subsidiary of a foreign
  institution that is engaged in the insurance business, letters patent
  to incorporate the insurance holding company may not be issued unless
  the Minister is satisfied that, if the application is made by a
  non-WTO Member foreign institution, treatment as favourable for
  insurance holding companies to which this Act applies exists or will
  be provided in the jurisdiction in which the foreign institution
  principally carries on business, either directly or through a
  subsidiary.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Part XII of the [Bank
  Act](/eng/acts/B-1.01)

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Nothing in subsection (1) affects the operation of
  Part XII of the [Bank Act](/eng/acts/B-1.01).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 710
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application for incorporation

**[[711]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-711 .sectionLabel}** An application for
letters patent to incorporate an insurance holding company setting out
the names of the first directors of the insurance holding company shall
be filed with the Superintendent, together with such other information,
material and evidence as the Superintendent may require.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 711
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Matters for consideration

**[[712]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-712 .sectionLabel}** Before issuing letters
patent to incorporate an insurance holding company, the Minister shall
take into account all matters that the Minister considers relevant to
the application, including

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the nature and sufficiency of the financial resources
  of the applicant or applicants as a source of continuing financial
  support for the company that is proposed to be its subsidiary;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the soundness and feasibility of the plans of the
  applicant or applicants for the future conduct and development of the
  business of the company that is proposed to be its subsidiary;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the business record and experience of the applicant
  or applicants;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the character and integrity of the applicant or
  applicants or, if the applicant or any of the applicants is a body
  corporate, its reputation for being operated in a manner that is
  consistent with the standards of good character and integrity;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} whether the insurance holding company will be
  operated responsibly by persons with the competence and experience
  suitable for involvement in the operation of a financial institution;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the impact of any integration of the businesses and
  operations of the applicant or applicants with those of the insurance
  holding company and its affiliates on the conduct of those businesses
  and operations; and

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the best interests of the financial system in Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 712
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents of letters patent

- **[[713]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-713
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} There shall be set out in the
  letters patent incorporating an insurance holding company

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name of the insurance holding company;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the province in which the head office of the
    insurance holding company is to be situated; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the date that the insurance holding company came,
    or is to come, into existence.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Provisions in letters patent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may set out in the letters patent
  incorporating an insurance holding company any provision not contrary
  to this Act that the Minister considers advisable in order to take
  into account the particular circumstances of the proposed insurance
  holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Terms and conditions

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may impose such terms and conditions in
  respect of the issuance of letters patent incorporating an insurance
  holding company as the Minister considers necessary or appropriate.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 713
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 305
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-713-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 713"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Letters patent of incorporation on
application of life company

- **[[714]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-714 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  the Minister, under section 708, issues letters patent incorporating
  an insurance holding company on the application of a life company,
  including a converted company, there may, on the request of the
  company, and with the approval of the Minister, be included in the
  letters patent of incorporation of the insurance holding company a
  provision deeming shares of the insurance holding company to be
  issued, on a share for share basis, to all shareholders of the company
  in exchange for all the issued and outstanding shares of the company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of provision

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Shares of an insurance holding company deemed to be
  issued under subsection (1) are subject to the same designation,
  rights, privileges and restrictions or conditions and, subject to any
  agreement to the contrary, to the same charges, encumbrances and other
  restrictions as the shares of the company for which they are exchanged
  and the shares of the company, on the issuance of the letters patent,
  become the property of the insurance holding company free and clear of
  any charge, encumbrance or other restriction.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of provision

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An exchange of shares of a company referred to in
  subsection (1) under a provision included in the letters patent
  incorporating an insurance holding company does not deprive a person
  who was a holder of shares of the company immediately before the
  exchange of any right or privilege with respect to the shares or
  relieve the person of any liability in respect of the shares, but that
  right or privilege must be exercised in accordance with this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transfer and voting of company shares

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (3), no share of an insurance
  holding company that is deemed to be issued under a provision included
  in the letters patent incorporating an insurance holding company may
  subsequently be transferred or voted contrary to this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholder and policyholder approval

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} No provision described in subsection (1) may be
  included in letters patent issued under section 708 unless the
  application for the letters patent is accompanied by evidence that the
  request for the provision was approved by a special resolution of the
  shareholders and the policyholders of the company who are entitled to
  vote at a meeting of shareholders and policyholders called to consider
  the application.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exchange of share certificates

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} If, under a provision included in the letters patent
  incorporating an insurance holding company, a share exchange is deemed
  to have taken place, the insurance holding company shall, within
  ninety days after the issuance of the letters patent, make provision
  for the issue of share certificates representing shares of the
  insurance holding company and for the exchange of those certificates
  for share certificates representing the shares of the company that
  were outstanding on the effective date of the letters patent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 714
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proposal involving fundamental change

- **[[715]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-715 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  application, made in accordance with the regulations, by a life
  company, including a converted company, to give effect to a proposal
  to incorporate an insurance holding company as the holding body
  corporate of the company, to continue a body corporate as an insurance
  holding company of the company or to amalgamate two or more bodies
  corporate and continue those bodies corporate as an insurance holding
  company of the company --- and to make any other fundamental change to
  the company, including an exchange of any or all of the shares of the
  company for shares of the insurance holding company ---, the Minister
  may, to give effect to the proposal,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} include in the letters patent of the insurance
    holding company issued under section 708, 721 or 863 any provision
    the Minister considers necessary; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} despite any provision of the Act specified in
    regulations made under paragraph (2)(e), give any approval that the
    Minister considers necessary.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council may make regulations

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} respecting applications referred to in subsection
    (1), including their form and the information to be contained in
    them, and authorizing the Superintendent to require additional
    information in respect of such applications;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} respecting proposals to which subsection (1)
    applies, including the information to be contained in the proposals
    and the times within which the transactions involved in them must
    occur;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} respecting the procedures to be followed by the
    company that makes an application under subsection (1);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} respecting the approval, confirmation or
    authorization, if any, of all or any portion of proposals to which
    subsection (1) applies, and including the approval of shareholders
    and policyholders and including the terms and conditions of those
    approvals, confirmations or authorizations and their effect; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} specifying provisions of the Act for the purpose of
    paragraph (1)(b).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 715
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of issue of letters patent

**[[716]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-716 .sectionLabel}** The Superintendent
shall cause to be published in the [Canada
Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) a notice of the issuance of letters
patent incorporating an insurance holding company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 716
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}First directors

**[[717]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-717 .sectionLabel}** The first directors of
an insurance holding company are the directors named in the application
for letters patent to incorporate the insurance holding company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 717
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of letters patent

**[[718]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-718 .sectionLabel}** An insurance holding
company comes into existence on the date provided therefor in its
letters patent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 718
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

#### [Continuance]{.HTitleText3} {#h-266363 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Federal corporations

- **[[719]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-719 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  body corporate incorporated under the [Canada Business Corporations
  Act](/eng/acts/C-44) or any other Act of Parliament, including a
  company but not including a federal credit union, may apply to the
  Minister for letters patent continuing the body corporate as an
  insurance holding company under this Part.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Other corporations

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A body corporate incorporated otherwise than by or
  under an Act of Parliament may, if so authorized by the laws of the
  jurisdiction where it is incorporated, apply to the Minister for
  letters patent continuing the body corporate as an insurance holding
  company under this Part.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 719
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2010, c. 12, s. 2120
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-719-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 719"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application for continuance

- **[[720]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-720
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where a body corporate applies for
  letters patent under subsection 719(1) or (2), sections 709 to 712
  apply in respect of the application, with such modifications as the
  circumstances require.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Special resolution approval

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a body corporate applies for letters patent
  under subsection 719(1) or (2), the application must be duly
  authorized by a special resolution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Copy of special resolution

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A copy of the special resolution referred to in
  subsection (2) shall be filed with the application.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 720
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Power to issue letters patent

- **[[721]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-721 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  the application of a body corporate under subsection 719(1) or (2),
  the Minister may, subject to this Division, issue letters patent
  continuing the body corporate as an insurance holding company under
  this Part.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Issue of letters patent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Section 713 applies in respect of the issue of
  letters patent under subsection (1), with such modifications as the
  circumstances require.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 721
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of letters patent

**[[722]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-722 .sectionLabel}** On the day set out in
the letters patent continuing a body corporate as an insurance holding
company under subsection 721(1),

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the body corporate becomes an insurance holding
  company as if it had been incorporated under this Part; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the letters patent are deemed to be the incorporating
  instrument of the continued insurance holding company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 722
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Copy of letters patent

- **[[723]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-723
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where a body corporate is continued
  as an insurance holding company under this Part, the Superintendent
  shall without delay send a copy of the letters patent to the
  appropriate official or public body in the jurisdiction in which the
  body corporate was authorized to apply to be continued under this
  Part.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of issuance of letters patent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent shall publish in the [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) a notice of the issuance of
  letters patent continuing a body corporate as an insurance holding
  company under this Part.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 723
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effects of continuance

**[[724]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-724 .sectionLabel}** Where a body corporate
is continued as an insurance holding company under this Part,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the property of the body corporate continues to be
  the property of the insurance holding company;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the insurance holding company continues to be liable
  for the obligations of the body corporate;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} an existing cause of action or claim by or against
  the body corporate or any liability of the body corporate to
  prosecution is unaffected;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a civil, criminal or administrative action or
  proceeding pending by or against the body corporate may continue to be
  prosecuted by or against the insurance holding company;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} a conviction against, or any ruling, order or
  judgment in favour of or against, the body corporate may be enforced
  by or against the insurance holding company;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} a person who, on the day the body corporate becomes
  an insurance holding company, is the holder of a security issued by
  the body corporate is not deprived of any right or privilege available
  to the person at that time in respect of the security or relieved of
  any liability in respect of it, but any such right or privilege may be
  exercised only in accordance with this Act; and

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the by-laws of the body corporate, except those that
  are in conflict with this Act, continue as the by-laws of the
  insurance holding company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 724
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transitional

- **[[725]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-725
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite any other provision of this
  Act or the regulations, the Minister may, on the recommendation of the
  Superintendent, by order, grant to an insurance holding company in
  respect of which letters patent were issued under subsection 721(1)
  permission to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} engage in a business activity specified in the
    order that the insurance holding company would not otherwise be
    permitted by this Act to engage in and that the body corporate
    continued as the insurance holding company was engaging in at the
    time the application for the letters patent was made;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} continue to have issued and outstanding debt
    obligations the issue of which is not authorized by this Act if the
    debt obligations were outstanding at the time the application for
    the letters patent was made;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} hold assets that the insurance holding company
    would not otherwise be permitted by this Act to hold, if the assets
    were held by the body corporate continued as the insurance holding
    company at the time the application for the letters patent was made;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} acquire and hold assets that the insurance holding
    company would not otherwise be permitted by this Act to acquire or
    hold, if the body corporate continued as the insurance holding
    company was obliged, at the time the application for the letters
    patent was made, to acquire those assets; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} maintain outside Canada any records or registers
    required by this Act to be maintained in Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duration

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The permission granted under subsection (1) shall be
  expressed to be granted for a period specified in the order not
  exceeding

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} with respect to any activity described in paragraph
    (1)(a), thirty days after the effective date of the letters patent
    or, where the activity is conducted pursuant to an agreement
    existing on the effective date of the letters patent, the expiration
    of the agreement;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} with respect to any matter described in paragraph
    (1)(b), ten years; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} with respect to any matter described in any of
    paragraphs (1)(c) to (e), two years.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Renewal

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), the Minister may, on the
  recommendation of the Superintendent, by order, renew a permission
  granted by order under subsection (1) with respect to any matter
  described in paragraphs (1)(b) to (d) for such further period or
  periods as the Minister considers necessary.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitation

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall not grant to an insurance holding
  company any permission

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} with respect to matters described in paragraph
    (1)(b), that purports to be effective more than ten years after the
    effective date of the letters patent of continuance issued to
    continue the insurance holding company under this Part, unless the
    Minister is satisfied on the basis of evidence on oath provided by
    an officer of the insurance holding company that the insurance
    holding company will not be able at law to redeem at the end of the
    ten years the outstanding debt obligations to which the permission
    relates; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} with respect to matters described in paragraphs
    (1)(c) and (d), that purports to be effective more than ten years
    after the effective date of the letters patent of continuance issued
    to continue the insurance holding company under this Part.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 725
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2007, c. 6, s. 311
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-725-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 725"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Discontinuance]{.HTitleText3} {#h-266432 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transferring to other Acts

- **[[726]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-726 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  insurance holding company may apply to be continued only as a body
  corporate under any other Act of Parliament or any Act of the
  legislature of a province, and it may do so only with the approval in
  writing of the Minister.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conditions for approval

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No approval referred to in subsection (1) may be
  given to an insurance holding company unless the Minister is satisfied
  that the application of the insurance holding company has been
  authorized by a special resolution.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 726
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2007, c. 6, s. 312
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-726-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 726"){.PITLink}
:::

Meaning of [[insurance holding company without a life company
subsidiary]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

- **[[727]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-727 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For
  the purpose of this section, [[insurance holding company without a
  life company subsidiary]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an insurance
  holding company that does not, at any time within one year after it
  came into existence, have a subsidiary that is a life company or that
  does not, for a period of one year, have a subsidiary that is a life
  company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation to apply

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An insurance holding company without a life company
  subsidiary must, within thirty days after becoming an insurance
  holding company without a life company subsidiary, apply to be
  continued under subsection 726(1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Cessation of existence

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Except for the sole purpose of winding up its
  affairs, an insurance holding company without a life company
  subsidiary that has no other subsidiary that fails to make an
  application under subsection (2) within the time provided for in that
  subsection ceases to exist on the expiration of that period.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 727
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Act ceases to apply

**[[728]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-728 .sectionLabel}** On the day specified by
the Minister, this Act ceases to apply to the body corporate continued
under the other Act of Parliament or under the Act of the legislature of
a province.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 728
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Withdrawing application

**[[729]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-729 .sectionLabel}** Where a special
resolution authorizing the application under subsection 726(1) so
states, the directors of an insurance holding company may, without
further approval of the shareholders, withdraw the application before it
is acted on.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 729
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

#### [Corporate Name]{.HTitleText3} {#h-266457 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibited names

**[[730]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-730 .sectionLabel}** An insurance holding
company may not be incorporated under this Part with a name

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} that is prohibited by an Act of Parliament;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} that is, in the opinion of the Superintendent,
  deceptively misdescriptive;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} that is the same as or, in the opinion of the
  Superintendent, substantially the same as or confusingly similar to
  any existing

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} trademark or trade name, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} corporate name of a body corporate,

  except where the trademark or trade name is being changed or the body
  corporate is being dissolved or is changing its corporate name and
  consent to the use of the trademark, trade name or corporate name is
  signified to the Superintendent in such manner as the Superintendent
  may require;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} that is the same as or, in the opinion of the
  Superintendent, substantially the same as or confusingly similar to
  the known name under or by which any entity carries on business or is
  identified; or

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} that is reserved under section 45 for a company or
  society or a proposed company or society or under section 734 for
  another insurance holding company or a proposed insurance holding
  company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 730
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- [2014, c. 20, s. 366(E)](#1034903-1145575){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1034903-1145575.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-730-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 730"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Affiliated insurance holding company

**[[731]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-731 .sectionLabel}** Despite section 730 and
subject to section 732, an insurance holding company that is affiliated
with another entity may, with the consent of that entity,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} be incorporated with, or change its name to,
  substantially the same name as that of the affiliated entity; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} subject to any terms and conditions that may be
  prescribed, carry on business under or identify itself by a name,
  other than its corporate name, that is substantially the same as the
  corporate name of the affiliated entity or that is another name under
  which or with which the affiliated entity carries on business or
  otherwise identifies itself.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 731
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2007, c. 6, s. 313
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-731-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 731"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction

**[[732]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-732 .sectionLabel}** An insurance holding
company may not be incorporated or continued with, or change its name to
or carry on business or identify itself by, a name that is substantially
the same as that of a company unless the name contains words that, in
the opinion of the Superintendent, indicate to the public that the
insurance holding company is distinct from any company that is a
subsidiary of the insurance holding company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 732
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}French or English form of name

- **[[733]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-733 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  name of an insurance holding company may be set out in its letters
  patent in an English form, a French form, an English form and a French
  form or in a combined English and French form, and the insurance
  holding company may use and be legally designated by any such form.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Mandatory abbreviation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite any other provision of this Act and subject
  to the regulations, every insurance holding company shall have as part
  of its name, the abbreviations "ihc" or "spa".

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Alternate name

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An insurance holding company may identify itself
  outside Canada by its name in any language and the insurance holding
  company may use and be legally designated by any such form of its name
  outside Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Other name

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (5) and section 880, an
  insurance holding company may carry on business under or identify
  itself by a name other than its corporate name.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directions

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If an insurance holding company is carrying on
  business under or identifying itself by a name other than its
  corporate name, the Superintendent may, by order, direct the insurance
  holding company not to use that other name if the Superintendent is of
  the opinion that that other name is a name referred to in any of
  paragraphs 730(a) to (e).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council may make regulations
  respecting the use of the abbreviations "ihc" or "spa" in the name of
  insurance holding companies.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 733
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reserved name

**[[734]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-734 .sectionLabel}** The Superintendent may,
on request, reserve for ninety days a name for a proposed insurance
holding company or for an insurance holding company that intends to
change its name.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 734
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directing change of name

- **[[735]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-735 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  through inadvertence or otherwise an insurance holding company

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} comes into existence or is continued with a name,
    or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} on an application to change its name, is granted a
    name

  that is prohibited by section 730 or 732, the Superintendent may, by
  order, direct the insurance holding company to change its name and the
  insurance holding company shall comply with that direction.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Revoking name

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where an insurance holding company has been directed
  under subsection (1) to change its name and has not, within sixty days
  after the service of the direction, changed its name to a name that is
  not prohibited by this Part, the Superintendent may revoke the name of
  the insurance holding company and assign to it a name and, until
  changed in accordance with section 849 or 851, the name of the
  insurance holding company is thereafter the name so assigned.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 735
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Subsidiaries

**[[736]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-736 .sectionLabel}** Despite subsection
47(1), a subsidiary of an insurance holding company may, with the
approval in writing of the Superintendent, use the word
"[assurance]{.otherLang lang="fr"}", "[assurances]{.otherLang
lang="fr"}", "insurance" or "lifeco" or any word or words of import
equivalent to any of those words in its name.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 736
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

Definition of [[reserved name]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

- **[[737]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-737 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In
  this section, [[reserved name]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a name that
  includes as part thereof the word "[assurance]{.otherLang lang="fr"}",
  "[assurances]{.otherLang lang="fr"}", "insurance", "lifeco",
  "[fiduciaire]{.otherLang lang="fr"}", "fiduciary",
  "[fiducie]{.otherLang lang="fr"}", "trust", "trustco", "loan",
  "loanco" or "[prêt]{.otherLang lang="fr"}" or any word or words of
  import equivalent to any of those words.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Termination of control required in
  certain cases

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person, other than a financial institution, who

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is carrying on business in Canada under a reserved
    name, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} has control or acquires control of an insurance
    holding company,

  shall control the insurance holding company one year after the date of
  acquisition of the control.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} No person, other than a financial institution, who

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} controls an entity that is not a financial
    institution that carries on business in Canada under a reserved
    name, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} has control or acquires control of an insurance
    holding company,

  shall control the insurance holding company one year after the date of
  the acquisition of the control.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Continuing control prohibited

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (3), where a financial institution
  controls an entity that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is not a financial institution,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} carries on business in Canada under a reserved
    name, and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} acquires control of an insurance holding company,

  the entity shall not control the insurance holding company one year
  after the date on which the entity acquires control of the insurance
  holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exceptions

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Subsections (2) to (4) do not apply with respect to a
  person or entity that was carrying on business in Canada under a
  reserved name on June 25, 1999.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 737
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

#### [Publication of Information]{.HTitleText3} {#h-266536 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication of information

**[[738]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-738 .sectionLabel}** The Superintendent
shall, within sixty days after the end of each year, cause a notice to
be published in the [Canada Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/), showing

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name of every insurance holding company; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the province in which the head office of the
  insurance holding company is situated.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 738
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 306
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-738-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 738"){.PITLink}
:::

### [DIVISION 4]{.HLabel2}[Organization and Commencement]{.HTitleText2} {#h-266543 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}First directors' meeting

- **[[739]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-739
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} After letters patent incorporating
  an insurance holding company are issued, a meeting of the directors of
  the insurance holding company shall be held at which the directors
  may, subject to this Division,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} make by-laws;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} adopt forms of share certificates and corporate
    records;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} authorize the issue of shares of the insurance
    holding company;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} appoint officers;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} appoint an auditor to hold office until the meeting
    called under subsection 740(1);

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} make banking arrangements; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} deal with any other matters necessary to organize
    the insurance holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Calling directors' meeting

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An incorporator or a director named in the
  application for letters patent may call the meeting referred to in
  subsection (1) by giving, subject to subsection 817(2), no fewer than
  five days notice of the purpose, time and place of the meeting to each
  director of the insurance holding company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 739
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Calling shareholders' meeting

- **[[740]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-740
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} After the meeting referred to in
  subsection 739(1) is held, the directors of the insurance holding
  company shall without delay call a meeting of the shareholders of the
  insurance holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Meeting of shareholders or
  incorporators

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The shareholders of an insurance holding company
  shall, by resolution at the meeting of shareholders called under
  subsection (1),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} approve, amend or reject any by-law made by the
    directors of the insurance holding company;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} subject to section 803, elect directors to hold
    office for a term expiring not later than the close of the third
    annual meeting of shareholders following the election; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} appoint an auditor to hold office until the close
    of the first annual meeting of shareholders.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 740
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Term of first directors

**[[741]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-741 .sectionLabel}** A director named in the
application for letters patent to incorporate an insurance holding
company holds office until the election of directors at the meeting of
shareholders called under subsection 740(1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 741
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

### [DIVISION 5]{.HLabel2}[Capital Structure]{.HTitleText2} {#h-266572 .Subheading}

#### [Share Capital]{.HTitleText3} {#h-266573 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Power to issue shares

- **[[742]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-742
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to this Part and the by-laws
  of the insurance holding company, shares of an insurance holding
  company may be issued at such times and to such persons and for such
  consideration as the directors of the insurance holding company may
  determine.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shares

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Shares of an insurance holding company shall be in
  registered form and shall be without nominal or par value.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shares of continued insurance holding
  company

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a body corporate is continued as an insurance
  holding company under this Part, shares with nominal or par value
  issued by the body corporate before it was so continued are deemed to
  be shares without nominal or par value.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed share conditions

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If any right of a holder of a share with nominal or
  par value of a body corporate continued as an insurance holding
  company under this Part, other than a voting right, was stated or
  expressed in terms of the nominal or par value of the share
  immediately before the continuance under this Part that right is
  thereafter deemed to be the same right stated or expressed without
  reference to the nominal or par value of the share.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 742
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Common shares

- **[[743]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-743 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  insurance holding company shall have one class of shares, to be
  designated as "common shares", which are non-redeemable and in which
  the rights of the holders thereof are equal in all respects, and those
  rights include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the right to vote at all meetings of shareholders
    except where only holders of a specified class of shares are
    entitled to vote;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the right to receive dividends declared on those
    shares; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the right to receive the remaining property of the
    insurance holding company on dissolution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Designations of shares

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No insurance holding company shall designate more
  than one class of its shares as "common shares" or any variation of
  that term.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Continued insurance holding company

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A body corporate continued as an insurance holding
  company under this Part that is not in compliance with subsection (2)
  on the date letters patent continuing it as an insurance holding
  company are issued shall, within twelve months after that date,
  redesignate its shares to comply with that subsection.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 743
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Classes of shares

- **[[744]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-744 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  by-laws of an insurance holding company may provide for more than one
  class of shares and, if they so provide, shall set out

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions
    attaching to the shares of each class; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the maximum number, if any, of shares of any class
    that the insurance holding company is authorized to issue.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholder approval

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a by-law referred to in subsection (1) is made,
  the directors of the insurance holding company shall submit the by-law
  to the shareholders at the next meeting of shareholders.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effective date

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A by-law referred to in subsection (1) is not
  effective until it is confirmed or confirmed with amendments by
  special resolution of the shareholders at the meeting referred to in
  subsection (2).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 744
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shares issued in series

- **[[745]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-745 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  by-laws of an insurance holding company may, subject to any
  limitations set out in them, authorize the issue of any class of
  shares in one or more series and may

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} fix the maximum number of shares in each series and
    determine the designation, rights, privileges, restrictions and
    conditions attaching to them; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} authorize the directors to do anything referred to
    in paragraph (a).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Series participation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If any cumulative dividend or amounts payable on
  return of capital in respect of a series of shares are not paid in
  full, the shares of all series of the same class participate rateably
  in respect of accumulated dividends and return of capital.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voting rights

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where voting rights are attached to any series of a
  class of shares, the shares of every other series of that class shall
  have the same voting rights.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction on series

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} No rights, privileges, restrictions or conditions
  attached to a series of shares authorized under this section confer on
  the series a priority in respect of dividends or return of capital
  over any other series of shares of the same class that are then
  outstanding.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Material to Superintendent

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If the directors exercise their authority under
  paragraph (1)(b), the directors shall, before the issue of shares of
  the series, send to the Superintendent particulars of the series of
  shares and a copy of the by-law that granted the authority to the
  directors.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 745
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 307
- 2007, c. 6, s. 314(E)
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-745-20060427.html "Link to previous version of section 745"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}One share, one vote

**[[746]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-746 .sectionLabel}** Where voting rights are
attached to a share of an insurance holding company, the voting rights
may confer only one vote in respect of that share.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 746
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shares non-assessable

**[[747]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-747 .sectionLabel}** Shares issued by an
insurance holding company are non-assessable and the shareholders are
not liable to the insurance holding company or to its creditors in
respect thereof.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 747
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Consideration for share

- **[[748]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-748 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No
  share of any class of shares of an insurance holding company shall be
  issued until it is fully paid for in money or, with the approval of
  the Superintendent, in property.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Other currencies

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} When issuing shares, an insurance holding company may
  provide that any aspect of the shares relating to money or involving
  the payment of or the liability to pay money be in a currency other
  than the currency of Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 748
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Stated capital account

- **[[749]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-749 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  insurance holding company shall maintain a separate stated capital
  account for each class and series of shares it issues.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Addition to stated capital account

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An insurance holding company shall record in the
  appropriate stated capital account the full amount of any
  consideration it receives for any shares it issues.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (2), an insurance holding company
  may, subject to subsection (4), record in the stated capital account
  maintained for the shares of a class or series any part of the
  consideration it receives in an exchange if it issues shares

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in exchange for

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} property of a person who immediately before the
      exchange did not deal with the insurance holding company at arm's
      length within the meaning of that expression in the [Income Tax
      Act](/eng/acts/I-3.3),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} shares of or another interest in a body
      corporate that immediately before the exchange or because of it
      did not deal with the insurance holding company at arm's length
      within the meaning of that expression in the [Income Tax
      Act](/eng/acts/I-3.3), or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} property of a person who immediately before the
      exchange dealt with the insurance holding company at arm's length
      within the meaning of that expression in the [Income Tax
      Act](/eng/acts/I-3.3) if the person, the insurance holding company
      and all of the holders of shares in the class or series of shares
      so issued consent to the exchange;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} under an agreement referred to in subsection
    858(1); or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} to shareholders of an amalgamating body corporate
    who receive the shares in addition to or instead of securities of
    the amalgamated insurance holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limit on addition to a stated capital
  account

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} On the issuance of a share, an insurance holding
  company shall not add to the stated capital account in respect of the
  share an amount greater than the amount of the consideration it
  receives for the share.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Constraint on addition to a stated
  capital account

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Where an insurance holding company that has issued
  any outstanding shares of more than one class or series proposes to
  add to a stated capital account that it maintains in respect of a
  class or series of shares an amount that was not received by the
  insurance holding company as consideration for the issue of shares,
  the addition must be approved by special resolution unless all the
  issued and outstanding shares are of not more than two classes of
  convertible shares referred to in subsection 759(4).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 749
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 308
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-749-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 749"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Stated capital of continued insurance
holding company

- **[[750]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-750
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where a body corporate is continued
  as an insurance holding company under this Part, the insurance holding
  company shall record in the stated capital account maintained for each
  class and series of shares then outstanding an amount that is equal to
  the aggregate of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aggregate amount paid up on the shares of each
    class and series of shares immediately before the body corporate was
    so continued, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the amount of the contributed surplus of the
    insurance holding company that is attributable to those shares.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contributed surplus entry

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The amount of any contributed surplus recorded in the
  stated capital account pursuant to paragraph (1)(b) shall be deducted
  from the contributed surplus account of the insurance holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shares issued before continuance

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Any amount unpaid in respect of a share issued by a
  body corporate before it was continued as an insurance holding company
  under this Part and paid after it was so continued shall be recorded
  in the stated capital account maintained by the insurance holding
  company for the shares of that class or series.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 750
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Pre-emptive right

- **[[751]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-751
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where the by-laws of an insurance
  holding company so provide, no shares of any class shall be issued
  unless the shares have first been offered to the shareholders holding
  shares of that class, and those shareholders have a pre-emptive right
  to acquire the offered shares in proportion to their holdings of the
  shares of that class, at such price and on such terms as those shares
  are to be offered to others.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite the existence of a pre-emptive right, a
  shareholder of an insurance holding company has no pre-emptive right
  in respect of shares of a class to be issued

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} for a consideration other than money;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} as a share dividend; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} pursuant to the exercise of conversion privileges,
    options or rights previously granted by the insurance holding
    company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite the existence of a pre-emptive right, a
  shareholder of an insurance holding company has no pre-emptive right
  in respect of shares to be issued

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where the issue of shares to the shareholder is
    prohibited by this Part; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where, to the knowledge of the directors of the
    insurance holding company, the offer of shares to a shareholder
    whose recorded address is in a country other than Canada ought not
    to be made unless the appropriate authority in that country is
    provided with information in addition to that submitted to the
    shareholders at the last annual meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 751
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conversion privileges

- **[[752]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-752 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  insurance holding company may issue conversion privileges, options or
  rights to acquire securities of the insurance holding company, and
  shall set out the conditions thereof

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the documents that evidence the conversion
    privileges, options or rights; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the securities to which the conversion
    privileges, options or rights are attached.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transferable rights

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Conversion privileges, options and rights to acquire
  securities of an insurance holding company may be made transferable or
  non-transferable, and options and rights to acquire such securities
  may be made separable or inseparable from any securities to which they
  are attached.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reserved shares

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where an insurance holding company has granted
  privileges to convert any securities issued by the insurance holding
  company into shares, or into shares of another class or series, or has
  issued or granted options or rights to acquire shares, if the by-laws
  limit the number of authorized shares, the insurance holding company
  shall reserve and continue to reserve sufficient authorized shares to
  meet the exercise of such conversion privileges, options and rights.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 752
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Holding of own shares

**[[753]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-753 .sectionLabel}** Except as provided in
sections 754 to 756, or unless permitted by the regulations, an
insurance holding company shall not

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} hold shares of the insurance holding company or of
  any body corporate that controls the insurance holding company;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} hold any ownership interests of any unincorporated
  entity that controls the insurance holding company;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} permit any of its subsidiaries to hold any shares of
  the insurance holding company or of any body corporate that controls
  the insurance holding company; or

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} permit any of its subsidiaries to hold any ownership
  interests of any unincorporated entity that controls the insurance
  holding company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 753
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Purchase and redemption of shares

- **[[754]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-754
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2) and to its
  by-laws, an insurance holding company may, with the consent of the
  Superintendent, purchase, for the purpose of cancellation, any shares
  issued by it, or redeem any redeemable shares issued by it at prices
  not exceeding the redemption price thereof calculated according to a
  formula stated in its by-laws or the conditions attaching to the
  shares.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restrictions on purchase and redemption

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An insurance holding company shall not make any
  payment to purchase or redeem any shares issued by it if there are
  reasonable grounds for believing that it is, or the payment would
  cause it to be, in contravention of subsection 992(1), any regulation
  made under subsection 992(2) or any order made under subsection
  992(3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Donated shares

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An insurance holding company may accept from any
  shareholder a share of the insurance holding company surrendered to it
  as a gift, but may not extinguish or reduce a liability in respect of
  an amount unpaid on any such share except in accordance with section
  757.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 754
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2007, c. 6, s. 315
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-754-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 754"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Holding as personal representative

- **[[755]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-755 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  insurance holding company may permit its subsidiaries to hold, in the
  capacity of a personal representative, shares of the insurance holding
  company or of any body corporate that controls the insurance holding
  company or ownership interests in any unincorporated entity that
  controls the insurance holding company, but only if the subsidiary
  does not have a beneficial interest in the shares or ownership
  interests.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Security interest

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An insurance holding company may permit its
  subsidiaries to hold, by way of a security interest, shares of the
  insurance holding company or of any body corporate that controls the
  insurance holding company or any ownership interests of any entity
  that controls the insurance holding company if the security interest
  is nominal or immaterial when measured by criteria established by the
  insurance holding company that have been approved in writing by the
  Superintendent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 755
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 309(F)
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-755-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 755"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- conditions before
acquisition

- **[[755.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-755.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An insurance holding company may
  permit any of its subsidiaries to acquire shares of the insurance
  holding company through the issuance of those shares by the insurance
  holding company to the subsidiary if the conditions prescribed for the
  purposes of this subsection are met before the subsidiary acquires the
  shares.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conditions after acquisition

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} After a subsidiary has acquired shares under the
  purported authority of subsection (1), the conditions prescribed for
  the purposes of this subsection must be met.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Non-compliance with conditions

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If an insurance holding company permits any of its
  subsidiaries to acquire shares of the insurance holding company under
  the purported authority of subsection (1) and one or more of the
  conditions prescribed for the purposes of subsections (1) and (2) were
  not met, are not met or cease to be met, as the case may be, then,
  despite section 702 and subsection 749(2), the insurance holding
  company must comply with the prescribed requirements.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 6, s. 316
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Cancellation of shares

- **[[756]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-756
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), where an
  insurance holding company purchases shares of the insurance holding
  company or fractions thereof or redeems or otherwise acquires shares
  of the insurance holding company, the insurance holding company shall
  cancel those shares.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Requirement to sell

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a subsidiary of an insurance holding company,
  through the realization of security, acquires any shares of the
  insurance holding company or of any body corporate that controls the
  insurance holding company or any ownership interests in an
  unincorporated entity that controls the insurance holding company, the
  insurance holding company shall cause its subsidiary to, within six
  months after the day of the realization, sell or otherwise dispose of
  the shares or ownership interests.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 756
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reduction of capital

- **[[757]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-757 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  stated capital of an insurance holding company may be reduced by
  special resolution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An insurance holding company shall not reduce its
  stated capital by special resolution if there are reasonable grounds
  for believing that the insurance holding company is, or the reduction
  would cause the insurance holding company to be, in contravention of
  subsection 992(1), any regulation made under subsection 992(2) or any
  order made under subsection 992(3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents of special resolution

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A special resolution to reduce the stated capital of
  an insurance holding company shall specify the stated capital account
  or accounts from which the reduction of stated capital effected by the
  special resolution will be deducted.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Approval by Superintendent

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A special resolution to reduce the stated capital of
  an insurance holding company has no effect until it is approved in
  writing by the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(4.1)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (4) does not apply if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the reduction in the stated capital is made solely
    as a result of changes made to the accounting principles referred to
    in subsection 331(4); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} there is to be no return of capital to shareholders
    as a result of the reduction.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conditions for approval

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} No approval to reduce the stated capital of an
  insurance holding company may be given by the Superintendent unless
  application therefor is made within three months after the time of the
  passing of the special resolution and a copy of the special
  resolution, together with a notice of intention to apply for approval,
  has been published in the [Canada Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Statements to be submitted

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} In addition to evidence of the passing of a special
  resolution to reduce the stated capital of an insurance holding
  company and of the publication thereof, statements showing

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the number of the insurance holding company's
    shares issued and outstanding,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the results of the voting by class of shares of the
    insurance holding company,

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the insurance holding company's assets and
    liabilities, and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the reason why the insurance holding company seeks
    the reduction of capital

  shall be submitted to the Superintendent at the time of the
  application for approval of the special resolution.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 757
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2007, c. 6, s. 317
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-757-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 757"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Recovery by action

- **[[758]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-758
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where any money or property was paid
  or distributed to a shareholder or other person as a consequence of a
  reduction of capital made contrary to section 757, a creditor of the
  insurance holding company may apply to a court for an order compelling
  the shareholder or other person to pay the money or deliver the
  property to the insurance holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shares held by personal representative

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person holding shares in the capacity of a
  personal representative and registered on the records of the insurance
  holding company as a shareholder and therein described as the personal
  representative of a named person is personally liable under subsection
  (1), but the named person is subject to all the liabilities imposed by
  that subsection.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitation

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An action to enforce a liability imposed by
  subsection (1) may not be commenced more than two years after the date
  of the act complained of.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Remedy preserved

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} This section does not affect any liability that
  arises under section 841.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 758
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Adjustment of stated capital account

- **[[759]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-759 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On a
  purchase, redemption or other acquisition by an insurance holding
  company of shares or fractions thereof issued by it, the insurance
  holding company shall deduct from the stated capital account
  maintained for the class or series of shares so purchased, redeemed or
  otherwise acquired an amount equal to the result obtained by
  multiplying the stated capital in respect of the shares of that class
  or series by the number of shares of that class or series so
  purchased, redeemed or otherwise acquired and dividing by the number
  of shares of that class or series outstanding immediately before the
  purchase, redemption or other acquisition.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Adjustment of stated capital account

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An insurance holding company shall adjust its stated
  capital account or accounts in accordance with any special resolution
  referred to in section 757.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shares converted to another class

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} On a conversion of outstanding shares of an insurance
  holding company into shares of another class or series, or on a change
  of outstanding shares of the insurance holding company into shares of
  another class or series, the insurance holding company shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} deduct from the stated capital account maintained
    for the class or series of shares converted or changed an amount
    equal to the result obtained by multiplying the stated capital of
    the shares of that class or series by the number of shares of that
    class or series converted or changed, and dividing by the number of
    outstanding shares of that class or series immediately before the
    conversion or change; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} record the result obtained under paragraph (a) and
    any additional consideration received pursuant to the conversion or
    change in the stated capital account maintained or to be maintained
    for the class or series of shares into which the shares have been
    converted or changed.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Stated capital of convertible shares

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (3) and subject to the
  insurance holding company's by-laws, where an insurance holding
  company issues two classes of shares and there is attached to each
  class a right to convert a share of one class into a share of the
  other class and a share is so converted, the amount of stated capital
  attributable to a share in either class is the aggregate of the stated
  capital of both classes divided by the number of outstanding shares of
  both classes immediately before the conversion.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conversion or change of shares

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Shares issued by an insurance holding company and
  converted into shares of another class or series, or changed under
  subsection 851(1) into shares of another class or series, become
  issued shares of the class or series of shares into which the shares
  have been converted or changed.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 759
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Addition to stated capital account

**[[760]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-760 .sectionLabel}** On a conversion of any
debt obligation of an insurance holding company into shares of a class
or series of shares, the insurance holding company shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} deduct from the liabilities of the insurance holding
  company the nominal value of the debt obligation being converted; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} record the result obtained under paragraph (a) and
  any additional consideration received for the conversion in the stated
  capital account maintained or to be maintained for the class or series
  of shares into which the debt obligation has been converted.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 760
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Declaration of dividend

- **[[761]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-761 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  directors of an insurance holding company may declare and an insurance
  holding company may pay a dividend by issuing fully paid shares of the
  insurance holding company or options or rights to acquire fully paid
  shares of the insurance holding company and, subject to subsection
  (4), the directors of an insurance holding company may declare and an
  insurance holding company may pay a dividend in money or property,
  and, where a dividend is to be paid in money, the dividend may be paid
  in a currency other than the currency of Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice to Superintendent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The directors of an insurance holding company shall
  notify the Superintendent of the declaration of a dividend at least 15
  days before the day fixed for its payment.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Share dividend

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If shares of an insurance holding company are issued
  in payment of a dividend, the insurance holding company shall record
  in the stated capital account maintained or to be maintained for the
  shares of the class or series issued in payment of the dividend the
  declared amount of the dividend stated as an amount of money.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}When dividend not to be declared

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The directors of an insurance holding company shall
  not declare and an insurance holding company shall not pay a dividend
