  if there are reasonable grounds for believing that the insurance
  holding company is, or the payment would cause the insurance holding
  company to be, in contravention of subsection 992(1), any regulation
  made under subsection 992(2) or any order made under subsection
  992(3).

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 761
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2007, c. 6, s. 318
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-761-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 761"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Subordinated Indebtedness]{.HTitleText3} {#h-266800 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction on subordinated indebtedness

- **[[762]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-762 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  insurance holding company shall not issue subordinated indebtedness
  unless the subordinated indebtedness is fully paid for in money or,
  with the approval of the Superintendent, in property.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}References to subordinated indebtedness

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person shall not in any prospectus, advertisement,
  correspondence or literature relating to any subordinated indebtedness
  issued or to be issued by an insurance holding company refer to the
  subordinated indebtedness otherwise than as subordinated indebtedness.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Other currencies

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} When issuing subordinated indebtedness, an insurance
  holding company may provide that any aspect of the subordinated
  indebtedness relating to money or involving the payment of or the
  liability to pay money in relation thereto be in a currency other than
  that of Canada including, without restricting the generality of the
  foregoing, the payment of any interest thereon.

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 762
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

#### [Security Certificates and Transfers]{.HTitleText3} {#h-266810 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Sections 85 to 139 apply

**[[763]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-763 .sectionLabel}** Sections 85 to 139
apply in respect of insurance holding companies, subject to the
following:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} references to "company" in those sections are to be
  read as references to "insurance holding company";

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} references to "this Act" in those sections are to be
  read as references to "this Part";

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} references to "Part VII" in those sections are to be
  read as references to "Division 7 of Part XVII";

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} references to "this Part" in those sections are to be
  read as references to "this Division";

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 92(1)(a) is to be read without reference to
  the words "other than section 427";

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the reference to "sections 142 to 145 and section
  149" in subsection 97(1) is to be read as a reference to "sections 766
  to 769 and 772"; and

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the reference to "section 75 or 81" in subsection
  101(3) is to be read as a reference to "section 754 or 759".

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, s. 763
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

### [DIVISION 6]{.HLabel2}[Corporate Governance]{.HTitleText2} {#h-266822 .Subheading}

#### [SUBDIVISION 1]{.HLabel3}[Shareholders]{.HTitleText3} {#h-266823 .Subheading}

##### [Place of Meetings]{.HTitleText4} {#h-266824 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Place of meetings

- **[[764]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-764
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Meetings of shareholders of an
  insurance holding company shall be held at the place within Canada
  provided for in the by-laws of the insurance holding company or, in
  the absence of any such provision, at the place within Canada that the
  directors determine.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Participation by electronic means

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Unless the by-laws provide otherwise, any person who
  is entitled to attend a meeting of shareholders may participate in the
  meeting by means of a telephonic, electronic or other communication
  facility that permits all participants to communicate adequately with
  each other during the meeting if the insurance holding company makes
  one available. A person who is participating in a meeting by one of
  those means is deemed for the purposes of this Part to be present at
  the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council may make regulations
  respecting the manner of and conditions for participating in a meeting
  by means of a telephonic, electronic or other communication facility
  that permits all participants to communicate adequately with each
  other during the meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 311
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-764-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 764"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Calling Meetings]{.HTitleText4} {#h-266834 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Calling meetings

- **[[765]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-765 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  directors of an insurance holding company

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} shall, after the meeting called under subsection
    740(1), call the first annual meeting of shareholders of the
    insurance holding company, which meeting must be held not later than
    six months after the end of the first financial year of the
    insurance holding company;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} shall subsequently call an annual meeting of
    shareholders, which meeting must be held not later than six months
    after the end of each financial year; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} may at any time call a special meeting of
    shareholders.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Order to delay calling annual meeting

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), the insurance holding company
  may apply to the court for an order extending the time for calling an
  annual meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation to notify Superintendent

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The insurance holding company shall give notice of
  the application to the Superintendent before any hearing concerning
  the application and shall provide the Superintendent with a copy of
  any order that is issued.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Superintendent's right to appear

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent is entitled to appear and be heard
  in person or by counsel at any hearing concerning the application.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 312
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-765-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 765"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Record Dates]{.HTitleText4} {#h-266849 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Authority to fix record date

- **[[766]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-766 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  directors may in advance fix a record date, that is within the
  prescribed period, for the determination of shareholders for any
  purpose, including for a determination of which shareholders are
  entitled to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} receive payment of a dividend;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} participate in a liquidation distribution;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} receive notice of a meeting of shareholders; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} vote at a meeting of shareholders.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Determination of record date

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If no record date is fixed,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the record date for the determination of
    shareholders who are entitled to receive notice of a meeting of
    shareholders is

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} at the close of business on the day immediately
      preceding the day on which the notice is given, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if no notice is given, the day on which the
      meeting is held; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the record date for the determination of
    shareholders for any other purpose, other than to establish a
    shareholder's right to vote, is at the close of business on the day
    on which the directors pass a resolution in respect of that purpose.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of record date

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a record date is fixed and unless notice of the
  record date is waived in writing by every holder of a share of the
  class or series affected whose name is set out in the securities
  register at the close of business on the day on which the directors
  fix the record date, notice of the record date shall be given within
  the prescribed period by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} advertisement in a newspaper in general circulation
    in the place where the insurance holding company's head office is
    situated and in each place in Canada where the insurance holding
    company has a transfer agent or where a transfer of its shares may
    be recorded; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} written notice to each stock exchange in Canada on
    which the insurance holding company's shares are listed for trading.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 313
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-766-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 766"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Notices of Meetings]{.HTitleText4} {#h-266869 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of meeting

- **[[767]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-767
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Notice of the time and place of a
  meeting of shareholders of an insurance holding company shall be sent
  within the prescribed period to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} each shareholder entitled to vote at the meeting;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} each director;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the auditor of the insurance holding company; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} In the case of an insurance holding company that is
  not a distributing insurance holding company, notice may be sent
  within any shorter period specified in its by-laws.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Number of eligible votes

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An insurance holding company in respect of which
  subsection 927(4) applies shall set out in the notice of a meeting the
  number of eligible votes, as defined under subsection 793(1), that may
  be cast at the meeting as of the record date for determining the
  shareholders entitled to receive the notice of meeting, or, if there
  are to be separate votes of shareholders at the meeting, the number of
  eligible votes, as defined in that subsection, in respect of each
  separate vote to be held at the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Waiver of notice

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An insurance holding company is not required under
  subsection (1) to send to a person notice of a meeting if the person
  waives notice of the meeting. That waiver may be in any manner.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Attendance constitutes waiver

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A person who attends a meeting of shareholders is
  deemed to have waived notice of the meeting, except where the person
  attends the meeting for the express purpose of objecting to the
  transaction of any business on the grounds that the meeting is not
  lawfully called.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication in newspaper

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} In addition to the notice required under subsection
  (1), where any class of shares of an insurance holding company is
  publicly traded on a recognized stock exchange in Canada, notice of
  the time and place of the meeting of shareholders shall be published
  once a week for at least four consecutive weeks before the date of the
  meeting in a newspaper in the place where the head office of the
  insurance holding company is situated and in each place in Canada
  where the insurance holding company has a transfer agent or where a
  transfer of the insurance holding company's shares may be recorded.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice not required

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Notice of a meeting of shareholders is not required
  to be sent to shareholders who are not registered on the records of
  the insurance holding company or the insurance holding company's
  transfer agent on the record date fixed under paragraph 766(1)(c) or
  determined under paragraph 766(2)(a).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of default

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} Failure to receive a notice of a meeting of
  shareholders does not deprive a shareholder of the right to vote at
  the meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 314
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-767-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 767"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of adjourned meeting

- **[[768]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-768 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a
  meeting of shareholders is adjourned for less than thirty days, it is
  not necessary, unless the by-laws otherwise provide, to give notice of
  the adjourned meeting, other than by announcement at the earliest
  meeting that is adjourned.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice after longer adjournment

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a meeting of shareholders is adjourned by one or
  more adjournments for a total of thirty days or more, notice of the
  continuation of the meeting shall be given as for an original meeting
  but, unless the meeting is adjourned by one or more adjournments for a
  total of more than ninety days, subsection 788(1) does not apply.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Special business

- **[[769]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-769 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} All
  matters dealt with at a special meeting of shareholders or at an
  annual meeting of shareholders are deemed to be special business,
  except that special business does not include consideration of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the financial statements;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the auditor's report;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the election of directors; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the remuneration of directors and reappointment of
    the incumbent auditor.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of special business

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Notice of a meeting of shareholders at which special
  business is to be transacted must

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} state the nature of the special business in
    sufficient detail to permit a shareholder to form a reasoned
    judgment thereon; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} contain the text of any special resolution to be
    submitted to the meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

##### [Shareholder Proposals]{.HTitleText4} {#h-266913 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proposals

- **[[770]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-770
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (1.1) and
  (1.2), a registered holder or a beneficial owner of shares that may be
  voted at an annual meeting of shareholders may

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} submit to the insurance holding company notice of
    any matter that they propose to raise at the meeting (in this
    section and section 771 referred to as a "proposal"); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} discuss at the meeting any matter in respect of
    which they would have been entitled to submit a proposal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Eligibility to submit proposal

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} To be eligible to submit a proposal a person shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} for at least the prescribed period be the
    registered holder or beneficial owner of at least the prescribed
    number of the insurance holding company's outstanding shares; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} have the support of persons who, in the aggregate
    and including or not including the person who submits the proposal,
    have for at least the prescribed period been the registered holders
    or beneficial owners of at least the prescribed number of the
    insurance holding company's outstanding shares.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information to be provided

  [(1.2)]{.lawlabel} A proposal is to be accompanied by the following
  information:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the person submitting the
    proposal and the names and addresses of their supporters, if any;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number of shares held or owned by the person
    and their supporters and the date that the shares were acquired.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information not part of proposal

  [(1.3)]{.lawlabel} The information provided under subsection (1.2)
  does not form part of a proposal or of the supporting statement
  referred to in subsection (3) and is not to be included for the
  purposes of the prescribed maximum number of words referred to in
  subsection (3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proof may be required

  [(1.4)]{.lawlabel} If the insurance holding company requests within
  the prescribed period that a person provide proof that they are
  eligible to submit a proposal, the person shall within the prescribed
  period provide proof that they meet the requirements of subsection
  (1.1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Circulation of proposal

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An insurance holding company shall attach any
  proposal of a shareholder submitted for consideration at a meeting of
  shareholders to the notice of the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Supporting statement

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} At the request of the person who submits a proposal,
  the insurance holding company shall attach to the notice of the
  meeting the person's statement in support of the proposal and their
  name and address. The statement and proposal together are not to
  exceed the prescribed maximum number of words.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Nomination of directors

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A proposal may include nominations for the election
  of directors if it is signed by one or more registered holders or
  beneficial owners of shares representing in the aggregate not less
  than 5% of the shares of the insurance holding company or 5% of the
  shares of a class of its shares entitled to vote at the meeting at
  which the proposal is to be presented.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exemption

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} An insurance holding company is not required to
  comply with subsections (2) and (3) if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the proposal is not submitted to the insurance
    holding company at least the prescribed number of days before the
    anniversary date of the notice of meeting that was sent to
    shareholders in respect of the previous annual meeting of
    shareholders;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} it clearly appears that the primary purpose of the
    proposal is to enforce a personal claim or redress a personal
    griev­ance against the insurance holding company or its directors,
    officers or security holders;

  - [(b.1)]{.lawlabel} it clearly appears that the proposal does not
    relate in a significant way to the business or affairs of the
    insurance holding company;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the person submitting the proposal failed within
    the prescribed period before the insurance holding company receives
    their proposal to present, in person or by proxy, at a meeting of
    shareholders a proposal that at their request had been attached to
    the notice of the meeting;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} substantially the same proposal was set out in or
    attached to a dissident's proxy circular or a notice of a meeting
    relating to, and presented to shareholders at, a meeting of
    shareholders held within the prescribed period before the receipt of
    the proposal and did not receive the prescribed minimum amount of
    support at the meeting; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the rights conferred by subsections (1) to (4) are
    being abused to secure publicity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Insurance holding company may refuse to
  include proposal

  [(5.1)]{.lawlabel} If a person who submits a proposal fails to
  continue to hold or own shares in accordance with paragraph (1.1)(a)
  or, as the case may be, does not continue to have the support of
  persons who are in the aggregate the registered holders or beneficial
  owners of the prescribed number of shares in accordance with paragraph
  (1.1)(b) until the end of the meeting, the insurance holding company
  is not required to attach any proposal submitted by that person to a
  notice of a meeting for any meeting held within the prescribed period
  after the day of the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Immunity for proposal and statement

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} No insurance holding company or person acting on
  behalf of an insurance holding company incurs any liability by reason
  only of circulating a proposal or statement in compliance with
  subsections (2) and (3).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 315
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-770-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 770"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of refusal

- **[[771]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-771 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  an insurance holding company refuses to attach a proposal to a notice
  of a meeting, it shall in writing notify the person submitting the
  proposal of its intention not to attach the proposal and of the
  reasons for the refusal. It shall notify the person within the
  prescribed period after either the day on which it receives the
  proposal or, if it has requested proof under subsection 770(1.4), the
  day on which it receives the proof.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application to court

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} On the application of a person submitting a proposal
  who claims to be aggrieved by an insurance holding company's refusal
  under subsection (1), a court may restrain the holding of the meeting
  at which the proposal is sought to be presented and make any further
  order that it thinks fit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appeal to court

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An insurance holding company or any person claiming
  to be aggrieved by a proposal may apply to a court for an order
  permitting the insurance holding company not to attach the proposal to
  the notice of the meeting, and the court, if it is satisfied that
  subsection 770(5) applies, may make such order as it thinks fit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice to Superintendent

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} An applicant under subsection (2) or (3) shall give
  the Superintendent written notice of the application and the
  Superintendent may appear and be heard at the hearing of the
  application in person or by counsel.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 316
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-771-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 771"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Shareholder List]{.HTitleText4} {#h-266962 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}List of shareholders entitled to notice

- **[[772]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-772 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  insurance holding company shall prepare an alphabetical list of
  shareholders entitled to receive notice of a meeting, showing the
  number of shares held by each shareholder

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if a record date is fixed under paragraph
    766(1)(c), no later than 10 days after that date; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if no record date is fixed, on the record date
    determined under paragraph 766(2)(a).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voting list

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The insurance holding company shall prepare an
  alphabetical list of shareholders entitled to vote as of the record
  date showing the number of shares held by each shareholder

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if a record date is fixed under paragraph
    766(1)(d), no later than 10 days after that date; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if no record date is fixed under paragraph
    766(1)(d), no later than 10 days after a record date is fixed under
    paragraph 766(1)(c) or no later than the record date determined
    under paragraph 766(2)(a), as the case may be.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Entitlement to vote

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 793, a shareholder whose name
  appears on a list prepared under subsection (2) is entitled to vote
  the shares shown opposite their name.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Examination of list

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A shareholder may examine the list of shareholders

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} during usual business hours at the head office of
    the insurance holding company or at the place where its central
    securities register is maintained; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} at the meeting of shareholders for which the list
    was prepared.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 317
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-772-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 772"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Quorum]{.HTitleText4} {#h-266980 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholders

- **[[773]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-773
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Unless the by-laws otherwise
  provide, a quorum of shareholders is present at a meeting of
  shareholders if the holders of a majority of the shares who are
  entitled to vote at the meeting are present in person or represented
  by proxyholders.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Quorum at opening

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a quorum is present at the opening of a meeting of
  shareholders, the shareholders present may, unless the by-laws
  otherwise provide, proceed with the business of the meeting,
  notwithstanding that a quorum is not present throughout the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No quorum at opening

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a quorum is not present at the opening of a
  meeting of shareholders, the shareholders present may adjourn the
  meeting to a fixed time and place but may not transact any other
  business.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}One shareholder meeting

**[[774]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-774 .sectionLabel}** If an insurance holding
company has only one shareholder, or only one holder of any class or
series of shares, the shareholder present in person or represented by a
proxyholder constitutes a meeting of shareholders or a meeting of
shareholders of that class or series.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

##### [Voting]{.HTitleText4} {#h-266994 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}One share --- one vote

**[[775]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-775 .sectionLabel}** Subject to section 793,
if a share of an insurance holding company entitles the holder of the
share to vote at a meeting of shareholders, that share entitles the
shareholder to one vote at the meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Representative shareholder

- **[[776]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-776 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  an entity is a shareholder of an insurance holding company, the
  insurance holding company shall recognize any natural person
  authorized by a resolution of the directors or governing body or
  similar authority of the entity to represent it at meetings of
  shareholders of the insurance holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers of representative

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A natural person authorized under subsection (1) to
  represent an entity may exercise on behalf of the entity all the
  powers the entity could exercise if the entity were a natural person
  who was a shareholder.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Joint shareholders

**[[777]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-777 .sectionLabel}** Unless the by-laws
otherwise provide, if two or more persons hold shares jointly, one of
those holders present at a meeting of shareholders may in the absence of
the others vote the shares, but if two or more of those persons who are
present in person or represented by proxyholder vote, they shall vote as
one on the shares jointly held by them.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voting by hands or ballot

- **[[778]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-778
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Unless the by-laws otherwise
  provide, voting at a meeting of shareholders shall take place by show
  of hands except when a ballot is demanded by a shareholder or
  proxyholder entitled to vote at the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ballot

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A shareholder or proxyholder may demand a ballot
  either before or after any vote by show of hands.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Electronic voting

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1) and unless the by-laws provide
  otherwise, any vote referred to in that subsection may be held
  entirely by means of a telephonic, electronic or other communication
  facility if the insurance holding company makes one available.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Voting while participating
  electronically

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Unless the by-laws provide otherwise, any person who
  is participating in a meeting of shareholders under subsection 764(2)
  and entitled to vote at that meeting may vote by means of the
  telephonic, electronic or other communication facility that the
  insurance holding company has made available for that purpose.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council may make regulations
  respecting the manner of and conditions for voting at a meeting of
  shareholders by means of a telephonic, electronic or other
  communication facility.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 318
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-778-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 778"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Resolution in lieu of Meeting]{.HTitleText4} {#h-267023 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Resolution in lieu of meeting

- **[[779]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-779
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except where a written statement is
  submitted by a director under section 809 or by an auditor under
  subsection 900(1),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a resolution in writing signed by all the
    shareholders entitled to vote on that resolution at a meeting of
    shareholders is as valid as if it had been passed at a meeting of
    the shareholders; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a resolution in writing dealing with all matters
    required by this Part to be dealt with at a meeting of shareholders,
    and signed by all the shareholders entitled to vote at that meeting,
    satisfies all the requirements of this Part relating to meetings of
    shareholders.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Filing resolution

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A copy of every resolution referred to in
  subsection (1) shall be kept with the minutes of the meetings of
  shareholders.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Evidence

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Unless a ballot is demanded, an entry in the minutes
  of a meeting that the chairperson declared a resolution to be carried
  or defeated is in the absence of evidence to the contrary proof of
  that fact without proof of the number or proportion of votes recorded
  in favour of or against the resolution.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 319
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-779-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 779"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Requisitioned Meetings]{.HTitleText4} {#h-267035 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Requisitioned meeting

- **[[780]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-780
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Shareholders who together hold not
  less than 5 per cent of the issued and outstanding shares of an
  insurance holding company that carry the right to vote at a meeting
  sought to be held may requisition the directors to call a meeting of
  shareholders for the purposes stated in the requisition.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Form

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A requisition referred to in subsection (1)

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} must state the business to be transacted at the
    meeting and must be sent to each director and to the head office of
    the insurance holding company; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} may consist of several documents of like form, each
    signed by one or more shareholders.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors calling meeting

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} On receipt of a requisition referred to in subsection
  (1), the directors shall call a meeting of shareholders to transact
  the business stated in the requisition, unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a record date has been fixed under paragraph
    766(1)(c) and notice of it has been given under subsection 766(3);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the directors have called a meeting of shareholders
    and have given notice thereof under section 767; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the business of the meeting as stated in the
    requisition includes matters described in paragraphs 770(5)(b) to
    (e).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholders' power

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the directors do not call a meeting within
  twenty-one days after receiving a requisition referred to in
  subsection (1), any shareholder who signed the requisition may call
  the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Procedure

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A meeting called under this section shall be called
  as nearly as possible in the manner in which meetings are to be called
  pursuant to the by-laws and this Part.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reimbursement

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Unless the shareholders otherwise resolve at a
  meeting called under subsection (4), the insurance holding company
  shall reimburse the shareholders for any expenses reasonably incurred
  by them in requisitioning, calling and holding the meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 320
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-780-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 780"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Powers of the Court]{.HTitleText4} {#h-267056 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Court may order meeting to be called

- **[[781]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-781 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  court may, on the application of a director, a shareholder who is
  entitled to vote at a meeting of shareholders or the Superintendent,
  order a meeting to be called, held or conducted in the manner that the
  court directs if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} it is impracticable to call the meeting within the
    time or in the manner in which it is to be called;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} it is impracticable to conduct the meeting in the
    manner required by this Part or the by-laws; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the court thinks that the meeting ought to be
    called, held or conducted within the time or in the manner that it
    directs for any other reason.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2005, c. 54, s. 321\]]{.Repealed}

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Varying quorum

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Without restricting the generality of subsection (1),
  a court may order that the quorum required by the by-laws or this Part
  be varied or dispensed with at a meeting called, held and conducted
  pursuant to this section.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Valid meeting

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A meeting called, held and conducted pursuant to this
  section is for all purposes a meeting of shareholders of the insurance
  holding company duly called, held and conducted.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 321
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-781-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 781"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Court review of election

- **[[782]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-782 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  insurance holding company or a shareholder or director of an insurance
  holding company may apply to a court to resolve any dispute in respect
  of the election or appointment of a director or an auditor of the
  insurance holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers of court

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} On an application under subsection (1), a court may
  make any order it thinks fit including, without limiting the
  generality of the foregoing,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an order restraining a director or auditor whose
    election or appointment is challenged from acting pending
    determination of the dispute;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an order declaring the result of the disputed
    election or appointment;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} an order requiring a new election or appointment,
    and including in the order directions for the management of the
    business and affairs of the insurance holding company until a new
    election is held or the new appointment is made; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} an order determining the voting rights of
    shareholders and persons claiming to own shares.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice to Superintendent

- **[[783]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-783 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person who makes an application under subsection 781(1) or 782(1)
  shall give notice of the application to the Superintendent before the
  hearing and shall deliver a copy of the order of the court, if any, to
  the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Superintendent representation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent may appear and be heard in person
  or by counsel at the hearing of an application referred to in
  subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

##### [Pooling Agreements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-267088 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Pooling agreement

**[[784]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-784 .sectionLabel}** A written agreement
between two or more shareholders may provide that in exercising voting
rights the shares held by them will be voted as provided in the
agreement.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

#### [SUBDIVISION 2]{.HLabel3}[Proxies and Restrictions on Voting]{.HTitleText3} {#h-267093 .Subheading}

##### [Proxies]{.HTitleText4} {#h-267094 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

**[[785]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-785 .sectionLabel}** The following
definitions apply in this Subdivision.

[[intermediary]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[intermediary]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person who holds a
    security on behalf of another person who is not the registered
    holder of the security, and includes

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a securities broker or dealer required to be
      registered to trade or deal in securities under the laws of any
      jurisdiction;

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a securities depositary;

    - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a financial institution;

    - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in respect of a clearing agency, a securities
      dealer, trust company, association within the meaning of section 2
      of the [Cooperative Credit Associations Act](/eng/acts/C-41.01),
      bank or other person, including another clearing agency, on whose
      behalf the clearing agency or its nominee holds securities of an
      issuer;

    - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a trustee or administrator of a self-administered
      retirement savings plan, retirement income fund or education
      savings plan or another similar self-administered savings or
      investment plan that is registered under the [Income Tax
      Act](/eng/acts/I-3.3);

    - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a nominee of a person referred to in any of
      paragraphs (a) to (e); and

    - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a person who performs functions similar to those
      performed by a person referred to in any of paragraphs (a) to (e)
      and holds a security registered in their name, or in the name of
      their nominee, on behalf of another person who is not the
      registered holder of the
      security. ([intermédiaire]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[registrant]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[registrant]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed, 2005, c. 54, s.
    322\]]{.Repealed}

[[solicitation]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[solicitation]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} includes

      - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a request for a proxy whether or not
        accompanied by or included in a form of proxy,

      - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a request to execute or not to execute or, in
        Quebec, to sign or not to sign a form of proxy or to revoke a
        proxy,

      - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the sending of a form of proxy or other
        communication to a shareholder under circumstances reasonably
        calculated to result in the procurement, withholding or
        revocation of a proxy, and

      - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the sending of a form of proxy to a
        shareholder under subsection 788(1); but

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} does not include

      - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the sending of a form of proxy in response to
        an unsolicited request made by or on behalf of a shareholder,

      - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the performance of administrative acts or
        professional services on behalf of a person soliciting a proxy,

      - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the sending by an intermediary of the
        documents referred to in subsection 791(1),

      - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a solicitation by a person in respect of
        shares of which they are the beneficial owner,

      - [(v)]{.lawlabel} a prescribed public announcement by a
        shareholder of how they intend to vote and the reasons for that
        decision,

      - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} a communication for the purposes of obtaining
        the support of persons in accord­ance with paragraph 770(1.1)(b),
        or

      - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} a communication, other than a solic­itation by
        or on behalf of the management of an insurance holding company,
        that is made to shareholders in the prescribed
        circumstances. ([sollicitation]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[solicitation by or on behalf of the management of an insurance holding company]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[solicitation by or on behalf of the management of an insurance
    holding company]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a solicitation by any
    person pursuant to a resolution or instruction of, or with the
    acquiescence of, the directors or a committee of the directors of
    the insurance holding company. ([sollicitation effectuée par la
    direction d'une société de portefeuille d'assurances ou pour son
    compte]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 322
- [2022, c. 10, s. 230(E)](#1357194-1485920){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1357194-1485920.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-785-20061128.html "Link to previous version of section 785"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointing proxyholder

- **[[786]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-786 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  shareholder who is entitled to vote at a meeting of shareholders may,
  by executing a form of proxy, appoint a proxyholder or one or more
  alternate proxyholders, who are not required to be shareholders, to
  attend and act at the meeting in the manner and to the extent
  authorized by the proxy and with the authority conferred by the proxy.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Execution of proxy

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A form of proxy shall be executed by a shareholder or
  by a shareholder's attorney authorized in writing to do so.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limit on authority

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} No appointment of a proxyholder provides authority
  for the proxyholder to act in respect of the appointment of an auditor
  or the election of a director unless a nominee proposed in good faith
  for the appointment or election is named in the form of proxy, a
  management proxy circular, a dissident's proxy circular or a proposal
  under subsection 770(1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Required information

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A form of proxy must indicate, in bold-face type,
  that the shareholder by whom or on whose behalf it is executed may
  appoint a proxyholder, other than a person designated in the form of
  proxy, to attend and act on the shareholder's behalf at a meeting to
  which the proxy relates, and must contain instructions as to the
  manner in which the shareholder may do so.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Validity of proxy

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A proxy is valid only at the meeting in respect of
  which it is given or at a continuation of the meeting after an
  adjournment.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Revocation of proxy

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} A shareholder may revoke a proxy

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} by depositing an instrument in writing executed by
    the shareholder or by the shareholder's attorney authorized in
    writing to do so

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} at the head office of the insurance holding
      company at any time up to and including the last business day
      before the day of a meeting, or a continuation of a meeting after
      an adjournment, at which the proxy is to be used, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} with the chairperson of the meeting on the day
      of the meeting or a continuation of the meeting after an
      adjournment; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in any other manner permitted by law.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deposit of proxies

- **[[787]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-787 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  directors may specify, in a notice calling a meeting of shareholders
  or a continuation of a meeting of shareholders after an adjournment, a
  time before which executed forms of proxy to be used at the meeting or
  the continued meeting must be deposited with the insurance holding
  company or its transfer agent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Time for deposit of proxies

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The time specified for the deposit of forms of proxy
  may not precede the meeting or the continued meeting by more than
  forty-eight hours, excluding Saturdays and holidays.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Mandatory solicitation

- **[[788]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-788
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) and
  768(2), the management of an insurance holding company shall,
  concurrently with sending notice of a meeting of shareholders, send a
  form of proxy that is in accordance with the regulations to each
  shareholder entitled to receive notice of the meeting under section
  767.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The management of an insurance holding company is not
  required to send a form of proxy under subsection (1) if the insurance
  holding company

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is not a distributing insurance holding company;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} has 50 or fewer shareholders who are entitled to
    vote at a meeting, two or more joint holders of a share being
    counted as one shareholder.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 323
- [2022, c. 10, s. 226](#1357180-1366988){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1357180-1366988.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-788-20061128.html "Link to previous version of section 788"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Soliciting proxies

- **[[789]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-789 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person shall not solicit proxies unless a proxy circular that is in
  accordance with the regulations is sent to the auditor of the
  insurance holding company, to each shareholder whose proxy is
  solicited and, in the case set out in paragraph (b), to the bank as
  follows:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of solicitation by or on behalf of the
    management of an insurance holding company, a management proxy
    circular, either as an appendix to or as a separate document
    accompanying the notice of the meeting; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of any other solicitation, a
    dissident's proxy circular stating the purposes of the solicitation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- limited solicitation

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), a person may solicit
  proxies, other than by or on behalf of the management of the insurance
  holding company, without sending a dissident's proxy circular, if the
  total number of shareholders whose proxies are solicited is 15 or
  fewer, with two or more joint holders being counted as one
  shareholder.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception --- solicitation by public
  broadcast

  [(1.2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), a person may solicit
  proxies, other than by or on behalf of the management of the insurance
  holding company, without sending a dissident's proxy circular if the
  solicitation is, in the prescribed circumstances, conveyed by public
  broadcast, speech or publication.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Copy to Superintendent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who sends a management proxy circular or
  dissident's proxy circular shall concurrently send to the
  Superintendent a copy of it together with the form of proxy, any other
  documents for use in connection with the meeting and, in the case of a
  management proxy circular, a copy of the notice of meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exemption by Superintendent

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} On the application of an interested person, the
  Superintendent may, on any terms that the Superintendent thinks fit,
  exempt the person from any of the requirements of subsection (1) and
  section 788, and the exemption may be given retroactive effect.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reporting exemptions

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent shall publish in a publication
  generally available to the public, a notice of a decision made by the
  Superintendent granting an exemption under subsection (3).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- [2022, c. 10, s. 227](#1357182-1367000){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1357182-1367000.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-789-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 789"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Attendance at meeting

- **[[790]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-790 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  person who solicits a proxy and is appointed proxyholder shall attend
  in person or cause an alternate proxyholder to attend every meeting in
  respect of which the proxy is valid, and the proxyholder or alternate
  proxyholder shall comply with the directions of the shareholder who
  executed the form of proxy.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Rights of proxyholder

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A proxyholder or an alternate proxyholder has the
  same rights as the appointing shareholder to speak at a meeting of
  shareholders in respect of any matter, to vote by way of ballot at the
  meeting and, except where a proxyholder or an alternate proxyholder
  has conflicting instructions from more than one shareholder, to vote
  at the meeting in respect of any matter by way of a show of hands.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Vote by show of hands

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsections (1) and (2) and unless a
  shareholder or proxyholder demands a ballot, if the chairperson of a
  meeting of shareholders declares to the meeting that, if a ballot were
  conducted, the total number of votes attached to shares represented at
  the meeting by proxy required to be voted against what, to the
  knowledge of the chairperson, would be the decision of the meeting on
  a matter or group of matters is less than 5% of all the votes that
  might be cast by shareholders in person or by proxy,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the chairperson may conduct the vote in respect of
    that matter or group of matters by way of a show of hands; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a proxyholder or alternate proxyholder may vote in
    respect of that matter or group of matters by way of a show of
    hands.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 325
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-790-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 790"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duty of intermediary

- **[[791]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-791
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Shares of an insurance holding
  company that are registered in the name of an intermediary or an
  intermediary's nominee and not beneficially owned by the intermediary
  may not be voted unless the intermediary sends to the beneficial owner

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a copy of the notice of the meeting, annual
    statement, management proxy circular and dissident's proxy circular
    and any other documents, other than the form of proxy, that were
    sent to shareholders by or on behalf of any person for use in
    connection with the meeting; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a written request for voting instructions except if
    the intermediary has already received written voting instructions
    from the beneficial owner.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}When documents to be sent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The intermediary shall send the documents referred to
  in subsection (1) without delay after they receive the documents
  referred to in paragraph (1)(a).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction on voting

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An intermediary or a proxyholder appointed by them
  may not vote shares that the intermediary does not beneficially own
  and that are registered in the name of the intermediary or their
  nominee unless the intermediary or proxyholder, as the case may be,
  receives written voting instructions from the beneficial owner.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Copies

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A person by or on behalf of whom a solicitation is
  made shall on request and without delay provide the intermediary, at
  the person's expense, with the necessary number of copies of the
  documents referred to in paragraph (1)(a).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Instructions to intermediary

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The intermediary shall vote or appoint a proxyholder
  to vote any shares referred to in subsection (1) in accordance with
  any written voting instructions received from the beneficial owner.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Beneficial owner as proxyholder

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} If a beneficial owner so requests and provides an
  intermediary with the appropriate documentation, the intermediary
  shall appoint the beneficial owner or a nominee of the beneficial
  owner as proxyholder.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of intermediary's failure to
  comply

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} The failure of an intermediary to comply with any of
  subsections (1) to (6) does not render void any meeting of
  shareholders or any action taken at the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Intermediary may not vote

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} Nothing in this Subdivision gives an intermediary the
  right to vote shares that they are otherwise prohibited from voting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 326
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-791-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 791"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations

**[[791.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-791.1 .sectionLabel}** The Governor in
Council may make regulations

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} respecting the powers that may be granted by a
  shareholder in a form of proxy;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} respecting proxy circulars and forms of proxy,
  including the form and content of those documents; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} respecting the conditions under which an insurance
  holding company is exempt from any of the requirements of sections 786
  to 791.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 326
- [2022, c. 10, s. 228](#1357187-1367007){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1357187-1367007.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-791.1-20061128.html "Link to previous version of section 791.1"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restraining order

- **[[792]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-792 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a
  form of proxy, management proxy circular or dissident's proxy circular
  contains an untrue statement of a material fact or omits to state a
  material fact that is required to be contained in it or that is
  necessary to make a statement contained in it not misleading in light
  of the circumstances in which the statement is made, an interested
  person or the Superintendent may apply to a court and the court may
  make any order it thinks fit including

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an order restraining the solicitation or the
    holding of the meeting, or restraining any person from implementing
    or acting on a resolution passed at the meeting, to which the form
    of proxy, management proxy circular or dissident's proxy circular
    relates;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an order requiring correction of any form of proxy
    or proxy circular and a further solicitation; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} an order adjourning the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of application

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a person other than the Superintendent is an
  applicant under subsection (1), the applicant shall give to the
  Superintendent notice of the application and the Superintendent is
  entitled to appear and to be heard in person or by counsel.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

##### [Restrictions on Voting]{.HTitleText4} {#h-267215 .Subheading}

Meaning of [[eligible votes]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

- **[[793]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-793 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In
  this section, [[eligible votes]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the total
  number of votes that may be cast by or on behalf of shareholders on a
  vote of shareholders or a vote of holders of a class or series of
  shares, as the case may be, in respect of any particular matter,
  calculated without regard to subsection (2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} At a meeting of shareholders of an insurance holding
  company in respect of which subsection 927(4) applies, no person and
  no entity controlled by any person may, in respect of any vote of
  shareholders or holders of any class or series of shares of the
  company, cast votes in respect of any shares beneficially owned by the
  person or the entity that are, in aggregate, more than 20 per cent of
  the eligible votes that may be cast in respect of that vote.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proxyholders

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} No person who is a proxyholder for a person or for an
  entity controlled by a person may cast votes to which the proxy
  relates that the person or entity may not cast by reason of subsection
  (2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subsections (2) and (3) do not apply in respect of a
  vote held under section 852.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Validity of vote

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A vote in respect of a particular matter is not
  invalid merely because a person voted contrary to subsection (2) or
  (3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disposition of shareholdings

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} If, with respect to any insurance holding company, a
  person contravenes subsection (2) or (3), the Minister may, by order,
  direct the shareholder of the shares to which the contravention
  relates or any person controlled by that shareholder to dispose of any
  number of shares of the insurance holding company beneficially owned
  by any of those persons that the Minister specifies in the order,
  within the time specified in the order and in the proportion, if any,
  as between the shareholder and the persons controlled by that
  shareholder that is specified in the order.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction on voting rights

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister makes an order under subsection (6),
  the person to whom the order relates may not, in person or by proxy,
  exercise any voting rights that are attached to shares of the company
  beneficially owned by the person.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Subsection (7) ceases to apply

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (7) shall cease to apply in respect of a
  person when the shares to which the order relates have been disposed
  of.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reliance on number in notice

  [(9)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of this section, a person is entitled
  to rely on the number of eligible votes set out in a notice of a
  meeting under subsection 767(2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Designation of persons

  [(10)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of this section, the Minister may,
  with respect to a particular insurance holding company, designate two
  or more persons who are parties to an agreement, commitment or
  understanding referred to in section 9 to be a single person.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

#### [SUBDIVISION 3]{.HLabel3}[Directors and Officers]{.HTitleText3} {#h-267239 .Subheading}

##### [Duties]{.HTitleText4} {#h-267240 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duty to manage

- **[[794]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-794
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to this Act, the directors
  of an insurance holding company shall manage or supervise the
  management of the business and affairs of the insurance holding
  company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Specific duties

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Without limiting the generality of subsection (1),
  the directors of an insurance holding company shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} establish an audit committee to perform the duties
    referred to in subsections 829(3) and (4);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} establish procedures to resolve conflicts of
    interest, including techniques for the identification of potential
    conflict situations and for restricting the use of confidential
    information;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} designate a committee of the board of directors to
    monitor the procedures referred to in paragraph (b); and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} establish investment and lending policies,
    standards and procedures in accordance with section 968.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Paragraph (2)(a) does not apply to the directors of
  an insurance holding company if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} all the voting shares of the insurance holding
    company are beneficially owned by a Canadian financial institution
    described by any of paragraphs (a) to (d) of the definition
    [[financial institution]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} in subsection 2(1);
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the audit committee of the Canadian financial
    institution referred to in paragraph (a) performs for and on behalf
    of the insurance holding company all the functions that would
    otherwise be required to be performed by the audit committee of the
    insurance holding company under this Part.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duty of care

- **[[795]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-795
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every director and officer of an
  insurance holding company in exercising any of the powers of a
  director or an officer and discharging any of the duties of a director
  or an officer shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} act honestly and in good faith with a view to the
    best interests of the insurance holding company; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} exercise the care, diligence and skill that a
    reasonably prudent person would exercise in comparable
    circumstances.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duty to comply

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Every director, officer and employee of an insurance
  holding company shall comply with this Act, the regulations, the
  insurance holding company's incorporating instrument and the by-laws
  of the insurance holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No exculpation

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} No provision in any contract, in any resolution or in
  the by-laws of an insurance holding company relieves any director,
  officer or employee of the insurance holding company from the duty to
  act in accordance with this Act and the regulations or relieves a
  director, officer or employee from liability for a breach thereof.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

##### [Qualification and Number --- Directors]{.HTitleText4} {#h-267267 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Minimum number of directors

- **[[796]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-796 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  insurance holding company shall have at least seven directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Residency requirement

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} At least one half of the directors of an insurance
  holding company that is a subsidiary of a foreign institution and a
  majority of the directors of any other insurance holding company must
  be, at the time of each director's election or appointment, resident
  Canadians.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2007, c. 6, s. 319
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-796-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 796"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disqualified persons

**[[797]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-797 .sectionLabel}** The following persons
are disqualified from being directors of an insurance holding company:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a person who is less than eighteen years of age;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a person who is of unsound mind and has been so found
  by a court in Canada or elsewhere;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a person who has the status of a bankrupt;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a person who is not a natural person;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} a person who is prohibited by subsection 793(7) or
  section 945 or 955 from exercising voting rights attached to shares of
  the insurance holding company;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} a person who is an officer, director or full-time
  employee of an entity that is prohibited by subsection 793(7) or
  section 945 or 955 from exercising voting rights attached to shares of
  the insurance holding company;

- [(f.1)]{.lawlabel} a person who is an officer, director, employee or
  agent of --- or any other person acting on behalf of --- an eligible
  agent within the meaning of section 406.1;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2013, c. 40, s. 165\]]{.Repealed}

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} a minister of Her Majesty in right of Canada or in
  right of a province; and

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} a person who is an agent or employee of the
  government of a foreign country or any political subdivision thereof.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2012, c. 19, s. 344, c. 31, s. 141
- 2013, c. 40, s. 165
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-797-20121214.html "Link to previous version of section 797"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No requirement to hold shares

**[[798]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-798 .sectionLabel}** A director of an
insurance holding company is not required to hold shares of the
insurance holding company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limit on directors

**[[799]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-799 .sectionLabel}** No more than 15 per
cent of the directors of an insurance holding company may, at each
director's election or appointment, be employees of the insurance
holding company or a subsidiary of the insurance holding company, except
that up to four persons who are employees of the insurance holding
company or a subsidiary of the insurance holding company may be
directors of the insurance holding company if those directors constitute
not more than one half of the directors of the insurance holding
company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

##### [Election and Tenure --- Directors]{.HTitleText4} {#h-267297 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Number of directors

- **[[800]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-800
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection 796(1) and
  sections 803 and 851, the directors of an insurance holding company
  shall, by by-law, determine the number of directors or the minimum and
  maximum number of directors, but no by-law that decreases the number
  of directors shortens the term of an incumbent director.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Election at annual meeting

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A by-law made pursuant to subsection (1) that
  provides for a minimum and maximum number of directors may provide
  that the number of directors to be elected at any annual meeting of
  the shareholders be such number as is fixed by the directors prior to
  the annual meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Election or appointment as director

**[[800.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-800.1 .sectionLabel}** The election or
appointment of a person as a director is subject to the following:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person was present at the meeting when the
  election or appointment took place and did not refuse to hold office
  as a director; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person was not present at the meeting when the
  election or appointment took place but

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} consented in writing to hold office as a director
    before the election or appointment or within 10 days after it, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} acted as a director after the election or
    appointment.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 327
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Term of directors

- **[[801]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except where this Part or the
  by-laws of an insurance holding company provide for cumulative voting,
  the insurance holding company may, by by-law, provide that the
  directors be elected for terms of one, two or three years.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Term of one, two or three years

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director elected for a term of one, two or three
  years holds office until the close of the first, second or third
  annual meeting of shareholders, as the case may be, following the
  election of the director.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No stated term

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A director who is not elected for an expressly stated
  term of office ceases to hold office at the close of the next annual
  meeting of shareholders following the election of the director.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Tenure of office

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} It is not necessary that all directors elected at a
  meeting of shareholders hold office for the same term.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Tenure of office

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If a by-law of an insurance holding company provides
  that the directors be elected for a term of two or three years, it may
  also provide that the term of office of each director be for the whole
  of that term, or that, as nearly as may be, one half of the directors
  retire each year if the term is two years, and that one third of the
  directors retire each year if the term is three years.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Composition requirements

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Where a director of an insurance holding company is
  elected or appointed for a term of more than one year, the insurance
  holding company shall comply with subsection 796(2) and section 799 at
  each annual meeting of shareholders during the director's term of
  office as if that director were elected or appointed on that date.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Determining election of directors

- **[[802]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-802
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except where this Part or the
  by-laws of an insurance holding company provide for cumulative voting,
  the persons, to the number authorized to be elected, who receive the
  greatest number of votes at an election of directors of an insurance
  holding company shall be the directors thereof.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Equal number of votes

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If, at any election of directors referred to in
  subsection (1), two or more persons receive an equal number of votes
  and there are not sufficient vacancies remaining to enable all the
  persons receiving an equal number of votes to be elected, the
  directors who receive a greater number of votes or the majority of
  them shall, in order to complete the full number of directors,
  determine which of the persons so receiving an equal number of votes
  are to be elected.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Cumulative voting

- **[[803]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-803
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where this Part or the by-laws
  provide for cumulative voting,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} there shall be a stated number determined by
    by-law, and not a minimum and maximum number, of directors;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} each shareholder entitled to vote at an election of
    directors to be elected by cumulative voting has the right to cast a
    number of votes equal to the number of votes attached to the shares
    held by the shareholder multiplied by the number of directors to be
    elected by cumulative voting, and the shareholder may cast all such
    votes in favour of one candidate or distribute them among the
    candidates in any manner;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a separate vote shall be taken with respect to each
    candidate nominated for a position that is to be filled by
    cumulative voting unless a resolution is passed unanimously
    permitting two or more persons to be elected by a single vote;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} if a shareholder has voted for more than one
    candidate without specifying the distribution of the votes among the
    candidates, the shareholder is deemed to have distributed the votes
    equally among the candidates for whom the shareholder voted;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} if the number of candidates nominated exceeds the
    number of positions to be filled, the candidates who receive the
    least number of votes shall be eliminated until the number of
    candidates remaining equals the number of positions to be filled;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} each director elected by cumulative voting ceases
    to hold office at the close of the next annual meeting of
    shareholders following the director's election;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a director may be removed from office only if the
    number of votes cast in favour of a motion to remove the director is
    greater than the product of the number of directors required by the
    by-laws and the number of votes cast against the motion; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the number of directors required by the by-laws may
    be decreased only if the number of votes cast in favour of a motion
    to decrease the number of directors is greater than the product of
    the number of directors required by the by-laws and the number of
    votes cast against the motion.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Mandatory cumulative voting

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where the aggregate of the voting shares beneficially
  owned by a person and any entities controlled by the person carries
  more than 10 per cent of the voting rights attached to all the
  outstanding voting shares of an insurance holding company, the
  directors shall be elected by cumulative voting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (2) does not apply if all the voting
  shares of the insurance holding company that are outstanding are
  beneficially owned by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} one person;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} one person and one or more entities controlled by
    that person; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} one or more entities controlled by the same person.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (2) does not apply to an insurance holding
  company in respect of which subsection 927(4) applies.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transitional election

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Where this Part or the by-laws of an insurance
  holding company provide for cumulative voting, the shareholders of the
  insurance holding company shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at the first annual meeting of shareholders held
    not earlier than ninety days following the date that cumulative
    voting is required under subsection (2) or provided for in the
    by-laws, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} at each succeeding annual meeting,

  elect the stated number of directors to hold office until the close of
  the next annual meeting of shareholders following their election.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Class or series of shares

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Nothing in this Part precludes the holders of any
  class or series of shares of an insurance holding company from having
  an exclusive right to elect one or more directors.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 328
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-803-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 803"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Re-election of directors

**[[804]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-804 .sectionLabel}** A director who has
completed a term of office is, if otherwise qualified, eligible for
re-election.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

##### [Incomplete Elections and Director Vacancies]{.HTitleText4} {#h-267368 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Void election or appointment

- **[[805]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-805 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If,
  immediately after the time of any purported election or appointment of
  directors, the board of directors would fail to comply with subsection
  796(2) or section 799, the purported election or appointment of all
  persons purported to be elected or appointed at that time is void
  unless the directors, within forty-five days after the discovery of
  the non-compliance, develop a plan, approved by the Superintendent, to
  rectify the non-compliance.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Failure to elect minimum

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If, at the close of a meeting of shareholders of an
  insurance holding company, the shareholders have failed to elect the
  number or minimum number of directors required by this Part or the
  by-laws of an insurance holding company, the purported election of
  directors at the meeting

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is valid if the directors purported to be elected
    and those incumbent directors, if any, whose terms did not expire at
    the close of the meeting, together constitute a quorum; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is void if the directors purported to be elected
    and those incumbent directors, if any, whose terms did not expire at
    the close of the meeting, together do not constitute a quorum.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors where elections incomplete or
void

- **[[806]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-806
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsections 801(2) and (3)
  and paragraphs 803(1)(f) and 807(1)(a), where subsection 805(1) or (2)
  applies at the close of any meeting of shareholders of an insurance
  holding company, the board of directors shall, until their successors
  are elected or appointed, consist solely of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where paragraph 805(2)(a) applies, the directors
    referred to in that paragraph; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where subsection 805(1) or paragraph 805(2)(b)
    applies, those persons who were the incumbent directors immediately
    before the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Where there is no approved
  rectification plan

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsections 801(2) and (3) and paragraphs
  803(1)(f) and 807(1)(a), where a plan to rectify the non-compliance
  referred to in subsection 805(1) has not been approved by the
  Superintendent by the end of the forty-five day period referred to in
  that subsection, the board of directors shall, until their successors
  are elected or appointed, consist solely of the persons who were the
  incumbent directors immediately before the meeting at which the
  purported election or appointment referred to in that subsection
  occurred.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors to call meeting

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where subsection (1) or (2) applies, the board of
  directors referred to in that subsection shall without delay call a
  special meeting of shareholders to fill the vacancies, where paragraph
  805(2)(a) applies, or elect a new board of directors, where subsection
  805(1) or paragraph 805(2)(b) applies.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholder may call meeting

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where the directors fail to call a special meeting
