  required by subsection (3), the meeting may be called by any
  shareholder.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ceasing to hold office

- **[[807]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-807 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  director ceases to hold office

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at the close of the annual meeting at which the
    director's term of office expires;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} when the director dies or resigns;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} when the director becomes disqualified under
    section 797 or ineligible to hold office pursuant to subsection
    837(2);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} when the director is removed under section 808; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} when the director is removed from office under
    section 1006 or 1007.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Date of resignation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The resignation of a director of an insurance holding
  company becomes effective at the time a written resignation is sent to
  the insurance holding company by the director or at the time specified
  in the resignation, whichever is later.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Removal of director

- **[[808]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-808
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to paragraph 803(1)(g) and
  this section, the shareholders of an insurance holding company may by
  resolution at a special meeting remove any director or all the
  directors from office.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Removal of director

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the holders of any class or series of shares of an
  insurance holding company have the exclusive right to elect one or
  more directors, a director so elected may be removed only by a
  resolution at a meeting of the shareholders of that class or series.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Vacancy by removal

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to paragraphs 803(1)(b) to (e), a vacancy
  created by the removal of a director may be filled at the meeting of
  the shareholders at which the director is removed or, if not so
  filled, may be filled under section 812 or 813.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Statement of director

- **[[809]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-809 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  director who

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} resigns,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} receives a notice or otherwise learns of a meeting
    of shareholders called for the purpose of removing the director from
    office, or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} receives a notice or otherwise learns of a meeting
    of directors or shareholders at which another person is to be
    appointed or elected to fill the office of director, whether because
    of the director's resignation or removal or because the director's
    term of office has expired or is about to expire,

  is entitled to submit to the insurance holding company a written
  statement giving the reasons for the resignation or the reasons why
  the director opposes any proposed action or resolution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Statement to Superintendent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a director resigns as a result of a
  disagreement with the other directors or the officers of an insurance
  holding company, the director shall submit to the insurance holding
  company and the Superintendent a written statement setting out the
  nature of the disagreement.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Circulation of statement

- **[[810]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-810 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  insurance holding company shall forthwith on receipt of a director's
  statement referred to in subsection 809(1) relating to a matter
  referred to in paragraph 809(1)(b) or (c), or a director's statement
  referred to in subsection 809(2), send a copy thereof to each
  shareholder entitled to receive a notice of meetings and to the
  Superintendent, unless the statement is attached to a notice of a
  meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Immunity for statement

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No insurance holding company or person acting on its
  behalf incurs any liability by reason only of circulating a director's
  statement in compliance with subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholders filling vacancy

**[[811]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-811 .sectionLabel}** The by-laws of an
insurance holding company may provide that a vacancy among the directors
is to be filled only by vote of

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the shareholders; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the holders of any class or series of shares having
  an exclusive right to elect one or more directors if the vacancy
  occurs among the directors elected by the holders of that class or
  series.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors filling vacancy

- **[[812]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-812
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite section 819 but subject to
  subsection (2) and sections 811 and 813, a quorum of directors may
  fill a vacancy among the directors except a vacancy resulting from a
  change in the by-laws by which the number or the minimum or maximum
  number of directors is increased or from a failure to elect the number
  or minimum number of directors provided for in the by-laws.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Where composition fails

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite sections 811 and 819, where by reason of a
  vacancy the number of directors or the composition of the board of
  directors fails to meet any of the requirements of section 796 or 799,
  the directors who, in the absence of any by-law, would be empowered to
  fill that vacancy shall do so forthwith.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 329
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-812-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 812"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Class vacancy

**[[813]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-813 .sectionLabel}** Despite section 819 but
subject to section 811, where the holders of any class or series of
shares of an insurance holding company have an exclusive right to elect
one or more directors and a vacancy occurs among those directors,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the remaining directors elected by the holders of
  that class or series of shares may fill the vacancy except one
  resulting from an increase in the number or the minimum or maximum
  number of directors for that class or series or from a failure to
  elect the number or minimum number of directors provided for in the
  by-laws for that class or series;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} if there are no such remaining directors and, by
  reason of the vacancy, the number of directors or the composition of
  the board of directors fails to meet any of the requirements of
  section 796 or 799, the other directors may fill that vacancy; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} if there are no such remaining directors and
  paragraph (b) does not apply, any holder of shares of that class or
  series may call a meeting of the holders thereof for the purpose of
  filling the vacancy.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 330
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-813-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 813"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Unexpired term

**[[814]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-814 .sectionLabel}** Unless the by-laws
otherwise provide, a director elected or appointed to fill a vacancy
holds office for the unexpired term of the director's predecessor in
office.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Additional directors

- **[[815]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-815 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  directors may appoint one or more additional directors if the by-laws
  of the insurance holding company allow them to do so and the by-laws
  determine the minimum and maximum numbers of directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Term of office

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director appointed under subsection (1) holds
  office for a term expiring not later than the close of the next annual
  meeting of shareholders of the insurance holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limit on number appointed

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The total number of directors appointed under
  subsection (1) may not exceed one third of the number of directors
  elected at the previous annual meeting of shareholders of the
  insurance holding company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

##### [Meetings of the Board]{.HTitleText4} {#h-267463 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Meetings required

- **[[816]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-816 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  directors shall meet at least four times during each financial year.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Place for meetings

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The directors may meet at any place unless the
  by-laws provide otherwise.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice for meetings

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The notice for the meetings must be given as required
  by the by-laws.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of meeting

- **[[817]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-817 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  notice of a meeting of directors shall specify each matter referred to
  in section 832 that is to be dealt with at the meeting but, unless the
  by-laws otherwise provide, need not otherwise specify the purpose of
  or the business to be transacted at the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Waiver of notice

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director may in any manner waive notice of a
  meeting of directors and the attendance of a director at a meeting of
  directors is a waiver of notice of that meeting except where the
  director attends the meeting for the express purpose of objecting to
  the transaction of any business on the grounds that the meeting is not
  lawfully called.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Adjourned meeting

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Notice of an adjourned meeting of directors is not
  required to be given if the time and place of the adjourned meeting
  was announced at the original meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Quorum

- **[[818]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-818
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 819, the number
  of directors referred to in subsection (2) constitutes a quorum at any
  meeting of directors or a committee of directors and, notwithstanding
  any vacancy among the directors, a quorum of directors may exercise
  all the powers of the directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Quorum

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The number of directors constituting a quorum at any
  meeting of directors or a committee of directors shall be

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a majority of the minimum number of directors
    required by this Part for the board of directors or a committee of
    directors; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} such greater number of directors than the number
    calculated pursuant to paragraph (a) as may be established by the
    by-laws of the insurance holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Director continues to be present

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A director who is present at a meeting of directors
  or of a committee of directors but is not, in accordance with
  subsection 837(1), present at any particular time during the meeting
  is considered to be present for the purposes of this section.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 331
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-818-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 818"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Resident Canadian majority

- **[[819]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-819 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  directors of an insurance holding company shall not transact business
  at a meeting of directors unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an insurance holding company that is
    the subsidiary of a foreign institution, at least one half of the
    directors present are resident Canadians; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of any other insurance holding company,
    a majority of the directors present are resident Canadians.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), the directors of an insurance
  holding company may transact business at a meeting of directors
  without the required proportion of directors who are resident
  Canadians if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a director who is a resident Canadian unable to be
    present approves, in writing or by telephonic, electronic or other
    communications facilities, the business transacted at the meeting;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} there would have been present the required
    proportion of directors who are resident Canadians had that director
    been present at the meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2013, c. 33, s. 108
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-819-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 819"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Electronic meeting

- **[[820]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-820
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the by-laws of an
  insurance holding company, a meeting of directors or of a committee of
  directors may be held by means of such telephonic, electronic or other
  communications facilities as permit all persons participating in the
  meeting to communicate adequately with each other during the meeting.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed present

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director participating in a meeting by any means
  referred to in subsection (1) is deemed for the purposes of this Part
  to be present at that meeting.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Resolution outside board meeting

- **[[821]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-821 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  resolution in writing signed by all the directors entitled to vote on
  that resolution at a meeting of directors is as valid as if it had
  been passed at a meeting of directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Filing directors' resolution

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A copy of the resolution referred to in
  subsection (1) shall be kept with the minutes of the proceedings of
  the directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Resolution outside committee meeting

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A resolution in writing signed by all the directors
  entitled to vote on that resolution at a meeting of a committee of
  directors, other than a resolution of the audit committee in carrying
  out its duties under subsection 829(3), is as valid as if it had been
  passed at a meeting of that committee.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Filing committee resolution

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} A copy of the resolution referred to in
  subsection (3) shall be kept with the minutes of the proceedings of
  that committee.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Evidence

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Unless a ballot is demanded, an entry in the minutes
  of a meeting that the chairperson declared a resolution to be carried
  or defeated is in the absence of evidence to the contrary proof of
  that fact without proof of the number or proportion of votes recorded
  in favour of or against the resolution.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 332
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-821-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 821"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Dissent of director

- **[[822]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-822 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  director of an insurance holding company who is present at a meeting
  of directors or a committee of directors is deemed to have consented
  to any resolution passed or action taken at that meeting unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the director requests that the director's dissent
    be entered or the director's dissent is entered in the minutes of
    the meeting;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the director sends a written dissent to the
    secretary of the meeting before the meeting is adjourned; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the director sends the director's dissent by
    registered mail or delivers it to the head office of the insurance
    holding company immediately after the meeting is adjourned.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Loss of right to dissent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director of an insurance holding company who votes
  for or consents to a resolution is not entitled to dissent under
  subsection (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Dissent of absent director

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A director of an insurance holding company who is not
  present at a meeting at which a resolution is passed or action taken
  is deemed to have consented thereto unless, within seven days after
  the director becomes aware of the resolution, the director

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} causes the director's dissent to be placed with the
    minutes of the meeting; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} sends the director's dissent by registered mail or
    delivers it to the head office of the insurance holding company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Record of attendance

- **[[823]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-823 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  insurance holding company shall keep a record of the attendance at
  each meeting of directors and each committee meeting of directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Statement to shareholders

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An insurance holding company shall attach to the
  notice of each annual meeting it sends to its shareholders a statement
  showing, in respect of the financial year immediately preceding the
  meeting, the total number of directors' meetings and directors'
  committee meetings held during the financial year and the number of
  those meetings attended by each director.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Meeting required by Superintendent

- **[[824]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-824
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where in the opinion of the
  Superintendent it is necessary, the Superintendent may, by notice in
  writing, require an insurance holding company to hold a meeting of
  directors of the insurance holding company to consider the matters set
  out in the notice.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Attendance of Superintendent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent may attend and be heard at a
  meeting referred to in subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

##### [By-laws]{.HTitleText4} {#h-267552 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-laws

- **[[825]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-825
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Unless this Part otherwise provides,
  the directors of an insurance holding company may by resolution make,
  amend or repeal any by-law that regulates the business or affairs of
  the insurance holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholder approval

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The directors shall submit a by-law, or an amendment
  to or a repeal of a by-law, that is made under subsection (1) to the
  shareholders at the next meeting of shareholders, and the shareholders
  may, by resolution, confirm or amend the by-law, amendment or repeal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effective date of by-law

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Unless this Part otherwise provides, a by-law, or an
  amendment to or a repeal of a by-law, is effective from the date of
  the resolution of the directors under subsection (1) until it is
  confirmed, confirmed as amended or rejected by the shareholders under
  subsection (2) or until it ceases to be effective under subsection (4)
  and, where the by-law is confirmed, or confirmed as amended, it
  continues in effect in the form in which it was so confirmed.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect where no shareholder approval

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a by-law, or an amendment to or a repeal of a
  by-law, is rejected by the shareholders, or is not submitted to the
  shareholders by the directors as required under subsection (2), the
  by-law, amendment or repeal ceases to be effective from the date of
  its rejection or the date of the next meeting of shareholders, as the
  case may be, and no subsequent resolution of the directors to make,
  amend or repeal a by-law having substantially the same purpose or
  effect is effective until it is confirmed, or confirmed as amended, by
  the shareholders.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholder proposal of by-law

**[[826]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-826 .sectionLabel}** A shareholder entitled
to vote at an annual meeting of shareholders may, in accordance with
sections 770 and 771, make a proposal to make, amend or repeal a by-law.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed by-laws

- **[[827]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-827 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Any
  matter provided for in the incorporating instrument of a body
  corporate continued as an insurance holding company at the time of
  continuance that, under this Part, would be provided for in the
  by-laws of an insurance holding company is deemed to be provided for
  in the by-laws of the insurance holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-law prevails

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a by-law of the insurance holding company made in
  accordance with sections 825 and 826 amends or repeals any matter
  referred to in subsection (1), the by-law prevails.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

##### [Committees of the Board]{.HTitleText4} {#h-267575 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Committees

**[[828]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-828 .sectionLabel}** The directors of an
insurance holding company may appoint from their number, in addition to
the committees referred to in subsection 794(2), such other committees
as they deem necessary and, subject to section 832, delegate to those
committees such powers of the directors, and assign to those committees
such duties, as the directors consider appropriate.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Audit committee

- **[[829]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-829 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  audit committee of an insurance holding company shall consist of at
  least three directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Membership

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} None of the members of the audit committee may be
  officers or employees of the insurance holding company or of any of
  its subsidiaries.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Duties of audit committee

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The audit committee of an insurance holding company
  shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} review the annual statement of the insurance
    holding company before the annual statement is approved by the
    directors;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} review such returns of the insurance holding
    company as the Superintendent may specify;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} require the management of the insurance holding
    company to implement and maintain appropriate internal control
    procedures;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} review, evaluate and approve those procedures;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} review such investments and transactions that could
    adversely affect the well-being of the insurance holding company as
    the auditor or any officer of the insurance holding company may
    bring to the attention of the committee;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} meet with the auditor to discuss the annual
    statement and the returns and transactions referred to in this
    subsection; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} meet with the chief internal auditor of the
    insurance holding company, or the officer or employee of the
    insurance holding company acting in a similar capacity, and with
    management of the insurance holding company, to discuss the
    effectiveness of the internal control procedures established for the
    insurance holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Report

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} In the case of the annual statement and returns of an
  insurance holding company that under this Part must be approved by the
  directors of the insurance holding company, the audit committee of the
  insurance holding company shall report thereon to the directors before
  the approval is given.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Required meeting of directors

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The audit committee of an insurance holding company
  may call a meeting of the directors of the insurance holding company
  to consider any matter of concern to the committee.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

##### [Directors and Officers --- Authority]{.HTitleText4} {#h-267600 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Chief executive officer

**[[830]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-830 .sectionLabel}** The directors of an
insurance holding company shall appoint from their number a chief
executive officer who must be ordinarily resident in Canada and, subject
to section 832, may delegate to that officer any of the powers of the
directors.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appointment of officers

- **[[831]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-831 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  directors of an insurance holding company may, subject to the by-laws,
  designate the offices of the insurance holding company, appoint
  officers thereto, specify the duties of those officers and delegate to
  them powers, subject to section 832, to manage the business and
  affairs of the insurance holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors as officers

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 799, a director of an insurance
  holding company may be appointed to any office of the insurance
  holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Two or more offices

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Two or more offices of an insurance holding company
  may be held by the same person.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limits on power to delegate

**[[832]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-832 .sectionLabel}** The directors of an
insurance holding company may not delegate any of the following powers,
namely, the power to

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} submit to the shareholders a question or matter
  requiring the approval of the shareholders;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} fill a vacancy among the directors, on a committee of
  directors or in the office of auditor, or appoint additional
  directors;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} issue or cause to be issued securities, including an
  issue of shares of a series that is authorized in accordance with
  section 745, except in accordance with any authorization made by the
  directors;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} declare a dividend;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} authorize the redemption or other acquisition by the
  insurance holding company pursuant to section 754 of shares issued by
  the insurance holding company;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} authorize the payment of a commission on a share
  issue;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} approve a management proxy circular;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} except as provided in this Part, approve the annual
  statement of the insurance holding company and any other financial
  statements issued by the insurance holding company; or

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} adopt, amend or repeal by-laws.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 333
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-832-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 832"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Remuneration of directors, officers and
employees

- **[[833]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-833
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to this section and the
  by-laws, the directors of an insurance holding company may fix the
  remuneration of the directors, officers and employees of the insurance
  holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-law required

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No remuneration shall be paid to a director as
  director until a by-law fixing the aggregate of all amounts that may
  be paid to all directors in respect of directors' remuneration during
  a fixed period of time has been confirmed by special resolution.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Validity of acts

- **[[834]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-834 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  act of a director or an officer of an insurance holding company is
  valid notwithstanding a defect in the director's qualification or an
  irregularity in the director's election or in the appointment of the
  director or officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Validity of acts

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An act of the board of directors of an insurance
  holding company is valid notwithstanding a defect in the composition
  of the board or an irregularity in the election of the board or in the
  appointment of a member of the board.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Right to attend meetings

**[[835]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-835 .sectionLabel}** A director of an
insurance holding company is entitled to attend and to be heard at every
meeting of shareholders.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

##### [Conflicts of Interest]{.HTitleText4} {#h-267645 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disclosure of interest

- **[[836]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-836 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  director or officer of an insurance holding company shall disclose to
  the insurance holding company, in writing or by requesting to have it
  entered in the minutes of a meeting of directors or a meeting of a
  committee of directors, the nature and extent of any interest they
  have in a material contract or material transaction with the insurance
  holding company, whether entered into or proposed, if they

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} are a party to the contract or transaction;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} are a director or officer of a party to the
    contract or transaction or a person acting in a similar capacity; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} have a material interest in a party to the contract
    or transaction.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Time of disclosure --- director

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The disclosure shall be made in the case of a
  director

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at the meeting of directors, or of a committee of
    directors, at which the proposed contract or transaction is first
    considered;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if at the time of the meeting referred to in
    paragraph (a) the director was not interested in the proposed
    contract or transaction, at the first one after they become
    interested in it;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the director becomes interested after a contract
    or transaction is entered into, at the first one after they become
    interested; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} if a person who is interested in a contract or
    transaction becomes a director, at the first one after they become a
    director.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Time of disclosure --- officer

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The disclosure required by subsection (1) shall be
  made in the case of an officer who is not a director

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} immediately after they become aware that the
    contract, transaction, proposed contract or proposed transaction is
    to be considered or has been considered at a meeting of directors or
    of a committee of directors;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if they become interested after the contract or
    transaction is entered into, immediately after they become
    interested; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if a person who is interested in a contract or
    transaction becomes an officer, immediately after they become an
    officer.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Time of disclosure --- contract not
  requiring approval

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the material contract or material transaction,
  whether entered into or proposed, is one that in the ordinary course
  of the insurance holding company's business would not require approval
  by the directors or shareholders, the director or officer shall
  disclose to the insurance holding company, in writing or by requesting
  to have it entered in the minutes of a meeting of directors or of a
  committee of directors, the nature and extent of their interest
  immediately after they become aware of the contract or transaction.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 334
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-836-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 836"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Director to abstain

- **[[837]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-837 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  director who is required to make a disclosure under subsection 836(1)
  shall not be present at any meeting of directors, or of a committee of
  directors, while the contract or transaction is being considered or
  vote on any resolution to approve it unless the contract or
  transaction

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} relates primarily to their remuneration as a
    director, officer, employee or agent of the insurance holding
    company, an entity controlled by the insurance holding company or an
    entity in which the insurance holding company has a substantial
    investment;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is for indemnity under section 846 or insurance
    under section 847; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} is with an affiliate of the insurance holding
    company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Ineligibility

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director who knowingly contravenes subsection (1)
  ceases to hold office as director and is not eligible, for a period of
  five years after the date on which the contravention occurred, for
  election or appointment as a director of any insurance holding
  company, any bank holding company or any financial institution that is
  incorporated or formed by or under an Act of Parliament.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Validity of acts

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An act of the board of directors of an insurance
  holding company or of a committee of the board of directors is not
  invalid because a person acting as a director had ceased under
  subsection (2) to hold office as a director.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 335
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-837-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 837"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}General notice

- **[[838]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-838 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For
  the purposes of subsection 836(1), a general notice to the directors
  declaring that a director or officer is to be regarded as interested
  for any of the following reasons in a contract or transaction entered
  into with a party, is a sufficient declaration of interest in relation
  to any contract or transaction with that party:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the director or officer is a director or officer of
    a party referred to in paragraph 836(1)(b) or (c) or a person acting
    in a similar capacity;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the director or officer has a material interest in
    the party; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} there has been a material change in the nature of
    the director's or officer's interest in the party.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Access to disclosures

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The shareholders of the insurance holding company may
  examine the portions of any minutes of meetings of directors or
  committees of directors that contain disclosures under subsection
  836(1), or the portions of any other documents that contain those
  disclosures, during the usual business hours of the insurance holding
  company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 336
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-838-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 838"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Avoidance standards

- **[[839]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-839 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  contract or transaction for which disclosure is required under
  subsection 836(1) is not invalid and a director or officer is not
  accountable to the insurance holding company or its shareholders for
  any profit realized from it by reason only of the director's or
  officer's interest in the contract or transaction or the fact that the
  director was present or was counted to determine whether a quorum
  existed at the meeting of directors, or of a committee of directors,
  that considered it if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the director or officer disclosed their interest in
    accordance with section 836 and subsection 838(1);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the directors approved the contract or transaction;
    and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the contract or transaction was reasonable and fair
    to the insurance holding company at the time that it was approved.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Confirmation by shareholders

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Even if the conditions set out in subsection (1) are
  not met, a director or officer acting honestly and in good faith is
  not accountable to the insurance holding company or its shareholders
  for any profit realized from a contract or transaction for which
  disclosure was required and the contract or transaction is not invalid
  by reason only of the director's or officer's interest in it if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the contract or transaction is approved or
    confirmed by special resolution at a meeting of shareholders;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} disclosure of the interest was made to the
    shareholders in a manner sufficient to indicate its nature before
    the contract or transaction was approved or confirmed; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the contract or transaction was reasonable and fair
    to the insurance holding company at the time that it was approved or
    confirmed.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 336
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-839-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 839"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Court may set aside or require accounting

**[[840]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-840 .sectionLabel}** If a director or
officer of an insurance holding company fails to comply with any of
sections 836 to 839, a court, on application of the insurance holding
company or any of its shareholders, may set aside the contract or
transaction on any terms that the court thinks fit and may require the
director or officer to account to the insurance holding company for any
profit or gain realized on it.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 336
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-840-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 840"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Liability, Exculpation and Indemnification]{.HTitleText4} {#h-267706 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Director liability

- **[[841]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-841
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Directors of an insurance holding
  company who vote for or consent to a resolution of the directors
  authorizing the issue of a share contrary to subsection 748(1) or the
  issue of subordinated indebtedness contrary to section 762 for a
  consideration other than money are jointly and severally, or
  solidarily, liable to the insurance holding company to make good any
  amount by which the consideration received is less than the fair
  equivalent of the money that the insurance holding company would have
  received if the share or subordinated indebtedness had been issued for
  money on the date of the resolution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Further liability

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Directors of an insurance holding company who vote
  for or consent to a resolution of the directors authorizing any of the
  following are jointly and severally, or solidarily, liable to restore
  to the insurance holding company any amounts so distributed or paid
  and not otherwise recovered by the insurance holding company and any
  amounts in relation to any loss suffered by the insurance holding
  company:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a redemption or purchase of shares contrary to
    section 754;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a reduction of capital contrary to section 757;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a payment of a dividend contrary to section 761; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a payment of an indemnity contrary to section 846.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 337(E)
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-841-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 841"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contribution

- **[[842]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-842 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  director who has satisfied a judgment in relation to the director's
  liability under section 841 is entitled to contribution from the other
  directors who voted for or consented to the unlawful act on which the
  judgment was founded.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Recovery

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director who is liable under section 841 is
  entitled to apply to a court for an order compelling a shareholder or
  other person to pay or deliver to the director any money or property
  that was paid or distributed to the shareholder or other person
  contrary to section 754, 757, 761 or 846.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Court order

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where an application is made to a court under
  subsection (2), the court may, where it is satisfied that it is
  equitable to do so,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} order a shareholder or other person to pay or
    deliver to a director any money or property that was paid or
    distributed to the shareholder or other person contrary to section
    754, 757, 761 or 846;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} order an insurance holding company to return or
    issue shares to a person from whom the insurance holding company has
    purchased, redeemed or otherwise acquired shares; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} make any further order it thinks fit.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitation

**[[843]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-843 .sectionLabel}** An action to enforce a
liability imposed by section 841 may not be commenced after two years
from the date of the resolution authorizing the action complained of.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors liable for wages

- **[[844]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-844
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) and (3),
  the directors of an insurance holding company are jointly and
  severally, or solidarily, liable to each employee of the insurance
  holding company for all debts not exceeding six months wages payable
  to the employee for services performed for the insurance holding
  company while they are directors.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conditions precedent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director is not liable under subsection (1) unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the insurance holding company has been sued for the
    debt within six months after it has become due and execution has
    been returned unsatisfied in whole or in part;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the insurance holding company has commenced
    liquidation and dissolution proceedings or has been dissolved and a
    claim for the debt has been proven within six months after the
    earlier of the date of commencement of the liquidation and
    dissolution proceedings and the date of dissolution; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the insurance holding company has made an
    assignment or a bankruptcy order has been made against it under the
    [Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act](/eng/acts/B-3) and a claim for the
    debt has been proven within six months after the date of the
    assignment or bankruptcy order.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitations

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A director is not liable under subsection (1) unless
  the director is sued for a debt referred to in that subsection while a
  director or within two years after the director has ceased to be a
  director.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Amount due after execution

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where execution referred to in paragraph (2)(a) has
  issued, the amount recoverable from a director is the amount remaining
  unsatisfied after execution.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Subrogation of director

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Where a director of an insurance holding company pays
  a debt referred to in subsection (1) that is proven in liquidation and
  dissolution or bankruptcy proceedings, the director is entitled to any
  preference that the employee would have been entitled to and, where a
  judgment has been obtained, the director is entitled to an assignment
  of the judgment.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contribution entitlement

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} A director of an insurance holding company who has
  satisfied a claim under this section is entitled to a contribution
  from the other directors of the insurance holding company who are
  liable for the claim.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2004, c. 25, s. 203
- 2005, c. 54, s. 338(E)
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-844-20041215.html "Link to previous version of section 844"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Defence --- due diligence

- **[[845]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-845 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  director, officer or employee of an insurance holding company is not
  liable under section 841 or 844 and has fulfilled their duty under
  subsection 795(2) if they exercised the care, diligence and skill that
  a reasonably prudent person would have exercised in comparable
  circumstances, including reliance in good faith on

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} financial statements of the insurance holding
    company that were represented to them by an officer of the insurance
    holding company or in a written report of the auditor of the
    insurance holding company fairly to reflect the financial condition
    of the insurance holding company; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a report of a person whose profession lends
    credibility to a statement made by them.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Defence --- good faith

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A director or officer of an insurance holding company
  has fulfilled their duty under subsection 795(1) if they relied in
  good faith on

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} financial statements of the insurance holding
    company that were represented to them by an officer of the insurance
    holding company or in a written report of the auditor of the
    insurance holding company fairly to reflect the financial condition
    of the insurance holding company; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a report of a person whose profession lends
    credibility to a statement made by them.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 339
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-845-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 845"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Indemnification

- **[[846]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-846 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  insurance holding company may indemnify a director or officer of the
  insurance holding company, a former director or officer of the
  insurance holding company or another person who acts or acted, at the
  insurance holding company's request, as a director or officer of or in
  a similar capacity for another entity against all costs, charges and
  expenses, including an amount paid to settle an action or satisfy a
  judgment, reasonably incurred by them in respect of any civil,
  criminal, administrative, investigative or other proceeding in which
  they are involved because of that association with the insurance
  holding company or other entity.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Advances

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An insurance holding company may advance amounts to
  the director, officer or other person for the costs, charges and
  expenses of a proceeding referred to in subsection (1). They shall
  repay the amounts if they do not fulfil the conditions set out in
  subsection (3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}No indemnification

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An insurance holding company may not indemnify a
  person under subsection (1) unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person acted honestly and in good faith with a
    view to the best interests of, as the case may be, the insurance
    holding company, or the other entity for which they acted at the
    insurance holding company's request as a director or officer or in a
    similar capacity; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a criminal or administrative action
    or proceeding that is enforced by a monetary penalty, the person had
    reasonable grounds for believing that their conduct was lawful.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Indemnification --- derivative actions

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} An insurance holding company may with the approval of
  a court indemnify a person referred to in subsection (1) or advance
  amounts to them under subsection (2) --- in respect of an action by or
  on behalf of the insurance holding company or other entity to procure
  a judgment in its favour to which the person is made a party because
  of the association referred to in subsection (1) with the insurance
  holding company or other entity --- against all costs, charges and
  expenses reasonably incurred by them in connection with that action if
  they fulfil the conditions set out in subsection (3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Right to indemnity

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), a person referred to in that
  subsection is entitled to be indemnified by the insurance holding
  company in respect of all costs, charges and expenses reasonably
  incurred by them in connection with the defence of any civil,
  criminal, administrative, investigative or other proceeding to which
  the person is subject because of the association referred to in
  subsection (1) with the insurance holding company or other entity
  described in that subsection if the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} was not judged by the court or other competent
    authority to have committed any fault or omitted to do anything that
    they ought to have done; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} fulfils the conditions set out in subsection (3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Heirs and personal representatives

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} An insurance holding company may, to the extent
  referred to in subsections (1) to (5) in respect of the person,
  indemnify the heirs or personal representatives of any person whom the
  insurance holding company may indemnify under those subsections.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 339
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-846-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 846"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directors' and officers' insurance

**[[847]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-847 .sectionLabel}** An insurance holding
company may purchase and maintain insurance for the benefit of any
person referred to in section 846 against any liability incurred by the
person

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the capacity of a director or an officer of the
  insurance holding company, except where the liability relates to a
  failure to act honestly and in good faith with a view to the best
  interests of the insurance holding company; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the capacity of a director or officer of another
  entity or while acting in a similar capacity for another entity, if
  they act or acted in that capacity at the insurance holding company's
  request, except if the liability relates to a failure to act honestly
  and in good faith with a view to the best interests of the entity.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 340
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-847-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 847"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application to court for indemnification

- **[[848]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-848 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  insurance holding company or a person referred to in section 846 may
  apply to a court for an order approving an indemnity under that
  section and the court may so order and make any further order it
  thinks fit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice to Superintendent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An applicant under subsection (1) shall give the
  Superintendent written notice of the application and the
  Superintendent is entitled to appear and to be heard at the hearing of
  the application in person or by counsel.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Other notice

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} On an application under subsection (1), the court may
  order notice to be given to any interested person and that person is
  entitled to appear and to be heard in person or by counsel at the
  hearing of the application.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

#### [SUBDIVISION 4]{.HLabel3}[Fundamental Changes]{.HTitleText3} {#h-267797 .Subheading}

##### [Amendments --- Letters Patent]{.HTitleText4} {#h-267798 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Incorporating instrument

**[[849]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-849 .sectionLabel}** On the application of
an insurance holding company duly authorized by special resolution, the
Minister may approve a proposal to add, change or remove any provision
that is permitted by this Part to be set out in the incorporating
instrument of the insurance holding company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Letters patent to amend

- **[[850]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-850 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  receipt of an application referred to in section 849, the Minister may
  issue letters patent to effect the proposal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of letters patent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Letters patent issued pursuant to subsection (1)
  become effective on the day stated in the letters patent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

##### [Amendments --- By-laws]{.HTitleText4} {#h-267810 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}By-laws

- **[[851]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-851 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  directors of an insurance holding company may make, amend or repeal
  any by-laws, in the manner set out in subsections (2) and (3) and
  sections 852 to 856, to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} change the maximum number, if any, of shares of any
    class that the insurance holding company is authorized to issue;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} create new classes of shares;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} change the designation of any or all of the
    insurance holding company's shares, and add, change or remove any
    rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions, including rights to
    accrued dividends, in respect of any or all of the insurance holding
    company's shares, whether issued or unissued;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} change the shares of any class or series, whether
    issued or unissued, into a different number of shares of the same
    class or series or into the same or a different number of shares of
    other classes or series;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} divide a class of shares, whether issued or
    unissued, into series and fix the maximum number of shares, if any,
    in each series and the rights, privileges, restrictions and
    conditions attached thereto;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} authorize the directors to divide any class of
    unissued shares into series and fix the maximum number of shares, if
    any, in each series and the rights, privileges, restrictions and
    conditions attached thereto;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} authorize the directors to change the rights,
    privileges, restrictions and conditions attached to unissued shares
    of any series;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} revoke, diminish or enlarge any authority conferred
    under paragraphs (f) and (g);

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} increase or decrease the number of directors,
    subject to subsection 796(1) and section 803;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} change the name of the insurance holding company;
    or

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} change the place in Canada where the head office of
    the insurance holding company is to be situated.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholder approval

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The directors shall submit a by-law, or an amendment
  to or a repeal of a by-law, that is made under subsection (1) to the
  shareholders entitled to vote, and the shareholders may, by special
  resolution, confirm, amend or reject the by-law, amendment or repeal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effective date of by-law

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} A by-law, or an amendment to or a repeal of a by-law,
  made under subsection (1) is not effective until it is confirmed or
  confirmed as amended by the shareholders under subsection (2) and, in
  the case of by-laws referred to in paragraph (1)(j), approved by the
  Superintendent in writing.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Class vote

- **[[852]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-852 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  holders of shares of a class or, subject to subsection (2), of a
  series are, unless the by-laws otherwise provide in the case of an
  amendment to the by-laws referred to in paragraph (a), (b) or (e),
  entitled to vote separately as a class or series on a proposal to
  amend the by-laws to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} increase or decrease any maximum number of
    authorized shares of that class, or increase any maximum number of
    authorized shares of a class having rights or privileges equal or
    superior to the shares of that class;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} effect an exchange, reclassification or
    cancellation of all or part of the shares of that class;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} add, change or remove the rights, privileges,
    restrictions or conditions attached to the shares of that class and,
    without limiting the generality of the foregoing,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} remove or change prejudicially rights to accrued
      dividends or rights to cumulative dividends,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} add, remove or change prejudicially redemption
      rights,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} reduce or remove a dividend preference or a
      liquidation preference, or

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} add, remove or change prejudicially conversion
      privileges, options, voting, transfer or pre-emptive rights, or
      rights to acquire securities of the insurance holding company, or
      sinking fund provisions;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} increase the rights or privileges of any class of
    shares having rights or privileges equal or superior to the shares
    of that class;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} create a new class of shares equal or superior to
    the shares of that class;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} make any class of shares having rights or
    privileges inferior to the shares of that class equal or superior to
    the shares of that class; or

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} effect an exchange or create a right of exchange of
    all or part of the shares of another class into the shares of that
    class.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Right limited

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The holders of a series of shares of a class are
  entitled to vote separately as a series under subsection (1) if that
  series is affected by an addition or amendment to the by-laws in a
  manner different from other shares of the same class.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Right to vote

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subsections (1) and (2) apply whether or not the
  shares of a class otherwise carry the right to vote.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Separate resolutions

**[[853]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-853 .sectionLabel}** A proposed addition or
amendment to the by-laws referred to in subsection 852(1) is adopted
when the holders of the shares of each class or series entitled to vote
separately thereon as a class or series have approved the addition or
amendment by a special resolution.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Revoking resolution

**[[854]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-854 .sectionLabel}** Where a special
resolution referred to in subsection 851(2) so states, the directors
may, without further approval of the shareholders, revoke the special
resolution.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proposal to amend

- **[[855]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-855
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), a
  director or a shareholder who is entitled to vote at an annual meeting
  of shareholders of an insurance holding company may, in accordance
  with sections 770 and 771, make a proposal to make an application
  referred to in section 849 or to make, amend or repeal the by-laws
  referred to in subsection 851(1) of the insurance holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of amendment

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Notice of a meeting of shareholders at which a
  proposal to amend the incorporating instrument or to make, amend or
  repeal the by-laws of an insurance holding company to effect any of
  the changes referred to in subsection 851(1) is to be considered must
  set out the proposal.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Rights preserved

**[[856]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-856 .sectionLabel}** No amendment to the
incorporating instrument or by-laws of an insurance holding company
affects an existing cause of action or claim or liability to prosecution
in favour of or against the insurance holding company or its directors
or officers, or any civil, criminal or administrative action or
proceeding to which the insurance holding company or any of its
directors or officers are a party.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

##### [Amalgamation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-267870 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application to amalgamate

**[[857]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-857 .sectionLabel}** On the joint
application of two or more bodies corporate incorporated by or under an
Act of Parliament, including a company or an insurance holding company
but not including a mutual company or a federal credit union, the
Minister may issue letters patent amalgamating and continuing the
applicants as one insurance holding company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2010, c. 12, s. 2121
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-857-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 857"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Amalgamation agreement

- **[[858]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-858 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Each
  applicant proposing to amalgamate shall enter into an amalgamation
  agreement.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Contents of agreement

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Every amalgamation agreement shall set out the terms
  and means of effecting the amalgamation and, in particular,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name of the amalgamated insurance holding
    company and the province in which its head office is to be situated;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name and place of ordinary residence of each
    proposed director of the amalgamated insurance holding company;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the manner in which any shares of each applicant
    are to be converted into shares or other securities of the
    amalgamated insurance holding company;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} if any shares of an applicant are not to be
    converted into shares or other securities of the amalgamated
    insurance holding company, the amount of money or securities that
    the holders of those shares are to receive in addition to or in lieu
    of shares or other securities of the amalgamated insurance holding
    company;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the manner of payment of money in lieu of the issue
    of fractional shares of the amalgamated insurance holding company or
    of any other body corporate that are to be issued in the
    amalgamation;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the proposed by-laws of the amalgamated insurance
    holding company;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} details of any other matter necessary to perfect
    the amalgamation and to provide for the subsequent management and
    operation of the amalgamated insurance holding company; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the proposed effective date of the amalgamation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Cross ownership of shares

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If shares of one of the applicants are held by or on
  behalf of another of the applicants, other than shares held in the
  capacity of a personal representative or by way of security, the
  amalgamation agreement must provide for the cancellation of those
  shares when the amalgamation becomes effective without any repayment
  of capital in respect thereof, and no provision shall be made in the
  agreement for the conversion of those shares into shares of the
  amalgamated insurance holding company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 341
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-858-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 858"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Approval of agreement by Superintendent

**[[859]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-859 .sectionLabel}** An amalgamation
agreement must be submitted to the Superintendent for approval and any
approval of the agreement under subsection 860(4) by the shareholders of
an applicant is invalid unless, before the date of the approval, the
Superintendent has approved the agreement in writing.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2007, c. 6, s. 320
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-859-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 859"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Approval by shareholders

- **[[860]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-860 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  directors of each applicant shall submit an amalgamation agreement for
  approval to a meeting of the shareholders of the body corporate of
  which they are directors and to the holders of each class or series of
  shares.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Right to vote

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Each share of an applicant carries the right to vote
  in respect of an amalgamation agreement whether or not it otherwise
  carries the right to vote.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Separate vote for class or series

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The holders of shares of a class or series of shares
  of each applicant are entitled to vote separately as a class or series
  in respect of an amalgamation agreement if the agreement contains a
  provision that, if it were contained in a proposed amendment to the
  by-laws or incorporating instrument of the applicant, would entitle
  those holders to vote separately as a class or series.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Special resolution

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), an amalgamation agreement
  is approved when it has been approved by special resolution by the
  shareholders of each applicant body corporate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Termination

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} An amalgamation agreement may provide that, at any
  time before the issue of letters patent of amalgamation, the agreement
  may be terminated by the directors of an applicant even though the
  agreement has been approved by the shareholders of all or any of the
  applicant bodies corporate.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 342
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-860-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 860"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Vertical short-form amalgamation

- **[[861]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-861 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  insurance holding company may, without complying with sections 858 to
  860, amalgamate with one or more bodies corporate that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} are incorporated by or under an Act of Parliament,
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} are wholly-owned subsidiaries of the insurance
    holding company

  if

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the amalgamation is approved by a resolution of the
    directors of the insurance holding company and of each amalgamating
    subsidiary, and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the resolutions provide that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the shares of each amalgamating subsidiary will
      be cancelled without any repayment of capital in respect thereof,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the letters patent of amalgamation and the
      by-laws of the amalgamated insurance holding company will be the
      same as the incorporating instrument and the by-laws of the
      amalgamating insurance holding company that is the holding body
      corporate, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} no securities will be issued by the amalgamated
      insurance holding company in connection with the amalgamation.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Horizontal short-form amalgamation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Two or more bodies corporate that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} are incorporated by or under an Act of Parliament,
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} are wholly-owned subsidiaries of the same holding
    body corporate

  may amalgamate and continue as one insurance holding company without
  complying with sections 858 to 860 if

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} at least one of the applicants is an insurance
    holding company,

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the amalgamation is approved by a resolution of the
    directors of each of the applicants, and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the resolutions provide that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the shares of all applicants, except those of one
      of the applicants that is an insurance holding company, will be
      cancelled without any repayment of capital in respect thereof,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the letters patent of amalgamation and the
      by-laws of the amalgamated insurance holding company will be the
      same as the incorporating instrument and the by-laws of the
      amalgamating insurance holding company whose shares are not
      cancelled, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the stated capital of the amalgamating
      insurance holding companies and bodies corporate whose shares are
      cancelled will be added to the stated capital of the amalgamating
      insurance holding company whose shares are not cancelled.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Joint application to Minister

- **[[862]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-862
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), unless an
  amalgamation agreement is terminated in accordance with subsection
  860(5), the applicants shall, within three months after the approval
  of the agreement in accordance with subsection 860(4) or the approval
  of the directors in accordance with subsection 861(1) or (2), jointly
  apply to the Minister for letters patent of amalgamation continuing
  the applicants as one insurance holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Conditions precedent to application

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} No application for the issue of letters patent under
  subsection (1) may be made unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} notice of intention to make such an application has
    been published at least once a week for a period of four consecutive
    weeks in the [Canada Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) and in a
    newspaper in general circulation at or near the place where the head
    office of each applicant is situated; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the application is supported by satisfactory
    evidence that the applicants have complied with the requirements of
    this Part relating to amalgamations.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application of sections 709 to 711

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where two or more bodies corporate, none of which is
  an insurance holding company, apply for letters patent under
  subsection (1), sections 709 to 711 apply in respect of the
  application with such modifications as the circumstances require.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Matters for consideration

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Before issuing letters patent of amalgamation
  continuing the applicants as one insurance holding company, the
  Minister shall take into account all matters that the Minister
  considers relevant to the application, including

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the sources of continuing financial support for any
    company that will be a subsidiary of the amalgamated insurance
    holding company;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the soundness and feasibility of the plans of the
    applicants for the future conduct and development of the business of
    any company that will be a subsidiary of the amalgamated insurance
    holding company;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the business record and experience of the
    applicants;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the reputation of the applicants for being operated
    in a manner that is consistent with the standards of good character
    and integrity;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} whether the amalgamated insurance holding company
    will be operated responsibly by persons with the competence and
    experience suitable for involvement in the operation of a financial
    institution;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the impact of any integration of the operations and
    businesses of the applicants on the conduct of those operations and
    businesses;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} if the insurance holding company is an insurance
    holding company in respect of which subsection 927(5) applies or an
    insurance holding company in respect of which subsection 927(6)
    applied at any time, the opinion of the Superintendent regarding the
    extent to which the proposed corporate structure of the amalgamated
    insurance holding company and its affiliates may affect the
    supervision and regulation of any company that will be its
    subsidiary, having regard to

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the nature and extent of the proposed financial
      services activities to be carried out by the affiliates of the
      amalgamated insurance holding company, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the nature and degree of supervision and
      regulation applying to the proposed financial services activities
      to be carried out by the affiliates of the amalgamated insurance
      holding company;

    and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the best interests of the financial system in
    Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may not, before January 1, 2002, issue
  letters patent under section 863 amalgamating a converted company in
  respect of which subsection 407(4) or (11) applies, a company to which
  subsection 407(5) or (12) applies or an insurance holding company to
  which subsection 407(6) or (13) applies with any other body corporate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} If one of the applicants for letters patent of
  amalgamation is a converted company in respect of which subsection
  407(4) applies, or a company to which subsection 407(5) applies or an
  insurance holding company to which subsection 407(6) applies, the
  Minister may not issue the letters patent of amalgamation unless the
  amalgamated insurance holding company is widely held.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deeming

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} If one of the applicants for letters patent of
  amalgamation is a converted company in respect of which subsection
  407(4) applies, a company to which subsection 407(5) applies or an
  insurance holding company to which subsection 407(6) applies and the
  letters patent of amalgamation are issued, the amalgamated insurance
  holding company is deemed to be an insurance holding company in
  respect of which subsection 927(4) applies.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Issue of letters patent

- **[[863]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-863
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where an application has been made
  to the Minister in accordance with section 862, the Minister may issue
  letters patent of amalgamation continuing the applicants as one
  insurance holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Letters patent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where letters patent are issued pursuant to this
  section, section 713 applies with such modifications as the
  circumstances require in respect of the issue of the letters patent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication of notice

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent shall cause to be published in the
  [Canada Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) notice of the issuance of
  letters patent pursuant to subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Court enforcement

- **[[864]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-864 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  an insurance holding company, or any director, officer, employee or
  agent of an insurance holding company, is contravening or has failed
  to comply with any term or condition made in respect of the issuance
  of letters patent of amalgamation, the Minister may, in addition to
  any other action that may be taken under this Act, apply to a court
  for an order directing the insurance holding company, or the director,
  officer, employee or agent to comply with the term or condition, cease
  the contravention or do any thing that is required to be done, and on
  the application the court may so order and make any other order it
  thinks fit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appeal

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An appeal from an order of a court under this section
  lies in the same manner as, and to the same court to which, an appeal
  may be taken from any other order of the court.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of letters patent

- **[[865]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-865 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  the day provided for in the letters patent issued under section 863,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the amalgamation of the applicants and their
    continuance as one insurance holding company become effective;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the property of each applicant continues to be the
    property of the amalgamated insurance holding company;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the amalgamated insurance holding company continues
    to be liable for the obligations of each applicant;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} any existing cause of action, claim or liability to
    prosecution is unaffected;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} any civil, criminal or administrative action or
    proceeding pending by or against an applicant may be continued to be
    prosecuted by or against the amalgamated insurance holding company;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} any conviction against, or ruling, order or
    judgment in favour of or against, an applicant may be enforced by or
    against the amalgamated insurance holding company;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} if any director or officer of an applicant
    continues as a director or officer of the amalgamated insurance
    holding company, any disclosure by that director or officer of a
    material interest in any contract made to the applicant shall be
    deemed to be disclosure to the amalgamated insurance holding
    company; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the letters patent of amalgamation are the
    incorporating instrument of the amalgamated insurance holding
    company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Minutes

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Any deemed disclosure under paragraph (1)(g) shall be
  recorded in the minutes of the first meeting of directors of the
  amalgamated insurance holding company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Transitional

- **[[866]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-866
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite any other provision of this
  Act or the regulations, the Minister may, by order, on the
  recommendation of the Superintendent, grant to an insurance holding
  company in respect of which letters patent were issued under
  subsection 863(1) permission to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} engage in a business activity specified in the
    order that the insurance holding company would not otherwise be
    permitted by this Act to engage in and that one or more of the
    amalgamating bodies corporate was engaging in at the time
    application for the letters patent was made;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} continue to have issued and outstanding debt
    obligations the issue of which is not authorized by this Act if the
    debt obligations were outstanding at the time the application for
    the letters patent was made;
