Version](section-1010-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 1010"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Service on companies, etc.

**[[1011]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1011 .sectionLabel}** A notice or document
required by this Act to be sent to or served on a company, a society, a
foreign company, a provincial company or an insurance holding company
may be sent by registered mail to the head office or chief agency, as
the case may be, of the company, society, foreign company, provincial
company or insurance holding company and, if so sent, is deemed to be
received or served at the time it would be delivered in the ordinary
course of mail unless there are reasonable grounds for believing that
the company, society, foreign company, provincial company or insurance
holding company did not receive the notice or document at that time or
at all.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Certificate of companies, etc.

- **[[1012]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1012 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  certificate issued on behalf of a company, a society or an insurance
  holding company stating any fact that is set out in the incorporating
  instrument, the by-laws, the minutes of the meetings of the directors,
  a committee of directors or the shareholders, policyholders or
  members, or in a contract to which the company, society or insurance
  holding company is a party, may be signed by a director or an officer
  of the company, society or insurance holding company.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Proof of certain cases

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} When introduced as evidence in any civil, criminal or
  administrative action or proceeding, the following are, in the absence
  of evidence to the contrary, proof of the facts so certified without
  proof of the signature or official character of the person appearing
  to have signed the certificate:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a fact stated in a certificate referred to in
    subsection (1);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a certified extract from a securities register of a
    company or of an insurance holding company; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a certified copy of, or an extract from, minutes of
    a meeting of shareholders, policyholders, members, directors or a
    committee of directors of a company, society or insurance holding
    company.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Entry in securities register

**[[1013]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1013 .sectionLabel}** An entry in the
securities register of, or on a security certificate issued by, a
company or an insurance holding company is evidence that the person in
whose name the security is registered is the owner of the securities
described in the register or in the certificate.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 363(F)
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1013-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 1013"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Verification of documents or fact

- **[[1014]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1014
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent may require that
  a document or a fact stated in a document that is required by or under
  this Act to be sent to the Superintendent or to the Minister be
  verified in accordance with subsection (2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Form of proof

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A document or fact required by this Act or by the
  Superintendent to be verified may be verified by affidavit made under
  oath or by statutory declaration under the [Canada Evidence
  Act](/eng/acts/C-5) before any commissioner for oaths or for taking
  affidavits.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Alternative means of publication

- **[[1015]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1015
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Anything that is required by a
  provision of this Act to be published in the [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) or to be published in any other
  way may, instead of being published in that way, be published in any
  manner that may be prescribed for the purpose of that provision.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Alternative means of publishing
  summaries

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Anything that is required by a provision of this Act
  to be summarized in a publication may instead be summarized and
  published in any manner that may be prescribed for the purpose of that
  provision.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Publication conditions

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Any condition under a provision of this Act that
  something be published in the [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) or in any other way is satisfied
  if that thing is published instead in any manner that may be
  prescribed for the purpose of that provision.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Other consequences

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a provision of this Act provides for consequences
  to follow the publication of something in the [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) or in any other manner, the same
  consequences follow the publication of that thing in any other manner
  that may be prescribed for the purpose of that provision.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

### [Approvals]{.HTitleText2} {#h-269722 .Subheading}

Definition of [[approval]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

**[[1016]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1016 .sectionLabel}** In sections 1016.1 to
1016.6, [[approval]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes any consent,
designation, order, exemption, extension or other permission granted by
the Minister or the Superintendent under this Act, and includes the
issuance of letters patent.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2007, c. 6, s. 330
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1016-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 1016"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Matters to take into account --- Minister

- **[[1016.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1016.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In addition to any matters or
  conditions provided for in this Act that are relevant to the granting
  of an approval, the Minister may, in considering whether to grant the
  approval, take into account all matters that he or she considers
  relevant in the circumstances, including

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} national security; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Canada's international relations and its
    international legal obligations.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Matters to take into account ---
  Superintendent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In addition to any matters or conditions provided for
  in this Act that are relevant to the granting of an approval and to
  any prudential considerations that the Superintendent considers
  relevant in the circumstances, the Superintendent may, in considering
  whether to grant the approval, take into account

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} national security; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Canada's international relations and its
    international legal obligations.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 6, s. 330
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Minister --- terms, conditions and
undertakings

- **[[1016.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1016.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In addition to any other action that
  may be taken under this Act, the Minister may, in granting an
  approval, impose any terms and conditions or require any undertaking
  that the Minister considers appropriate, including any terms,
  conditions or undertakings specified by the Superintendent to maintain
  or improve the safety and soundness of any financial institution
  regulated under an Act of Parliament to which the approval relates or
  that might be affected by it or to ensure that such a financial
  institution has adequate policies and procedures to protect itself
  against threats to its integrity or security.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Commissioner --- supervision of terms,
  conditions and undertakings

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister specifies that the Commissioner is
  to supervise a company to determine if it is complying with any terms
  and conditions that are imposed, or undertakings that are required, by
  the Minister for the protection of the company's customers, the
  Commissioner may take the same measures that the Commissioner could
  take if the terms and conditions or undertaking were a consumer
  provision.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Superintendent --- terms, conditions
  and undertakings

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In addition to any other action that may be taken
  under this Act, the Superintendent may, in granting an approval,
  impose any terms and conditions or require any undertaking that the
  Superintendent considers appropriate.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 6, s. 330
- 2010, c. 12, s. 1860
- [2023, c. 26, s. 604](#1411137-1415828){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1411137-1415828.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1016.2-20100712.html "Link to previous version of section 1016.2"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Revocation, suspension or amendment of
approval --- Minister

- **[[1016.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1016.3
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may revoke, suspend or
  amend any approval granted by the Minister if he or she considers it
  appropriate to do so. In deciding whether to take any of those
  actions, the Minister may take into account all matters that he or she
  considers relevant in the circumstances, including

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} national security; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Canada's international relations and its
    international legal obligations.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Revocation, suspension or amendment of
  approval --- Superintendent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent may revoke, suspend or amend any
  approval granted by the Superintendent if he or she considers it
  appropriate to do so. In deciding whether to take any of those
  actions, the Superintendent may take into account any prudential
  considerations that he or she considers relevant in the circumstances
  and

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} national security; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Canada's international relations and its
    international legal obligations.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Representations

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Before taking any action under subsection (1) or (2),
  the Minister or the Superintendent, as the case may be, shall give the
  person concerned a reasonable opportunity to make representations.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Temporary amendment or suspension

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If, in the Minister's opinion, the length of time
  required for representations to be made under subsection (3) might be
  prejudicial to the public interest, the Minister may temporarily
  suspend or amend any approval granted by the Minister.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Cessation of effect

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A temporary suspension or amendment of an approval
  ceases to have effect on the earlier of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the expiry of 30 days after the day on which it
    takes effect or of a shorter period that is specified by the
    Minister, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the approval is revoked, suspended or amended
    under subsection (1), the day on which the revocation, suspension or
    amendment takes effect.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 6, s. 330
- [2023, c. 26, s. 605](#1411139-1415837){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1411139-1415837.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1016.3-20070420.html "Link to previous version of section 1016.3"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Confidential undertaking

- **[[1016.31]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1016.31
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If, in the Minister's opinion, the
  disclosure of information about an undertaking required under
  subsection 1016.2(1) or 1016.3(1) or (4), or information that could
  reveal the existence of the undertaking, could pose a threat to the
  integrity or security of the financial institution to which the
  undertaking relates or could be injurious to national security, the
  Minister may specify that the information is confidential and shall be
  treated accordingly.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite anything in this Act but subject to
  subsection (3), it is prohibited to disclose any confidential
  information referred to in subsection (1) except in accordance with
  any terms or conditions that the Minister may specify in the
  undertaking.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice --- Committee and Review Agency

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister specifies under subsection (1) that
  information referred to in that subsection is confidential for reasons
  related to national security, the Minister shall, within 30 days after
  the day on which the undertaking in question is required, notify

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the [[Committee]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}, as defined
    in section 2 of the [National Security and Intelligence Committee of
    Parliamentarians Act](/eng/acts/N-16.6); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the [[Review Agency]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}, as
    defined in section 2 of the [National Security and Intelligence
    Review Agency Act](/eng/acts/N-16.62).

::: HistoricalNote
- [2023, c. 26, s. 606](#1411141-1415848){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1411141-1415848.html"
  role="button"}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of non-compliance on approval

- **[[1016.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1016.4
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Unless otherwise expressly provided
  in this Act, a failure to comply with a term, condition or undertaking
  imposed or required under any provision of this Act does not
  invalidate the approval to which the term, condition or undertaking
  relates.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Non-compliance

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In addition to any other action that may be taken
  under this Act, in the case of non-compliance by a person with a term,
  condition or undertaking imposed or required under any provision of
  this Act, the Minister or the Superintendent, as the case may be, may

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} revoke, suspend or amend the approval to which the
    term, condition or undertaking relates; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} apply to a court for an order directing the person
    to comply with the term, condition or undertaking, and on such an
    application the court may make the order and any other order that it
    thinks fit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Representations

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Before taking any action under subsection (2), the
  Minister or the Superintendent, as the case may be, shall give the
  person concerned a reasonable opportunity to make representations.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Revocation, suspension or amendment

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} At the request of the person concerned, the Minister
  or the Superintendent, as the case may be, may revoke, suspend or
  amend any terms or conditions imposed by him or her and may revoke or
  suspend an undertaking given to him or her or approve its amendment.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 6, s. 330
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Multiple approval --- other approvals

**[[1016.5]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1016.5 .sectionLabel}** The Minister or
the Superintendent may grant more than one approval, other than letters
patent, in a single instrument if he or she considers it appropriate to
do so, and if the Minister or Superintendent does so, he or she may
specify different effective dates for each of the approvals.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 6, s. 330
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exemption in relation to notices of
intention

**[[1016.6]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1016.6 .sectionLabel}** The
Superintendent may, on application, exempt an applicant or applicants
from the provisions of this Act respecting the publication of a notice
of intention in respect of applications for approvals and impose any
terms and conditions respecting the publication of the notice of
intention that he or she considers appropriate.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 6, s. 330
:::

### [Exceptions to Generally Accepted Accounting Principles]{.HTitleText2} {#h-269781 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Calculations --- generally accepted
accounting principles

- **[[1016.61]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1016.61
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If, as a result of a change to the
  accounting principles referred to in subsections 331(4) and 887(4) ---
  whether the change is made before or after this section comes into
  force --- the Superintendent considers, given any prudential
  considerations that he or she considers relevant, that any amount,
  calculation or valuation under this Act or the regulations is not
  appropriate, the Superintendent may specify the amount that is to be
  used or the calculation or valuation that is to be performed instead.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}[Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/)

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Superintendent shall cause a notice of the
  specification to be published in the [Canada
  Gazette](http://www.gazette.gc.ca/) within 60 days after the day on
  which the specification has effect.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Five-year limit

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The specification ceases to have effect on the day
  indicated in the notice, which may be no later than five years after
  the day on which the specification is made.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2012, c. 5, s. 159
:::

### [Orders to Exempt or Adapt]{.HTitleText2} {#h-269791 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Order

- **[[1016.7]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1016.7
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On the recommendation of the
  Minister, the Governor in Council may, by order,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} provide that any provision of this Act or the
    regulations shall not apply to a company, to Her Majesty in right of
    Canada or an agent or agency of Her Majesty or to any other person
    otherwise subject to the provision; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} provide that any provision of this Act or the
    regulations applies to a company, to Her Majesty in right of Canada
    or Her Majesty's agent or agency or to any other person subject to
    the provision only in the manner and to the extent provided for in
    the order, and adapt the provision for the purposes of that
    application.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Minister's recommendation

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may make a recommendation under
  subsection (1) only if the Minister

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is of the opinion that the order would relate to

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the acquisition, holding, sale or other
      disposition of, or other dealing with, shares of a company by, or
      the transfer or issue of shares of a company to, Her Majesty in
      right of Canada or Her Majesty's agent or agency, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the management of the business and affairs or
      the regulation and supervision of a company during the time that
      Her Majesty or Her Majesty's agent or agency is acquiring,
      holding, selling or otherwise disposing of, or otherwise dealing
      with, shares of the company, or during the time that shares of the
      company are transferred or issued to Her Majesty or Her Majesty's
      agent or agency; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is of the opinion --- after considering measures
    other than an order under that subsection and after consulting with
    the Superintendent, the Governor of the Bank of Canada and the Chief
    Executive Officer of the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation ---
    that the order will promote the stability of the financial system in
    Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Terms and conditions

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} On the recommendation of the Minister, the Governor
  in Council may, by order, impose any terms and conditions relating to
  the acquisition of shares of a company by, or transfer or issue of
  shares of a company to, Her Majesty in right of Canada or Her
  Majesty's agent or agency.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Repeal of order under subsection (1)

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may recommend the repeal of an order
  made under subsection (1) without regard to subsection (2).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Terms, conditions and undertakings

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} From the time that Her Majesty in right of Canada or
  an agent or agency of Her Majesty acquires shares of a company to the
  time that the shares are sold or otherwise disposed of, the Minister
  may, by order, impose any terms and conditions on --- or require any
  undertaking from --- the company that the Minister considers
  appropriate, including any terms and conditions or undertakings
  relating to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the remuneration of the company's senior officers,
    as defined in section 678.01, and directors;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the appointment or removal of the company's senior
    officers, as defined in section 678.01, and directors;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the payment of dividends by the company; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the company's lending policies and practices.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Acquisition

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Despite Part X of the [Financial Administration
  Act](/eng/acts/F-11), the Minister or an agent or agency of Her
  Majesty in right of Canada may, on any terms and conditions imposed
  under subsection (3), acquire and hold shares of a company on behalf
  of or in trust for Her Majesty if, as a result of an order under
  subsection (1), the company may record in its securities register the
  transfer or issue of shares to Her Majesty or an agent or agency of
  Her Majesty.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Payment out of C.R.F.

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} On the requisition of the Minister, there may be paid
  out of the Consolidated Revenue Fund the amount that the Minister or
  an agent or agency of Her Majesty in right of Canada is required to
  pay for the acquisition of shares under subsection (6) and any costs
  and expenses incurred in connection with the acquisition, holding,
  sale or other disposition of, or other dealing with, the shares.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registration of shares

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} Shares acquired under subsection (6) by the Minister
  or an agent or agency of Her Majesty in right of Canada shall be
  registered in the name of the Minister, agent or agency, as the case
  may be, in the company's securities register if they are capable of
  being registered in it, and the shares shall be held by the Minister,
  agent or agency, as the case may be, on behalf of or in trust for Her
  Majesty.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disposition by Minister

  [(9)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may, at any time, sell or otherwise
  dispose of shares acquired under subsection (6). The [Surplus Crown
  Assets Act](/eng/acts/S-27) and section 61 of the [Financial
  Administration Act](/eng/acts/F-11) do not apply to the sale or
  disposition.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disposition by agent or agency

  [(10)]{.lawlabel} An agent or agency of Her Majesty in right of Canada
  --- at the request of the Minister, which may be made at any time ---
  shall sell or otherwise dispose of shares acquired under subsection
  (6). The [Surplus Crown Assets Act](/eng/acts/S-27) and section 61 of
  the [Financial Administration Act](/eng/acts/F-11) do not apply to the
  sale or disposition.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Consideration by Minister

  [(11)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister or an agent or agency of Her Majesty
  in right of Canada is holding shares of a company on behalf of or in
  trust for Her Majesty on the day that is two years after the day on
  which the shares were acquired, the Minister shall consider whether
  holding the shares continues to promote the stability of the financial
  system in Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Mandatory disposition

  [(12)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister, under subsection (11), considers
  that holding shares acquired under subsection (6) no longer continues
  to promote the stability of the financial system in Canada, the
  Minister --- or, at the request of the Minister, the agent or agency
  of Her Majesty in right of Canada --- shall take the measures that the
  Minister considers practicable in the circumstances to sell or
  otherwise dispose of the shares. The [Surplus Crown Assets
  Act](/eng/acts/S-27) and section 61 of the [Financial Administration
  Act](/eng/acts/F-11) do not apply to the sale or disposition.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Not a Crown corporation

  [(13)]{.lawlabel} Even if the acquisition of a company's shares under
  subsection (6) would otherwise cause the company to be a Crown
  corporation, as defined in subsection 83(1) of the [Financial
  Administration Act](/eng/acts/F-11), the company is not a Crown
  corporation for the purposes of that Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}[Statutory Instruments
  Act](/eng/acts/S-22)

  [(14)]{.lawlabel} The [Statutory Instruments Act](/eng/acts/S-22) does
  not apply to an order made under this section.

- Definition of [[shares]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  [(15)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section,
  [[shares]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any conversion or exchange privilege, option or
    right to acquire shares; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in reference to a company, participating shares, as
    defined in section 83.01.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Insurance holding company

  [(16)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section other than
  paragraph (15)(b), a reference to a "company" includes a reference to
  an "insurance holding company", and the references to "section 678.01"
  in paragraphs (5)(a) and (b) are to be read, in relation to an
  insurance holding company, as references to "section 1005".

::: HistoricalNote
- 2009, c. 2, s. 287
- 2016, c. 7, s. 176
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1016.7-20090312.html "Link to previous version of section 1016.7"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Orders and Directives]{.HTitleText2} {#h-269839 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Not statutory instruments

**[[1017]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1017 .sectionLabel}** An instrument issued
or made under this Act and directed to a single company, society,
foreign company, provincial company, insurance holding company or
person, other than an order referred to in section 532, is not a
statutory instrument for the purposes of the [Statutory Instruments
Act](/eng/acts/S-22).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Form

**[[1018]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1018 .sectionLabel}** The Superintendent
may, by order, establish the form of any application to be made to the
Minister or the Superintendent under this Act.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

### [Applications to Superintendent]{.HTitleText2} {#h-269848 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Content of applications

- **[[1019]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1019
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The following applications to the
  Superintendent must contain the information, material and evidence
  that the Superintendent may require:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} applications for approval under subsection 69(1),
    76(2), 79(4), 84(1), 178(1), 238(3), 472(1), 495(8) or (12), 498(1)
    or (2) or 512(1), subparagraph 519(2)(b)(vi), section 522,
    subsection 523(2), 527(3) or (4) or 528.3(1), section 542.09 or
    subsection 544.1(2), 557(1) or (2), 569(1), 597(1), 748(1), 755(2),
    757(4), 762(1), 805(1), 851(3), 964(1), 971(6) or (10), 974(1) or
    987(1);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} applications for consent under subsection 75(1) or
    754(1);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} applications for exemptions under subsection
    164.04(3) or 789(3); and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} applications for extensions of time under
    subsection 498(3) or (5), 499(4), 500(4), 557(3) or (5), 558(4),
    559(4), 974(2) or (4), 975(3) or 976(3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Receipt

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Without delay after receiving the application, the
  Superintendent shall send a receipt to the applicant certifying the
  date on which it was received.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of decision to applicant

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), the Superintendent shall,
  within a period of thirty days after the receipt of the application,
  send to the applicant

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a notice approving the application, subject to any
    terms and conditions that the Superintendent considers appropriate;
    or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the Superintendent is not satisfied that the
    application should be approved, a notice to that effect.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Extension of period

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the Superintendent is unable to complete the
  consideration of the application within the period referred to in
  subsection (3), the Superintendent shall, within that period, send a
  notice to the applicant informing the applicant that the
  Superintendent has extended the period for a further period set out in
  the notice.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed approval

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If the applicant does not receive the notice required
  by subsection (3) or, where applicable, subsection (4), within the
  required period, the Superintendent is deemed to have approved the
  application and granted the approval, consent, exemption or extension
  to which the application relates, regardless of whether the approval,
  consent, extension or exemption is to be in writing or not.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2007, c. 6, s. 331
- 2012, c. 5, s. 160
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1019-20070420.html "Link to previous version of section 1019"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Applications for Certain Approvals]{.HTitleText2} {#h-269868 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application for certain approvals

- **[[1019.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1019.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An application for the prior written
  approval of the Minister in respect of any of the following provisions
  must be filed with the Superintendent and contain the information,
  material and evidence that the Superintendent may require:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} paragraphs 441(1)(d), (d.1) and (h);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} paragraphs 495(7)(b.1), (c), (d) and (d.1);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 542(2)(a);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} subsection 554(5), in relation to an entity that is
    engaging in any activity referred to in section 441; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} paragraphs 971(5)(b.1), (c), (d) and (d.1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Certification of receipt of application

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If, in the opinion of the Superintendent, the
  application contains all the required information, the Superintendent
  must refer it to the Minister, together with his or her analysis in
  relation to the application, and send a receipt to the applicant
  certifying the date on which the application was referred to the
  Minister.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Incomplete application

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If, in the opinion of the Superintendent, the
  application is incomplete, the Superintendent must send a notice to
  the applicant specifying the information required by the
  Superintendent to complete it.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of decision

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (5), the Minister must, within
  30 days after the certified date referred to in subsection (2), send
  to the applicant

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a notice approving the application; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the Minister is not satisfied that the
    application should be approved, a notice to that effect.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Extension of period

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister is unable to complete the
  consideration of an application within the 30-day period, the Minister
  must, within that period, send a notice to the applicant informing the
  applicant that the Minister has extended the period for a further
  period set out in the notice.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed approval

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister does not send the notice referred to
  in subsection (4) or, where applicable, subsection (5), within the
  required period, the Minister is deemed to have approved the
  application.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 6, s. 332
- 2012, c. 5, s. 161
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1019.1-20070420.html "Link to previous version of section 1019.1"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Appeals]{.HTitleText2} {#h-269891 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appeal to Federal Court

- **[[1020]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1020 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  appeal lies to the Federal Court from any direction of the Minister
  made under subsection 428(7), 432(1), 432.1(1), 954(7) or 956(1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Powers

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Federal Court may, in an appeal under subsection
  (1),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} dismiss the appeal;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} set aside the direction or decision; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} set aside the direction or decision and refer the
    matter back for redetermination.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Certificate

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of an appeal under subsection (1),
  the Minister shall, at the request of the company, society, foreign
  company, provincial company, insurance holding company or person
  making the appeal, provide the company, society, foreign company,
  provincial company, insurance holding company or person with a
  certificate in writing setting out the direction or decision appealed
  from and the reasons why the direction or decision was made.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2012, c. 31, s. 152
- [2023, c. 26, s. 607](#1411143-1415850){.wb-lbx
  aria-controls="centred-popup" ajax-after="1411143-1415850.html"
  role="button"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1020-20121214.html "Link to previous version of section 1020"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Regulations]{.HTitleText2} {#h-269904 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Power to make regulations

- **[[1021]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1021
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council may make
  regulations

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} prescribing anything that is required or authorized
    by this Act to be prescribed;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} prescribing the way in which anything that is
    required or authorized by this Act to be prescribed is to be
    determined;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} respecting, for any purpose of any provision of the
    Act, the determination of the equity of a company or an insurance
    holding company;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} defining words and expressions to be defined for
    the purposes of this Act;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} requiring the payment of a fee in respect of the
    filing, examining or issuing of any document or in respect of any
    action that the Superintendent is required or authorized to take
    under this Act, and fixing the amount of the fee or the manner of
    determining its amount;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} respecting the regulatory capital and total assets
    of a company, a society, a provincial company or an insurance
    holding company;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} respecting the standards of sound business and
    financial practices for companies, societies, provincial companies
    and foreign companies;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} respecting the retention, in Canada, of assets of a
    company, a society or an insurance holding company;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} respecting the value of assets of a company, a
    society or an insurance holding company to be held in Canada and the
    manner in which those assets are to be held;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} respecting the protection and maintenance of assets
    of a company, a society or an insurance holding company, including
    regulations respecting the bonding of directors, officers and
    employees of a company, a society or an insurance holding company;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} respecting the holding of shares and ownership
    interests for the purposes of section 74, 78 or 753;

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} respecting information, in addition to the
    information required by section 670 or 996, to be maintained in the
    register referred to in that section; and

  - [(m)]{.lawlabel} generally for carrying out the purposes and
    provisions of this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Incorporation by reference

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The regulations may incorporate any material by
  reference regardless of its source and either as it exists on a
  particular date or as amended from time to time.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Incorporated material is not a
  regulation

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Material does not become a regulation for the
  purposes of the [Statutory Instruments Act](/eng/acts/S-22) because it
  is incorporated by reference.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 364
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1021-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 1021"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Delegation]{.HTitleText2} {#h-269927 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Delegation

**[[1022]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1022 .sectionLabel}** The Minister may
delegate any of the Minister's powers, duties and functions under this
Act to any Minister of State appointed under the [Ministries and
Ministers of State Act](/eng/acts/M-8) to assist the Minister.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

## [PART XIX]{.HLabel1}[Sanctions]{.HTitleText1} {#h-269932 .Part}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Offence

**[[1023]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1023 .sectionLabel}** Every person who,
without reasonable cause, contravenes any provision of this Act or the
regulations is guilty of an offence.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}False or misleading information

**[[1023.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1023.1 .sectionLabel}** Every person who
knowingly provides false or misleading information in relation to any
matter under this Act or the regulations is guilty of an offence.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2007, c. 6, s. 333
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Undue preference to creditor

**[[1024]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1024 .sectionLabel}** Every director,
officer or employee of a company or a society who wilfully gives or
concurs in giving to any creditor of the company or society any
fraudulent, undue or unfair preference over other creditors, by giving
security to the creditor, by changing the nature of the creditor's claim
or otherwise, is guilty of an offence.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Failure to provide information

**[[1025]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1025 .sectionLabel}** Every person who,
without reasonable cause, refuses or fails to comply with a requirement
made under paragraph 674(3)(b) or 1000(3)(b) is guilty of an offence.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Use of name

**[[1026]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1026 .sectionLabel}** Except to the extent
permitted by the regulations, every person who uses the name of a
company or of an insurance holding company in a prospectus, offering
memorandum, takeover bid circular, advertisement for a transaction
related to securities or in any other document in connection with a
transaction related to securities is guilty of an offence.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Punishment

- **[[1027]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1027
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every person who is guilty of an
  offence under any of sections 1023 to 1026 is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a natural person, liable

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than
      \$100,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more than twelve
      months, or to both, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not
      more than \$1,000,000 or to imprisonment for a term of not more
      than five years, or to both; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an entity, liable

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} on summary conviction, to a fine of not more than
      \$500,000, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} on conviction on indictment, to a fine of not
      more than \$5,000,000.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Order to comply

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a person has been convicted of an offence under
  this Act, the court may, in addition to any punishment it may
  otherwise impose, order the person to comply with the provisions of
  this Act or the regulations in respect of which the person was
  convicted.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Additional fine

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a person has been convicted of an offence under
  this Act, the court may, if it is satisfied that as a result of the
  commission of the offence the convicted person acquired any monetary
  benefits or that monetary benefits accrued to the convicted person or
  their spouse, common-law partner or other dependant, order the
  convicted person to pay, despite the maximum amount of any fine that
  may otherwise be imposed under this Act, an additional fine in an
  amount equal to three times the court's estimation of the amount of
  those monetary benefits.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 365
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1027-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 1027"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Liability of officers, directors, etc.

**[[1028]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1028 .sectionLabel}** If an entity commits
an offence under this Act, any officer, director or agent of the entity
who directed, authorized, assented to, acquiesced in or participated in
the commission of the offence is a party to and guilty of the offence
and liable on summary conviction or on conviction on indictment to the
punishment provided under paragraph 1027(1)(a) for the offence, whether
or not the entity has been prosecuted or convicted.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitation period

- **[[1029]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1029
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Proceedings by way of summary
  conviction in respect of an offence under a provision of this Act may
  be commenced at any time within, but not later than, two years after
  the day on which the subject-matter of the proceedings became known,
  in the case of an offence under a consumer provision, to the
  Commissioner and, in any other case, to the Superintendent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Certificate of Superintendent or
  Commissioner

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A document appearing to have been issued by the
  Superintendent or Commissioner, as the case may be, certifying the day
  on which the subject-matter of any proceedings became known to the
  Superintendent or Commissioner is admissible in evidence without proof
  of the signature or official character of the person appearing to have
  signed it and is, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, proof of
  the matter asserted in it.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Effect of offence on contracts

**[[1030]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1030 .sectionLabel}** Unless otherwise
expressly provided in this Act, a contravention of any provision of this
Act or the regulations does not invalidate any contract entered into in
contravention of the provision.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Compliance or restraining order

- **[[1031]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1031 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  a company, a society, a foreign company, a provincial company or an
  insurance holding company or any director, officer, employee or agent
  of one does not comply with any provision of this Act or the
  regulations other than a consumer provision, or, in the case of a
  company, a society or an insurance holding company, of the
  incorporating instrument or any by-law of the company, society or
  insurance holding company, the Superintendent, any complainant or any
  creditor of the company, society or insurance holding company may, in
  addition to any other right that person has, apply to a court for an
  order directing the company, society, foreign company, provincial
  company, insurance holding company, director, officer, employee or
  agent to comply with --- or restraining the company, society, foreign
  company, provincial company, insurance holding company, director,
  officer, employee or agent from acting in breach of --- the provision
  and, on the application, the court may so order and make any further
  order it thinks fit.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Compliance or restraining order ---
  consumer provisions

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a company or a foreign company or any director,
  officer, employee or agent of one does not comply with any applicable
  consumer provision, the Commissioner or any complainant may, in
  addition to any other right that person has, apply to a court for an
  order directing the company, foreign company, director, officer,
  employee or agent to comply with --- or restraining the company,
  foreign company, director, officer, employee or agent from acting in
  breach of --- the consumer provision and, on the application, the
  court may so order and make any further order it thinks fit.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appeal of final order

- **[[1032]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1032 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An
  appeal lies to the court of appeal of a province from any final order
  made by a court of that province under this Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appeal with leave

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} An appeal lies to the court of appeal of a province
  from any order, other than a final order made by a court of that
  province, only with leave of the court of appeal in accordance with
  the rules applicable to that court.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
- 2005, c. 54, s. 366
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1032-20030101.html "Link to previous version of section 1032"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Recovery and application of fines

**[[1033]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1033 .sectionLabel}** All fines payable
under this Act are recoverable and enforceable, with costs, at the suit
of Her Majesty in right of Canada, instituted by the Attorney General of
Canada, and, when recovered, belong to Her Majesty in right of Canada.

**\[Note: Sections 712 to 763, enacted by 1991, c. 47 have been replaced
with provisions enacted by 2001, c. 9, s. 465.\]**

**--- 1991, c. 47, s. 763 read as follows:**

- Coming into force

  [[Footnote
  ]{.wb-invisible}^\*^](#I-11.8_en_3){#I-11.8_en_3-ID0EBBCBA}[(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject
  to subsection (2), this Act or any Part thereof, other than
  subsections 702(4), 713(2), 715(2), 716(2), 719(3), 720(2), 721(2),
  722(2), 723(2) and (4), 724(2), 725(2), 726(2), 727(2), 736(2),
  742(2), 743(2) and (4), 745(2) and 746(2) and sections 753 to 760,
  shall come into force on a day or days to be fixed by order of the
  Governor in Council.

- Idem

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsections 268(1) and (2) shall come into force on
  the day that is six months after the coming into force of section 261.

<!-- -->

- ::: Footnote
  [[Return to footnote
  ]{.wb-invisible}^\*^](#I-11.8_en_3-ID0EBBCBA){#I-11.8_en_3}\[Note:
  Act, except the provisions set out in section 763, in force June 1,
  1992, *see* SI/92-91.\]
  :::

::: HistoricalNote
- 2001, c. 9, s. 465
:::

## [PART XX]{.HLabel1}[Documents in Electronic or Other Form]{.HTitleText1} {#h-270006 .Part}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

**[[1034]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1034 .sectionLabel}** The following
definitions apply in this Part.

[[electronic document]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[electronic document]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means, except in section
    1043, any form of representation of information or concepts that is
    fixed in any medium in or by electronic, optical or other similar
    means and that can be read or perceived by a person or by any
    means. ([document électronique]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[information system]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[information system]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a system used to
    generate, send, receive, store or otherwise process an electronic
    document. ([système de traitement de l'information]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 367
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application

**[[1035]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1035 .sectionLabel}** This Part other than
sections 1046 and 1047 does not apply in respect of any notice, document
or other information that under this Act or the regulations is sent to
or issued by the Minister, the Superintendent or the Commissioner or any
prescribed notice, document or information.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 367
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Use not mandatory

**[[1036]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1036 .sectionLabel}** Nothing in this Act
or the regulations requires a person to create or provide an electronic
document.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 367
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Consent and other requirements

- **[[1037]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1037
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite anything in this Part, a
  requirement under this Act or the regulations to provide a notice,
  document or other information is not satisfied by providing an
  electronic document unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the addressee consents and designates an
    information system for the receipt of the electronic document;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the electronic document is, unless otherwise
    prescribed, provided to the designated information system; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the prescribed requirements are complied with.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Consent and notice in electronic form

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), the requirements referred
  to in paragraph (1)(c) may provide that the consent referred to in
  paragraph (1)(a) and any notice related to that consent may be
  provided in electronic form.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations --- revocation of consent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Governor in Council may make regulations
  respecting the revocation of the consent referred to in paragraph
  (1)(a).

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 367
- 2018, c. 27, s. 154
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1037-20110601.html "Link to previous version of section 1037"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Creation or provision of information

**[[1038]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1038 .sectionLabel}** A requirement under
this Act or the regulations to create or provide a notice, document or
other information is satisfied by creating or providing an electronic
document if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the incorporating instrument or by-laws of the
  company, insurance holding company, foreign company, society or
  provincial company, as the case may be, do not provide otherwise; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the prescribed requirements are complied with.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 367
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Creation of information in writing

**[[1039]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1039 .sectionLabel}** A requirement under
this Act or the regulations to create a notice, document or other
information in writing is satisfied by creating an electronic document
if in addition to the conditions set out in section 1038

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the information in the electronic document is
  accessible so as to be usable for subsequent reference; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the prescribed requirements are complied with.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 367
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Provision of information in writing

**[[1040]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1040 .sectionLabel}** A requirement under
this Act or the regulations to provide a notice, document or other
information in writing is satisfied by providing an electronic document
if in addition to the conditions set out in section 1038

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the information in the electronic document is
  accessible by the addressee and capable of being retained by them so
  as to be usable for subsequent reference; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the prescribed requirements are complied with.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 367
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Multiple copies

**[[1041]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1041 .sectionLabel}** A requirement under
this Act or the regulations to provide two or more copies of a document
at the same time to one addressee is satisfied by providing one copy of
the electronic document.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 367
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Registered mail

**[[1042]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1042 .sectionLabel}** A requirement under
this Act or the regulations to provide a document by registered mail is
not satisfied by providing an electronic document except in the
prescribed circumstances.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 367
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Statutory declarations and affidavits

- **[[1043]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1043 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  statutory declaration or affidavit required under this Act or the
  regulations may be created or provided in an electronic document if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person who makes the statutory declaration or
    affidavit signs it with their secure electronic signature;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the authorized person before whom the statutory
    declaration or affidavit is made signs it with their secure
    electronic signature; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the requirements of sections 1036 to 1042 are
    complied with.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section, [[electronic
  document]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} and [[secure electronic
  signature]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} have the same meaning as in subsection
  31(1) of the [Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents
  Act](/eng/acts/P-8.6).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}References to "electronic document"

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of complying with paragraph (1)(c),
  references to [[electronic document]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} in sections
  1036 to 1042 are to be read as references to "electronic document
  within the meaning of subsection 31(1) of the [Personal Information
  Protection and Electronic Documents Act](/eng/acts/P-8.6)".

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 367
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Signatures

**[[1044]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1044 .sectionLabel}** A requirement under
this Act or the regulations for a signature or for a document to be
executed, except in respect of a statutory declaration or affidavit, is
satisfied in respect of an electronic document if the prescribed
requirements are complied with and the signature results from the
application by the person of a technology or process that permits the
following to be proved:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the signature resulting from the use by the person of
  the technology or process is unique to the person;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the technology or process is used by the person to
  incorporate their signature into, attach it to or associate it with
  the electronic document; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the technology or process can be used to identify the
  person using the technology or process.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 367
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Regulations --- provision and receipt of
documents

**[[1045]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1045 .sectionLabel}** The Governor in
Council may make regulations respecting the time and place at which and
the circumstances under which an electronic document is considered to be
provided or received.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 367
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Content and form of notices and documents

**[[1046]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1046 .sectionLabel}** The Minister,
Superintendent or Commissioner may establish the requirements for the
content and fix the form, including electronic and other forms, of
notices and documents sent to or issued by each of them under this Act
or the regulations, including

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the notices and documents that may be sent in
  electronic or other form;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the persons or classes of persons who may send
  notices and documents;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} their signature in electronic or other form or their
  execution, adoption or authorization in a manner that is to have the
  same effect for the purposes of this Act as their signature;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the time and place at which and the circumstances
  under which electronic documents are considered to be sent or
  received; and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} any matter necessary for the purposes of the
  application of this section.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 367
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exemption

**[[1047]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1047 .sectionLabel}** In the prescribed
circumstances, the Minister, the Superintendent or the Commissioner may,
on any conditions that they consider appropriate, exempt from the
application of any provision of this Act requiring a notice or document
to be sent to them any notice or document, or class of notice or
document, containing information similar to that contained in a notice
or document required to be made public under any other Act of Parliament
or any Act of the legislature of a province.

::: HistoricalNote
- 2005, c. 54, s. 367
:::

::: {}
## [SCHEDULE]{.scheduleLabel}[(Section 12)]{.OriginatingRef}[Classes of Insurance]{.scheduleTitleText}  {#h-270096 .scheduleLabel}
:::

> ::: ReadAsText
>
> [[accident and sickness insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
>
> :   [[accident and sickness insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means
>     insurance
>
>     - [(a)]{.lawlabel} against loss resulting from bodily injury to,
>       or the death of, a person caused by an accident;
>
>     - [(b)]{.lawlabel} under which an insurer undertakes to pay a sum
>       or sums of money in the event of bodily injury to, or the death
>       of, a person caused by an accident;
>
>     - [(c)]{.lawlabel} against loss resulting from the sickness or
>       disability of a person not caused by an accident, but excludes
>       loss resulting from the death of the person as a consequence of
>       sickness;
>
>     - [(d)]{.lawlabel} under which an insurer undertakes to pay a sum
>       or sums of money in the event of the sickness or disability of a
>       person not caused by an accident; or
>
>     - [(e)]{.lawlabel} under which an insurer undertakes to pay a sum
>       of money in respect of the health care --- including dental care
>       and preventative care --- of a person. ([accidents et
>       maladie]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})
>
> [[aircraft insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
>
> :   [[aircraft insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means insurance against
>
>     - [(a)]{.lawlabel} liability arising out of bodily injury to, or
>       the death of, a person, or the loss of, or damage to, property,
>       in each case caused by an aircraft or the use of an aircraft; or
>
>     - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the loss of, the loss of use of, or damage to,
>       an aircraft. ([assurance- aviation]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})
>
> [[automobile insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
>
> :   [[automobile insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means insurance
>
>     - [(a)]{.lawlabel} against liability arising out of bodily injury
>       to, or the death of, a person, or the loss of, or damage to,
>       property, in each case caused by an automobile or the use or
>       operation of an automobile;
>
>     - [(b)]{.lawlabel} against the loss of, the loss of use of, or
>       damage to, an automobile; or
>
>     - [(c)]{.lawlabel} that falls within paragraph (a) or (b) of the
>       class of accident and sickness insurance, if the accident is
>       caused by an automobile or the use or operation of an
>       automobile, whether or not liability exists in respect of the
>       accident, and the policy includes insurance against liability
>       arising out of bodily injury to, or the death of, a person
>       caused by an automobile or the use or operation of an
>       automobile. ([automobile]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})
>
> [[boiler and machinery insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
>
> :   [[boiler and machinery insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means
>     insurance
>
>     - [(a)]{.lawlabel} against liability arising out of bodily injury
>       to, or the death of, a person, or the loss of, or damage to,
>       property, or against the loss of, or damage to, property, in
>       each case caused by the explosion or rupture of, or accident to,
>       pressure vessels of any kind or pipes, engines and machinery
>       connected to or operated by those pressure vessels; or
>
>     - [(b)]{.lawlabel} against liability arising out of bodily injury
>       to, or the death of, a person, or the loss of, or damage to,
>       property, or against the loss of, or damage to, property, in
>       each case caused by a breakdown of machinery. ([chaudières et
>       panne de machines]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})
>
> [[credit insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
>
> :   [[credit insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means insurance against
>     loss to a person who has granted credit if the loss is the result
>     of the insolvency or default of the person to whom the credit was
>     given. ([crédit]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})
>
> [[credit protection insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
>
> :   [[credit protection insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means
>     insurance under which an insurer undertakes to pay off credit
>     balances or debts of an individual, in whole or in part, in the
>     event of an impairment or potential impairment in the individual's
>     income or ability to earn an income. ([protection de
>     crédit]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})
>
> [[fidelity insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
>
> :   [[fidelity insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means
>
>     - [(a)]{.lawlabel} insurance against loss caused by the theft, the
>       abuse of trust or the unfaithful performance of duties, by a
>       person in a position of trust; and
>
>     - [(b)]{.lawlabel} insurance under which an insurer undertakes to
>       guarantee the proper fulfilment of the duties of an
>       office. ([détournements]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})
>
> [[fire insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
>
> :   [[fire insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed, 2007, c. 6, s.
>     334\]]{.Repealed}
>
> [[hail insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
>
> :   [[hail insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means insurance against the
>     loss of, or damage to, crops in the field caused by
>     hail. ([grêle]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})
>
> [[legal expenses insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
>
> :   [[legal expenses insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means insurance
>     against the costs incurred by a person or persons for legal
>     services specified in the policy, including any retainer and fees
>     incurred for the services, and other costs incurred in respect of
>     the provision of the services. ([frais
>     juridiques]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})
>
> [[liability insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
>
> :   [[liability insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means insurance, other
>     than insurance that falls within another class of insurance,
>
>     - [(a)]{.lawlabel} against liability arising out of bodily injury
>       to, or the disability or death of, a person, including an
>       employee;
>
>     - [(b)]{.lawlabel} against liability arising out of the loss of,
>       or damage to, property; or
>
>     - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the policy includes the insurance described
>       in paragraph (a), against expenses arising out of bodily injury
>       to a person other than the insured or a member of the insured's
>       family, whether or not liability
>       exists. ([responsabilité]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})
>
> [[life insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
>
> :   [[life insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
>
>     - [(a)]{.lawlabel} means any insurance that is payable
>
>       - [(i)]{.lawlabel} on death,
>
>       - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} on the happening of an event or contingency
>         dependent on human life,
>
>       - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} at a fixed or determinable future time, or
>
>       - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} for a term dependent on human life; and
>
>     - [(b)]{.lawlabel} without restricting the generality of paragraph
>       (a), includes insurance under which an insurer
>
>       - [(i)]{.lawlabel} undertakes to pay an additional sum of money
>         in the event of the death by accident of the person whose life
>         is insured,
>
>       - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} undertakes to pay a sum of money or to
>         provide other benefits in the event that the person whose life
>         is insured becomes disabled as a result of bodily injury or
>         disease, or
>
>       - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} undertakes to provide an annuity --- or
>         what would be an annuity except that the periodic payments may
>         be unequal in amount --- for a term dependent solely or partly
>         on the life of a person. ([assurance-vie]{.DefinedTermLink
>         lang="fr"})
>
> [[loss of employment insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
>
> :   [[loss of employment insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed,
>     2007, c. 6, s. 334\]]{.Repealed}
>
> [[marine insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
>
> :   [[marine insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means insurance against
>
>     - [(a)]{.lawlabel} liability arising out of
>
>       - [(i)]{.lawlabel} bodily injury to, or the death of, a person,
>         or
>
>       - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the loss of, or damage to, property, or
>
>     - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the loss of, or damage to, property,
>
>     occurring during a voyage or marine adventure at sea or on an
>     inland waterway, or during a delay or a transit other than by
>     water that is incidental to a voyage or marine adventure at sea or
>     on an inland waterway. ([maritime]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})
>
> [[mortgage insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
>
> :   [[mortgage insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means insurance against
>     loss caused by default on the part of a borrower under a loan
>     secured by a mortgage or charge on, or other security interest in,
>     real property. ([hypothèque]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})
>
> [[other approved products insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
>
> :   [[other approved products insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means
>     insurance against risks that do not fall within another class of
>     insurance. ([autres produits approuvés]{.DefinedTermLink
>     lang="fr"})
>
> [[property insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
>
> :   [[property insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means insurance against
>     the loss of, or damage to, property and includes insurance against
>     loss caused by forgery. ([assurances de biens]{.DefinedTermLink
>     lang="fr"})
>
> [[surety insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
>
> :   [[surety insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means insurance under
>     which an insurer undertakes to guarantee the due performance of a
>     contract or undertaking or the payment of a penalty or indemnity
>     for any default. ([caution]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})
>
> [[title insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
>
> :   [[title insurance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means insurance against
>     loss or damage caused by
>
>     - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the existence of a mortgage, charge, lien,
>       encumbrance, servitude or any other restriction on real
>       property;
>
>     - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the existence of a mortgage, charge, lien,
>       pledge, encumbrance or any other restriction on personal
>       property;
>
>     - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a defect in any document that evidences the
>       creation of any restriction referred to in paragraph (a) or (b);
>
>     - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a defect in the title to property; or
>
>     - [(e)]{.lawlabel} any other matter affecting the title to
>       property or affecting the right to the use and enjoyment of
>       property. ([titres]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})
> :::

::: HistoricalNote
- 1991, c. 47, Sch.
- 1997, c. 15, s. 333
- SOR/2006-157
- 2007, c. 6, s. 334
- SOR/2010-199(F)

- --- 2015, c. 36, s. 243

  - ###### Retroactivity --- section 672.2 of [Insurance Companies Act](/eng/acts/I-11.8) {#retroactivity-section-672.2-of-insurance-companies-act .MarginalNote}

    [243]{.lawlabel} Section 672.2 of the [Insurance Companies
    Act](/eng/acts/I-11.8) applies to information referred to in that
    section that has been used or in relation to which oral testimony
    has been given or a document has been produced, before the day on
    which this Division comes into force, in any civil proceedings in
    respect of which a final decision has not been made before that day.

- --- 2015, c. 36, s. 244

  - ###### Retroactivity --- section 999.1 of [Insurance Companies Act](/eng/acts/I-11.8) {#retroactivity-section-999.1-of-insurance-companies-act .MarginalNote}

    [244]{.lawlabel} Section 999.1 of the [Insurance Companies
    Act](/eng/acts/I-11.8) applies to information referred to in that
    section that has been used or in relation to which oral testimony
    has been given or a document has been produced, before the day on
    which this Division comes into force, in any civil proceedings in
    respect of which a final decision has not been made before that day.

- --- 2015, c. 36, s. 250

  - ###### Regulations apply --- section 672.2 of [Insurance Companies Act](/eng/acts/I-11.8) {#regulations-apply-section-672.2-of-insurance-companies-act .MarginalNote}

    [250]{.lawlabel} The regulations made under paragraph 1021(1)(a) of
    the [Insurance Companies Act](/eng/acts/I-11.8) that prescribe
    supervisory information for the purposes of section 672.1 of that
    Act apply for the purposes of section 672.2 of that Act until
    regulations made under that paragraph for the purposes of that
    section 672.2 are in force.

- --- 2015, c. 36, s. 251

  - ###### Regulations apply --- section 999.1 of [Insurance Companies Act](/eng/acts/I-11.8) {#regulations-apply-section-999.1-of-insurance-companies-act .MarginalNote}

    [251]{.lawlabel} The regulations made under paragraph 1021(1)(a) of
    the [Insurance Companies Act](/eng/acts/I-11.8) that prescribe
    supervisory information for the purposes of section 999 of that Act
    apply for the purposes of section 999.1 of that Act until
    regulations made under that paragraph for the purposes of that
    section 999.1 are in force.

      [Insurance Companies Act](/eng/acts/I-11.8), as enacted by that
      subsection 347(1), is renumbered as subsection 971(2.01) and, if
      necessary, is repositioned accordingly.

    - [(9)]{.lawlabel} On the first day on which both subsections 337(2)
      and 347(3) of this Act are in force, subparagraphs 971(3)(d)(ii)
      and (iii) of the [Insurance Companies Act](/eng/acts/I-11.8) are
      replaced by the following:

      :::: section
      ::: AmendedText
      - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an entity, other than a
        permitted infrastructure entity, that is not controlled by the
        insurance holding company, a company would be permitted to
        acquire a substantial investment in the other entity under
        subsection 493(2), paragraph 493(3)(b) or (c) or subsection
        493(4) or 495(1), (2), (2.01) or (2.1),

      - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a permitted infrastructure
        entity, whether or not that entity is controlled by the
        insurance holding company, a company would be permitted to
        acquire a substantial investment in the other entity under
        subsection 495(2.01); or
      :::
      ::::

    - [(10)]{.lawlabel} On the first day on which both subsection 337(1)
      and section 348 of this Act are in force, paragraph 977(e) of the
      [Insurance Companies Act](/eng/acts/I-11.8) is replaced by the
      following:

      :::: section
      ::: AmendedText
      - [(e)]{.lawlabel} for the purposes of subsection 971(2.01),
        establishing terms and conditions respecting the acquisition of
        control of, or the acquisition or increase of a substantial
        investment in, a permitted infrastructure entity by an insurance
        holding company.
      :::
      ::::

- --- 2024, c. 15, s. 192

  - - [192]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subsection 140(1) of the French
      version of the [Insurance Companies Act](/eng/acts/I-11.8) is
      replaced by the following:

      :::: section
      ::: {.AmendedText lang="fr"}
      - ###### Lieu des assemblées {#lieu-des-assemblées .MarginalNote}

        - [140]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} Les assemblées des
          actionnaires ou des souscripteurs se tiennent au Canada, au
          lieu que prévoient les règlements administratifs ou, à défaut,
          que choisissent les administrateurs.
      :::
      ::::

    - [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection 140(2) of the Act is replaced by the
      following:

      :::: section
      ::: AmendedText
      - ###### Participation by electronic means {#participation-by-electronic-means .MarginalNote}

        [(2)]{.lawlabel} Unless the by-laws provide otherwise and in
        accordance with any regulations, any person who is entitled to
        attend a meeting of shareholders or policyholders may
        participate in the meeting by means of a telephonic, electronic
        or other communication facility that permits all participants to
        communicate adequately with each other during the meeting if the
        company makes one available. A person who is participating in a
        meeting by one of those means is deemed for the purposes of this
        Act to be present at the meeting.

      - ###### Meeting held by electronic means {#meeting-held-by-electronic-means .MarginalNote}

        [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} If the directors, shareholders or
        policyholders of a company call a meeting of shareholders or
        policyholders under this Act, those directors, shareholders or
        policyholders may determine that the meeting shall be held, in
        accordance with any regulations, entirely by means of a
        telephonic, electronic or other communication facility that
        permits all participants to communicate adequately with each
        other during the meeting, if the by-laws so provide.
      :::
      ::::

- --- 2024, c. 15, s. 193

  - [193]{.lawlabel} Subsection 157(4) of the Act is replaced by the
    following:

    :::: section
    ::: AmendedText
    - ###### Voting while participating electronically {#voting-while-participating-electronically .MarginalNote}

      [(4)]{.lawlabel} Unless the by-laws provide otherwise and in
      accordance with any regulations, any person who is participating
      in a meeting of shareholders or policyholders under subsection
      140(2) or (2.1) and entitled to vote at that meeting may vote by
      means of the telephonic, electronic or other communication
      facility that the company has made available for that purpose.
    :::
    ::::

        [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} If the directors or shareholders of an

    - ###### Voting while participating electronically {#voting-while-participating-electronically-1 .MarginalNote}

      [(4)]{.lawlabel} Unless the by-laws provide otherwise and in

- --- 2024, c. 17, s. 400

  - [400]{.lawlabel} The [Insurance Companies Act](/eng/acts/I-11.8) is
    amended by adding the following after section 166:

    :::: section
    ::: AmendedText
    ##### [Disclosure Relating to Diversity]{.HTitleText3} {#disclosure-relating-to-diversity .SchedHeadL3}

    - ###### Diversity {#diversity .MarginalNote}

      - [166.1]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} The directors of a company
        of a prescribed class must make available, in accordance with
        regulations made under subsection (2), information respecting
        diversity among directors and members of senior management, as
        defined by regulation, at the same time that a notice of annual
        meeting is sent under subsection 143(1) to shareholders and
        policy holders entitled to receive that notice and to the
        Superintendent.

      - ###### Regulations {#regulations-10 .MarginalNote}

        [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), the
        Governor in Council may make regulations respecting the
        disclosure of information related to diversity among the
        directors and members of senior management of a company of a
        prescribed class.
    :::
    ::::

- --- 2024, c. 17, s. 401

  - [401]{.lawlabel} The Act is amended by adding the following after
    section 795:

    :::: section
    ::: AmendedText
    ###### [Disclosure Relating to Diversity]{.HTitleText4} {#disclosure-relating-to-diversity-1 .SchedHeadL4}

    - ###### Diversity {#diversity-1 .MarginalNote}

      - [795.1]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} The directors of an
        insurance holding company of a prescribed class must make
        available, in accordance with regulations made under subsection
        (2), information respecting diversity among directors and
        members of senior management, as defined by regulation, at the
        same time that a notice of annual meeting is sent under
        subsection 767(1) to shareholders entitled to receive that
        notice and to the Superintendent.

      - ###### Regulations {#regulations-11 .MarginalNote}

        [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of subsection (1), the Governor
        in Council may make regulations respecting the disclosure of
        information related to diversity among the directors and members
        of senior management of an insurance holding company of a
        prescribed class.
    :::
    ::::
